9.meaning: 'He / it commanded us' or 'he ordered us' — the completed act of giving us an order or instruction.
9.grammar: Past-tense verb 'amara' (he commanded) with the attached object pronoun '-nā' ('us'). The '-a-' on the stem marks a third-person masculine singular doer ('he') and a completed action.
9.root: ء-م-ر (ʾ-m-r) — commanding, ordering

10.meaning: with it / by it — a preposition meaning 'with' or 'by means of' joined to a pronoun referring to a single feminine (or grammatically feminine) thing.
10.grammar: The bi- prefix is a preposition meaning 'with', 'by', or 'by means of'. The attached -hā is an object pronoun meaning 'it' or 'her', referring to something feminine in gender. Together they mean 'with it' or 'by means of it'.

11.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
11.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

12.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
12.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

13.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
13.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

14.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
14.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

15.meaning: 'He commands / orders / bids' — the act of giving orders or enjoining, said of a single doer, in the present tense.
15.grammar: Present-tense verb. The 'ya-' prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it'). The final '-u' is the indicative mood, signalling an ongoing or general/habitual action.
15.root: ء-م-ر (ʾ-m-r) — commanding, ordering

16.meaning: A prepositional phrase, 'to/with immorality (al-faḥshāʾ)' — al-faḥshāʾ being gross indecency, shameful and outrageous conduct, especially sexual immorality and any flagrant moral excess.
16.grammar: A definite noun governed by the preposition bi- ('with, by, to'). The final -i is the genitive ending, which is required after a preposition and marks the noun as the object of that preposition.
16.root: ف-ح-ش (f-ḥ-sh) — to be excessive, grossly indecent

17.meaning: A question 'Do you (plural) say…?' — challenging or asking a group whether they assert or claim something, in the present tense.
17.grammar: An interrogative particle 'a-' ('do…?') prefixed to a present-tense verb. The 'ta-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks a masculine plural addressee ('you all') in the indicative (ongoing action); the leading 'a-' turns the statement into a question.
17.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speaking

18.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
18.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
18.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

19.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
19.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

20.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
20.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

21.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
21.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

22.meaning: A verb addressed to a group: 'you (all) know', 'you have knowledge', 'you are aware'. From the root meaning 'to know'.
22.grammar: The 'ta-' prefix marks a present/future verb addressed to 'you'. The '-ūna' ending marks a masculine plural subject and is the full 'indicative' form, signalling an ongoing, factual statement ('you (all) do know'), as opposed to the shortened '-ū' used after certain particles.

1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
1.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

2.meaning: A verb meaning 'he commanded', 'he ordered', or 'he enjoined' — to issue an authoritative instruction that something be done.
2.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'). The bare three-letter stem ending in -a denotes a completed action by a single male subject: 'he gave a command'. It commonly takes a person commanded and a thing commanded.

3.meaning: 'My Lord' — the Master, Sustainer and Nurturer, claimed in close personal relation by the speaker.
3.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord') with the attached pronoun -ī meaning 'my'. This 'my' ending merges with the case-vowel of the noun, so a single long -ī is heard. The sense is 'the Lord who is mine'.
3.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord/master, to nurture and sustain

4.meaning: Justice, fairness, equity — giving each thing its rightful due and acting with balanced, upright dealing. The attached preposition gives the sense 'with justice' or 'in fairness'.
4.grammar: A noun preceded by the preposition 'bi' ('with/by') and the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The final '-i' is the genitive case, which is the form a noun regularly takes after a preposition; the whole conveys 'with the justice' or 'in fairness'.
4.root: ق-س-ط (q-s-ṭ) — justice, equity, fair measure

5.meaning: And establish / set up / perform fully — a command to make something stand firm and upright, to carry it out properly and consistently (used especially of performing prayer rightly).
5.grammar: The conjunction wa- ('and') joined to a plural command verb of the causative (af'ala) pattern, meaning to make something stand/be upright. The -ū ending marks a masculine-plural addressee being told to do it.
5.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise, be upright; to establish

6.meaning: Faces belonging to a plural 'you' — the front of the heads, the part one turns and directs toward something; can also figuratively mean attention, orientation, or one's whole self as turned somewhere.
6.grammar: A plural noun (singular wajh, 'face') carrying the attached pronoun -kum, 'your' for a group. The -a ending before the pronoun is accusative, the case typically used for the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon, e.g. what is turned or directed).
6.root: و-ج-ه (w-j-h) — face, direction, to turn toward

7.meaning: 'With / in the presence of / near' — an adverb of place and relation meaning at, by, in the sight or estimation of someone. It indicates nearness, possession, or what holds in someone's view (as in 'with Allah' = in His sight).
7.grammar: An adverb of place that is always followed by a noun it relates to. It carries a fixed -a ending; this accusative-type vowel is characteristic of such adverbs of place and shows the word is functioning to locate something ('at, near, in the presence of').

8.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
8.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.

9.meaning: A place of prostration and worship — a mosque; literally the spot where one bows down to the ground in submission to Allah.
9.grammar: A noun of place built on the pattern maf'il, naming the location where an action happens (here, the place of prostration). The ending '-in' (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a mosque') and in the genitive case — the form used after a preposition or in a possessive link.
9.root: س-ج-د (s-j-d) — to prostrate, bow down in worship

10.meaning: 'And call upon Him / invoke Him' — a command to a group to call out to, supplicate, and appeal to Him.
10.grammar: An imperative (command) verb addressed to a plural 'you', joined by 'wa' ('and') and carrying the object pronoun '-hu' ('Him'). The long '-ū' ending is the plural-command marker, directing more than one person to perform the act of calling/invoking.

11.meaning: Being sincere and single-hearted — making one's devotion purely and exclusively for Allah, with no rival motive mixed in. It describes a group of people in this state.

parts.en: one who is sincere / devotes purely

11.grammar: A Form IV active participle (pattern muf'il, from the verb akhlaṣa 'to make pure / devote sincerely'), describing the one who purifies and dedicates his devotion. It is in the sound masculine plural, and the '-īna' ending marks the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) case, so it describes a plural group as those who make their worship purely and sincerely for Allah.
11.root: خ-ل-ص (kh-l-ṣ) — to be pure, sincere, unmixed

12.meaning: To him / for him / he has — the preposition 'to/for' fused with a pronoun meaning 'him.' It expresses belonging, benefit, or possession (something is 'his' or done 'for him').
12.grammar: A preposition 'li-/la-' ('to, for') with the attached 3rd-person masculine singular pronoun 'him.' The pairing means 'to him' or 'for him' and often conveys possession ('he has …') or that an action is directed toward his benefit or detriment.
12.root: — (particle with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

13.meaning: Religion, the way of life and obedience owed to Allah — encompassing faith, devotion, the binding code of worship, and the final reckoning. A weighty term broader than the English 'religion'.
13.grammar: A definite noun ('the dīn') with the article 'al-' (its 'l' assimilating into the following 'd'). The final '-a' is the accusative case, the form a noun takes when it is the direct object of a verb or otherwise governed into that state.

14.meaning: 'Just as / in the same way that' — a phrase of comparison joining 'like / as' to 'what', meaning 'like that which...' or 'in the manner that...'.
14.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like / as') joined to mā ('what / that which'). Together they introduce a likeness or manner — 'just as...', 'in the same way that...' — comparing one thing or action to another.

15.meaning: 'He originated / brought you into being' — He began and first created you, starting your existence from nothing. Addressed to a plural 'you'.
15.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third-person masculine singular ('He …'), carrying the object pronoun '-kum' ('you', plural). The bare verb form with no added subject ending signals a completed act done by 'He'.
15.root: ب-د-أ (b-d-ʾ) — to begin, originate, bring into being

16.meaning: 'You will return / be brought back' — a plural 'you' returning or being made to return to a starting point or destination.
16.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The 'ta-' prefix marks second-person address ('you'), and the '-ūna' ending marks the masculine plural in the indicative mood, giving 'you (all) return / will return'.
16.root: ع-و-د (ʿ-w-d) — to return, come back, repeat

1.meaning: A group, faction, party, or portion of people — a section split off from a larger body.
1.grammar: A singular indefinite noun. The -an (tanwīn fatḥ) ending marks the accusative case with indefiniteness, typically signalling the direct object of a verb ('a group'), or an adverbial sense.

2.meaning: 'He guided' — He showed the right way, led to the correct path, and directed toward the truth. A completed act by 'He'.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('He guided'). Its final root letter is a weak one that surfaces as the long vowel '-ā' (written with alif maqṣūra), the regular shape such verbs take in the completed 'He' form.

3.meaning: A group, party, or faction — a distinct portion of people. Joined by 'and,' it introduces a further such group, often contrasted with another previously mentioned.
3.grammar: A noun ('a group') with the -an ending, the accusative indefinite case, which typically marks the object of a verb or a fronted noun. The wa- prefix means 'and,' coordinating it with something mentioned before.
3.root: ف-ر-ق (f-r-q) — to separate, divide; a division/party

4.meaning: Due right, just measure, rightful claim; that which is true and rightly owed — here used to mean 'as is truly its due'.
4.grammar: A noun meaning 'truth, right, due'. The final -a (accusative) often marks the object of a verb, and in a possessive phrase like this it commonly conveys the sense 'with the full right/due OF …', i.e. as something deserves to be done.
4.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, that which is due and real

5.meaning: 'Upon them / against them' — the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, against') carrying an attached plural pronoun referring to a group of males.
5.grammar: ʿalā ('upon') takes the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The -him ending is the attached pronoun for a masculine plural 'them'; its final vowel appears as -u (himu) to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with the definite article.

6.meaning: Error, misguidance, straying — the state of having lost or wandered off the right path, the opposite of guidance.
6.grammar: A definite feminine noun ('the straying') with the article 'al-' (its 'l' assimilating into 'ḍ'). The final '-u' is the nominative case, the form a noun takes when it is the subject of a sentence or otherwise stands in that base state.
6.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, go astray, err

7.meaning: 'Indeed they / truly they' — combines an emphatic opener that strongly affirms what follows ('indeed, certainly') with the pronoun 'they'.
7.grammar: The emphatic particle 'inna' ('indeed/truly'), which strengthens and confirms a statement, joined to the attached pronoun 'they'. After 'inna' this pronoun stands as the subject being spoken about; the 'u' on '-humu' is a connecting vowel eased before the next word.

8.meaning: Past-tense verb (reflexive form), third person plural: 'they took for themselves, adopted, chose.' A completed act of taking something on as one's own.
8.grammar: A completed-action (past) verb in a reflexive pattern (taking something for oneself). The '-ū' ending (with silent trailing alif) marks the subject as 'they' (masculine plural). The opening 'i-' is a helping vowel that lets the cluster of consonants be pronounced.

9.meaning: The devils / satans — rebellious, malevolent beings who tempt and lead astray; the plural of shayṭān.
9.grammar: A definite (with al- 'the') broken plural in the accusative case. The plural pattern itself is shayāṭīn-; the accusative is marked by the single final vowel -a added to that stem (giving shayāṭīn-a), which typically marks the object of a verb or a noun governed by a particle such as inna/lākinna. As a diptote plural it takes no nunation.
9.root: ش-ط-ن (sh-ṭ-n) — to be remote/rebellious; hence a devil

10.meaning: Allies, protectors, intimate friends — those taken as close supporters, patrons, or guardians, with whom one stands in mutual loyalty (plural of walī).
10.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of 'walī.' Being a 'diptote' (a noun that resists the usual full set of endings), it takes a single final '-a' here for the accusative case, which commonly marks the direct object of a verb or signals 'as / being' something — and notably without the usual '-n' (no nunation).

11.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
11.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

12.meaning: A noun used to mean 'besides', 'other than', 'apart from', or 'short of'. It points to something or someone set apart from, or lower/lesser than, a named party. Often used in the phrase 'besides Allah'.
12.grammar: 'dūn' functions as an adverb-like noun of place/relation. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, which appears because it follows a preposition (such as 'min', 'from') and because it links to a following noun ('other than …'). It commonly heads the construction 'besides/other than [someone]'.
12.root: د-و-ن (d-w-n) — to be low/beneath, to fall short; hence 'below, other than, besides'

13.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
13.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

14.meaning: 'And they think / reckon / suppose' — they hold an opinion or assume something to be the case, often an assumption that may prove mistaken.
14.grammar: A present-tense verb joined by 'wa' ('and/while'). The 'ya-' prefix marks third-person ('they'), and the '-ūna' ending marks the masculine plural in the indicative mood, giving 'they think / reckon'.

15.meaning: 'That they…' — an emphatic connector 'anna' ('that, indeed') fused with the pronoun 'they,' used to introduce an affirmed clause as the content of a thought or statement.
15.grammar: Built on the particle 'anna' ('that…, indeed'), which introduces and affirms a following clause (often after verbs of knowing, thinking, or saying) and puts its noun into the accusative. The attached '-hum' is the pronoun 'they/them' for a male-inclusive group.

16.meaning: Those who are rightly guided — people who have found and follow the correct path. It describes a plural group in that guided state.
16.grammar: An active participle of a reflexive pattern (one who has accepted/found guidance for himself), in the masculine plural. The '-ūna' ending is the sound masculine plural in the nominative (subject) form, describing a group as 'rightly guided ones'.
16.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, be rightly guided

1.meaning: 'O Children of … / O descendants of …' — a vocative call addressing the offspring or lineage of someone (literally 'sons of'), used to summon a people by their ancestry.
1.grammar: The vocative particle yā ('O') prefixed to the plural of 'son' in its construct (possessive-linking) form. As a construct noun it is set to be followed by a possessor ('… OF …'), giving 'O Children of …'. The -ī form here is the plural in the genitive/accusative shape used in construct.
1.root: ب-ن-ي (b-n-y) — to build; (banūn) sons, children, descendants

2.meaning: 'Adam' — the proper name of the first human being and first prophet.
2.grammar: A proper name that is a diptote (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf) — it takes a restricted set of endings. Its final -a here does double duty: it marks the accusative case (e.g., as a direct object) and, because the name is a diptote, it stands in place of the usual nominative -u while also blocking the tanwīn (-n) that fully inflected nouns would take.

3.meaning: "Take! / Hold! / Grasp!" — a command to take hold of something firmly, to grasp, seize, or hold fast; addressed to a group.
3.grammar: An imperative (command) verb addressed to a masculine plural 'you all'. The '-ū' ending is what directs the order at a group; the written 'alif' after it is silent and merely caps the plural verb form. The imperative is built on the same root as 'to take' but drops the root's initial hamza.

4.meaning: 'Your adornment' — that with which a person beautifies or decorates themselves: fine clothing, ornament, and pleasing appearance. Belonging to a plural 'you'.
4.grammar: A feminine noun carrying the possessive pronoun '-kum' ('your', plural). The '-a' before the pronoun marks the accusative case, the form taken when the noun is a direct object or otherwise governed into that state.
4.root: ز-ي-ن (z-y-n) — to adorn, beautify, decorate

5.meaning: 'With / in the presence of / near' — an adverb of place and relation meaning at, by, in the sight or estimation of someone. It indicates nearness, possession, or what holds in someone's view (as in 'with Allah' = in His sight).
5.grammar: An adverb of place that is always followed by a noun it relates to. It carries a fixed -a ending; this accusative-type vowel is characteristic of such adverbs of place and shows the word is functioning to locate something ('at, near, in the presence of').
5.root: — (adverb of place)

6.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
6.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.

7.meaning: A place of prostration and worship — a mosque; literally the spot where one bows down to the ground in submission to Allah.
7.grammar: A noun of place built on the pattern maf'il, naming the location where an action happens (here, the place of prostration). The ending '-in' (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a mosque') and in the genitive case — the form used after a preposition or in a possessive link.
7.root: س-ج-د (s-j-d) — to prostrate, bow down in worship

8.meaning: 'And eat' — a command to a group to eat, partake of food, or consume.
8.grammar: An imperative (command) verb addressed to a plural 'you', joined by 'wa' ('and'). The long '-ū' ending is the plural-command marker (written with a silent final alif), directing more than one person to eat.

9.meaning: 'And drink!' — a command addressed to a group to drink, joined to what precedes by 'and'.
9.grammar: A command (imperative) verb with a connecting 'wa' ('and') prefixed. The -ū ending directs the order at a plural 'you' (a group of males or a mixed group): 'and you all, drink!' The initial vowel of the stem is a helping vowel that drops after the prefix.
9.root: ش-ر-ب (sh-r-b) — drinking

10.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
10.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

11.meaning: That you act wastefully or go to excess; to overstep the proper limit, squander, or be immoderate. It conveys spending or doing beyond what is right or needed.
11.grammar: A present-tense verb in a form that often follows particles of negation, prohibition, or purpose. The 'tu-' prefix plus '-ū' ending mean 'you (plural)'. The final short vowel is dropped (showing 'tusrifū' not 'tusrifūna'), which signals the verb is governed by such a particle (e.g. 'do not…' or 'so that…').
11.root: س-ر-ف (s-r-f) — to exceed the limit, waste, be extravagant

12.meaning: An emphasis particle fused with a pronoun, meaning 'indeed He' or 'truly He'. The particle inna strongly affirms and certifies the statement that follows ('it is certainly the case that…'), with 'He' as its subject.
12.grammar: The emphasising particle inna ('indeed/truly') with the attached pronoun -hu ('He'). inna affirms and strengthens the whole statement and grammatically takes a following noun or pronoun as its subject. The lengthened -hū is how this pronoun is pronounced after an -u vowel.

13.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
13.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

14.meaning: He loves / likes / holds dear. To have affection for and approval of something or someone.
14.grammar: A present-tense verb in the fourth pattern, third-person masculine singular ('he…'). The yu- prefix signals a single masculine subject, and the final -u ending marks the indicative mood, presenting the action as an established fact or ongoing reality.
14.root: ح-ب-ب (ḥ-b-b) — love, affection; to hold dear

15.meaning: Those who are wasteful and excessive — people who overstep proper limits, squander, and go to extremes, especially in spending or conduct.
15.grammar: A definite active participle ('the wasteful ones') with the article 'al-'. The '-īna' ending marks the sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) form, describing a plural group as those who are extravagant and overstep bounds.
15.root: س-ر-ف (s-r-f) — to be excessive, wasteful, exceed bounds

1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
1.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

2.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
2.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

3.meaning: 'He forbade / made unlawful / declared sacredly off-limits.' To prohibit something firmly, to render it ḥarām — barred and inviolable, set outside what is permitted.
3.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) Form II verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he [did it],' a completed past action. The doubled middle root letter (Form II) gives an intensive/causative force — 'to make something forbidden/inviolable.'

4.meaning: Adornment, beauty, finery — that which decorates and makes something attractive, whether ornament, fine clothing, or pleasing splendour.
4.grammar: A feminine noun. The final '-a' is the accusative case, the form a noun takes as a direct object or when otherwise governed into that state; the 't' here is the feminine marker pronounced in connected reading.
4.root: ز-ي-ن (z-y-n) — to adorn, beautify, decorate

5.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
5.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

6.meaning: A feminine singular relative pronoun: 'the one which / that which / who' (referring to a single feminine thing). It introduces a descriptive clause that tells us more about a preceding feminine noun.
6.grammar: A relative pronoun, feminine singular, fixed in form (it does not change for case). It links a feminine noun to a following clause describing it, the equivalent of English 'which,' 'that,' or 'who.'

7.meaning: 'He brought out / expelled / drove out' — to make someone or something come out, the completed act of one male doer.
7.grammar: Past-tense verb in the causative pattern 'afʿala' ('akhraja' = to cause to go out). The bare stem with a final '-a' and no added subject marks a third-person masculine singular doer ('he') and a completed action.

8.meaning: 'For His servants/slaves' — belonging to or directed toward those who are His worshippers, the human beings who are wholly His. The preposition adds 'for/to'.
8.grammar: A plural noun ('servants') preceded by the preposition 'li' ('for/to') and carrying the possessive pronoun '-hi' ('His'). The '-i' is the genitive case, regularly used after a preposition and in a possessive link; the pronoun takes the form '-hi' after this 'i' vowel.

9.meaning: 'And the good/pure things' — wholesome, lawful, agreeable things, especially good food and what is fine and clean. The plural refers to such good things collectively.
9.grammar: A definite adjective/noun used substantively ('the good things'), joined by 'wa' ('and') with the article 'al-' (its 'l' assimilating into 'ṭ'). The '-āti' ending is the sound feminine plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) form.
9.root: ط-ي-ب (ṭ-y-b) — to be good, pure, wholesome, pleasant

10.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
10.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

11.meaning: Provision, sustenance — what Allah bestows to support life: food, livelihood, and every granted blessing one lives on.
11.grammar: A definite noun ('the provision') with the article 'al-' (its 'l' assimilating into 'r'). The final '-i' is the genitive case, the form taken after a preposition or in a possessive link ('… of …').
11.root: ر-ز-ق (r-z-q) — to provide, sustain, bestow livelihood

12.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
12.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

13.meaning: A standalone pronoun meaning 'she' or 'it' (feminine). Arabic has no neuter, so 'it' for a feminine noun is expressed with this word. Used independently for emphasis or to stand as the subject of a sentence.
13.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person feminine singular. It stands on its own (not attached to another word) and most often functions as the subject of a nominal sentence ('she/it is …'). Its form is fixed and does not take case endings.

14.meaning: A compound meaning 'for those who' or 'belonging to those who'. It joins the preposition 'for/to' with a masculine plural relative pronoun ('those who'), introducing a clause that describes a group of people by something they do or possess.
14.grammar: The prefix 'li-' is a preposition meaning 'for', 'to', or expressing ownership/benefit ('belonging to'). The relative pronoun is 'alladhīna' ('those who'), but when 'li-' attaches to it the connecting hamza of 'al-' drops out and the two lām sounds merge into one doubled lām, so the form is written and read 'lilladhīna' rather than 'li-alladhīna'. 'alladhīna' has a fixed shape and does not change for case.

15.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
15.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.
15.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, security, trust, faith

16.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
16.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
16.root: — (particle)

17.meaning: 'The life' — living existence, the state of being alive.
17.grammar: The definite article al- with the feminine noun ḥayāt ('life'); the waw belongs to the stem and the tā' marbūṭa is its feminine suffix. The final -i is the genitive case vowel, which typically marks the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to a following noun.
17.root: ح-ي-ي (ḥ-y-y) — life, being alive, living

18.meaning: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
18.grammar: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
18.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world

19.meaning: An adjective meaning 'pure / unmixed / exclusive' — something purely and solely one thing, free of any admixture, reserved for one party alone.
19.grammar: A feminine adjective (the ة marks the feminine form). The ending -an (written -tan with the feminine ة) is the indefinite accusative — the case often used for the object of a verb or for a descriptive/state word, and the extra -n (nunation) signals 'a/an', i.e. indefinite. It conveys '(being) purely/exclusively'.

20.meaning: Day — a span of time; frequently used to denote a momentous appointed Day, especially the Day of Resurrection and Judgment.
20.grammar: A noun ending in the accusative vowel -a. On a time-word like this the accusative commonly works adverbially to mean 'on the day (when…)' or 'on a day', setting the time-frame for an action.

21.meaning: "the Resurrection" — the standing-up of all people from death to be judged; literally the act of rising or standing up.
21.grammar: The al- prefix means "the." The -i ending (on the feminine -t) is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ("the … OF this") or follows a preposition.

22.meaning: 'Like that / thus / in this manner.' A comparison word meaning that something is done or is the case in the way just mentioned.
22.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like/as') prefixed to the demonstrative 'that'. Together they form a fixed adverbial expression, 'like that / thus', which does not change its ending with grammatical position.
22.root: — (a particle of comparison joined to a demonstrative; no root)

23.meaning: 'We set out in detail / expound clearly' — to distinguish a thing part by part, laying it out distinctly and explaining it in full detail.
23.grammar: A present-tense verb of the intensive (form II) pattern, which adds the sense of doing something thoroughly or part by part. The nu- prefix marks a first-person plural subject ('we'). The final -u is the indicative ending, marking a plain ongoing or habitual action ('we expound in detail').
23.root: ف-ص-ل (f-ṣ-l) — separating, distinguishing, setting apart in detail

24.meaning: 'The signs / the verses' — the plural of 'sign,' referring to clear indicators, proofs, miracles, or the verses of revelation that point to truth.
24.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun ('the signs'), made definite by the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The sound feminine plural takes the -i ending when it is an object of a verb or linked after a preposition or possessor — that is, when it is grammatically governed rather than serving as the subject.

25.meaning: 'For a people / for a folk' — directed toward a community or group of human beings considered collectively.
25.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('for/to') joined to a noun 'people.' Because it follows a preposition, the noun takes the genitive, and the tanwīn (the -in ending) marks it as indefinite ('a people'). The whole phrase means 'for a people,' directing something toward that group.
25.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand/rise; a people, community

26.meaning: They know; they have knowledge, understanding, or awareness of something. The verb denotes possessing knowledge as an ongoing state.
26.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'). The ya- prefix marks the subject and the -ūna ending marks a masculine plural in the ordinary (indicative) present tense, describing ongoing or habitual knowing.
26.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — knowledge, knowing, awareness

1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
1.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

2.meaning: 'Only / nothing but' — a restrictive particle that limits and emphasizes, asserting that the matter is exclusively so and no other ('it is only...'). It combines the emphatic 'inna' with the restricting 'mā'.
2.grammar: A compound particle formed from the emphatic inna ('indeed') and mā, which together work as a tool of restriction meaning 'only / nothing but'. It both stresses and confines the statement that follows to a single truth, excluding all alternatives.

3.meaning: 'He forbade / made unlawful / declared sacredly off-limits.' To prohibit something firmly, to render it ḥarām — barred and inviolable, set outside what is permitted.
3.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) Form II verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he [did it],' a completed past action. The doubled middle root letter (Form II) gives an intensive/causative force — 'to make something forbidden/inviolable.'

4.meaning: My Lord, Master, and Sustainer — the One who owns, nurtures, and governs me; expressing ownership together with intimate care.
4.grammar: A masculine noun with the attached first-person possessive ("my"). The suffix -iya means "my" and, being a possessive ending, fixes the noun's relationship rather than leaving it to a case vowel. It denotes that the Lord is being claimed as one's own.
4.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, ownership, nurturing and sustaining to completion

5.meaning: Gross indecencies and shameful deeds; acts of flagrant immorality whose ugliness is plain, especially sexual sins. The word names sins that exceed all bounds of decency.
5.grammar: A definite broken (irregular) plural noun ('al-' = 'the'). The final '-a' is accusative, the case typically marking the noun as the object of a verb (the things done, forbidden, or approached).
5.root: ف-ح-ش (f-ḥ-sh) — to be excessive, grossly indecent

6.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
6.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

7.meaning: It became apparent, visible, or open; it came out into the open. The verb means to show or manifest plainly, and can also carry the sense of being outward or external as opposed to hidden.
7.grammar: A past-tense (completed action) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it'). The 3ms past form carries no overt subject suffix; the final fatḥa is the inherent vowel of the verb's own pattern, not a subject-marking ending. It presents the becoming-apparent as something that has happened.
7.root: ظ-ه-ر (ẓ-h-r) — to appear, become manifest, be outward

8.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'min' ('from / out of / some of') joined to the pronoun 'it' (feminine). Together: 'from it / out of it / of it,' indicating a source or a portion taken from a feminine thing.
8.grammar: A preposition 'min' with the attached pronoun '-hā' ('it/her'), referring to a feminine noun. 'Min' indicates origin, source, or a part taken from a whole; the attached pronoun is in the object form required after a preposition.

9.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
9.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
9.root: — (relative pronoun / particle)

10.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'it was hidden, concealed, or inward' — to be on the inside, out of sight, beneath the surface, as opposed to what is open and visible.
10.grammar: A third-person masculine singular verb in the past (perfect) tense; the bare -a ending marks 'he/it' as the doer of a completed action. Built on the simple Form I pattern faʿala.
10.root: ب-ط-ن (b-ṭ-n) — belly, interior, what is hidden/inward

11.meaning: 'And sin / wrongdoing' — a moral offence, an act of disobedience that incurs blame and guilt before Allah.
11.grammar: A definite noun ('the sin'), joined by 'wa' ('and') with the article 'al-'. The final '-a' is the accusative case, the form a noun takes as a direct object or when otherwise governed into that state.
11.root: ا-ث-م (ʾ-th-m) — to sin, do wrong, incur guilt

12.meaning: 'And transgression / wrongful aggression' — overstepping just limits against others: oppression, insolence, and unjust assault on what is right.
12.grammar: A definite noun ('the transgression'), joined by 'wa' ('and') with the article 'al-'. The final '-a' is the accusative case, the form taken as a direct object or when otherwise governed into that state.
12.root: ب-غ-ي (b-gh-y) — to transgress, oppress, exceed bounds

13.meaning: 'Without' or 'other than' — the preposition bi- joined to ghayr, a noun meaning 'other than / not / lacking', together conveying the absence of something ('with no …', 'wrongfully').
13.grammar: bi- is a preposition that takes the genitive; ghayr is a noun of exception/negation ('other than'). Its -i ending is genitive (required after bi-) and it also links to a following noun in a possessive 'of' relationship, so 'bi-ghayri X' means 'without X / other than X'.
13.root: غ-ي-ر (gh-y-r) — otherness, difference, being other than

14.meaning: 'The truth', 'the right', 'what is rightfully due' — that which is real, correct, and justly owed; the opposite of falsehood and wrongdoing.
14.grammar: A definite masculine noun (the al- prefix means 'the'). The -i ending is genitive, the case typically taken after a preposition or when the word links to a preceding noun ('… of the truth / by right').
14.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, rightness, that which is established and due

15.meaning: A two-part connector: 'and that.' The 'wa' joins what precedes, and 'an' is the subordinating particle 'that,' which introduces a following verb-clause (often steering it into the subjunctive) — used to report or quote a command, statement, or purpose.
15.grammar: The conjunction wa- ('and') plus the particle an, a subordinator meaning 'that' which heads a clause and commonly puts a following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood (often expressing purpose, intention, or reported speech). It is a particle and does not itself take a case ending.

16.meaning: You (plural) associate / set up a partner — to ascribe partners or equals to a deity, treating another as sharing in what belongs to Allah alone.
16.grammar: A present/imperfect Form IV verb (base أَشْرَكَ, imperfect stem -shrik-, 'to make a partner/associate'). The tu- prefix marks second-person address and the -ū ending marks a plural (male/mixed) subject: 'you all associate.' The verb is tushrikū, not the indicative tushrikūna: the missing final nūn marks a non-indicative mood (here typically after the prohibitive lā or in a jussive context). The trailing alif is a silent orthographic alif (alif al-fāriqah) written after plural -ū.
16.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — partnership, sharing; to associate partners (with Allah)

17.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
17.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
17.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

18.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
18.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

19.meaning: A negating particle, 'not', used specifically to deny that an action happened in the past, even though it attaches to a present-tense verb form. It turns 'you do X' into 'you did not do X'.

parts.en: did not (negation of a completed act)

19.grammar: An indeclinable particle that governs the verb after it, putting that verb into the jussive (clipped) mood and giving it past-time meaning. In short: lam + a present-form verb = 'did not [verb]'.

20.meaning: He sends down — to send something down from a higher place to a lower one, gradually or in stages. The intensive form suggests a sending-down by degrees.
20.grammar: A present-tense verb in the intensive 'fa''ala' pattern (sending down by degrees), third-person masculine singular ('he'). The vowelless final -l marks the jussive mood — the form used after certain particles (such as those for negation of the past or conditions), giving e.g. 'he did not send down' or 'let him send down'.
20.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down; to send down

21.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
21.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

22.meaning: Authority, sanction, or compelling proof — power or warrant given to back something up, whether kingly authority or a decisive argument. 'Sulṭān' is authorizing power or evidence.
22.grammar: A single noun ('authority') carrying the accusative indefinite ending -an (tanwīn al-naṣb). This one ending does two things at once: the -a marks the accusative case (typically the direct object of a verb), and the final -n sound (nunation) shows the noun is indefinite ('an authority / any warrant'). The nunation is a diacritic on the case vowel, not a separable suffix, so the word stays one undivided token.

23.meaning: 'And that' — links a clause with 'and', then introduces a following statement or verbal idea with 'that' (as in 'and that you should …'), often serving to name or specify what is meant.
23.grammar: Two particles: 'wa' ('and') joined to 'an' ('that'). 'An' typically precedes a verb and turns the clause into a noun-like idea ('that you do …'), commonly putting that following verb into the subjunctive mood.

24.meaning: You (all) say / utter — referring to speaking or saying words, addressed to a group. In context it is the form used after a particle so that it reads 'do not say' / 'that you may say'.
24.grammar: Present-tense verb, second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The ta- prefix marks the second person; plurality is supplied by the -ū ending. The plain ending here (without final -na) is the form a verb takes after certain particles such as 'do not' or 'so that', signalling command-prohibition or purpose.

25.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
25.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
25.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

26.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
26.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

27.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
27.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

28.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
28.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

29.meaning: A verb addressed to a group: 'you (all) know', 'you have knowledge', 'you are aware'. From the root meaning 'to know'.
29.grammar: The 'ta-' prefix marks a present/future verb addressed to 'you'. The '-ūna' ending marks a masculine plural subject and is the full 'indicative' form, signalling an ongoing, factual statement ('you (all) do know'), as opposed to the shortened '-ū' used after certain particles.

1.meaning: 'And for every / for each' — assigns or relates something to each individual member of a class, with the sense 'and to every (one) …'.
1.grammar: The quantifier 'kull' ('every/each/all') preceded by 'wa' ('and') and the preposition 'li' ('for/to'). The final '-i' is the genitive case, the form regularly taken after a preposition.

2.meaning: A community, nation, or people — a body of people bound together by shared faith, way of life, or origin; one collective group.
2.grammar: A feminine noun. The final -in (genitive with 'nunation') marks it as indefinite ('a community') and links it to a preceding noun or preposition ('… of a community'). The feminine -t sound surfaces before the ending.

3.meaning: 'A term / appointed time / fixed span' — 'ajal' is a set period or the deadline at its end; the appointed time fixed for something to occur or end. Indefinite ('a term').
3.grammar: A noun with the ending '-un' (nunation), which marks it as indefinite ('a term') and in the nominative case — the form used for the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified.

4.meaning: A connecting phrase meaning 'then when / and when', introducing a circumstance whose occurrence triggers a following response. 'Fa-' links it to what precedes; 'idhā' sets up a 'when … (then) …' condition for something expected to happen.
4.grammar: A particle cluster, not a noun or verb, so it has no case ending. 'Idhā' is a conditional/temporal particle ('when') used for events regarded as bound to occur, and it normally introduces a clause followed by a main response. The prefixed fa- ('then/so') ties the whole condition to the preceding statement.
4.root: — (particles)

5.meaning: He/it came, arrived, or came about — the act of coming into presence or of something occurring.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb with no prefix and no personal suffix, naming a completed act by a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it came'). All three letters here are root letters: jā spells the first radical plus the lengthened weak middle radical, and the final hamza (ء) is the third root consonant — not an ending. The fatḥa (-a) on that hamza is simply the past-tense vocalization for a 'he' subject sitting on the last root letter; there is no separable suffix.
5.root: ج-ي-ء (j-y-ʾ) — to come, to arrive

6.meaning: 'Their term / appointed time' — the fixed span or deadline set for them, the determined point at which something is due to end or occur. Belonging to a plural 'them'.
6.grammar: A noun carrying the possessive pronoun '-hum' ('their'). The '-u' before the pronoun marks the nominative case, the base form a noun takes as the subject of a sentence or when standing in that primary state.
6.root: ا-ج-ل (ʾ-j-l) — appointed term, fixed span of time

7.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
7.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

8.meaning: They seek to put (something) back, ask for it to be postponed, or hold it off to a later time. The verb carries the sense of actively requesting or trying to obtain a delay.
8.grammar: Present-tense verb, masculine plural. The ya- prefix marks the third person, and the Form X pattern (sta-) adds the meaning of seeking or asking for the action. Plurality is not in the prefix: it is the -ūna ending that shows a masculine plural subject ('they') and marks the indicative mood — the plain statement form, 'they (seek to delay)'.
8.root: ا-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — being last, coming later, delay

9.meaning: An hour; more broadly a span of time, a moment, or the appointed 'Hour' (the climactic moment of resurrection and judgement). Its underlying sense is a defined stretch or point of time.
9.grammar: A feminine noun in the indefinite accusative. The -an ending (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('an hour, some hour') and as accusative — the case used for the direct object of a verb or for adverbial expressions of time and extent (e.g. 'for an hour').
9.root: س-و-ع (s-w-ʿ) — a moment or span of time

10.meaning: 'And not' — a connector 'and' joined to the negative particle 'not,' negating a following statement.
10.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the negator lā ('not'). Lā commonly negates a present-tense verb or a noun. Neither particle takes case endings.

11.meaning: They seek to put (something) forward, ask for it to be brought ahead, or try to advance it to an earlier time. The opposite of seeking delay.
11.grammar: Present-tense verb, masculine plural. The ya- prefix marks the third person, and the Form X pattern (sta-) adds the sense of seeking or asking for the action. Plurality comes from the -ūna ending, which shows a masculine plural subject ('they') and marks the indicative mood, the ordinary statement form.
11.root: ق-د-م (q-d-m) — coming before, precedence, advancing forward

1.meaning: 'O Children of … / O descendants of …' — a vocative call addressing the offspring or lineage of someone (literally 'sons of'), used to summon a people by their ancestry.
1.grammar: The vocative particle yā ('O') prefixed to the plural of 'son' in its construct (possessive-linking) form. As a construct noun it is set to be followed by a possessor ('… OF …'), giving 'O Children of …'. The -ī form here is the plural in the genitive/accusative shape used in construct.
1.root: ب-ن-ي (b-n-y) — to build; (banūn) sons, children, descendants

2.meaning: 'Adam' — the proper name of the first human being and first prophet.
2.grammar: A proper name that is a diptote (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf) — it takes a restricted set of endings. Its final -a here does double duty: it marks the accusative case (e.g., as a direct object) and, because the name is a diptote, it stands in place of the usual nominative -u while also blocking the tanwīn (-n) that fully inflected nouns would take.

3.meaning: A conditional particle meaning 'if' or 'whether'; it often introduces alternatives ('if … or'/'whether … or'), pairing two possibilities. It is essentially 'in' (if) reinforced with 'mā', strengthening the conditional sense.
3.grammar: A particle, not a noun or verb, so it has no case ending. It functions as a connector that sets up a condition or a choice between options ('either … or', 'whether … or'), and it does not change form.

4.meaning: A verb meaning 'it shall surely come to you' or 'it will certainly reach you (plural)'. It expresses an action of coming/arriving directed at a group, stamped with heavy emphasis that it definitely will occur.
4.grammar: A present/future verb 'comes' (third-person masculine singular, 'he/it'), reinforced by the heavy emphatic ending -anna ('shall surely'), and followed by the object pronoun -kum ('you all'). Before this heavy emphatic ending the verb keeps its final -ya vowel (yatiya-). The -anna is the strong-affirmation ending that pairs with a preceding conditional, stressing the action will certainly happen.
4.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — coming, arriving, bringing

5.meaning: Messengers — the plural of 'messenger': those sent with a commission to convey a message; in religious usage, prophets sent with revelation.
5.grammar: A plural noun. The final '-un' (tanwīn ḍamma) is the indefinite nominative: it marks 'messengers' (no 'the') and signals that the word is functioning as a subject or naming a thing rather than being possessed or governed by a preposition.
5.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send, dispatch a message

6.meaning: 'From you / among you (plural)' — indicating a part taken out of, or belonging to, a group of people being addressed.
6.grammar: The preposition min ('from, of, among') joined to the attached pronoun -kum ('you all,' masculine plural). Together they express partition or origin: a part drawn 'from / among' the addressed group.

7.meaning: They narrate, recount, or relate — to tell out a report or story in sequence, following its thread from start to finish.
7.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb. The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending marks 'they' (a male group) as the doers; the retained final -na shows the plain, unmodified present form.
7.root: ق-ص-ص (q-ṣ-ṣ) — to follow a trail; to narrate, recount

8.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
8.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

9.meaning: My signs / My verses — clear tokens, proofs, or revealed verses that point to a truth, here belonging to the speaker ('My').
9.grammar: A sound feminine plural noun ('signs') with the attached possessive -ī meaning 'my'. The plural is built with the -āt ending; the long -ī suffix marks first-person singular ownership.
9.root: ا-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — a sign, mark, or token

10.meaning: A two-part connector meaning 'so/then whoever'. It joins a clause to what precedes ('so', 'then') and introduces a conditional or general statement about any person who does something ('whoever, anyone who').
10.grammar: The prefix fa- is a connecting particle meaning 'so/then', linking this to a prior statement. man is a conditional/relative word for persons ('whoever'); its base form is man, and the final vowel here is read -i simply to ease pronunciation before a following consonant cluster, not a case ending.

11.meaning: He guarded himself / was mindful and god-fearing. To exercise taqwā: to shield oneself by being conscious of Allah and dutifully cautious of wrongdoing, keeping a protective awareness against what brings harm or displeasure.

parts.en: he guarded himself / was god-fearing (verb stem)

11.grammar: A past-tense verb in the eighth (reflexive) pattern, third-person masculine singular ('he…'). The final -ā vowel results from the weak final root letter and marks the completed action of a single masculine subject.
11.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to guard, shield, protect; the source of taqwā (god-consciousness)

12.meaning: "and he set right / reformed / made amends" — a completed-action verb of putting things right, correcting, or acting righteously, opening with the connector "and."
12.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ("he/it"), opened by the connector "and." It is from the causative pattern (form IV), meaning to make something sound/right or to put it in order. The final "-a" is the standard past-tense ending for a single male doer.
12.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound, right, good; to set right, reform

13.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
13.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

14.meaning: 'Fear' — a state of being afraid, dread, or alarm; apprehension of something harmful or threatening.
14.grammar: A singular indefinite noun. The '-un' ending (nunation) marks it as nominative and indefinite — 'a fear' or simply 'fear' — and the nominative typically signals the doer or subject of a sentence, or the subject of an existential statement ('there is fear').

15.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
15.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
15.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

16.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
16.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

17.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
17.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

18.meaning: 'They grieve / will grieve' — to feel sorrow, sadness, or distress; to be saddened over loss or hardship.
18.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, third-person masculine plural. The 'ya-' prefix marks third person, and the '-ūna' ending marks a masculine plural subject ('they') with the verb in its full (indicative) form, describing ongoing or future action. Read together the word is 'yaḥzanūna.'

1.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

2.meaning: They denied / they cried lies; they declared (something or someone) to be false. An intensive verb meaning to reject as a lie, to disbelieve and brand untrue — directed by a plural 'they'.

parts.tr: kadhdhab (doubled dh; simplified transliterations may write 'kadhab')
parts.en: denied / branded as lies (past stem, intensive)

2.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in an intensive pattern (to treat as false, to repeatedly deny). The middle radical carries a shadda (doubling), which is exactly what marks this as the intensive form: kadhdhab- (not the simple kadhab-). The ending -ū marks the doers as 'they' — a plural, grammatically masculine group, so the whole reconstructs to kadhdhabū. Note that simplified transliterations sometimes omit the doubling and write 'kadhabū', but the doubled dh is essential to the form. The perfect tense denotes a completed action.
2.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie; in this form, to call a lie, to deny as false

3.meaning: By/in Our signs. Āyāt is the plural of āya — a sign, token, or evidence. Signs are pointers that indicate a greater reality. With the prefixed particle and pronoun it means 'with/in Our signs'.
3.grammar: A plural noun preceded by the preposition bi- ('with, in, by'), which requires the following noun to take the -i (genitive) ending. The attached -nā means 'our' when joined to a noun. The genitive here is governed by the preposition.

4.meaning: 'And they acted arrogantly / were haughty' — to have been proud and overbearing, swelling with self-importance and refusing to submit.
4.grammar: Prefix wa- means 'and'. The verb is past-tense, intensive reflexive (form X). The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject: 'they (a group) were arrogant' (a completed action).
4.root: ك-ب-ر (k-b-r) — to be great; (form X) to deem oneself great, to be arrogant

5.meaning: From it / about it / away from it — a preposition meaning 'from' or 'off of', attached to a feminine 'it'.
5.grammar: 'ʿan' is a preposition conveying departure or removal — 'away from / off of / concerning'. The attached -hā is 'it/her', referring to a single feminine thing. Prepositions like this put the following pronoun in the genitive.

6.meaning: 'those / those ones' — a demonstrative pointing to a group of people or things at a distance ('those there').
6.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those.' The -ka element adds the sense of pointing to something farther off (as opposed to 'these' near at hand). Being a fixed pronoun, it keeps one form regardless of case.

7.meaning: 'Companions / people of, dwellers, owners' — those closely associated with something, its inseparable folk, fellows, or inmates; literally the people who 'keep company with' a thing.
7.grammar: A masculine plural noun (the plural of ṣāḥib, 'companion'). The '-u' ending is nominative, typically marking the subject of a sentence; it appears here without nunation because the word is in a possessive construction ('companions OF …') with a following noun.

8.meaning: 'The Fire' — fire, flame; in religious usage often the Fire of Hell, the blazing punishment of the Hereafter.
8.grammar: The definite article 'al-' ('the') plus the feminine noun 'nār' ('fire'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (so it is pronounced 'an-nār'). The '-i' ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or to link the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the Fire').

9.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
9.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

10.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
10.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

11.meaning: 'Ones who abide / remain forever; everlasting dwellers.' The plural of an active participle describing those who stay, persist, and endure in a state or place without end — abiding permanently.
11.grammar: An active participle in the masculine plural. The -ūna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the nominative case — the form used when such a group is the subject of a sentence or is being described as being in that state.
11.root: خ-ل-د (kh-l-d) — to remain forever, endure, be everlasting

1.meaning: A compound meaning 'then whoever' or 'so whoever'. It combines 'then/so' with the conditional/relative 'who', introducing whatever person meets a stated condition.
1.grammar: The connector fa- ('then/so', often answering or following a condition) joined to man ('whoever / the one who'), which refers to people and introduces a condition: 'whoever does X…'. man does not change its ending; the clause after it supplies the rest of the meaning.

2.meaning: An elative adjective meaning 'more / most wrongdoing, unjust, or oppressive' — comparing degrees of ẓulm (placing things out of their rightful place, transgression).
2.grammar: An elative (comparative/superlative) noun on the pattern afʿal, meaning 'more/most unjust'. It ends in -u (nominative), the case typical of a subject or predicate.
2.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — wrongdoing, injustice, putting something where it does not belong

3.meaning: A combination meaning 'than whoever / than one who' or 'from whoever' — the preposition min ('from/than') merged with man ('who/whoever'). It links a comparison or origin to an unspecified person.
3.grammar: The preposition min ('from', and 'than' in comparisons) fused with the relative/indefinite pronoun man ('who(ever)'). The nūn of min assimilates into the mīm of man, so min + man becomes mimman. The whole final nūn belongs to man, not to min; the kasrah on it (-i) is a liaison (waṣl) vowel added to keep two unvowelled consonants (sukūns) from meeting before the next word. Read together: mimmani, 'than/from the one who'.

4.meaning: 'He fabricated, invented, forged (a lie); he concocted falsely' — made something up and falsely attributed it, especially a lie. A verb of deliberate fabrication.

parts.en: connecting (helping) vowel for the verb pattern
past-tense 3rd person masculine singular ending '-ā' (from a weak final root letter)

4.grammar: A past-tense verb, 3rd person masculine singular ('he fabricated'). It is a Form VIII (ifta'ala) verb. The final '-ā' (written as alif maqṣūra) is how the past-tense '-a' ending appears when the root ends in a weak letter (w/y). The initial 'i-' is a helping vowel that lets the consonant cluster of this pattern be pronounced.
4.root: ف-ر-ي (f-r-y) — to fabricate, forge, invent (a falsehood)

5.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
5.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
5.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

6.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
6.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

7.meaning: A noun meaning 'a lie / falsehood' — a deliberately false statement, an untruth fabricated against the truth.
7.grammar: An indefinite noun ('a lie') with the accusative -an ending (tanwīn). The accusative commonly marks the object of a verb (e.g. fabricating a lie); the -an tanwīn shows it is indefinite.
7.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie, to declare false

8.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
8.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

9.meaning: A verb meaning 'he denied / cried lies against / rejected as false' — to treat something or someone as a lie, refusing to accept it as true and openly rejecting it.
9.grammar: Past-tense verb (form II, intensive), third-person masculine singular ('he denied / rejected as false'). The doubled middle letter (kadhdhaba) gives the sense of actively declaring something false. The final -a is the past-tense ending for a masculine singular doer.
9.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie; (form II) to deny, to call a lie

10.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in / by His signs' — the preposition bi- ('with/in/by') joined to āyāt ('signs, verses, tokens') and 'His'. Āyāt are signs or proofs pointing to Allah, including revealed verses and observable signs.
10.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in/by/with') governing the plural noun āyāt ('signs'), which takes the genitive -i ending because it follows a preposition; the attached -hi means 'His'. The genitive is the case used after prepositions and to show possession ('signs OF His'). The pronoun appears as -hi (rather than -hu) in harmony with the preceding -i vowel.

11.meaning: 'those / those ones' — a demonstrative pointing to a group of people or things at a distance ('those there').
11.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those.' The -ka element adds the sense of pointing to something farther off (as opposed to 'these' near at hand). Being a fixed pronoun, it keeps one form regardless of case.

12.meaning: It reaches them, comes to them, or attains/befalls them — used of something (a share, a benefit, or a fate) coming within reach of people and overtaking them.
12.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it'). The ya- prefix marks the third person. The -u before the attached pronoun is the indicative ending — the plain statement form. The suffix -hum is the object pronoun 'them', so the whole means 'it reaches them'.

13.meaning: Their share, portion, or allotted part — what is assigned or due to someone out of a larger whole, whether of good or of fate.
13.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The -u ending is nominative — the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified ('the share is …'). The suffix -hum means 'their', so together it is 'their share'.
13.root: ن-ص-ب (n-ṣ-b) — setting up, fixing; an allotted/fixed portion

14.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
14.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

15.meaning: 'The Book / the Scripture' — a written record or revealed scripture; literally that which is written.
15.grammar: The definite article al- with the noun kitāb ('book, scripture'), itself a verbal noun from 'to write.' The -i ending is genitive, typically marking the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to a preceding noun.
15.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — writing, inscribing, recording

16.meaning: A particle meaning 'until, up to the point that,' or 'so that.' It marks an end-limit in time, place, or purpose — the boundary at which something culminates or the goal toward which it moves.
