16.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It introduces an end-point or goal; when followed by a verb it can express purpose or result ('until' / 'so that').

17.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
17.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.
17.root: — (a time particle; no triliteral root)

18.meaning: A verb meaning 'she/it came to them' — the act of coming or arriving, directed toward a group of people. Built on the verb 'to come,' with the comers' goal ('them') attached.
18.grammar: A past-tense verb 'came.' The -t suffix is the feminine marker, showing the subject is grammatically feminine ('she/it came') or a feminine plural such as 'messengers/signs.' The attached -hum is the object pronoun 'them' (a group of males or mixed).

19.meaning: A noun meaning 'messengers' joined to 'our' — those sent with a message or commission, envoys; in scripture, the prophets sent by Allah. The form means 'our messengers.'
19.grammar: rusul is the plural of rasūl ('messenger/envoy'). The vowel -u before the pronoun is the nominative ending, which typically marks the word as the subject/doer ('the messengers [did]…'). The attached -nā is the possessive 'our.'
19.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — sending, dispatching; a message or one sent with it

20.meaning: They take them fully (in death) — taking or collecting souls completely at the end of life. The verb conveys taking something in full, leaving nothing behind.

parts.en: take in full / receive completely (Form V)

20.grammar: Present-tense verb, masculine plural, with an object pronoun. The ya- prefix marks the third person; plurality comes from the -na subject marker ('they'). The Form V pattern here is transitive and directed outward — the doers take the souls of others in full, not an action done to or for themselves. The suffix -hum is the object 'them', so the whole means 'they take them (in full)'.
20.root: و-ف-ي (w-f-y) — fulfilling, completing, paying in full

21.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
21.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

22.meaning: Where / wherever. An interrogative or conditional adverb of place: it asks 'where?' or, in a conditional sense, sets up 'wherever / in whatever place'.
22.grammar: An indeclinable adverb of place fixed on a final -a; it does not change for case. It functions either as a question word ('where?') or as a conditional particle introducing a clause ('wherever'), often pairing with a following verb in the jussive mood.

23.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
23.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

24.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
24.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
24.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

25.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (all) call upon, invoke, summon, or pray to.' The root spans calling out, naming, inviting, and supplicating — especially calling on someone for help.
25.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ta- prefix with the -ūna ending marks 'you all' (masculine plural) as the doers. The final -na is the indicative marker, signalling an ongoing or habitual action (a complete, non-shortened present-tense verb).
25.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, invoke, summon, pray

26.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
26.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
26.root: — (preposition)

27.meaning: A noun used to mean 'besides', 'other than', 'apart from', or 'short of'. It points to something or someone set apart from, or lower/lesser than, a named party. Often used in the phrase 'besides Allah'.
27.grammar: 'dūn' functions as an adverb-like noun of place/relation. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, which appears because it follows a preposition (such as 'min', 'from') and because it links to a following noun ('other than …'). It commonly heads the construction 'besides/other than [someone]'.
27.root: د-و-ن (d-w-n) — to be low/beneath, to fall short; hence 'below, other than, besides'

28.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
28.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

29.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
29.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

30.meaning: 'they went astray / erred' — to lose the right way, to wander off into error or misguidance.
30.grammar: A past-tense verb with the -ū ending meaning 'they' (masculine plural). It conveys a completed action: 'they went astray / erred.'
30.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, lose the way, go astray

31.meaning: 'From us / away from us' — the preposition 'from, away from, off of' joined to the pronoun 'us', indicating removal or separation away from the speakers.
31.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. ʿan means 'away from / off of' (motion or removal away from something), and the suffix -nā is the object 'us'.

32.meaning: 'And they bore witness / testified / affirmed' — a completed act of attesting to and openly affirming the truth of something.
32.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') on a past-tense verb. The stem shahid- carries the meaning; the separate -ū ending marks a completed action done by a third-person masculine plural subject ('they').
32.root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d) — to witness, testify, be present

33.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on, upon, over,' and by extension 'against' or 'incumbent upon.' It can mark something resting on top of, an obligation laid on someone, or being set over/above something.
33.grammar: An indeclinable preposition (its form never changes). It governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case, and conveys location 'on/upon,' or figuratively duty or opposition ('against').

34.meaning: Themselves / their own selves — the noun nafs ('self, soul, person, inner being') joined to a pronoun 'their'. Used reflexively it means 'their own selves' and conveys the inmost self, the seat of desires and the person as a whole.
34.grammar: The plural noun anfus ('selves') carries the genitive -i ending followed by the possessive pronoun -him ('their'). The genitive marks the noun as governed by a preposition or joined to a preceding word; -him makes it 'their selves'.
34.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — self, soul, breath, inner being

35.meaning: 'That they…' — an emphatic connector 'anna' ('that, indeed') fused with the pronoun 'they,' used to introduce an affirmed clause as the content of a thought or statement.
35.grammar: Built on the particle 'anna' ('that…, indeed'), which introduces and affirms a following clause (often after verbs of knowing, thinking, or saying) and puts its noun into the accusative. The attached '-hum' is the pronoun 'they/them' for a male-inclusive group.

36.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
36.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
36.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

37.meaning: Disbelievers, deniers, ingrates — those who reject faith and cover over the truth; the plural describing such people.
37.grammar: An active participle (one doing the action) in the masculine sound plural. The '-īn' ending is the accusative/genitive form of that plural — used when the word is an object, a descriptive 'state', or follows a preposition. It names people characterized by rejecting faith.
37.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; hence to disbelieve, be ungrateful

1.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
1.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

2.meaning: 'Enter!' — a command to a group to go into or enter a place.
2.grammar: An imperative (command) verb. The -ū ending directs the command at a group ('you all, enter!'). The initial alif is a helping-vowel prefix that lets the word begin (pronounced 'u-' here), needed because the stem would otherwise start with a vowelless consonant. The silent alif after the wāw spells the plural ending.

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
3.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

4.meaning: A noun meaning 'nations, communities, or peoples' — the plural of 'umma,' a group bound together as one community.
4.grammar: A plural noun. The ending -in is genitive and indefinite (the doubled 'nunation' marking 'some, an indefinite'). The genitive case typically follows a preposition or links the noun to a preceding noun (the 'of' relationship), and the -in shows it is indefinite ('some communities').
4.root: أ-م-م (ʾ-m-m) — community, people, to lead/intend

5.meaning: A short particle placed before a verb to emphasize or affirm it. Before a past-tense verb it means 'indeed / certainly / has already (happened)'; before a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes / may'. It sharpens and confirms the verb that follows.
5.grammar: An indeclinable particle (its form never changes). It does not take case or tense endings; its job is to color the following verb — affirming and intensifying a past action ('has indeed done') or signaling occasional possibility with a present verb.
5.root: — (no triliteral root; an emphasizing particle)

6.meaning: 'It passed away / went by, came to an end' — said of a community, time, or era that has elapsed and is now gone. The root carries the sense of being emptied out, hence of time or people that have passed.
6.grammar: Past-tense verb. The -t (sukūn-marked -at) suffix marks a third-person feminine singular subject, 'she/it,' used here because the noun it refers to is grammatically feminine. The past tense states a completed action.
6.root: خ-ل-و (kh-l-w) — to be empty/vacant; to pass away, elapse

7.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
7.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

8.meaning: 'before you,' 'prior to you' — an expression of precedence in time or place, here relating that precedence to 'you (plural).' The core word denotes the 'before' side, what comes earlier or in front.
8.grammar: An adverb of time/place ('before') joined to the pronoun '-kum' ('you, plural'). The '-i' ending is genitive: such words of place/time regularly take this case, especially after a preposition, and the attached pronoun completes the sense as 'before you.'

9.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
9.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

10.meaning: A noun meaning 'the jinn' — a class of unseen beings created from smokeless fire, possessing free will and accountability like humankind.
10.grammar: A definite noun with the article al- ('the'). The -i (genitive) ending typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun in a possessive 'of' relationship.
10.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — to cover, conceal, be hidden from sight

11.meaning: And humankind — human beings collectively, mankind, especially as contrasted with the unseen jinn. Carries a sense of sociability and familiarity.
11.grammar: A collective noun with the prefixed 'and' plus 'the'. The final -i is the genitive case ending, which typically follows a preposition or oath particle, or links the word to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship.

12.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
12.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

13.meaning: 'The Fire' — fire, flame; in religious usage often the Fire of Hell, the blazing punishment of the Hereafter.
13.grammar: The definite article 'al-' ('the') plus the feminine noun 'nār' ('fire'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (so it is pronounced 'an-nār'). The '-i' ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or to link the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the Fire').

14.meaning: 'whenever / every time' — a compound expressing that something recurs each and every time a condition is met.
14.grammar: A compound of kull ('every', in the accusative -a used adverbially) and mā ('what / the time that'). Together it works as a conditional time-word, 'each time that …', linking a repeated condition to its repeated result.

15.meaning: She/it entered, went in, or came into a place. The basic act of passing from outside to inside.
15.grammar: Past-tense verb. The -at ending marks the subject as third-person feminine singular ('she/it did'), so the word means 'she/it entered'. Past-tense verbs in Arabic carry the subject in their ending rather than a prefix.
15.root: د-خ-ل (d-kh-l) — entering, going in

16.meaning: 'A community / a nation, a people' — a body of people bound together as a single group, often by shared faith, way, or era.
16.grammar: A singular indefinite noun. The -un ending is nominative plus nunation: the -n sound signals 'a/an' (indefinite), and the -u marks the nominative case, the form used when the word is the subject or the thing being named.
16.root: ء-م-م (ʾ-m-m) — to head toward; a community, way, model

17.meaning: She/it cursed — invoked a curse on someone, called for their being cast away from mercy and good. The verb's core is condemnation and the wish for someone to be driven off.

parts.en: curse, condemn, drive away from mercy

17.grammar: Past-tense verb. The -at ending marks the subject as third-person feminine singular ('she/it did'), so the word means 'she/it cursed'. The subject is carried in the ending, as is normal for the Arabic past tense.
17.root: ل-ع-ن (l-ʿ-n) — cursing, condemning, expelling from mercy

18.meaning: Its/her sister — a female sibling, and by extension a counterpart, fellow, or one of a like pair. The accusative form here makes it the thing acted upon.
18.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The -a ending is accusative — the case used for the direct object of a verb (the thing receiving the action). The suffix -hā means 'her/its', so together it is 'her/its sister (as object)'.

19.meaning: 'Until / up to the point that; so that' — a particle marking a limit or goal. It expresses the end-point reached ('until') or the purpose aimed at ('so that, in order that').
19.grammar: A particle indicating a goal or limit. When followed by a present-tense verb it places that verb in the subjunctive mood (clipping its ending to -a), conveying 'until / so that' something comes about. Ḥattā itself is invariable.

20.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
20.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.

21.meaning: They successively caught up with one another, followed on each other's heels, and so all came together in sequence — a crowd or generations arriving one after another until they are gathered.

parts.en: catch up with one another, follow on (Form VI, with assimilated t)

21.grammar: Past-tense verb, masculine plural. The Form VI pattern conveys people doing something to one another (mutual or successive action) — here catching up with and following on one another. In this verb the ta- of Form VI has assimilated into the following consonant, producing a doubled dd-; the initial alif is hamzat al-waṣl, a prosthetic helping vowel added so the word can begin on that doubled consonant. The -ū ending marks a masculine plural subject ('they did').

22.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
22.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

23.meaning: A word meaning 'all together', 'all of them', or 'the whole lot' — emphasising that no one and nothing is left out of a group.
23.grammar: A noun meaning 'all/entirety' carrying the -an ending: accusative case with tanwīn (the indefinite '-n'). This accusative form is typical of a word that comes alongside another to specify it as 'all of them, every one', describing the manner or extent.

24.meaning: She said — a completed act of speaking or saying, attributed to a single female.
24.grammar: A past-tense verb with the -at ending that marks a single female doer ('she said'). The plain past form presents the action as a completed whole.

25.meaning: The later/last of them — the group or generation that came afterward, the rear or following party of a people. A feminine 'latter one' standing for a later batch.
25.grammar: A feminine noun-adjective ('the latter one') with an attached possessive pronoun. The base form ukhrā ends in a fixed long -ā that does not change for case. The suffix -hum means 'of them', so the whole means 'the later one of them'.
25.root: ا-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — being last, coming later

26.meaning: For/about the earlier/first of them — concerning the group or generation that came before, the foremost or leading party of a people. Introduced by 'for/about'.
26.grammar: A preposition li- ('for/about/to') attached to a feminine noun-adjective ('the former one') with a possessive pronoun. The base ūlā ends in a fixed long -ā that does not change for case. The suffix -hum means 'of them', so the whole means 'for/about the earlier one of them'.
26.root: ا-و-ل (ʾ-w-l) — being first, coming before, priority

27.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

parts.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

27.grammar: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
27.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

28.meaning: These / those — a plural demonstrative pointing to a group of people or things. Its core sense is the near demonstrative 'these', but it is very commonly rendered 'those' in translation when the group it points to has already been described or named rather than being physically present.
28.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, used for a group of either gender. Its base value is near-deixis ('these'), built from an attention-drawing prefix 'hā-' ('lo!, here') plus the base 'ulāʾi'. In practice it is often translated 'those' when the referent is already mentioned or understood rather than literally nearby. Its form is fixed and does not change for grammatical case; it points to a group rather than naming it.

29.meaning: They led us astray, misguided us, or caused us to lose the way — making someone deviate from the right path. The form adds an object ('us').
29.grammar: Past-tense verb, masculine plural, with an object pronoun. The a- prefix is the Form IV causative ('to make someone go astray'). The -ū ending marks a masculine plural subject ('they did'), and the suffix -nā is the object 'us', so the whole means 'they led us astray'.
29.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — going astray, erring, losing the way

30.meaning: So give them / bring to them — a command to grant, hand over, or bring something to people. The 'so/then' links it as a consequence; the verb is the order 'give!'
30.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to one person ('you, give!'), formed from the Form IV verb meaning 'to give/bring'. The fa- prefix means 'so/then', linking it as a result. The attached -him is the object 'them', so the whole means 'so give them'. The final -i is the trimmed end of the command form of this weak-ending verb.
30.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — coming; (Form IV) bringing or giving

31.meaning: 'A punishment / torment.' A noun naming chastisement or painful suffering inflicted as a penalty.
31.grammar: A masculine noun. The -an ending marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the accusative case — the form a noun takes as the object of a verb or as the thing being described/quantified.

32.meaning: A double, twofold amount, or multiplied portion (of punishment, reward, or anything else). The accusative form presents it as the thing given or measured out.
32.grammar: A noun in the indefinite accusative. The -an ending (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a double, a multiple') and accusative — the case used for the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon or given).

33.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
33.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

34.meaning: The Fire — the blazing fire, and by its definite, weighty use the Fire of the Hereafter (Hell) as a place of punishment.
34.grammar: A definite feminine noun ('the fire'). The -i ending is genitive — the case that typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …') or follows a preposition (e.g. 'of/in the Fire'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (pronounced an-nār).

35.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
35.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

36.meaning: 'For each one / to every one' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to a word meaning 'each, every, the whole', expressing that something pertains to every member of a group taken individually.
36.grammar: The preposition li- ('for/to') prefixed to the quantifier kull ('each/every'). The ending -in is the indefinite genitive: the tanwīn (doubled n) marks indefiniteness, and the -i is the genitive case required after the preposition. Standing alone with tanwīn, kull means 'each one' without naming what is counted.

37.meaning: A double, twofold amount, or multiplied portion. The same word as the accusative 'double', but here in the nominative, presenting it as the subject or the thing identified ('there is a double').
37.grammar: A noun in the indefinite nominative. The -un ending (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a double') and nominative — the case used for the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified or stated to exist.

38.meaning: 'but / however' — a particle that introduces a contrast or correction, setting what follows against what was just said. The opening 'wa-' connects it ('and').
38.grammar: A contrasting particle ('but, however') that signals a turn against the preceding idea. It does not change endings on words; it simply introduces a corrective or opposing clause. The 'wa-' prefix links it to what came before.

39.meaning: 'Not' — a particle of negation. Depending on context it denies a present fact, forbids an action, or rules something out ('do not / there is no').
39.grammar: A negating particle, 'not / no'. It is used to deny or prohibit — negating present-tense statements, expressing 'there is no...', or, with a command form, forbidding an action ('do not...').

40.meaning: A verb addressed to a group: 'you (all) know', 'you have knowledge', 'you are aware'. From the root meaning 'to know'.
40.grammar: The 'ta-' prefix marks a present/future verb addressed to 'you'. The '-ūna' ending marks a masculine plural subject and is the full 'indicative' form, signalling an ongoing, factual statement ('you (all) do know'), as opposed to the shortened '-ū' used after certain particles.

1.meaning: And she said / and a (feminine) group said — introducing speech that was spoken or declared.
1.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb joined by 'wa-' ('and'). The '-at' ending marks a third-person feminine singular subject — 'she' said, or an action attributed to a grammatically feminine noun.

2.meaning: The earlier/first of them — the group or generation that came before, the foremost or leading party of a people. A feminine 'former one' standing for an earlier batch.
2.grammar: A feminine noun-adjective ('the former one') with an attached possessive pronoun. The base ūlā ends in a fixed long -ā that does not change for case. The suffix -hum means 'of them', so the whole means 'the earlier one of them'.
2.root: ا-و-ل (ʾ-w-l) — being first, coming before, priority

3.meaning: To/for the later/last of them — directed toward the group or generation that came afterward, the rear or following party of a people. Introduced by 'to/for'.
3.grammar: A preposition li- ('to/for') attached to a feminine noun-adjective ('the latter one') with a possessive pronoun. The base ukhrā ends in a fixed long -ā that does not change for case. The suffix -hum means 'of them', so the whole means 'to/for the later one of them'.

4.meaning: A two-part expression: 'so/then' joined to a negating word 'not.' The first piece links to what precedes (drawing a result or sequence), and the second negates the statement that follows. Together roughly: 'so… not / and so it did not…'
4.grammar: A connective particle fa- ('so, then,' showing result or sequence) plus the negating particle mā. When mā precedes a past-tense verb, it denies that the action happened ('did not…').

5.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

5.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.
5.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existence; to be

6.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
6.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

7.meaning: 'Upon us' / 'over us' / 'against us' — the preposition ʿalā ('on, over, upon') with an attached 'us'. It conveys something resting on, incumbent upon, or bearing against the group.
7.grammar: A preposition (ʿalā, 'upon/over') with an attached pronoun, first person plural (-nā, 'us'). When a pronoun is attached, ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay-. Such prepositional phrases put their pronoun in the object/genitive role.

8.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
8.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

9.meaning: Bounty, grace, favor; an overflowing generosity or surplus given freely. It denotes goodness and abundance bestowed beyond what is owed or expected, and by extension excellence or superiority.
9.grammar: The -in ending is genitive plus 'tanwīn' (the -n indicating indefiniteness, 'a bounty'). The genitive case typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF bounty') or follows a preposition.
9.root: ف-ض-ل (f-ḍ-l) — bounty, grace, excess goodness, superiority

10.meaning: So taste! — a command to a group to 'taste' or experience something, often used figuratively of undergoing a consequence or punishment.
10.grammar: A command (imperative). The fa- prefix means 'so' or 'then', linking it to what precedes. The -ū ending directs the order to a masculine plural addressee ('you all'): 'so taste!'. The final silent alif is a spelling convention after this plural ending.

11.meaning: The punishment, chastisement, or torment — a penalty inflicted as retribution, especially the painful suffering of divine reckoning.
11.grammar: A definite masculine noun ('the punishment'). The final -a is the accusative ending, which generally marks the word as the direct object of a verb or the subject/predicate after certain particles.
11.root: ع-ذ-ب (ʿ-dh-b) — to punish, torment; the inflicting of pain

12.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
12.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

13.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
13.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
13.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

14.meaning: You (plural) earn, gain, acquire, or bring upon yourselves — the gaining of something through one's own deeds, whether good earnings or the consequences one incurs.
14.grammar: Present-tense verb, masculine plural, second person. The ta- prefix marks 'you', and the -ūna ending shows a masculine plural subject ('you all') and marks the indicative mood — the plain statement form, 'you (all) earn'.
14.root: ك-س-ب (k-s-b) — earning, acquiring, gaining by effort

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: They denied / they cried lies; they declared (something or someone) to be false. An intensive verb meaning to reject as a lie, to disbelieve and brand untrue — directed by a plural 'they'.

parts.tr: kadhdhab (doubled dh; simplified transliterations may write 'kadhab')
parts.en: denied / branded as lies (past stem, intensive)

3.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in an intensive pattern (to treat as false, to repeatedly deny). The middle radical carries a shadda (doubling), which is exactly what marks this as the intensive form: kadhdhab- (not the simple kadhab-). The ending -ū marks the doers as 'they' — a plural, grammatically masculine group, so the whole reconstructs to kadhdhabū. Note that simplified transliterations sometimes omit the doubling and write 'kadhabū', but the doubled dh is essential to the form. The perfect tense denotes a completed action.
3.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie; in this form, to call a lie, to deny as false

4.meaning: By/in Our signs. Āyāt is the plural of āya — a sign, token, or evidence. Signs are pointers that indicate a greater reality. With the prefixed particle and pronoun it means 'with/in Our signs'.
4.grammar: A plural noun preceded by the preposition bi- ('with, in, by'), which requires the following noun to take the -i (genitive) ending. The attached -nā means 'our' when joined to a noun. The genitive here is governed by the preposition.
4.root: أ-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — sign, token, mark

5.meaning: 'And they acted arrogantly / were haughty' — to have been proud and overbearing, swelling with self-importance and refusing to submit.
5.grammar: Prefix wa- means 'and'. The verb is past-tense, intensive reflexive (form X). The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject: 'they (a group) were arrogant' (a completed action).
5.root: ك-ب-ر (k-b-r) — to be great; (form X) to deem oneself great, to be arrogant

6.meaning: From it / about it / away from it — a preposition meaning 'from' or 'off of', attached to a feminine 'it'.
6.grammar: 'ʿan' is a preposition conveying departure or removal — 'away from / off of / concerning'. The attached -hā is 'it/her', referring to a single feminine thing. Prepositions like this put the following pronoun in the genitive.

7.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
7.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

8.meaning: It is opened wide / is flung open repeatedly — the being thrown open of something (such as doors), with the intensive form suggesting many or repeated openings.

parts.en: open wide / fling open repeatedly (Form II intensive)

8.grammar: Present-tense passive verb, third-person feminine singular ('it is …'). The tu- prefix with the vowel pattern marks the passive ('is being done to it'), and the Form II shape (doubled middle letter) gives an intensive or repeated sense ('flung wide open'). The -u ending marks the indicative mood, the plain statement form.

9.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
9.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

10.meaning: The doors, gates, or openings — the plural of 'door', the entryways through which one passes in or out.
10.grammar: A plural noun ('doors'). The -u ending is nominative — the case used for the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified (e.g. the doors that 'are opened'). 'Abwāb' is a broken (internal) plural of 'bāb', door.

11.meaning: The sky or heaven — the canopy overhead; the expanse above the earth, also that which is elevated or raised over something. With the definite article it means 'the sky / the heaven'.
11.grammar: A noun with the definite article al- ('the'), in the genitive marked by the -i ending. (The 'l' of al- assimilates in sound into the following 's', a 'sun letter', though it is still written.) The genitive -i ending typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').

12.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
12.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

13.meaning: 'they enter' — to go into or pass inside a place.
13.grammar: A present/future verb, 3rd-person masculine plural ('they …'). The ending -ūna combines the plural 'they' (-ū) with the indicative marker -na, signalling a simple ongoing or future statement. The ya- prefix marks the third person.
13.root: د-خ-ل (d-kh-l) — to enter, go in, penetrate

14.meaning: The Garden / Paradise — the place of lush, shaded greenery promised as the abode of bliss; literally a garden whose foliage covers the ground.
14.grammar: 'al-' is 'the'. 'janna' is a feminine noun (the tā marbūṭa ending). The final -a is accusative, the form typically marking a word as the object of a verb or, with place-nouns, the destination/location toward which an action occurs.

15.meaning: 'Until / up to the point that; so that' — a particle marking a limit or goal. It expresses the end-point reached ('until') or the purpose aimed at ('so that, in order that').
15.grammar: A particle indicating a goal or limit. When followed by a present-tense verb it places that verb in the subjunctive mood (clipping its ending to -a), conveying 'until / so that' something comes about. Ḥattā itself is invariable.
15.root: — (particle)

16.meaning: It enters / passes through (as a thread passes through the eye of a needle) — the going-in of something into a narrow opening. The verb's core is penetrating into a tight space.
16.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it'). The ya- prefix marks the third person. The -a ending is the subjunctive mood — the form a verb takes after particles meaning 'that', 'until', or 'so that', expressing a possible or purposed action rather than a flat fact ('that it (should) enter').
16.root: و-ل-ج (w-l-j) — entering, penetrating into a narrow place

17.meaning: The camel — the large desert pack-animal. With the definite article it points to the camel as a known or specific instance, or to camels as a kind.
17.grammar: A singular masculine noun carrying the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The final '-u' is the nominative ending, the form a noun takes when it is the subject of a sentence or otherwise the thing being spoken about.
17.root: ج-م-ل (j-m-l) — beauty/comeliness; also the camel

18.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
18.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

19.meaning: Hole, bore, or eye — the small opening or perforation through something, such as the eye of a needle. In the construct form it leans on a following noun to specify the hole 'of' what.
19.grammar: A singular noun in the construct (possessive) state, written without the article because it is bound to a following noun. The '-i' ending is genitive; it marks the word as the first term of a possessive chain meaning 'the eye/hole OF …'.
19.root: س-م-م (s-m-m) — to pierce/perforate; a small opening (also poison)

20.meaning: The needle — the slender pointed sewing tool. With the article it names the needle as a known or definite object.
20.grammar: A singular noun with the definite article 'al-'. The '-i' ending is genitive: it typically marks the second term of a possessive phrase ('… OF the needle') or follows a preposition.

21.meaning: 'And likewise / and in the same way / and thus' — a connective phrase pointing back to a manner just mentioned and saying 'in that very way…'. Built from 'and' + 'like' + 'that'.
21.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'; the prefix ka- means 'like/as'; 'dhālika' is the demonstrative 'that' (pointing to something distant or already mentioned). Because ka- acts like a preposition, the word after it stands in the genitive, though the demonstrative 'dhālika' keeps a fixed form and shows no visible case change. The whole means 'and just like that / and thus'.

22.meaning: 'We reward / We requite' — to repay or recompense someone for their deeds, whether with good or with due consequence.
22.grammar: A present-tense verb. The 'na-' prefix means 'we'. The stem ends in a long '-ī' (a weak final root letter); in the plain indicative this final '-ī' is what is heard, giving 'we reward'.
22.root: ج-ز-ي (j-z-y) — to repay, to recompense, to requite

23.meaning: Those who commit grave sins and crimes; wrongdoers who deliberately break Allah's law and cut themselves off in guilt. The word denotes hardened, culpable offenders, not those who err by accident.
23.grammar: An active participle (one who does the action) of Form IV, made definite by 'al-' ('the'). The '-īna' ending marks a masculine sound plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) case, so it names a group as the object of a verb or the complement of a preposition, rather than the subject.
23.root: ج-ر-م (j-r-m) — to commit a crime or grave sin

1.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
1.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

2.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
2.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

3.meaning: Jahannam — a proper name for the Fire of punishment in the Hereafter, the abode of torment. It is a name rather than a descriptive common noun.
3.grammar: A proper name. Because it is a special, non-fully-inflecting noun (it does not take tanwīn), it shows the -a ending in places where most nouns would otherwise take -i; here the single -a serves for both accusative and genitive positions. As a name it carries no general dictionary 'meaning' but designates the abode of punishment.
3.root: — (a proper name; commonly treated as having no Arabic triliteral root)

4.meaning: A bed, resting-place, or spread-out cradle — a surface levelled and made smooth so one can lie or rest on it; figuratively a place prepared as a couch or abode.
4.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The '-un' ending (nunation) marks it as both nominative — the form used for the subject or predicate of a sentence — and indefinite ('a bed', not 'the bed').
4.root: م-ه-د (m-h-d) — to spread out/smooth/prepare; a cradle or couch

5.meaning: And from / and out of — the conjunction 'and' joined to the preposition 'from', expressing origin, source, starting-point, or 'some of'.
5.grammar: A compound particle: the connector 'wa' ('and') prefixed to the preposition 'min' ('from'). 'Min' governs a following noun in the genitive case and conveys starting-point, source, or partition ('some of').

6.meaning: Above them / over them — the place or position over the top of someone or something, joined to 'them'.
6.grammar: A noun of place meaning 'above/over,' commonly used to mean 'over …'. The -i (kasra) is the genitive ending, here triggered by the following possessor; the attached '-him' is 'them' (its vowel is 'hi' after an -i sound).
6.root: ف-و-ق (f-w-q) — to be above; aboveness, superiority

7.meaning: Coverings / overspreading layers — things that envelop and conceal from above, like enveloping sheets of fire or shrouds drawn over something. A plural of a noun meaning that which overspreads or veils.
7.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural. The '-in' ending marks it as indefinite and genitive — the genitive being the case used after prepositions or as the second term of a possessive phrase; in such 'defective' plurals the final root-letter drops and the indefinite ending appears as '-in'.

8.meaning: 'And likewise / and in the same way / and thus' — a connective phrase pointing back to a manner just mentioned and saying 'in that very way…'. Built from 'and' + 'like' + 'that'.
8.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'; the prefix ka- means 'like/as'; 'dhālika' is the demonstrative 'that' (pointing to something distant or already mentioned). Because ka- acts like a preposition, the word after it stands in the genitive, though the demonstrative 'dhālika' keeps a fixed form and shows no visible case change. The whole means 'and just like that / and thus'.

9.meaning: 'We reward / We requite' — to repay or recompense someone for their deeds, whether with good or with due consequence.
9.grammar: A present-tense verb. The 'na-' prefix means 'we'. The stem ends in a long '-ī' (a weak final root letter); in the plain indicative this final '-ī' is what is heard, giving 'we reward'.
9.root: ج-ز-ي (j-z-y) — to repay, to recompense, to requite

10.meaning: The wrongdoers — those who do wrong or injustice; literally those who put things out of their rightful place, transgressing limits and harming themselves or others. The root sense is darkness.
10.grammar: 'al-' is 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the 'ẓ', doubling it). The stem is an active participle ('one who wrongs') made plural for masculine people. The -īna ending is the object/genitive form of the sound masculine plural, marking the word as an object of a verb or governed by a preposition.

1.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

2.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
2.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

3.meaning: A two-part word: 'and' + 'they did / worked / performed.' The verb denotes doing deeds, working, putting effort into action — practical doing as opposed to mere speaking or believing.
3.grammar: A conjunction 'wa' + a past-tense verb, 3rd person masculine plural. The -ū ending marks the subject as 'they' (a group of males or a mixed group): 'and they did / worked.'

4.meaning: 'The righteous deeds / good works' — the definite plural of a word meaning that which is sound, wholesome, upright, and beneficial. As a noun it refers to good, virtuous actions that set things right.
4.grammar: A definite sound feminine plural noun ('the good deeds'). The -i ending is the oblique case used by feminine plurals to mark either the genitive ('… of …' / after a preposition) or the accusative (direct object); for this plural pattern the accusative and genitive share the same -i ending.
4.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound, good, upright, set right

5.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
5.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

6.meaning: A verb meaning 'We impose as a duty / We burden (someone) with a charge' — to assign a task or obligation that requires effort, with 'We' as the doer.
6.grammar: A Form II present-tense verb; the nu- prefix marks the first-person plural 'we' as the doer, and the -u ending marks the ordinary (indicative) present, describing an ongoing or habitual action. The doubled middle consonant gives the causative sense 'to make (someone) bear'.
6.root: ك-ل-ف (k-l-f) — to charge with, impose a burden/obligation

7.meaning: A 'self' or 'soul' — the living person, the inner self, and by extension a human being or life. It can mean one's very self, one's soul, or simply 'a person/a life'.
7.grammar: A feminine noun. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative case, which typically marks the word as the object of a verb ('a soul / a person' as the thing acted upon).
7.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — soul, self, breath, living being

8.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
8.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

9.meaning: Its capacity / its scope — the extent, range, or full measure of what someone or something can hold or do, with an attached 'its/her'. Conveys 'as much as it can bear', the limit of ability.
9.grammar: A noun with the attached possessive pronoun '-hā' ('its' / 'her'). The '-a' ending is accusative, the case used for the direct object of a verb or for an adverbial 'extent/amount', i.e. 'to the measure of its capacity'.
9.root: و-س-ع (w-s-ʿ) — to be wide/spacious; capacity/ability

10.meaning: 'those / those ones' — a demonstrative pointing to a group of people or things at a distance ('those there').
10.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those.' The -ka element adds the sense of pointing to something farther off (as opposed to 'these' near at hand). Being a fixed pronoun, it keeps one form regardless of case.

11.meaning: 'Companions / people of, dwellers, owners' — those closely associated with something, its inseparable folk, fellows, or inmates; literally the people who 'keep company with' a thing.
11.grammar: A masculine plural noun (the plural of ṣāḥib, 'companion'). The '-u' ending is nominative, typically marking the subject of a sentence; it appears here without nunation because the word is in a possessive construction ('companions OF …') with a following noun.

12.meaning: The Garden / Paradise — a definite noun literally meaning 'the garden'; the term for the Garden of Paradise, the abode of reward in the Hereafter.
12.grammar: Definite noun: 'al-' is 'the'. The '-i' ending (on the feminine '-at-') is genitive, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF …') or follows a preposition. 'janna' originally means a lush, shaded garden.
12.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — to cover, conceal (a garden's dense foliage 'covers' the ground)

13.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
13.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

14.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
14.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

15.meaning: 'Ones who abide / remain forever; everlasting dwellers.' The plural of an active participle describing those who stay, persist, and endure in a state or place without end — abiding permanently.
15.grammar: An active participle in the masculine plural. The -ūna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the nominative case — the form used when such a group is the subject of a sentence or is being described as being in that state.
15.root: خ-ل-د (kh-l-d) — to remain forever, endure, be everlasting

1.meaning: And We removed / drew out / stripped away — to pull something out from where it was rooted or lodged, presented as a completed past action attributed to 'We'.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb prefixed with 'wa' ('and'). The suffix '-nā' is the first-person plural subject marker: it tells us the doer is 'we'. The past tense presents the action as already accomplished.

2.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
3.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

4.meaning: Their breasts / their chests — the bosoms of a group of males, the chest regarded as the seat of feelings and inner thoughts, with an attached 'their'.
4.grammar: A plural noun ('breasts') with the attached pronoun '-him' ('their', referring to a group of males). The '-i' before the pronoun is the genitive ending, signalling that the noun follows a preposition or is the possessed term in a possessive phrase.
4.root: ص-د-ر (ṣ-d-r) — chest/breast; to issue forth/proceed

5.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
5.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

6.meaning: Rancour, spite, hidden grudge — the concealed ill-feeling, malice, or resentment lodged in the heart toward others.
6.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The '-in' ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite and genitive — the genitive case being used after prepositions (such as 'of/from') or as the second term of a possessive phrase.
6.root: غ-ل-ل (gh-l-l) — to harbour rancour; also to bind/shackle

7.meaning: A verb 'it flows, runs, streams' — used of water and rivers moving along, and of things that run or course freely. It describes continuous, ongoing motion.
7.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, 3rd person feminine singular. The ta- prefix here marks a feminine 'it/she' subject. The verb describes an ongoing or habitual action: 'it flows / keeps flowing.'

8.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
8.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

9.meaning: Beneath them / underneath them — the spatial 'under' joined to an attached 'them', indicating the place directly below a group of males.
9.grammar: An adverb of place ('under') in the genitive, bound to the attached pronoun 'them'. As a locational word it normally follows a preposition like 'from', taking the genitive '-i'; the pronoun's vowel appears as '-himu' for ease of joining to the next word.
9.root: ت-ح-ت (t-ḥ-t) — under/below (locational)

10.meaning: 'The rivers / the streams' — the definite plural of a word for a flowing river or watercourse. It denotes large, running channels of water.
10.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the rivers'). The -u ending is the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence — the doer of the verb or the thing being described.

11.meaning: And they said — to utter or declare in speech, with the action presented as completed by a group.
11.grammar: The prefix 'wa-' means 'and'. 'qāla' is the past-tense verb 'to say'; the '-ū' suffix marks a completed action done by 'they' (a masculine or mixed group). The stem shown here ('qālu') carries only the stem vowel before the suffix, with the plural '-ū' supplied by the separate ending. Past tense, so the speaking is presented as already finished.

12.meaning: The praise — all commendation, thanks, and laudation. With the article it conveys praise as a whole, in its entirety, belonging by right to the one praised.
12.grammar: A verbal noun with the definite article 'al-'. The '-u' ending is nominative, marking it as the subject/topic of a sentence; with the article it carries the sense of 'all praise' as an entire, comprehensive category.

13.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'li-' meaning 'to', 'for', or 'belonging to', attached to the name 'Allah'. It conveys 'to Allah' or 'for Allah'.
13.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('to/for') pulls the following noun into the genitive case, which is why 'Allah' ends in '-i' (llāhi). The '-i' ending is the regular result of a noun governed by a preposition.

14.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
14.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

15.meaning: 'He guided us' — a past-tense verb of guiding, showing the right way, or leading aright, with the object 'us' attached. The root denotes guidance and right direction.
15.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb with a third-person masculine singular subject built into it — 'he.' The long final -ā belongs to a weak-ending root (its last letter is a vowel-like letter). The attached -nā is the object 'us,' so the whole means 'he guided us.'
15.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — guidance, to guide, to show the right way

16.meaning: For this / to this — the preposition 'for, to' attached to the near demonstrative 'this', pointing to something close at hand or just mentioned, and assigning it as goal or beneficiary.
16.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('for/to', indicating purpose, direction, or benefit) prefixed to the masculine singular near-demonstrative 'hādhā' ('this'). Demonstratives are indeclinable, so their ending does not change for case.

17.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
17.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
17.root: — (relative pronoun / particle)

18.meaning: 'We were' — the past tense of the verb 'to be,' establishing a past state or condition for a group including the speaker. It is the basic verb of existence and of 'being something.'
18.grammar: The past tense of 'to be' in the first-person plural ('we were'). The subject suffix is -nā ('we'); its nūn is written with a shadda (نَّ) because it merges with the final nūn of the verb stem kun-, and the alif spells the long -ā. A hollow verb, its middle weak letter drops in this form. It sets up a past state, and what follows describes how 'we' were.
18.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to come into being, existence

19.meaning: That we might be guided / find the right way — to be led to and travel the correct path, expressed as a purpose ('so that we…') with 'we' as the actor.
19.grammar: A present-tense verb of the self-directed (Form VIII) pattern, opened by purpose 'li-' ('so that'). The 'na-' prefix marks the subject as 'we'. Because 'li-' makes it subjunctive, the verb takes the '-a' ending (here '-ya' on the weak final letter), giving the sense 'in order that we be guided'.

20.meaning: A particle of urging or exhortation meaning 'why not …?' — used to press for or demand that something be done, and sometimes to express a wish, often with a tone of reproach ('why does … not happen?').
20.grammar: An indivisible particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ). Although written as one form, it is not built up from the conditional 'if' plus a negation; in this prompting usage it is a single fixed particle meaning 'why not?' / 'if only.' Followed by a verb it presses for that action. (Note: in a different construction the same form can mean 'were it not for,' but that is a separate usage.) It is a particle and takes no case ending.

21.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
21.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

22.meaning: 'He guided us' — a past-tense verb of guiding, showing the right way, or leading aright, with the object 'us' attached. The root denotes guidance and right direction.
22.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb with a third-person masculine singular subject built into it — 'he.' The long final -ā belongs to a weak-ending root (its last letter is a vowel-like letter). The attached -nā is the object 'us,' so the whole means 'he guided us.'
22.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — guidance, to guide, to show the right way

23.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
23.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

24.meaning: A two-part emphasis particle meaning 'surely, indeed (already)' — 'la-' strongly affirms, and 'qad' before a past verb stresses that the action has definitely occurred.
24.grammar: Two particles fused for emphasis. 'la-' is the affirming prefix 'surely / truly.' 'qad,' when it precedes a past-tense verb, confirms and intensifies that the action really happened ('has indeed …'). Together they give a strong oath-like assurance to the statement that follows.

25.meaning: she/it came / arrived. A verb of coming, arriving, or presenting itself, in the feminine.
25.grammar: A completed-action (past-tense) verb. The suffix -t marks a single feminine subject: 'she/it came.' Past tense presents the arrival as already accomplished.
25.root: ج-ي-أ (j-y-ʾ) — to come, arrive, bring

26.meaning: 'Messengers', those sent with a message or mission, especially the prophets sent by Allah. This is the plural of 'rasūl' (an envoy, one dispatched to deliver a message).
26.grammar: A plural noun (plural of 'rasūl'). The -u ending marks the nominative case, the form a noun takes when it is the subject of a sentence or the doer of an action ('the messengers …').
26.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; a sending, message, messenger

27.meaning: Our Lord, Master, and Sustainer: the One who owns, governs, nurtures, and brings to completion. Rabb combines ownership, authority, and loving cultivation of what He sustains; the '-our' joins the speakers to Him as those under His care.
27.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord, Master, Sustainer') with the attached possessive pronoun -nā ('our'). The -i before the pronoun is the genitive case, used after a preposition, after a calling/oath, or to link the word to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship.
27.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, own

28.meaning: 'With the truth / by means of what is true and right.' Combines the preposition 'with/by' and 'the truth' — that which is real, established, correct, and rightfully due, as opposed to falsehood.
28.grammar: A noun governed by the attached preposition bi- ('with/by'). The -i ending is the genitive case, which is required after a preposition; here it links 'the truth' to 'with', giving 'with the truth'.
28.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, reality, that which is established and due

29.meaning: And they were called out to / proclaimed to — a group was addressed by a herald's call or announcement, expressed as a completed action done to them ('they were called'), with 'and' prefixed.
29.grammar: A past-tense passive verb (Form III) with 'wa' ('and') prefixed. The '-ū' ending is the masculine plural marker 'they'. Being passive, the subjects are the ones receiving the action — 'they were called out to'.

30.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
30.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

31.meaning: That (one, addressed to several of you) — a far demonstrative 'that', combined with a marker showing the speaker is addressing a plural audience. It points out something distant or notable while flagging 'you all' as those addressed.
31.grammar: A feminine singular far-demonstrative ('that') carrying the address-suffix '-kum' ('you all'), which marks the people being spoken to rather than acting as a possessive. Demonstratives do not change for case; the final vowel appears as '-kumu' to join smoothly to the next word.

32.meaning: The Garden — the lush, walled garden of bliss; by extension Paradise, the abode of eternal reward. The article presents it as the well-known Garden.
32.grammar: A singular feminine noun with the article 'al-'. The '-u' ending is nominative, the case for a subject or for the predicate after 'is' (e.g. '… is the Garden'). The root sense of concealment underlies it: a garden whose ground is hidden by foliage.

33.meaning: You were given it as an inheritance / made its heirs — a group was caused to inherit and take possession of something, expressed as a completed action done to 'you all', with 'it' as the thing inherited.
33.grammar: A past-tense passive, causative (Form IV) verb. The '-tum' subject suffix ('you all', masculine plural) is vowelled '-tumū' (with the long ū written by the wāw) to link to the following object pronoun; the attached '-hā' ('it/her') is the thing received. As a passive causative it means 'you were made to inherit it'.

34.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
34.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

35.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
35.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
35.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

36.meaning: You (all) do / work / act — to carry out deeds or labor.
36.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form I). The 'ta-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks the second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The '-ūna' (with final 'n') is the indicative form, marking a plain ongoing or habitual statement.
36.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

1.meaning: And he called out / cried aloud — to raise the voice in a summons or proclamation toward someone, expressed as a completed past act by a single male, with 'and' prefixed.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb of the Form III pattern (an action directed toward another), prefixed with 'wa' ('and'). It carries no added subject ending, which by default marks the doer as a single male — 'he called out'. The final long 'ā' reflects the verb's weak final root letter.

2.meaning: 'Companions / people of, dwellers, owners' — those closely associated with something, its inseparable folk, fellows, or inmates; literally the people who 'keep company with' a thing.
2.grammar: A masculine plural noun (the plural of ṣāḥib, 'companion'). The '-u' ending is nominative, typically marking the subject of a sentence; it appears here without nunation because the word is in a possessive construction ('companions OF …') with a following noun.

3.meaning: The Garden / Paradise — a definite noun literally meaning 'the garden'; the term for the Garden of Paradise, the abode of reward in the Hereafter.
3.grammar: Definite noun: 'al-' is 'the'. The '-i' ending (on the feminine '-at-') is genitive, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF …') or follows a preposition. 'janna' originally means a lush, shaded garden.
3.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — to cover, conceal (a garden's dense foliage 'covers' the ground)

4.meaning: Plural of ṣāḥib: 'companions, associates, people belonging to / dwellers of.' It denotes those who keep company with something or are bound to it, hence 'the people of …' or 'the folk of …'.
4.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun. The final -a ending is the accusative case; in a possessive chain it also signals that a following noun completes the phrase ('companions OF …'). The accusative typically marks the object of a verb or follows certain particles.
4.root: ص-ح-ب (ṣ-ḥ-b) — companionship, accompanying

5.meaning: 'The Fire' — fire, flame; in religious usage often the Fire of Hell, the blazing punishment of the Hereafter.
5.grammar: The definite article 'al-' ('the') plus the feminine noun 'nār' ('fire'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (so it is pronounced 'an-nār'). The '-i' ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or to link the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the Fire').
5.root: ن-و-ر (n-w-r) — fire, blaze, burning

6.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
6.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

7.meaning: A short particle placed before a verb to emphasize or affirm it. Before a past-tense verb it means 'indeed / certainly / has already (happened)'; before a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes / may'. It sharpens and confirms the verb that follows.
7.grammar: An indeclinable particle (its form never changes). It does not take case or tense endings; its job is to color the following verb — affirming and intensifying a past action ('has indeed done') or signaling occasional possibility with a present verb.

8.meaning: 'We found / came upon / discovered' — to find something, either by encountering it or by determining it to be in a certain state.
8.grammar: A past-tense verb with the '-nā' ending meaning 'we'. So it means 'we found' or 'we came upon'. The '-nā' suffix attached to the past-tense stem marks the doers as a 'we' (first-person plural).
8.root: و-ج-د (w-j-d) — to find, to come upon, to discover

9.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
9.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

10.meaning: He promised us / pledged to us — to make a binding promise or commitment, expressed as a completed past act by a single male, with 'us' as the recipients of the promise.
10.grammar: A past-tense verb. The bare stem with the '-a' vowel marks the subject as a single male ('he'), and the attached '-nā' is the object 'us'. The past tense frames the promise as already given.

11.meaning: 'Our Lord' — 'Rabb' (Lord, Master, Sustainer who creates, owns, nurtures and governs) joined to 'our'. A weighty term for Allah as the One who brings up and sustains all that exists.
11.grammar: A noun with the attached possessive pronoun '-nā' ('our'). The -u before the pronoun is the nominative case, used when the word is the subject or predicate of a sentence ('[He] is our Lord').
11.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master; lordship

12.meaning: A right, a due, or an obligation — that which is true, real, and rightfully owed; an established duty. As an adverbial accusative it conveys "as a duty/obligation, in truth, bindingly."
12.grammar: A noun in the indefinite accusative. The '-an' (nunation on the fatḥa, with a following alif) often functions adverbially here — "as a binding duty" or "in truth" — describing the manner or affirming the statement.
12.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — to be true, right, established; truth, right

13.meaning: 'So/then — is it the case that…?' A linking 'then' joined to an interrogative particle that introduces a yes/no question, often carrying a sense of urging, challenge, or expectation ('will you not…?').
13.grammar: A compound of the connective fa- ('so, then', linking to what precedes) and the question particle hal, which turns a statement into a yes/no question and frequently implies expectation or exhortation. Particles like this are invariable — they take no case or mood ending.

14.meaning: You found / came upon — to discover, encounter, or find something to be in a certain state, expressed as a completed past act by 'you all'.
14.grammar: A past-tense verb with the suffix '-tum', the masculine plural subject marker 'you all'. The doubled 't' arises as the stem's final 'd' assimilates into the suffix's 't'. The past tense presents the finding as completed.
14.root: و-ج-د (w-j-d) — to find/come upon; to experience
