15.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
15.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.
15.root: — (particle; no root)

16.meaning: 'He promised / pledged' — a completed act of giving one's word that something will come about, whether a reward or a consequence.
16.grammar: A past-tense verb with no attached pronoun, so the doer is 'he' (third-person masculine singular) and the action is complete. The final -a is the standard past-tense vowel.
16.root: و-ع-د (w-ʿ-d) — promise, pledge

17.meaning: Your (plural) Lord — 'Rabb' means the Master, Owner, Sustainer, and Nurturer who creates, provides for, and brings a thing to its completion. It combines lordship with loving upbringing and care.
17.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The suffix '-kum' means 'your' (plural possessor). The '-u' on 'rabbu' before the suffix is the nominative case, marking the word as a subject or as a predicate standing on its own.
17.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, master, sustain, own

18.meaning: A right, a due, or an obligation — that which is true, real, and rightfully owed; an established duty. As an adverbial accusative it conveys "as a duty/obligation, in truth, bindingly."
18.grammar: A noun in the indefinite accusative. The '-an' (nunation on the fatḥa, with a following alif) often functions adverbially here — "as a binding duty" or "in truth" — describing the manner or affirming the statement.
18.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — to be true, right, established; truth, right

19.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
19.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

20.meaning: Yes / indeed — a particle of affirmation that confirms a statement or answers a question in the positive, asserting that what was said is so.
20.grammar: An indeclinable particle of affirmative reply; it has a fixed form and takes no case or tense endings. It functions to affirm or assent to a preceding statement or question.

21.meaning: Then he announced / proclaimed aloud — and so a single male made a public call or proclamation; the 'fa-' adds the sense of 'then / and so', linking it as a consequence.
21.grammar: A past-tense verb of the intensive (Form II) pattern, opened by the connector 'fa-' ('then / so'). The bare stem with final '-a' marks the doer as a single male, 'he'. Form II here conveys making a formal, public proclamation.
21.root: ا-ذ-ن (ʾ-dh-n) — to give ear/listen; to announce/permit

22.meaning: An announcer / herald / proclaimer — one who makes a public call or proclamation, the active doer of announcing.
22.grammar: An active participle of the intensive (Form II) pattern, naming the one who performs the action ('one who announces'). The '-un' ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('an announcer') and nominative, the case used for the subject of a sentence.
22.root: ا-ذ-ن (ʾ-dh-n) — to give ear/listen; to announce/permit

23.meaning: An adverb of place meaning 'between' or 'among', here joined to the attached pronoun 'them'; together it conveys 'between them / amongst them', signalling something situated in the midst of a group or shared among parties.
23.grammar: An adverb of place (ẓarf) ending in -a, the accusative marker typical of such adverbs, indicating a location or relationship. The attached suffix '-hum' is a possessive/object pronoun meaning 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
23.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies in the midst

24.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
24.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

25.meaning: A curse: a pronouncement of expulsion and being shut out from mercy and good. The noun names the act or state of being cursed — condemnation that drives someone far from grace.
25.grammar: A feminine singular noun. The final -u is the nominative ending, the case that typically marks a word as the subject of a verb or the topic being spoken about.
25.root: ل-ع-ن (l-ʿ-n) — to curse, to drive far from mercy

26.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
26.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

27.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
27.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
27.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

28.meaning: The wrongdoers — those who do wrong or injustice; literally those who put things out of their rightful place, transgressing limits and harming themselves or others. The root sense is darkness.
28.grammar: 'al-' is 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the 'ẓ', doubling it). The stem is an active participle ('one who wrongs') made plural for masculine people. The -īna ending is the object/genitive form of the sound masculine plural, marking the word as an object of a verb or governed by a preposition.

1.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
1.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

2.meaning: they turn away / they bar (others) — to hold back, hinder, or avert; to turn oneself or others aside from something. The verb describes an ongoing, present action by a group.
2.grammar: A present-tense Form I verb. The ya- prefix marks a third-person subject, and the ending -ūna (the -ū fused into the doubled d, written ṣuddūna) marks masculine plural plus the indicative mood — a plain ongoing statement ('they turn away'). The doubled d reflects the geminate root.
2.root: ص-د-د (ṣ-d-d) — to turn away, avert, hinder, bar

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on behalf of,' 'for,' 'about,' or 'away from.' It often conveys removing a burden from someone or acting in their place.

parts.en: on behalf of / for / away from

3.grammar: A preposition (a linking particle). It governs the noun that follows it, putting that noun into the genitive case. It does not change form.

4.meaning: 'path, way, road' — a route or course; figuratively a cause or way of life one travels along. In construct ('the way OF ...').
4.grammar: A singular noun with the '-i' (genitive) ending, which typically links it to a following noun ('the way OF ...') or follows a preposition. It marks the word as connected to or possessed by what comes after.
4.root: س-ب-ل (s-b-l) — way, path, road

5.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
5.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

6.meaning: And they seek it: a present-tense verb of seeking after and desiring something, with an attached pronoun for what is sought.
6.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ū plus -na ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they') in the indicative mood; the attached -hā is a feminine singular object pronoun ('it'). The wa- prefix means 'and'.
6.root: ب-غ-ي (b-gh-y) — to seek, desire, to deviate

7.meaning: Crookedness, deviation, distortion — a bend or twist away from straightness; figuratively a moral or spiritual deviation from the right path.
7.grammar: A noun. The '-an' ending is accusative and indefinite: the accusative often marks the direct object of a verb or a descriptive complement, and the final 'n' sound marks it indefinite ('crookedness'). The word names a deviation from what is straight.
7.root: ع-و-ج (ʿ-w-j) — to bend, be crooked, deviate

8.meaning: 'While they / and they' — the word 'wa' (here 'while' or 'and') joined to the standalone pronoun 'hum' ('they'), referring to a masculine plural group.
8.grammar: A connective 'wa' — often circumstantial 'while' — plus the independent subject pronoun 'hum' ('they'), used for a masculine plural group. As an independent pronoun it usually stands as the subject of a following statement.

9.meaning: The noun 'the Hereafter / the next life / the world to come,' linked by 'with / for / in exchange for' (bi-). The base word means 'the last, the latter, the final' (state of affairs) and is used as the standing name for the everlasting life after this world.
9.grammar: A definite feminine noun ('the Hereafter') governed by the preposition 'bi-' ('with / for / in exchange for'). The '-i' ending is genitive: the case a noun takes after a preposition (or when linked to a preceding noun as '…of…'). Here it appears because the preposition 'bi-' requires the genitive form; the tā' marbūṭa of the stem is sounded as 't' before this ending.
9.root: ا-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — being last, coming after, the end

10.meaning: Disbelievers / deniers: those who reject faith and cover over the truth. The active participle names people characterized by ungrateful rejection of what should be acknowledged.
10.grammar: A masculine plural active participle. The -ūna ending marks a masculine plural in the nominative case — the form used when the word is the subject or predicate (as opposed to -īna for object/genitive).
10.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal, disbelieve, be ungrateful

1.meaning: And between the two of them: a word marking the space, distinction, or relation that lies in the middle of two parties or things, here referring to a pair.
1.grammar: An adverb of place ('between') with an attached pronoun. The suffix -humā is the dual pronoun, meaning specifically 'the two of them' (two parties, not more). The wa- prefix means 'and'.
1.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

2.meaning: A barrier, veil, or partition: something that screens off and separates one side from another, blocking sight or passage between them.
2.grammar: A masculine singular noun. The -un ending is the nominative case with nunation (the final -n), which marks the noun as indefinite — 'a barrier' rather than 'the barrier'.
2.root: ح-ج-ب (ḥ-j-b) — to screen, veil, block from view

3.meaning: A two-part phrase: the joining word 'and' plus the preposition 'on / upon / incumbent upon,' often used to express an obligation resting on someone.
3.grammar: The connector 'wa' ('and') joined to the preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon'). Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending; a noun governed by 'ʿalā' takes the genitive.

4.meaning: The heights / elevated places: high ridges or raised ground. The plural noun denotes upper, prominent stretches of ground or a barrier — also linked to 'recognizing,' as a height affords a vantage to discern.
4.grammar: A plural noun with the definite article 'the.' The final -i is the genitive ending, the case that typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …') or follows a preposition.
4.root: ع-ر-ف (ʿ-r-f) — to know, recognize; a raised ridge or crest

5.meaning: Men: adult male human beings. The plural noun denotes men as a group, sometimes carrying the sense of people of standing or strength.
5.grammar: A masculine plural noun (the plural of rajul, 'a man'). The -un ending is the nominative case with nunation, marking it as indefinite — 'men' rather than 'the men.'
5.root: ر-ج-ل (r-j-l) — man, manhood; also foot/on foot

6.meaning: They recognize / they know: a present-tense verb of identifying and discerning something by its features, perceiving a thing for what it truly is.
6.grammar: A present-tense verb. The -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they') and signals the indicative mood, the form used for plain statements of fact or ongoing action.
6.root: ع-ر-ف (ʿ-r-f) — to know, recognize, discern by feature

7.meaning: A word meaning 'each one,' 'every one,' or 'all (of them)' taken individually — it singles out every member of a group. Here it stands in the indefinite, pointing to 'each' as the object or focus.
7.grammar: A noun of totality ('each / every'). The ending -an is the accusative with indefinite (tanwīn) marking; the accusative typically flags the word as the object of a verb or otherwise governed, and the doubled-n sound (tanwīn) shows it is indefinite ('a/an, some').

8.meaning: By their mark / sign: a distinguishing feature, badge, or outward token by which someone or something is identified. The noun denotes a recognizable sign stamped upon a person or thing.
8.grammar: A noun governed by the preposition bi- ('by/with'), with an attached possessive pronoun. The suffix -hum means 'their' (masculine plural). The noun sīmā is invariable (it shows no visible case ending) but stands in the genitive by position, the case used after prepositions.
8.root: س-و-م (s-w-m) — to mark, brand, set a distinguishing sign

9.meaning: And they called out: a completed-action verb of summoning or hailing aloud, calling to someone at a distance or proclaiming a call.
9.grammar: A past-tense (completed-action) verb in Form III, which often carries the sense of doing something toward or at another party. The -aw ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The wa- prefix means 'and.'
9.root: ن-د-و / ن-د-ي (n-d-w/y) — to call out, summon, hail

10.meaning: Plural of ṣāḥib: 'companions, associates, people belonging to / dwellers of.' It denotes those who keep company with something or are bound to it, hence 'the people of …' or 'the folk of …'.
10.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun. The final -a ending is the accusative case; in a possessive chain it also signals that a following noun completes the phrase ('companions OF …'). The accusative typically marks the object of a verb or follows certain particles.

11.meaning: The Garden / Paradise — a definite noun literally meaning 'the garden'; the term for the Garden of Paradise, the abode of reward in the Hereafter.
11.grammar: Definite noun: 'al-' is 'the'. The '-i' ending (on the feminine '-at-') is genitive, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF …') or follows a preposition. 'janna' originally means a lush, shaded garden.
11.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — to cover, conceal (a garden's dense foliage 'covers' the ground)

12.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
12.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

13.meaning: Peace, soundness, safety, well-being — freedom from harm and discord; a word of greeting and of the wholeness and security that comes from being safe and at peace.
13.grammar: A noun. The ending -un is the indefinite nominative: the -u marks the nominative (the form a subject or a stated/announced word takes), and the final -n ('tanwīn') marks it as indefinite ('peace', not 'the peace').

14.meaning: A combination meaning roughly 'upon/over you (plural)' or 'against you (plural)'. The preposition denotes resting on, being incumbent upon, or being directed against, while the attached pronoun refers to a group of people being addressed.
14.grammar: A preposition with a fused object pronoun. The base form ʿalā shortens to ʿalay- before an attached pronoun. The ending -kum marks a masculine plural addressee ('you all'); whatever the preposition governs is in the genitive by virtue of following it.

15.meaning: A negating particle, 'not', used specifically to deny that an action happened in the past, even though it attaches to a present-tense verb form. It turns 'you do X' into 'you did not do X'.

parts.en: did not (negation of a completed act)

15.grammar: An indeclinable particle that governs the verb after it, putting that verb into the jussive (clipped) mood and giving it past-time meaning. In short: lam + a present-form verb = 'did not [verb]'.
15.root: — (particle; no triliteral root)

16.meaning: They enter it: a present-tense verb of going into or entering a place, with an attached pronoun for the place entered.
16.grammar: A present-tense verb in the indicative mood. The plural subject ('they') is here written as bare -ū rather than the full -ūna: the final -na of the indicative is dropped because an object pronoun is suffixed directly to the verb (a regular rule — the nūn falls away before the attached pronoun). The attached -hā is a feminine singular object pronoun ('it').
16.root: د-خ-ل (d-kh-l) — to enter, go in

17.meaning: 'While they / and they' — the word 'wa' (here 'while' or 'and') joined to the standalone pronoun 'hum' ('they'), referring to a masculine plural group.
17.grammar: A connective 'wa' — often circumstantial 'while' — plus the independent subject pronoun 'hum' ('they'), used for a masculine plural group. As an independent pronoun it usually stands as the subject of a following statement.

18.meaning: They hope / yearn: a present-tense verb of eager longing and expectation, coveting or aspiring toward something desired.
18.grammar: A present-tense verb. The -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they') and the indicative mood, used for plain statements of ongoing action or fact.
18.root: ط-م-ع (ṭ-m-ʿ) — to covet, yearn, hope eagerly

1.meaning: 'And when...' — a linking phrase joining 'and' to 'when', used to introduce a circumstance or a recurring situation: 'and whenever / and at the time that...'.
1.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to idhā ('when'). Idhā is a particle pointing to a time or condition, generally referring to something expected or recurring in the future ('when / whenever' it happens), and it normally introduces a following clause that states what occurs at that time.

2.meaning: It was turned / diverted: a completed-action passive verb meaning something was redirected, averted, or made to face another way — the doer is unnamed and the focus is on the thing turned.
2.grammar: A past-tense passive verb (the u-i vowel pattern, ṣurifa, signals the passive — 'was turned'). The -at ending marks a third-person feminine singular subject ('she/it'), agreeing with a feminine noun.
2.root: ص-ر-ف (ṣ-r-f) — to turn away, divert, redirect

3.meaning: Their eyes / their sights: the organs of sight, or by extension acts of seeing and glances. The plural noun denotes eyes belonging to a group.
3.grammar: A plural noun (plural of baṣar, 'sight/eye') with an attached possessive pronoun. The -u is the nominative ending, marking it typically as the subject; the suffix -hum means 'their' (masculine plural).

4.meaning: Toward / in the direction of: a word denoting the facing-place or direction opposite something — the side one turns to face. It functions as 'toward' or 'in front of.'
4.grammar: A noun used adverbially to mean 'toward, facing.' The final -a is the accusative ending, which here functions adverbially to express direction ('toward …'); it typically links to a following noun in the genitive.
4.root: ل-ق-ي (l-q-y) — to meet, encounter, face

5.meaning: Companions, associates, fellows; those who keep company with or belong to a thing — people closely bound to something (often 'people/inhabitants of …').
5.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of ṣāḥib ('companion'). The final -i is the genitive ending, which typically links the word to a following noun ('companions OF …') or follows a preposition. As a plural it denotes a group, here in a possessive/linking relationship.
5.root: ص-ح-ب (ṣ-ḥ-b) — companionship, to accompany, keep company

6.meaning: 'The Fire' — fire, flame; in religious usage often the Fire of Hell, the blazing punishment of the Hereafter.
6.grammar: The definite article 'al-' ('the') plus the feminine noun 'nār' ('fire'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (so it is pronounced 'an-nār'). The '-i' ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or to link the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the Fire').

7.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
7.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

8.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

parts.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

8.grammar: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
8.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

9.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
9.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

10.meaning: You place us / make us: a present-tense verb of putting, setting, or rendering something into a state, with an attached pronoun 'us' as its object.
10.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ta- prefix with no plural ending marks a second-person masculine singular subject ('you'). The bare (vowelless) ending shows the jussive mood, the form used after particles of command or prohibition. The attached -nā is the object pronoun 'us.'
10.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, place, render, appoint

11.meaning: With, together with, alongside — indicating company, accompaniment, or being in the same place or time as another.
11.grammar: A preposition of accompaniment ('with, alongside'); grammatically it is an adverbial of place/time (ẓarf) that governs the genitive. It is placed before a following noun to put one thing in the company of another, and that following noun stands in the genitive. The -a is its fixed ending.

12.meaning: 'The people / the folk' — a collective noun for a community, nation, or group of people regarded as a body. Often it carries the nuance of one's own people or a particular group sharing a trait.
12.grammar: A collective noun with the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The final '-i' is the genitive ending, which typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun in an 'of …' relationship.
12.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand/rise; a people, community

13.meaning: The wrongdoers; those who commit injustice, oppression, or place things outside their right setting. Ẓulm is putting something where it does not belong and so transgressing against truth or against others.
13.grammar: An active participle ('the ones who do X') with the definite article 'al-' (its 'l' assimilates into the 'ẓ', a sun letter). The '-īna' ending marks a masculine sound plural in the accusative or genitive — the form used as an object or after a preposition.
13.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — injustice, wrongdoing, placing a thing wrongly

1.meaning: And he called out / cried aloud — to raise the voice in a summons or proclamation toward someone, expressed as a completed past act by a single male, with 'and' prefixed.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb of the Form III pattern (an action directed toward another), prefixed with 'wa' ('and'). It carries no added subject ending, which by default marks the doer as a single male — 'he called out'. The final long 'ā' reflects the verb's weak final root letter.

2.meaning: 'Companions / people of, dwellers, owners' — those closely associated with something, its inseparable folk, fellows, or inmates; literally the people who 'keep company with' a thing.
2.grammar: A masculine plural noun (the plural of ṣāḥib, 'companion'). The '-u' ending is nominative, typically marking the subject of a sentence; it appears here without nunation because the word is in a possessive construction ('companions OF …') with a following noun.

3.meaning: The heights / elevated places: high ridges or raised ground. The plural noun denotes upper, prominent stretches of ground or a barrier — also linked to 'recognizing,' as a height affords a vantage to discern.
3.grammar: A plural noun with the definite article 'the.' The final -i is the genitive ending, the case that typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …') or follows a preposition.
3.root: ع-ر-ف (ʿ-r-f) — to know, recognize; a raised ridge or crest

4.meaning: Men — the plural of 'man' (an adult male); also carries the sense of menfolk as distinct from women.
4.grammar: A plural noun in the indefinite accusative, marked by the -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa). This ending typically signals the word is a direct object, or names something brought about/scattered ('[He made/produced] men…').
4.root: ر-ج-ل (r-j-l) — man, manhood; on foot

5.meaning: They recognize them: a present-tense verb of identifying and knowing someone by their features, with an attached pronoun for those recognized.
5.grammar: A present-tense verb. The -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they') in the indicative mood; the attached -hum is a masculine plural object pronoun ('them').
5.root: ع-ر-ف (ʿ-r-f) — to know, recognize, discern by feature

6.meaning: By their mark / sign: a distinguishing feature, badge, or outward token by which someone or something is identified. The noun denotes a recognizable sign stamped upon a person or thing.
6.grammar: A noun governed by the preposition bi- ('by/with'), with an attached possessive pronoun. The suffix -hum means 'their' (masculine plural). The noun sīmā is invariable (it shows no visible case ending) but stands in the genitive by position, the case used after prepositions.
6.root: س-و-م (s-w-m) — to mark, brand, set a distinguishing sign

7.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
7.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

8.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
8.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

9.meaning: It availed / enriched / sufficed: a completed-action verb meaning something was of use or benefit, made one independent of need, or warded off a want.
9.grammar: A past-tense (completed-action) verb in Form IV, third-person masculine singular ('he/it'). The Form IV pattern is causative, giving the sense of 'making free of need' or 'being of avail.' The final long -ā is the verb's weak (defective) ending.
9.root: غ-ن-ي (gh-n-y) — to be free of need, rich, self-sufficient

10.meaning: 'From you / off you' (addressing a group). The preposition 'ʿan' (denoting moving away from, or 'concerning') fused with a plural 'you'.
10.grammar: A preposition 'ʿan' with an attached pronoun object. 'ʿan' conveys moving away or off from something (and so pairs naturally with pardoning — lifting a fault away); the suffix '-kum' means a plural 'you'.

11.meaning: Your gathering / your assembled multitude: the act of being gathered together, or the assembled group itself. The verbal noun names a collected mass of people or things belonging to those addressed.
11.grammar: A verbal noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The -u is the nominative ending, marking it typically as the subject; the suffix -kum means 'your' (addressing a masculine plural 'you').

12.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
12.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

13.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
13.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
13.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

14.meaning: You act arrogantly / haughtily — to be proud, to puff oneself up, to scorn the truth and disdain to submit. The form X pattern conveys deeming oneself great and above others.
14.grammar: A present/imperfect verb (form X). The ta- prefix with the -una ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'). The -una ending (not -u) signals the indicative mood, used for ongoing or factual statements. Form X here carries the reflexive sense of 'consider oneself great'.
14.root: ك-ب-ر (k-b-r) — greatness, bigness; here pride and self-magnification

1.meaning: Are these (people)? — a near-demonstrative 'these' carried into a question. It points to a group close at hand while the opening hamza turns the pointing into a query.
1.grammar: The plural near-demonstrative 'these' (hāʾulāʾ) prefixed by the interrogative hamza ('are these…?'). Demonstratives like this are fixed forms that do not change for case the way ordinary nouns do; the closing -i here is the connecting vowel that smooths it into what follows.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: You swore / took an oath: a completed-action verb of solemnly vowing or asserting under oath. The Form IV pattern gives the sense of binding oneself by a sworn declaration.
3.grammar: A past-tense (completed-action) verb in Form IV. The -tum ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all swore'). Form IV here conveys the act of taking a binding oath.
3.root: ق-س-م (q-s-m) — to swear an oath; also to divide, apportion

4.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
4.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

5.meaning: It reaches them / attains them / befalls them: a present-tense verb meaning something comes to reach, touch, or be granted to someone, with an attached pronoun for those it reaches.
5.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('it/he'). The -u ending marks the indicative mood, used for plain statements. The attached -hum ('them,' masculine plural) takes a helping vowel -u (becoming -humu) to ease pronunciation before a following word.
5.root: ن-ي-ل (n-y-l) — to attain, reach, obtain, grant

6.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
6.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

7.meaning: With mercy / by mercy: tender compassion and active kindness that relieves and benefits. The noun names mercy as a quality and an outpouring of grace.
7.grammar: A feminine noun governed by the preposition bi- ('with/by'). The -in ending is the genitive case with nunation — genitive because it follows a preposition, and the final -n marks it as indefinite ('a mercy').

8.meaning: Enter! / go in!: a command verb directing the addressees to go into a place. It is the imperative of the verb 'to enter.'
8.grammar: An imperative (command) verb. The -ū ending directs a masculine plural 'you' — a command addressed to a group ('enter, all of you'). The opening vowel (alif) is a helping vowel needed to begin pronunciation of the command.

9.meaning: The Garden / Paradise — the place of lush, shaded greenery promised as the abode of bliss; literally a garden whose foliage covers the ground.
9.grammar: 'al-' is 'the'. 'janna' is a feminine noun (the tā marbūṭa ending). The final -a is accusative, the form typically marking a word as the object of a verb or, with place-nouns, the destination/location toward which an action occurs.
9.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — to cover, conceal, hide

10.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
10.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

11.meaning: 'Fear' — a state of being afraid, dread, or alarm; apprehension of something harmful or threatening.
11.grammar: A singular indefinite noun. The '-un' ending (nunation) marks it as nominative and indefinite — 'a fear' or simply 'fear' — and the nominative typically signals the doer or subject of a sentence, or the subject of an existential statement ('there is fear').

12.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
12.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

13.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
13.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

14.meaning: You — the standalone pronoun for a group of people ('you all', masculine or mixed). It is used for emphasis or as the subject standing on its own.
14.grammar: A detached subject pronoun meaning 'you all' (second-person masculine/mixed plural). Unlike pronoun endings attached to verbs or nouns, this word stands alone — typically to emphasize the subject or to begin an equational sentence ('you [are]…'). Its form is fixed and does not change for case.

15.meaning: You grieve: a present-tense verb of feeling sorrow, sadness, or grief over loss or distress. It denotes inner mourning and heaviness of heart.
15.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ta- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'); the -na also signals the indicative mood, used for plain statements (and is dropped when a particle of negation or command governs the verb).
15.root: ح-ز-ن (ḥ-z-n) — grief, sorrow, sadness

1.meaning: And he called out / cried aloud — to raise the voice in a summons or proclamation toward someone, expressed as a completed past act by a single male, with 'and' prefixed.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb of the Form III pattern (an action directed toward another), prefixed with 'wa' ('and'). It carries no added subject ending, which by default marks the doer as a single male — 'he called out'. The final long 'ā' reflects the verb's weak final root letter.

2.meaning: 'Companions / people of, dwellers, owners' — those closely associated with something, its inseparable folk, fellows, or inmates; literally the people who 'keep company with' a thing.
2.grammar: A masculine plural noun (the plural of ṣāḥib, 'companion'). The '-u' ending is nominative, typically marking the subject of a sentence; it appears here without nunation because the word is in a possessive construction ('companions OF …') with a following noun.

3.meaning: 'The Fire' — fire, flame; in religious usage often the Fire of Hell, the blazing punishment of the Hereafter.
3.grammar: The definite article 'al-' ('the') plus the feminine noun 'nār' ('fire'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (so it is pronounced 'an-nār'). The '-i' ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or to link the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the Fire').

4.meaning: Plural of ṣāḥib: 'companions, associates, people belonging to / dwellers of.' It denotes those who keep company with something or are bound to it, hence 'the people of …' or 'the folk of …'.
4.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun. The final -a ending is the accusative case; in a possessive chain it also signals that a following noun completes the phrase ('companions OF …'). The accusative typically marks the object of a verb or follows certain particles.
4.root: ص-ح-ب (ṣ-ḥ-b) — companionship, accompanying

5.meaning: The Garden / Paradise — a definite noun literally meaning 'the garden'; the term for the Garden of Paradise, the abode of reward in the Hereafter.
5.grammar: Definite noun: 'al-' is 'the'. The '-i' ending (on the feminine '-at-') is genitive, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF …') or follows a preposition. 'janna' originally means a lush, shaded garden.
5.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — to cover, conceal (a garden's dense foliage 'covers' the ground)

6.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
6.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

7.meaning: A command to pour forth and move off in a throng — to set out streaming together with the crowd, hence 'press onward / depart en masse'.
7.grammar: A command (imperative) verb, Form IV, addressed to a group: the plural wāw (-ū) means 'you (plural masculine), do it!'. The initial a- (with the long vowel in the stem, fīḍ-) is the Form IV imperative marker. So it means 'pour forth / stream away, all of you'.
7.root: ف-ي-ض (f-y-ḍ) — to overflow, pour forth, stream abundantly

8.meaning: 'Upon us' / 'over us' / 'against us' — the preposition ʿalā ('on, over, upon') with an attached 'us'. It conveys something resting on, incumbent upon, or bearing against the group.
8.grammar: A preposition (ʿalā, 'upon/over') with an attached pronoun, first person plural (-nā, 'us'). When a pronoun is attached, ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay-. Such prepositional phrases put their pronoun in the object/genitive role.

9.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
9.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

10.meaning: The water — water as a substance, the liquid essential to life. With the attached definite article it points to water as a known or specific body or quantity of water.
10.grammar: A definite noun (al- = 'the'). The final -i ending is the genitive case: it typically marks the word as the object of a preposition or as the second term of a possessive link ('… OF …').

11.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
11.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

12.meaning: From what / from that which — a fusion of the preposition 'from' with the relative 'what/which', introducing the thing or situation being referred to.
12.grammar: A merger of 'min' ('from') and 'mā' ('what/that which'); the 'n' of 'min' assimilates into the 'm' of 'mā', doubling it. The combination means 'from what ...' and typically introduces a following clause describing the thing referred to. Being particles, neither part takes a case ending.

13.meaning: A construction meaning 'He provided you / granted you sustenance' — to bestow provision (food, wealth, any good thing) upon someone. The provider is 'He'; 'you' are the recipients.
13.grammar: A past-tense verb for a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'); the final -a is the standard past-tense ending. The attached -kum ('you all') is the object; its vowel is raised to -kumu for ease before a following word beginning with the article.
13.root: ر-ز-ق (r-z-q) — provision, sustenance, bestowal of livelihood

14.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
14.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

15.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
15.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.
15.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, utterance

16.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
16.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

17.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
17.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
17.root: — (proper name)

18.meaning: He made the two of them forbidden / prohibited them both — a third-person past verb conveying that a single male agent declared or rendered two things unlawful, with the doubled middle root letter intensifying the sense to 'absolutely forbade.'
18.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in the intensive (form II) pattern, third-person masculine singular: the bare stem with no prefix and the -a vowel signals 'he' completed the action. The doubled middle consonant adds force ('utterly forbade'). The suffix -humā is a dual object pronoun, 'the two of them.'

19.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
19.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
19.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

20.meaning: The disbelievers / the ungrateful — those who reject faith and cover over the truth; the word also carries the sense of covering up or being ungrateful for what one has been given.
20.grammar: 'al-' is 'the'. The stem is an active participle ('one who disbelieves/is ungrateful') made plural for masculine people. The -īna ending is the accusative/genitive form of the sound masculine plural: it marks the word as an object of a verb or as governed by a preposition, as opposed to the subject form -ūna.
20.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; ingratitude, disbelief

1.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
1.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

2.meaning: Past-tense verb (reflexive form), third person plural: 'they took for themselves, adopted, chose.' A completed act of taking something on as one's own.
2.grammar: A completed-action (past) verb in a reflexive pattern (taking something for oneself). The '-ū' ending (with silent trailing alif) marks the subject as 'they' (masculine plural). The opening 'i-' is a helping vowel that lets the cluster of consonants be pronounced.

3.meaning: Their religion / way of life — the concept of dīn: the complete system of belief, worship, obligation, and obedience by which one lives and to which one is accountable; also rendered 'faith,' 'judgment,' or 'recompense' depending on context. Here joined to 'their.'

parts.en: religion, way of life, system of obedience and accountability

3.grammar: A noun with the attached possessive pronoun -hum ('their,' a group of men). The -a vowel before the pronoun reflects the accusative case — the form typically used when the noun is the direct object of a verb ('… their religion' as the thing acted upon).
3.root: د-ي-ن (d-y-n) — religion, obedience, judgment, requital, debt/accountability

4.meaning: Idle play, diversion, amusement — passing entertainment or distraction that occupies a person without serious purpose, often carrying a tone of frivolity or that which turns one away from what matters.
4.grammar: An indefinite noun. The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the accusative case used indefinitely ('a / some'); it commonly marks a direct object or, very often, expresses manner or purpose — 'as amusement' / 'for diversion.'
4.root: ل-ه-و (l-h-w) — diversion, distraction

5.meaning: "And amusement / play / sport," the noun "laʿib" denoting idle play, frivolous fun, and games — activity pursued for diversion rather than serious purpose.
5.grammar: The "wa-" prefix means "and." The "-an" tanwīn ending marks the noun as indefinite and in the accusative case — the case used for a direct object of a verb or other complement within a sentence.
5.root: ل-ع-ب (l-ʿ-b) — to play; play, sport, amusement

6.meaning: And it/they deluded them, beguiled them, lured them with false hopes — to deceive by making something appear attractive or safe when it is not. Joined to 'them.'
6.grammar: A past-tense verb with the feminine ending -t ('she/it [did]'), carrying the attached object -hum(u) ('them'). The base vowel -a is the past-tense marker; the -t shows a feminine or non-human subject. The object's vowel is lengthened to -humu to ease the join with a following word.

7.meaning: 'The life' — earthly existence, the span of living in this world. The word denotes life as the state of being alive, vitality, and the worldly life as a whole.
7.grammar: 'al-' is the definite article 'the'. The final '-u' is the nominative ending, which typically marks the word as the subject of a sentence (the one doing or being something), or as the predicate naming what something is.

8.meaning: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
8.grammar: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
8.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world

9.meaning: So / then — the day; a connective particle joined to the noun 'the day.' It links to what precedes (drawing a consequence or sequence, 'so / then') and names the day.
9.grammar: The prefix fa- is a connector meaning 'so / then,' marking a result or sequence. al- is 'the.' The final -a is the accusative case, which often marks a direct object or, with time-words like 'day,' an adverbial sense ('on the day').
9.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day

10.meaning: We forget them / We leave them neglected — a first-person plural present verb. Of Allah it does not mean true forgetfulness but a deliberate disregarding or abandoning, treating someone as forgotten in requital for their own neglect.
10.grammar: A present-tense verb with the na- prefix meaning 'we.' The suffix -hum is a masculine plural object pronoun, 'them.' The verb ends in the weak vowel ā (from a final-weak root), the ordinary present form for an ongoing or habitual action.

11.meaning: 'Just as / in the same way that' — a phrase of comparison joining 'like / as' to 'what', meaning 'like that which...' or 'in the manner that...'.
11.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like / as') joined to mā ('what / that which'). Together they introduce a likeness or manner — 'just as...', 'in the same way that...' — comparing one thing or action to another.

12.meaning: A verb meaning 'they forgot' or 'they neglected/abandoned.' The root spans both genuine forgetfulness and the willful neglect of something one chooses to put out of mind.
12.grammar: A past-tense verb. The ending -ū marks a completed action by 'they' (masculine plural). The silent 'alif' written after the -ū is a spelling convention and is not pronounced.

13.meaning: Meeting, encounter, or coming-face-to-face — the event of two parties meeting, often used of the encounter with one's Lord or an appointed reckoning.
13.grammar: A verbal noun (the act of meeting) on the 'fiʿāl' pattern. The final -a is the accusative case ending, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb or otherwise governed into that case.
13.root: ل-ق-ي (l-q-y) — to meet, encounter, come upon

14.meaning: Their day — the noun 'day' joined to a possessive pronoun, denoting a day belonging to or appointed for a group, such as a fixed time or occasion that is uniquely theirs.
14.grammar: A noun with the attached possessive pronoun -him ('their,' masculine plural). The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or as the possessed term in a possessive link.

15.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
15.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

16.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
16.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
16.root: — (relative pronoun / particle)

17.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
17.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
17.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

18.meaning: By/in Our signs. Āyāt is the plural of āya — a sign, token, or evidence. Signs are pointers that indicate a greater reality. With the prefixed particle and pronoun it means 'with/in Our signs'.
18.grammar: A plural noun preceded by the preposition bi- ('with, in, by'), which requires the following noun to take the -i (genitive) ending. The attached -nā means 'our' when joined to a noun. The genitive here is governed by the preposition.

19.meaning: A verb meaning 'they knowingly reject / deny / repudiate.' Its distinctive sense is denying something one inwardly recognizes to be true — rejection against better knowledge.

parts.en: they (the prefix marking a third-person subject)
plural marker, with the -na of the ongoing/present

19.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb, third-person masculine plural. The ya- prefix marks 'they,' and -ūna marks a plural subject and an ongoing or repeated action. The retained -na is the mark of the indicative mood, the verb's default unbroken form.
19.root: ج-ح-د (j-ḥ-d) — to deny or reject what one knows to be true

1.meaning: "And indeed / and most certainly" — combines 'and' with the emphatic 'la-' and the particle 'qad'; before a past-tense verb 'qad' affirms that the action has definitely and already happened, reinforced into 'and indeed it surely did'.
1.grammar: The conjunction 'and' plus the emphatic 'la-' ('surely') plus the particle 'qad'. With a past-tense verb, 'qad' stresses that the act is real and completed ('has indeed happened'); together they form a strong oath-like affirmation. These are function words and are not inflected.

2.meaning: We brought them / came to them — a first-person plural past verb meaning 'we came,' here with an object, so 'we brought (something) to them' or 'we came to them (with something).'
2.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The suffix -nā attached to the stem marks the doer as 'we.' The further suffix -hum is the masculine plural object pronoun, 'them.' Together: 'we came to / brought them.'

3.meaning: With a book / a scripture — the preposition 'with / by means of' joined to the indefinite noun 'book,' i.e. a written record or revealed scripture. The 'with' often conveys bringing or coming bearing something.
3.grammar: The prefix bi- is a preposition, 'with / by means of.' The noun ends in -in (tanwīn kasra), the indefinite genitive ('a book') — the genitive case is required because the noun follows the preposition bi-.

4.meaning: We expounded it / set it out in detail — a first-person plural past verb meaning to distinguish, detail, and explain something part by part, with an object pronoun referring to that thing.
4.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in the intensive (form II) pattern, whose doubled middle consonant conveys doing the action thoroughly ('detailed out fully'). The suffix -nā marks the doer as 'we'; the final -hu is the masculine singular object pronoun, 'it / him.'
4.root: ف-ص-ل (f-ṣ-l) — separating, distinguishing in detail

5.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
5.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

6.meaning: 'Knowledge.' A noun denoting sure, established knowing — to know a thing as it truly is. In its indefinite form it often appears in the sense 'any knowledge (at all).'
6.grammar: A noun with the -in ending (genitive with nunation, 'tanwīn'), marking it as indefinite ('any knowledge'). The genitive -i is the form used after a preposition such as 'of' or 'by' — e.g. 'of any knowledge.'

7.meaning: Guidance — right direction, the showing of the correct way and the leading along it. The term combines pointing out the path and granting success in following it; more than mere information, it is direction toward what is right.

parts.en: indefinite (tanwin) ending on a shortened final vowel

7.grammar: An indefinite masculine singular noun. The -an (tanwin) ending marks indefiniteness — 'a guidance' rather than 'the guidance'. Because the word ends in a weak final letter, its case is not audibly distinguished, so this single form covers more than one grammatical position.

8.meaning: 'Mercy' — compassion and loving kindness shown by bestowing good and relieving hardship. From the same root as 'womb,' it carries a sense of nurturing tenderness.
8.grammar: A feminine singular noun ending in tāʾ marbūṭa (ة), an integral letter of the word. The tanwīn fatḥ on that ة (-tan) marks it as indefinite and accusative — the case of a direct object or of something granted. The wa- prefix means 'and'; the shadda written on وَّ reflects a recitation convention (idghām at the junction with the preceding word), not an assimilation of the conjunction itself.

9.meaning: For a people, for a folk or community; a group of human beings considered together. Joined to the preposition 'li' ('for / to').
9.grammar: The preposition 'li' ('for / to') plus an indefinite singular noun ('a people'). The -in ending (nunation) marks indefiniteness; it is the genitive form, required because nouns governed by 'li' stand in the genitive.
9.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a people/community

10.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'they believe / they have faith' — to trust and affirm with the heart, to hold something true and place one's security in it.
10.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb built on the form IV pattern, which here functions intransitively, 'to have faith / to believe' (not a causative making someone else believe). The yu- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they.' The full -ūna ending (indicative mood) presents the action as ongoing or habitual fact: 'they (do) believe.'

1.meaning: An interrogative particle that turns a statement into a yes/no question, roughly "is it that…?" or "do…?". It can also carry a rhetorical or expectant tone rather than a literal request for information.
1.grammar: A question particle placed before a sentence to ask whether something is the case. It has no case ending and does not change form; it simply marks the words that follow as a yes/no question.

2.meaning: They look toward, watch for, or await; a present-tense act of a group either gazing at something or expecting/waiting for it to happen.
2.grammar: A present/ongoing verb. The ya- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ("they"). The full -ūna ending also signals the indicative mood, used for stating an action that is happening or habitual.

3.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
3.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

4.meaning: Its interpretation, ultimate meaning, or final outcome: tracing a thing back to what it really signifies or to how it ultimately turns out. The '-its' refers to a masculine singular thing being interpreted.
4.grammar: A verbal noun of the second form (the act of carrying a matter back to its origin or true sense), with an attached possessive pronoun -hu ('its/his'). The -a before the pronoun is the accusative case, typically marking the direct object of a verb or a word governed by certain particles; the pronoun keeps its base -hu form after that -a vowel.
4.root: أ-و-ل (ʾ-w-l) — to return, trace back to origin; interpret

5.meaning: The noun 'day' — a span of time, often used for a momentous Day or appointed time; in the accusative it frequently functions as 'on the day (when…)', marking the time at which something occurs.
5.grammar: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
5.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

6.meaning: he brings / he comes with — a third-person verb meaning to bring something forward or cause it to come, often by fetching or producing it.
6.grammar: A present/future tense verb. The ya- prefix marks a third-person singular masculine doer ('he/it'). Built on a weak root ending in a long vowel, it carries the sense of bringing or coming forth. The form expresses an ongoing or habitual action.

7.meaning: Its outcome / interpretation / final fulfilment — the noun 'taʾwīl' (the ultimate meaning, real significance, or eventual realization of a thing) joined to a possessive pronoun, 'its.'
7.grammar: A verbal noun (from form II) with the attached possessive pronoun -hu ('its / his'). The -u vowel before the pronoun is the nominative case, the form typically used for the subject of a sentence or the thing being talked about.
7.root: ا-و-ل (ʾ-w-l) — returning to an origin; hence interpreting, final outcome

8.meaning: 'He says' or 'he is saying' — the act of speaking or uttering words. The imperfect tense conveys an ongoing, habitual, or present/future action.
8.grammar: Imperfect (present/future) verb, third person masculine singular. The ya- prefix marks 'he', the stem qūl carries the meaning 'say', and the final -u is the indicative ending, signalling a plain factual statement (as opposed to a subjunctive -a or jussive sukūn used after certain particles).

9.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
9.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

10.meaning: They forgot it / neglected it — a third-person masculine plural past verb meaning a group let something slip from mind or deliberately disregarded it, with an object pronoun, 'it.'
10.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person masculine plural; the long -ū ending is the plural-subject marker meaning 'they (men) did' the action. The suffix -hu is the masculine singular object pronoun, 'it / him.'

11.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
11.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

12.meaning: An adverb of time meaning 'before / beforehand / previously,' pointing to a moment or state that precedes something else in time. When used with the final vowel -u (qablu), it stands cut off from an explicit following noun, conveying 'before(hand)' or 'previously' in an absolute sense — the thing it is 'before' is understood rather than stated.
12.grammar: An adverb of time. The final -u ending here is the indeclinable (mabnī) form taken when the word is severed from a following genitive: rather than 'before X,' it means 'before(hand)' on its own, with the reference point left implicit.
12.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to come before, precede, be in front; to receive/accept

13.meaning: A short particle placed before a verb to emphasize or affirm it. Before a past-tense verb it means 'indeed / certainly / has already (happened)'; before a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes / may'. It sharpens and confirms the verb that follows.
13.grammar: An indeclinable particle (its form never changes). It does not take case or tense endings; its job is to color the following verb — affirming and intensifying a past action ('has indeed done') or signaling occasional possibility with a present verb.

14.meaning: she/it came / arrived. A verb of coming, arriving, or presenting itself, in the feminine.
14.grammar: A completed-action (past-tense) verb. The suffix -t marks a single feminine subject: 'she/it came.' Past tense presents the arrival as already accomplished.

15.meaning: 'Messengers', those sent with a message or mission, especially the prophets sent by Allah. This is the plural of 'rasūl' (an envoy, one dispatched to deliver a message).
15.grammar: A plural noun (plural of 'rasūl'). The -u ending marks the nominative case, the form a noun takes when it is the subject of a sentence or the doer of an action ('the messengers …').
15.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; a sending, message, messenger

16.meaning: Our Lord, Master, and Sustainer: the One who owns, governs, nurtures, and brings to completion. Rabb combines ownership, authority, and loving cultivation of what He sustains; the '-our' joins the speakers to Him as those under His care.
16.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord, Master, Sustainer') with the attached possessive pronoun -nā ('our'). The -i before the pronoun is the genitive case, used after a preposition, after a calling/oath, or to link the word to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship.
16.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, own

17.meaning: 'With the truth / by means of what is true and right.' Combines the preposition 'with/by' and 'the truth' — that which is real, established, correct, and rightfully due, as opposed to falsehood.
17.grammar: A noun governed by the attached preposition bi- ('with/by'). The -i ending is the genitive case, which is required after a preposition; here it links 'the truth' to 'with', giving 'with the truth'.
17.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, reality, that which is established and due

18.meaning: So / then — is there…? : a connective particle joined to the question-word 'hal,' which opens a yes/no question. Combined, it introduces an inquiry tied to what precedes ('so, is there…?'), and can carry a rhetorical force.
18.grammar: Two particles. fa- is a connector, 'so / then,' linking to a result or sequence. hal is an interrogative particle that turns the following statement into a yes/no question; it is invariable and has no case ending.

19.meaning: 'For us / to us' — indicating that something is directed toward, or belongs to, the speaker's group.
19.grammar: The preposition li- ('for / to') with the attached pronoun -nā ('us'). When this pronoun is added, the preposition's vowel becomes 'la-'. The whole expresses benefit or direction toward 'us' — what is done for, or owed to, the speaker's group.
19.root: — (li- is a particle/preposition; -nā is a pronoun)

20.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
20.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

21.meaning: Intercessors — those who plead or mediate on another's behalf, seeking to gain favor, pardon, or benefit for someone before one in authority. This is the plural, 'advocates / mediators.'
21.grammar: A plural noun on an intensive/plural pattern. The final -a is the accusative case; this word is a 'diptote,' meaning it takes a plain -a (not tanwīn) for the accusative. The accusative typically marks a direct object or the subject of certain particles.

22.meaning: So that they may intercede / then they would intercede — a connective particle joined to a third-person plural present verb meaning a group pleads or mediates on another's behalf.
22.grammar: The prefix fa- here links to a purpose or consequence ('so that / then'). The verb is present-tense, third-person masculine plural; the prefix ya- marks 'he/they (masc.),' and the -ū ending marks the plural subject 'they.' The stem carries no indicative -u vowel, because the plural -ū ending takes its place; the absence of a final -n marks the subjunctive, reflecting dependence on the preceding particle — 'so that they may intercede.'

23.meaning: A combination of the preposition 'for / to' with the pronoun 'us', meaning 'for us' or 'to us / on our behalf'.
23.grammar: A preposition ('for / to') joined to the attached pronoun 'us'. The pronoun -nā always means 'us / our' regardless of position. Together they express benefit or direction toward the speakers ('for us').

24.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
24.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

25.meaning: "We are sent back / returned / brought back." A present-tense passive verb: the "we" are returned by another to a former place or state, not returning by their own act.
25.grammar: An ongoing/present-tense verb in the passive voice, "we" (first-person plural). The nu- prefix with its u-vowel marks both the "we" subject and the passive sense (the action is done to us). The final -u is the default present-tense ending used when the verb stands on its own.
25.root: ر-د-د (r-d-d) — to send back, return, repel

26.meaning: So that we may act / then we would do (deeds) — a connective particle joined to a first-person plural present verb meaning 'to do, work, or act,' especially to perform deeds.
26.grammar: The prefix fa- links to a purpose or consequence ('so that / then'). The verb is present-tense with the na- prefix meaning 'we.' The final -a (instead of the usual -u) is the subjunctive ending, signaling that the action depends on a preceding particle — hence 'so that we may do.'
26.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — working, doing, deeds

27.meaning: 'Other than / different from / not'. A noun used to express difference or negation — 'something other than X', and so 'not-X'. It functions to exclude or contrast with what follows.
27.grammar: A noun of difference/exception. The -a ending marks the accusative case, the form it takes when it serves as a direct object or as a descriptive substitute standing in an object position; it governs a following noun in the genitive ('other than …'). That it takes case endings and tanwīn confirms it is a true noun, not a particle.
27.root: غ-ي-ر (gh-y-r) — to be other, different; otherness, change

28.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
28.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

29.meaning: 'We were' — the past tense of the verb 'to be,' establishing a past state or condition for a group including the speaker. It is the basic verb of existence and of 'being something.'
29.grammar: The past tense of 'to be' in the first-person plural ('we were'). The subject suffix is -nā ('we'); its nūn is written with a shadda (نَّ) because it merges with the final nūn of the verb stem kun-, and the alif spells the long -ā. A hollow verb, its middle weak letter drops in this form. It sets up a past state, and what follows describes how 'we' were.
29.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to come into being, existence

30.meaning: We do / we act — a first-person plural present verb meaning to do, work, or perform deeds, describing ongoing or habitual action.
30.grammar: A present-tense verb with the na- prefix meaning 'we.' The final -u ending is the indicative, the plain present form used for a real, ongoing, or habitual action ('we do / we are doing').

31.meaning: A short particle placed before a verb to emphasize or affirm it. Before a past-tense verb it means 'indeed / certainly / has already (happened)'; before a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes / may'. It sharpens and confirms the verb that follows.
31.grammar: An indeclinable particle (its form never changes). It does not take case or tense endings; its job is to color the following verb — affirming and intensifying a past action ('has indeed done') or signaling occasional possibility with a present verb.

32.meaning: 'They lost', 'they have suffered loss', 'they ruined themselves' — said of a group of males who have come out as losers, forfeiting or wasting something of value, especially their own selves.
32.grammar: Past-tense verb. The -ū ending means the subject is 'they' (more than one male) and the action is presented as completed: 'they lost'.
32.root: خ-س-ر (kh-s-r) — loss, to lose, to suffer ruin

33.meaning: A noun meaning 'their own selves' or 'themselves' — the plural of 'nafs' (self, soul, person, inner self), joined to the pronoun 'their.' It commonly conveys the reflexive idea of acting upon one's own self.
33.grammar: A noun (a broken/irregular plural of 'nafs') with the attached possessive pronoun '-hum' ('their/them,' masculine plural). The -a case ending before the pronoun is accusative, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb — i.e. the self upon which the action falls.

34.meaning: "And it went astray / was lost / went to ruin." A past-tense verb meaning that something strayed from the right path, missed its target, or vanished and came to nothing. The opening wa- adds "and."
34.grammar: A completed-action (past-tense) verb in the "he/it" third-person masculine singular form. With no subject pronoun attached, the bare verb itself carries the sense "he/it strayed."
34.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to go astray, be lost, err

35.meaning: From them; away from them; concerning them. The preposition ʿan conveys moving away from, departing from, or 'on behalf of / concerning', combined with the pronoun 'them'.
35.grammar: A preposition joined to the attached pronoun -hum, 'them' (referring to a group, grammatically masculine plural). The preposition ʿan basically signals separation or removal ('away from'), and can also mean 'about/concerning' or 'on behalf of' depending on usage.

36.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
36.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.

37.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
37.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
37.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be
