10.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
10.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

11.meaning: 'You (plural) take / adopt / make for yourselves' — the act of taking something for oneself, adopting or fashioning it into something.
11.grammar: A present-tense Form VIII verb meaning 'to take for oneself, adopt, make into.' The 'ta-…-ūna' frame marks a second-person masculine plural subject, 'you all take/adopt.' The full '-ūna' ending (with nūn) is the indicative, the ordinary statement form used for an ongoing or habitual action.

12.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
12.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

13.meaning: 'Its plains / its level lowlands' — the plural 'suhūl' (smooth, flat lands, plains) bound to a feminine possessor 'its.'
13.grammar: 'Suhūl' is the plural of 'sahl' (a plain, smooth/easy ground). The '-i' (kasra) is the genitive ending, here because the noun is bound to a following possessor. The attached '-hā' is the possessive 'its/her' (feminine): 'its plains.'

14.meaning: Palaces — grand, stately mansions or fortified residences; the plural of a noun denoting an imposing built structure for nobility or rulers. Marked as indefinite ('palaces' rather than 'the palaces').
14.grammar: A plural noun. The final -an (tanwīn with alif) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case — the case typically used for the direct object of a verb or for nouns in similar object-like roles. So it signals 'palaces' as something being acted upon, and 'a/some' rather than 'the'.
14.root: ق-ص-ر (q-ṣ-r) — to fall short, confine, or be enclosed; hence a 'qaṣr', an enclosed/fortified mansion

15.meaning: And you carve out / hew — to cut and shape something hard such as rock, sculpting it into a desired form. The form addresses a group: 'you (all) carve'.
15.grammar: A present/imperfect verb. The ta- prefix plus the -ūna ending together mark a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'); the -ūna ending also signals the indicative mood, i.e. a plain factual or ongoing action ('you do carve'). Prefixed wa means 'and'.
15.root: ن-ح-ت (n-ḥ-t) — to carve, chisel, or hew (especially stone)

16.meaning: The mountains — large natural elevations of rock and earth. A plural noun made definite by 'the'.
16.grammar: A definite plural noun. The prefixed al- means 'the'. The final -a marks the accusative case — typically the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon).
16.root: ج-ب-ل (j-b-l) — mountain; by extension that which is firmly fixed or innate

17.meaning: Homes / houses — dwelling places where people live and shelter; the plural of 'bayt' (house). Marked as indefinite ('homes' rather than 'the homes').
17.grammar: A plural noun. The final -an (tanwīn with alif) marks it indefinite and accusative — the case for a direct object or, as often with such forms, a noun expressing purpose or result ('as homes'). It signals 'houses/homes' indefinitely, not 'the houses'.
17.root: ب-ي-ت (b-y-t) — to spend the night, lodge; hence 'bayt', a house/dwelling

18.meaning: Then remember / make mention of — to call to mind and keep something present in the mind, and also to mention it aloud; a command to a group.
18.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a masculine plural ('you all remember'). The -ū ending directs the order to a group. The leading fa- is a connecting particle meaning 'then' or 'so', linking this command to what precedes; the helping vowel at the start (u-) eases pronunciation.
18.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, mention, call to mind

19.meaning: "favors, bounties, blessings" — the gracious gifts and benefits bestowed (especially the many blessings of Allah).
19.grammar: A plural noun meaning "favors/bounties" (singular alā / ilā). The final -a marks the accusative (object) state, typically used when the word is the object of a verb.

20.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
20.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

21.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
21.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

22.meaning: A verb meaning to act with corruption, wreak havoc, or work mischief and ruin — to spread disorder and harm.
22.grammar: A present-tense verb directed at a plural 'you' (a group of males or a mixed group). The 'ta-' prefix signals 'you', and the -aw ending marks the plural 'you' subject. The vowelless (cut-off) form here is the mood used after certain particles, e.g. in prohibitions ('do not …').
22.root: ع-ث-و / ع-ث-ي (ʿ-th-w/y) — wreaking corruption and havoc

23.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
23.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

24.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
24.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

25.meaning: An active participle (the doer of an action) meaning 'corrupters', 'those who spread corruption' — people who cause ruin, disorder, and moral or social decay.
25.grammar: An active participle on the 'mu-' pattern, naming the one who performs the action of the related verb (to cause corruption). The -īna ending makes it a plural of males in the accusative or genitive case — the form used when the word is an object or otherwise governed, including as a circumstantial description ('… being corrupters').
25.root: ف-س-د (f-s-d) — corruption, spoiling, ruin

1.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
1.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

2.meaning: The chiefs, leading men, or notables — the prominent council of a people; a collective term for the elite whose standing fills the eyes.
2.grammar: A definite noun (the al- prefix means 'the') with the -u (nominative) ending, the case that typically marks the subject of a sentence — the ones doing or being something. Though singular in form, it refers collectively to the leading body of a people.

3.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
3.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

4.meaning: They were arrogant / haughty — they acted with pride, deeming themselves great and looking down on others, refusing to submit. A past-tense action of a group.
4.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in the derived 'ista-' pattern, which here conveys deeming oneself great or behaving as though great. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). Being perfect, it denotes a completed action.
4.root: ك-ب-ر (k-b-r) — to be great/big; in this pattern, to consider oneself great, i.e. arrogance

5.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
5.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
5.root: — (preposition)

6.meaning: 'His people / his folk' — the community, tribe, or nation to which a person belongs, with the attached pronoun 'his'.
6.grammar: A noun with the attached pronoun '-hi' ('his'). The '-i' ending is genitive: it typically marks the word as the object of a preposition or as linked to a preceding noun ('… of …'). The pronoun appears as '-hi' (rather than '-hu') because of this genitive '-i'.
6.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to rise; a people who stand together

7.meaning: A compound meaning 'for those who' or 'belonging to those who'. It joins the preposition 'for/to' with a masculine plural relative pronoun ('those who'), introducing a clause that describes a group of people by something they do or possess.
7.grammar: The prefix 'li-' is a preposition meaning 'for', 'to', or expressing ownership/benefit ('belonging to'). The relative pronoun is 'alladhīna' ('those who'), but when 'li-' attaches to it the connecting hamza of 'al-' drops out and the two lām sounds merge into one doubled lām, so the form is written and read 'lilladhīna' rather than 'li-alladhīna'. 'alladhīna' has a fixed shape and does not change for case.

8.meaning: They were deemed weak / oppressed — they were treated as lowly and powerless, made vulnerable and downtrodden by others. A past-tense action done TO a group (passive).
8.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in the passive voice — the inner vowel pattern (u–u–i) shows the subjects received the action rather than performed it ('were deemed/made weak'). The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The 'ista-' pattern adds the sense of reckoning or treating someone as weak.
8.root: ض-ع-ف (ḍ-ʿ-f) — to be weak; in this pattern, to be considered/made weak, i.e. oppressed

9.meaning: 'for whoever / to the one who' — the preposition 'for/to' joined with the relative word 'who', introducing the person(s) about whom something is said.
9.grammar: A preposition ('for/to') combined with the relative/interrogative word 'man' ('who, whoever'). Together they single out a person or group as the focus ('for the one(s) who...').

10.meaning: 'He believed' — he had faith, trusted, and affirmed. The basic past-tense form of the verb meaning to believe and to find security in faith.
10.grammar: A past-tense verb on the causative (Form IV) pattern, from the root for security and faith. The -a ending marks a third-person masculine singular subject, 'he (believed)', stating a completed act of coming to faith.

11.meaning: From them / among them — the preposition min ('from, out of, part of') joined to the pronoun 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
11.grammar: The preposition min ('from / among / part of') with the attached third-person masculine plural pronoun -hum ('them'). Pronouns after a preposition are in the genitive; the combination expresses origin, partition ('some of them'), or belonging to that group.

12.meaning: Do you know? — a question put to a group asking whether they possess knowledge or awareness of something. Combines a yes/no question marker with the verb 'you (all) know'.
12.grammar: A present/imperfect verb fronted by the interrogative prefix a- ('is it that…?'), turning it into a yes/no question. The ta- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'); the -ūna ending also signals the indicative mood (a plain statement turned into a question): 'do you (all) know?'

13.meaning: An emphatic particle meaning 'that' (as in 'I know that...') or 'indeed/surely.' It introduces a statement and gives it certainty and emphasis, presenting what follows as an established fact.
13.grammar: An emphatic particle that introduces a noun-clause ('that...'). It puts the following noun into the accusative case and lends the whole statement a sense of certainty and assertion. It typically comes after verbs of knowing, saying, or informing.

14.meaning: 'Ṣāliḥ' — a proper name meaning literally 'righteous / sound / upright one'; it is the name of a prophet, and also functions generally as the active participle 'one who is righteous.'
14.grammar: Active participle of Form I, 'one who is sound/righteous,' also used as the prophet's name. The final '-an' (tanwīn fatḥa) marks it indefinite and accusative — the case typically used for the direct object of a verb.
14.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound, good, righteous, in good order

15.meaning: One who is sent — an envoy or messenger dispatched with a commission; literally 'a sent one'. A passive participle. Marked as indefinite ('a messenger').
15.grammar: A passive participle (a 'mu-…-al' form) naming the one who undergoes the action — here, one who has been sent. The final -un (tanwīn) marks it indefinite ('a …') and in the nominative case — the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or the thing being described.
15.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; from it 'rasūl' (messenger) and 'risāla' (message)

16.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
16.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

17.meaning: A phrase meaning 'his Lord'. 'Lord' (rabb) denotes the Master, Owner, Sustainer, and Nurturer who creates, provides for, and governs — far richer than a mere title; here joined to 'his'.
17.grammar: The noun 'Lord' with the genitive -i ending followed by the attached pronoun -hi ('his'). The genitive case appears because the noun is linked to a preceding word ('… OF his Lord') or follows a preposition. The lengthened -hī reflects how this pronoun is pronounced after an -i vowel.
17.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, nurturing, ownership, sustaining and bringing to completion

18.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
18.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

19.meaning: A two-part expression: an emphatic particle that strongly affirms and confirms a statement ('truly, indeed, certainly'), fused with the attached pronoun 'we.' Together: 'truly we…' / 'indeed we…'
19.grammar: The particle inna gives strong emphasis and certainty to the clause it opens. The attached -ā is the pronoun 'we,' serving as the subject being emphasized: 'truly we…'

20.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
20.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

21.meaning: A past, passive event: '(he/it) was sent' — to be dispatched or commissioned, as a messenger or message is sent forth by a sender.

parts.en: was sent (3rd masc. sing., past passive)

21.grammar: This is a past-tense passive verb: the u- vowel at the start plus the internal vowelling show that the subject did not act but had the action done to it ('was sent'). It stands in its base, unmarked form, which by itself denotes a single masculine subject — there is no separate person-suffix; the final vowel is part of the verb's own stem.
21.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send, to dispatch (a messenger)

22.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
22.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

23.meaning: Believers: those who have faith — people who inwardly trust and outwardly affirm Allah and what He has revealed. The active participle describes ones characterized by īmān (secure, committed belief).
23.grammar: A masculine plural active participle ('ones who believe'). The suffix -ūna (written wāw + nūn) is a single unit marking the masculine sound plural in the nominative case: it names a group performing or characterized by the action and is the form used when the word is the doer or topic of a sentence.
23.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — to be secure, to trust, to have faith

1.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
1.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: They were arrogant / haughty — they acted with pride, deeming themselves great and looking down on others, refusing to submit. A past-tense action of a group.
3.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in the derived 'ista-' pattern, which here conveys deeming oneself great or behaving as though great. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). Being perfect, it denotes a completed action.
3.root: ك-ب-ر (k-b-r) — to be great/big; in this pattern, to consider oneself great, i.e. arrogance

4.meaning: A two-part expression: an emphatic particle that strongly affirms and confirms a statement ('truly, indeed, certainly'), fused with the attached pronoun 'we.' Together: 'truly we…' / 'indeed we…'
4.grammar: The particle inna gives strong emphasis and certainty to the clause it opens. The attached -ā is the pronoun 'we,' serving as the subject being emphasized: 'truly we…'

5.meaning: A combination meaning 'with/for the one that' or 'in exchange for that which'. It fuses the preposition bi- (with, by, in exchange for) onto the masculine singular relative pronoun alladhī ('the one who/that'), introducing a clause that further identifies the referred-to thing.

parts.en: the one who/that (masc. sing. relative pronoun)

5.grammar: bi- is a preposition that always governs a genitive; alladhī is an indeclinable masculine singular relative pronoun whose form does not change for case. It points to a single masculine entity and requires a following clause to complete its sense ('the one that …').

6.meaning: 'You (all) have believed / you came to faith' — to affirm trust and belief, especially faith in Allah and what He has revealed.

parts.en: believed (initial long vowel of the Form IV stem 'to have faith')
you all (2nd person masculine plural subject)

6.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb, second person masculine plural: the ending '-tum' means 'you all (did) …'. The Form IV pattern (with the long initial ā) carries the sense of coming to and holding faith. It states a completed act: 'you have believed'.
6.root: ا-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, trust; to believe, have faith

7.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
7.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

8.meaning: Disbelievers / deniers: those who reject faith and cover over the truth. The active participle names people characterized by ungrateful rejection of what should be acknowledged.
8.grammar: A masculine plural active participle. The -ūna ending marks a masculine plural in the nominative case — the form used when the word is the subject or predicate (as opposed to -īna for object/genitive).
8.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal, disbelieve, be ungrateful

1.meaning: Then they hamstrung / slaughtered (it) — they crippled an animal by cutting its leg tendons, and so killed it. A past-tense action of a group, opening with 'then/so'.
1.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb expressing a completed act. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The prefixed fa means 'then' or 'so', signalling sequence or consequence.
1.root: ع-ق-ر (ʿ-q-r) — to wound in the leg, hamstring; hence to cripple and slaughter

2.meaning: The she-camel — a female camel; a single, specific (definite) animal.
2.grammar: A definite singular noun. The prefixed al- ('the') has its 'l' assimilated into the following 'n' (so it is pronounced an-nāqa). The final -a marks the accusative case — typically the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon).

3.meaning: And they were insolent / overstepped — they rebelled and behaved with arrogant defiance, brazenly exceeding all bounds. A past-tense action of a group.
3.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb from a root ending in a weak letter, so its plural 'they' subject shows as the ending -aw (written with the silent alif). It denotes a completed action. Prefixed wa means 'and'.
3.root: ع-ت-و / ع-ت-ي (ʿ-t-w) — to exceed bounds, be insolent or rebellious

4.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on behalf of,' 'for,' 'about,' or 'away from.' It often conveys removing a burden from someone or acting in their place.

parts.en: on behalf of / for / away from

4.grammar: A preposition (a linking particle). It governs the noun that follows it, putting that noun into the genitive case. It does not change form.

5.meaning: Command / matter / affair — an authoritative order, or more broadly a matter, decree, or business at hand. The exact sense ranges from a direct 'command' to a general 'affair'.
5.grammar: A singular noun. The final -i marks the genitive case: it typically links the word to a following noun ('… of …') — e.g. 'the command of …' — or follows a preposition.
5.root: ا-م-ر (ʾ-m-r) — to command; also 'amr' as a matter/affair

6.meaning: 'Their Lord' — the base 'rabb' means Lord, Master, Sustainer: the one who owns, nurtures, governs, and brings to maturity. As a divine title it conveys Allah as Creator and Sustainer of all.
6.grammar: The noun 'rabb' ('Lord, Sustainer') with the attached pronoun '-him' ('their'). The '-i' before the pronoun is the genitive case, the form used after a preposition or, as in a possessive linkage, to show belonging ('of/their').
6.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, master, sustain; lordship

7.meaning: And they said — to utter or declare in speech, with the action presented as completed by a group.
7.grammar: The prefix 'wa-' means 'and'. 'qāla' is the past-tense verb 'to say'; the '-ū' suffix marks a completed action done by 'they' (a masculine or mixed group). The stem shown here ('qālu') carries only the stem vowel before the suffix, with the plural '-ū' supplied by the separate ending. Past tense, so the speaking is presented as already finished.

8.meaning: O Ṣāliḥ — a direct call ('O …') to a person named Ṣāliḥ, the name of a prophet. The name itself derives from a word meaning 'righteous, sound, upright'.
8.grammar: A proper name preceded by the vocative particle yā ('O'), used to call or address someone directly. The name does inflect for case as a diptote (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf): it takes -u in the nominative and -a in the genitive/accusative, always without tanwīn. When addressed as a single, named vocative like this, it takes the nominative form -u with no tanwīn — a requirement of the vocative construction rather than a sign that the name is indeclinable.
8.root: — (proper name; from ص-ل-ح, ṣ-l-ḥ, 'to be righteous/sound')

9.meaning: 'Come!' (to more than one person, or with the sense 'come to us') — a command to approach or come forward. The base verb means to come or arrive.
9.grammar: An imperative (command) verb addressed to someone, built on the verb 'to come.' Its initial vowel is a helping (connecting) vowel that lets the consonant cluster be pronounced. The attached -nā means 'us,' giving the sense 'come to us.'
9.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come, to arrive, to bring

10.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
10.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

11.meaning: "you promise us / you threaten us" — the present-tense act of pledging or warning of something to come, by a single "you," with "us" as recipient.
11.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ta- prefix marks a single "you" (male) as doer; the -u before the suffix is the indicative present (ongoing/general action). The suffix -nā is the object "us."

12.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
12.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

13.meaning: 'You (single male) were / used to be' — the past tense of 'to be', describing a past state, and often an ongoing or habitual condition in the past ('you used to…').
13.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) form of the verb 'to be'. The suffix -ta marks the subject as 'you', a single male. It states a condition that held in the past; paired with a following present-tense verb it often gives the sense 'you used to / you would (habitually)'.
13.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, becoming, coming to exist

14.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
14.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

15.meaning: "the messengers / the ones sent" — the definite plural of mursal, a passive participle meaning 'one who is sent'; it denotes those commissioned and dispatched, i.e. the divine messengers.
15.grammar: A definite masculine sound plural passive participle ('the sent ones'). The -īna ending is the accusative/genitive (object or after-preposition) form of the masculine plural, as opposed to -ūna which would mark the subject form.
15.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send, message, messenger

1.meaning: '…so it seized / struck / took hold of them.' The connector 'so/then' plus a past-tense verb of seizing with a feminine-singular subject and an attached object 'them' — a completed act of being gripped or overtaken (as by a punishment or force).
1.grammar: A completed-action (past) verb prefixed with 'fa-' ('so/then'). The '-t' marks the subject as feminine singular ('she/it'). The attached '-hum(u)' is an object pronoun meaning 'them'; its vowel is lengthened to '-humu' to ease pronunciation before the next word.

2.meaning: The earthquake — a violent shaking or convulsion of the ground; a definite singular noun naming the quaking event itself.
2.grammar: A definite singular noun. The prefixed al- ('the') has its 'l' assimilated into the following 'r' (pronounced ar-rajfa). The unit ending -t (tā' marbūṭa) often marks a single instance of an action. The final -u marks the nominative case — typically the subject of a sentence.
2.root: ر-ج-ف (r-j-f) — to quake, shake violently, convulse

3.meaning: "And they came to be / and they became," from a verb that originally means "to enter upon the morning" and by extension "to end up in a certain state / to become." It describes a group transitioning into a new condition.
3.grammar: The "fa-" prefix means "so" or "and then," marking a result or sequence. The verb is in the completed (past) tense; the "-ū" ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ("they"). As one of the "sisters of kāna," this verb links a subject to a predicate state, hence "they became (something)."
3.root: ص-ب-ح (ṣ-b-ḥ) — morning / the coming of daybreak; by extension, to come to be in a state

4.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
4.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
4.root: — (particle)

5.meaning: Their home / dwelling — a dwelling-place or abode belonging to 'them'. Combines the noun 'home' with the possessor 'their'.
5.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The -i ending is genitive — here triggered because the word follows a preposition or links to another noun. The suffix -him means 'their' (referring to a group of males); its 'i' vowel is the form taken after a genitive -i.
5.root: د-و-ر (d-w-r) — to turn/encircle; hence 'dār', an enclosed dwelling or abode

6.meaning: Fallen prone / lying lifeless — describing people collapsed motionless on their knees and faces, crouched and still as in death. A plural descriptive form.
6.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' form) describing those in a state of crouching motionless. The -īna ending marks a masculine plural in the accusative/genitive — the form used for objects, or, as often here, for a descriptive 'state' word (telling how the subjects were: 'fallen prostrate').
6.root: ج-ث-م (j-th-m) — to crouch low and stay still; to lie collapsed/prone

1.meaning: So he turned away — he turned his back and went off, departing from something. A past-tense action of a single male, opening with 'so/then'.

parts.en: he (3rd-person masculine singular), on a weak-ending verb

1.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in the reflexive 't-' pattern (turning oneself away). From a root ending in a weak letter, its third-person masculine singular 'he' form ends in the long -ā (written as alif maqṣūra). It denotes a completed action. Prefixed fa means 'so' or 'then'.
1.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — to be near / turn toward; in this pattern, to turn away or take charge

2.meaning: From them; away from them; concerning them. The preposition ʿan conveys moving away from, departing from, or 'on behalf of / concerning', combined with the pronoun 'them'.
2.grammar: A preposition joined to the attached pronoun -hum, 'them' (referring to a group, grammatically masculine plural). The preposition ʿan basically signals separation or removal ('away from'), and can also mean 'about/concerning' or 'on behalf of' depending on usage.

3.meaning: 'And he said' — the act of speaking or stating, attributed to one masculine speaker, joined to what precedes by 'and.'
3.grammar: The connector 'wa-' ('and') with a past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he said.' The ending -a marks a completed action by one male, with the doer 'he' contained in the verb.

4.meaning: 'O my people!' — a vocative call: 'people' (one's own community/folk) addressed directly, with 'my' attached. A speaker uses it to summon and appeal to his own community.
4.grammar: The particle yā- is the vocative ('O …'), used to call or address someone. The final -i here is the remnant of the possessive 'my' (the fuller -ī), commonly shortened to -i in direct address, so the whole means 'O my people!' The case ending proper is suppressed because the noun is being called, not used as subject or object.
4.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to rise; a people who stand together

5.meaning: A two-part emphasis particle meaning 'surely, indeed (already)' — 'la-' strongly affirms, and 'qad' before a past verb stresses that the action has definitely occurred.
5.grammar: Two particles fused for emphasis. 'la-' is the affirming prefix 'surely / truly.' 'qad,' when it precedes a past-tense verb, confirms and intensifies that the action really happened ('has indeed …'). Together they give a strong oath-like assurance to the statement that follows.

6.meaning: I have conveyed to you / delivered to you — I passed on and made reach you (a group) some message in full. Combines the verb 'I delivered' with the object 'you all'.
6.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in the causative 'a-' pattern (to make something reach). The ending -tu marks a first-person singular subject ('I'). The attached -kum is the object pronoun 'you all', the ones reached. A completed action: 'I have conveyed to you'.
6.root: ب-ل-غ (b-l-gh) — to reach/arrive; in this pattern, to make reach, i.e. to convey or deliver

7.meaning: Message / commission — that which a messenger is charged to deliver; a communication or mandate entrusted for conveying. Closely tied to the idea of a prophetic message.
7.grammar: A singular noun. The unit ending -t (tā' marbūṭa) marks it as a single, discrete thing. The final -a marks the accusative case — typically the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon, e.g. delivered).
7.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; hence 'risāla', that which is sent, a message

8.meaning: 'My Lord' — the Master, Sustainer and Nurturer, claimed in close personal relation by the speaker.
8.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord') with the attached pronoun -ī meaning 'my'. This 'my' ending merges with the case-vowel of the noun, so a single long -ī is heard. The sense is 'the Lord who is mine'.
8.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord/master, to nurture and sustain

9.meaning: And I advised / counselled sincerely — and I gave heartfelt, well-meaning counsel, sincerely seeking the good of the one advised. A past-tense action of a single speaker.
9.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb denoting a completed action. The ending -tu marks a first-person singular subject ('I'). Prefixed wa means 'and'. The verb carries the sense of sincere, well-intentioned counsel.
9.root: ن-ص-ح (n-ṣ-ḥ) — to be sincere; to give genuine, well-meaning counsel

10.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
10.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

11.meaning: 'But / however / yet' — a particle of correction and contrast that sets aside what came before and affirms something different instead.
11.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to lākin ('but / however'). Lākin is a particle of rectification: it draws a contrast with, or corrects, the preceding idea and introduces an opposing or qualifying statement ('... but rather...').

12.meaning: 'Not' — a particle of negation. Depending on context it denies a present fact, forbids an action, or rules something out ('do not / there is no').
12.grammar: A negating particle, 'not / no'. It is used to deny or prohibit — negating present-tense statements, expressing 'there is no...', or, with a command form, forbidding an action ('do not...').

13.meaning: You (plural) love, are devoted to, or hold dear — an imperfect verb of affection addressed to a group. The underlying sense is loving, cherishing, and being drawn toward someone or something.
13.grammar: A present/future (imperfect) verb of Form IV (the standard verb 'to love', aḥabba / yuḥibbu, from a doubled root). The tu- prefix marks a second-person subject ('you'), and the -ūna ending marks masculine plural ('you all') in the indicative mood — the plain factual form for ongoing/future action. Dropping the final -na would signal subjunctive or jussive instead.

14.meaning: Those who give sincere counsel; well-wishing advisers who genuinely seek another's good. An active participle in the masculine sound plural denoting people characterized by honest, faithful advice.
14.grammar: A definite masculine sound plural of an active participle ('one who advises sincerely'). The -īna ending is the genitive/accusative plural ('more than two males'), used after a preposition or as an object; the nominative counterpart would be -ūna.
14.root: ن-ص-ح (n-ṣ-ḥ) — to give sincere, pure advice; faithful well-wishing

1.meaning: 'And Lot (Lūṭ)' — the proper name of the prophet, prefixed with 'and'.
1.grammar: A proper name prefixed with 'wa' ('and'). Unusually for a foreign name, it is treated as fully declinable here: the '-an' ending marks the accusative case (the direct object) together with nunation ('-n').

2.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
2.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

3.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
3.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

4.meaning: 'To/for his people' — a compound joining the preposition 'to/for', the noun 'people' (a community or folk, especially one's own kinfolk and nation), and 'his'. It expresses a community belonging to, or addressed by, a single male individual.
4.grammar: The preposition li- ('to/for') governs the noun, which therefore takes the genitive -i ending — the case that regularly follows a preposition or links one noun to another ('… of …'). The attached -hi means 'his'; the i-vowel form -hi (rather than -hu) is used because it harmonises with the preceding -i sound.
4.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to rise; a people who stand together

5.meaning: Do you commit / approach? — a question put to a group asking whether they do or come to (some act). Combines a yes/no question marker with the verb 'you (all) come to / commit'.
5.grammar: A present/imperfect verb fronted by the interrogative prefix a- ('is it that…?'), making it a yes/no question. The ta- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'); the -ūna ending also signals the indicative mood: 'do you (all) come to / commit?'
5.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come, arrive, approach; figuratively to do or perpetrate

6.meaning: 'The immorality' / 'the gross indecency' — a flagrant, shameful act; an enormity that exceeds the bounds of decency. With the article it denotes the gross indecent act.
6.grammar: A definite feminine singular noun. The -a ending is the accusative case, marking it as the object of a verb (the thing committed or done).

7.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
7.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

8.meaning: He/it preceded you / came before you — he went ahead of, or did something earlier than, 'you' (a group). Combines the verb 'he preceded' with the object 'you all'.
8.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb denoting a completed action. The verb's bare form (ending -a before the suffix) marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it'). The attached -kum is the object pronoun 'you all', the ones preceded.
8.root: س-ب-ق (s-b-q) — to precede, go before, outstrip

9.meaning: with it / by it — a preposition meaning 'with' or 'by means of' joined to a pronoun referring to a single feminine (or grammatically feminine) thing.
9.grammar: The bi- prefix is a preposition meaning 'with', 'by', or 'by means of'. The attached -hā is an object pronoun meaning 'it' or 'her', referring to something feminine in gender. Together they mean 'with it' or 'by means of it'.
9.root: — (preposition with pronoun)

10.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
10.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

11.meaning: One; anyone; a single individual. Often used in negative or conditional contexts to mean 'anyone (at all)'.
11.grammar: An indefinite noun in the genitive case. The -in ending combines the genitive marker -i (the form taken after a preposition or in a possessive link, '… of …') with nunation (-n), the sign of an indefinite 'a / any'.

12.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
12.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

13.meaning: The worlds, all created realms — the totality of beings and peoples; in 'Lord of the worlds,' the whole of creation across all its kinds.
13.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the worlds') with 'al-' ('the'). The '-īna' ending marks a masculine sound plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) form — the form used after a preposition, in an 'of' linkage, or as a direct object.
13.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; a 'world' as a sign by which the Creator is known

1.meaning: 'Indeed you (plural)' — the emphatic particle inna ('truly, indeed, surely'), which strongly affirms and stresses the statement that follows, fused with the attached pronoun 'you (all)'. Inna has no single English word; it functions to underline certainty.
1.grammar: Inna is an emphasising particle that introduces and strengthens a sentence; grammatically it places the following noun or pronoun in the accusative-like role of its 'subject'. The attached -kum is the masculine plural object/possessive pronoun 'you (all)'. Together: 'indeed you (all)…'.

2.meaning: You surely do approach / come to — emphatic assertion that 'you' (a group) indeed do or come to (some act). Combines an emphasis particle with the verb 'you (all) come to'.
2.grammar: A present/imperfect verb fronted by the emphatic prefix la- ('surely, indeed'), which stresses the truth of the statement. The ta- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'); the -ūna ending also signals the indicative mood: 'you all surely do come to'.
2.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come, arrive, approach; figuratively to do or perpetrate

3.meaning: The men — adult males; the plural of 'rajul' (man), made definite by 'the'.
3.grammar: A definite plural noun. The prefixed al- ('the') has its 'l' assimilated into the following 'r' (pronounced ar-rijāl). The final -a marks the accusative case — typically the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon).
3.root: ر-ج-ل (r-j-l) — man; manhood, the male of the species

4.meaning: An intense desire, craving, or appetite — a strong inclination of the self toward something it wants, often carrying the sense of passion or lust.
4.grammar: A singular feminine noun. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥa, carried on the tā' marbūṭa) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case — the case used for the direct object of a verb or, very often, to express manner ('out of …', 'as …'). So it reads 'a craving' or 'in passion/lust'.
4.root: ش-ه-و (sh-h-w) — to desire, crave, long for

5.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
5.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

6.meaning: A noun used to mean 'besides', 'other than', 'apart from', or 'short of'. It points to something or someone set apart from, or lower/lesser than, a named party. Often used in the phrase 'besides Allah'.
6.grammar: 'dūn' functions as an adverb-like noun of place/relation. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, which appears because it follows a preposition (such as 'min', 'from') and because it links to a following noun ('other than …'). It commonly heads the construction 'besides/other than [someone]'.
6.root: د-و-ن (d-w-n) — to be low/beneath, to fall short; hence 'below, other than, besides'

7.meaning: 'The women' — the plural used for women/females collectively. (It serves as the plural of mar'a, 'woman.')
7.grammar: A plural noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending is genitive: it marks the word as following a preposition or standing in a possessive ('of …') relationship. The l of al- assimilates into the following n in pronunciation (a 'sun letter').

8.meaning: A particle of retraction meaning 'rather,' 'no, but,' or 'nay' — it cancels or sets aside what was just said and shifts to a corrected or contrasting statement that follows.
8.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it never changes form). Its function is to redirect the discourse: it dismisses a prior idea and introduces what is actually the case.

9.meaning: You — the standalone pronoun for a group of people ('you all', masculine or mixed). It is used for emphasis or as the subject standing on its own.
9.grammar: A detached subject pronoun meaning 'you all' (second-person masculine/mixed plural). Unlike pronoun endings attached to verbs or nouns, this word stands alone — typically to emphasize the subject or to begin an equational sentence ('you [are]…'). Its form is fixed and does not change for case.

10.meaning: 'A people / folk / community' — a group of people bound together, often by kinship, tribe, or shared identity.
10.grammar: An indefinite collective noun ('a people'), grammatically singular but referring to a group. The -un ending is indefinite ('a') and nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence.
10.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a group that stands together

11.meaning: Those who go to excess — people who transgress proper limits, are wasteful or immoderate, and squander what should be restrained.
11.grammar: An active participle (one who does the action) of the verb that means 'to exceed all bounds'. The -ūna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the nominative case — the case used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate ('they are …'). So it denotes 'those who go to excess'.
11.root: س-ر-ف (s-r-f) — to exceed the limit, be wasteful or extravagant

1.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

2.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

2.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

3.meaning: An answer, a reply, a response given back to something said or asked.
3.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The final -a marks the accusative case, typically used for the direct object of a verb. If it heads a possessive (iḍāfa) construction, this same accusative ending stays on it ('the answer of …'), since only the following, possessed noun takes the genitive.

4.meaning: 'His people / his folk' — the community, tribe, or nation to which a person belongs, with the attached pronoun 'his'.
4.grammar: A noun with the attached pronoun '-hi' ('his'). The '-i' ending is genitive: it typically marks the word as the object of a preposition or as linked to a preceding noun ('… of …'). The pronoun appears as '-hi' (rather than '-hu') because of this genitive '-i'.
4.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to rise; a people who stand together

5.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
5.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.
5.root: — (particle)

6.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
6.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

7.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
7.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

8.meaning: A command addressed to a group: 'put them out!', 'expel them!', 'drive them out!' — to cause people to leave or exit from a place.
8.grammar: A command (imperative) verb in the causative form, meaning 'cause to go out'. The -ū ending directs the order to a plural masculine 'you' (all of you), and the attached -hum is the object 'them'. Altogether: '(you all) drive them out!'
8.root: خ-ر-ج (kh-r-j) — to go out, exit, depart

9.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
9.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

10.meaning: A settled place of dwelling — a town, village, or community where people live.
10.grammar: A singular feminine noun with the attached possessive pronoun -kum ('your', addressing several people). The -i ending before the pronoun marks the genitive case, typically used after a preposition or to link the noun to another in possession ('… of …'). So it reads 'your town'.
10.root: ق-ر-ي (q-r-y) — to gather, collect (whence a place where people gather)

11.meaning: 'Indeed they' — the emphatic particle 'inna' ('truly, indeed') joined to the pronoun 'them/they', strongly affirming a statement about a group.
11.grammar: The emphatic particle inna ('indeed / truly'), which strengthens and affirms a sentence, with the attached pronoun -hum ('they'). Inna places its attached noun or pronoun in the accusative, so -hum here functions as 'they' serving as the subject of the emphasized statement ('indeed they...').

12.meaning: Human beings, people, folk — humankind considered as a group of persons.
12.grammar: A plural noun referring to people (a quasi-plural with no singular of its own root pattern). The final -un (tanwīn ḍamma) marks it as indefinite and in the nominative case — used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate ('they are people …'). So it reads 'people' or '(some) folk'.
12.root: ا-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — to be sociable, familiar; humankind

13.meaning: They thoroughly cleanse and purify themselves — keep themselves clean and pure, both physically and morally, through deliberate effort.
13.grammar: A present-tense verb in the reflexive, intensive form (one purifies one's own self with effort). The ya- … -ūna frame marks a masculine plural 'they', and the present tense conveys ongoing or habitual action: 'they keep purifying themselves'.
13.root: ط-ه-ر (ṭ-h-r) — to be pure, clean, free of defilement

1.meaning: So We rescued him / delivered him to safety — 'We' brought a single masculine figure out of danger to safety, with a connector ('so/then') marking it as the outcome.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb in the causative pattern ('to bring to safety / cause to be saved') with the -nā ending marking 'we' as the doer. It is opened by fa- ('so/then'), linking it as a consequence. The attached -hu is the object 'him'.
1.root: ن-ج-و (n-j-w) — deliverance, escape, being brought to safety

2.meaning: And his household — his family and the people belonging to his home and close kin.
2.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') joined to a singular noun with the attached possessive pronoun -hu ('his'). The -a ending marks the accusative case, used for the direct object of a verb or what is joined to one. So it reads 'and his family'.
2.root: ا-ه-ل (ʾ-h-l) — to be settled, belong; family, kin, people of a place

3.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
3.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

4.meaning: A woman, specifically a wife — a man's spouse.
4.grammar: A singular feminine noun with the attached possessive pronoun -hu ('his'), giving 'his wife'. The -a ending marks the accusative case, used for the direct object of a verb or what is grammatically joined to it.
4.root: م-ر-ء (m-r-ʾ) — relating to a person; the feminine denotes 'woman'

5.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'she was / it was / it became' — from the core verb of being, linking a subject to a description or state, often setting it in past or established time.
5.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb of being. The ending -at marks a third-person feminine-singular subject, 'she' or 'it (feminine)', so it reads 'she/it was'. As a being-verb it normally introduces a description of that subject.
5.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

6.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
6.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

7.meaning: Those who remain behind and stay put — people who linger, are left behind, and so perish with a place rather than leaving it; literally 'those who tarry / pass away'.
7.grammar: An active participle (one who does the action) with the definite article al- ('the'). The -īna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive (oblique) case — used for an object or after a preposition. So it reads 'the ones who stayed behind'.
7.root: غ-ب-ر (gh-b-r) — to remain, stay behind, linger; also dust

1.meaning: And We rained down — We caused rain (or something falling like rain) to pour upon a target, often as a sending-down of punishment.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb in the causative form ('to make rain fall'), joined by wa- ('and'). The attached -nā marks the doer as 'we'. So it reads 'and We rained down / We sent down (rain) upon'.

2.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
2.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
2.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

3.meaning: Rain — water falling from the sky; by extension, a downpour of something sent down.
3.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥa) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case — here the kind used for the direct object of a verb. So it reads 'a rain' or '(a) downpour'.

4.meaning: So look! / then observe! — a command to one person to look at, consider, and reflect upon something.
4.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a single 'you', prefixed by fa- ('so/then'), which links it as a consequence of what precedes. The verb urges one to look and reflect: 'so look!' / 'then consider!'
4.root: ن-ظ-ر (n-ẓ-r) — to look, see, observe, consider

5.meaning: An interrogative meaning 'how?' — asking about the manner, condition, or state of something ('how?', 'in what way?'). It can also express astonishment.
5.grammar: An interrogative particle (kayfa) ending in an invariable -a; it does not change for case. It asks about the manner or state of an action ('how…?') and is sometimes used rhetorically to express wonder or rebuke rather than a genuine question.
5.root: — (interrogative particle; no triliteral root)

6.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

6.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

7.meaning: The outcome, end-result, or final consequence — what a matter or a course of conduct ultimately comes to. It names the end that follows from a beginning.
7.grammar: A feminine noun. The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or, without nunation as here, the first term of a possessive phrase ('the outcome of …'). It denotes that which comes at the heel — the consequence that follows on.
7.root: ع-ق-ب (ʿ-q-b) — to follow, come after (at the heel); an end, consequence

8.meaning: 'The criminals / evildoers' — those who commit crimes and sins, the guilty who cut themselves off through wrongdoing.
8.grammar: The al- prefix is the definite article 'the'. The stem mujrim is an active participle ('one who commits crime/sin'). The ending -īna is the masculine plural marker used when the noun is in the genitive or accusative case, giving 'the criminals'.
8.root: ج-ر-م (j-r-m) — committing a crime or sin, guilt

1.meaning: "and to / toward" — the connective "and" joined to the preposition meaning "to, toward, up to (an end-point)."
1.grammar: A particle cluster: the connective wa- ("and") plus the preposition ilā ("to/toward"), which indicates direction or destination and puts the following noun into the genitive case. Particles do not inflect.

2.meaning: Madyan (Midian) — the proper name of an ancient people and the land they inhabited.
2.grammar: A proper name. As a diptote (not fully declinable) noun, it takes a single -a ending in place of both accusative and genitive and does not receive tanwīn. It names a people and their territory.

3.meaning: "their brother" — the noun "brother" (a male sibling, or by extension a kinsman/fellow member of a community) with the possessor "their."
3.grammar: "Brother" is one of the special "five nouns" whose case is shown by a long vowel: the -ā here marks the accusative (object) state. The suffix -hum means "their," referring to a group of males.

4.meaning: Shuʿayb — the proper name of a prophet sent to the people of Madyan.
4.grammar: A proper name (the diminutive form of a name) that is fully declinable (triptote). The -an ending marks the accusative case — fitting when the name is the one being sent or mentioned as object. The tanwīn here signals that the name belongs to the fully declinable class, not indefiniteness, since a proper name is inherently definite.

5.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
5.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.
5.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, uttering

6.meaning: 'O my people!' — a vocative call: 'people' (one's own community/folk) addressed directly, with 'my' attached. A speaker uses it to summon and appeal to his own community.
6.grammar: The particle yā- is the vocative ('O …'), used to call or address someone. The final -i here is the remnant of the possessive 'my' (the fuller -ī), commonly shortened to -i in direct address, so the whole means 'O my people!' The case ending proper is suppressed because the noun is being called, not used as subject or object.
6.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to rise; a people who stand together

7.meaning: 'Serve!,' 'worship!,' 'devote yourselves in obedience!' — a command to render worship and humble service. The underlying sense is to submit oneself wholly, in reverence and obedience, to the one served.
7.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a group. The '-ū' ending means the order is given to several people: 'you all do it!' The initial vowel is a helping prosthetic vowel that lets the word begin, since the bare command stem would otherwise start with a vowelless letter.
7.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to worship, to serve, devotion

8.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
8.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

9.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
9.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

10.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
10.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

11.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
11.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

12.meaning: 'A god / a deity' — any object of worship; the general word for a deity (as opposed to the proper name Allah).
12.grammar: A singular indefinite noun 'a god'. The -in ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a/any') and in the genitive case — the form used after a preposition or in an 'of' relationship. It denotes a deity in general.
12.root: ا-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, that which is worshipped

13.meaning: Other than him, someone or something besides him — denoting difference or exception from a masculine referent.
13.grammar: A noun of exception meaning 'other than', carrying the -u (nominative) ending, which typically marks the subject of a sentence. The attached -hu is a genitive pronoun ('him/it') in a possessive-style link, so the whole word reads 'other than him'.

14.meaning: A short particle placed before a verb to emphasize or affirm it. Before a past-tense verb it means 'indeed / certainly / has already (happened)'; before a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes / may'. It sharpens and confirms the verb that follows.
14.grammar: An indeclinable particle (its form never changes). It does not take case or tense endings; its job is to color the following verb — affirming and intensifying a past action ('has indeed done') or signaling occasional possibility with a present verb.

15.meaning: 'She/it has come to you (plural)' — a completed act of coming/arriving, with a feminine subject reaching a plural 'you.'
15.grammar: Past-tense verb 'to come.' The '-at' suffix marks a third-person feminine singular subject, 'she/it came.' The attached '-kum' is the object 'you all' (masculine plural). Together: 'she/it has come to you.'
15.root: ج-ي-أ (j-y-ʾ) — to come, arrive

16.meaning: A clear proof, a plain piece of evidence, something self-evidently manifest that makes the truth obvious. As a noun it denotes a clarifying sign or demonstration that removes doubt.
16.grammar: A feminine singular noun. The final -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a clear proof') and in the nominative case, the form used for the subject of a sentence. The feminine -a(t) ending is built into the word.
16.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — clarity, distinctness, making plain

17.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
17.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

18.meaning: 'Your Lord' (addressing a group). 'Rabb' is a rich term: the Master, Owner, Sustainer and Nurturer who creates, possesses, provides for, and brings a thing to its proper completion — far more than a mere ruler.
18.grammar: A noun ('Lord') with an attached possessive pronoun, forming a possessive pairing. 'Rabb' carries a doubled (geminated) 'b' — the shaddah — at its core. The '-i' vowel on 'rabb' is its case ending, determined by 'Lord's' own role in the sentence (not by the suffix); the attached '-kum' is the possessor ('your'), addressing a plural 'you', and as the possessed-to term it sits in the genitive.

19.meaning: So give in full and fulfil — a command to a group to render measures, weights, or pledges completely, leaving nothing short.
19.grammar: A command (imperative) verb in the causative form ('to make complete, give fully'), prefixed by fa- ('so/then'). The -ū ending directs the order to a masculine plural 'you'. So it reads '(you all) give full measure!'
19.root: و-ف-ي (w-f-y) — to fulfil, complete, give in full, keep faith

20.meaning: 'The measure' — the act or standard of measuring out a quantity (especially of grain or goods), and the measuring-vessel itself.
20.grammar: A definite masculine singular noun in the accusative case, shown by the -a ending; the accusative typically marks the direct object of a verb (e.g. 'give full measure').
20.root: ك-ي-ل (k-y-l) — to measure out (by volume), a measure

21.meaning: 'And the balance / the scales' — the instrument for weighing, and by extension the principle of just weight and equilibrium.
21.grammar: The conjunction wa- ('and') plus a definite masculine singular noun in the accusative case, shown by the -a ending; the accusative typically marks the direct object of a verb. The mīzān pattern (mifʿāl) denotes an instrument — here a thing used for weighing.

22.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
22.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

23.meaning: To diminish or shortchange — to give people less than their due, to defraud or deprive them of part of what is theirs.
23.grammar: A present-tense verb addressed to a masculine plural 'you' (the ta- … -ū frame). With its short final -ū (no nūn), it stands in the form used after a negative or prohibitive word, so it carries the sense 'do not shortchange / that you not diminish'.
23.root: ب-خ-س (b-kh-s) — to diminish, give short measure, defraud

24.meaning: Mankind, humanity, people in general — the collective of human beings.
24.grammar: A definite noun ('the people') with the attached 'al-' ('the'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (a sun letter), which is why the 'n' is doubled — this is a pronunciation effect, not a separate piece. The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the one being acted upon) or the subject of certain particles.
24.root: ن-و-س (n-w-s) — to move/sway; by extension, people

25.meaning: Their things — the items, goods, or belongings that pertain to them; the plural of 'thing'.
25.grammar: A plural noun with the attached possessive pronoun -hum ('their'). The -a ending marks the accusative case (used for the direct object of a verb); this plural pattern is a diptote and does not take tanwīn. So it reads 'their things / their goods'.
25.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — thing, to will; the basic notion of 'a thing'

26.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
26.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

27.meaning: '(That) you cause corruption / spread mischief' — to ruin, disorder, or work harm, the opposite of putting things right. Built on a causative pattern: to actively bring about corruption.
27.grammar: A present/imperfect verb on the causative (Form IV) pattern, meaning to bring corruption about. The tu-...-ū combination marks a second-person masculine plural subject, 'you (all)'. The ending is -ū rather than -ūna, showing a non-indicative mood (subjunctive or jussive) — the form used after certain particles such as those of negation, prohibition, or purpose.
27.root: ف-س-د (f-s-d) — corruption, spoiling, disorder

28.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
28.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

29.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
29.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

30.meaning: After; following in time or order — the point or moment subsequent to something.
30.grammar: An adverb of time functioning much like a preposition ('after'). It is fixed in the accusative form ending in -a, and is normally followed by a noun in the 'of' relationship, giving 'after (the) …'.
30.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — afterness, that which comes later; distance/remoteness

31.meaning: Its setting-right; the act of reforming, repairing, mending, or putting it into a good and sound condition. A verbal noun denoting the work of making something wholesome and properly ordered.
31.grammar: A verbal noun (the action of "reforming") with an attached possessive "its/her." The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun or preposition ("… of …") or follows a preposition.
31.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound, right, good; to set in order, reform

32.meaning: A demonstrative meaning 'that' addressed to a group of people (plural 'you'). It points to something at a distance — whether physical, or to a previously mentioned matter — and is directed at multiple listeners.
32.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun for something distant. The base 'dhā' carries the sense 'that', the 'li' is an element of distance, and the ending '-kum' tells you the speaker is addressing a plural 'you' — it specifies the audience, not the thing pointed at. It does not change for case.

33.meaning: 'Better / best; good' — an adjective of comparison meaning more good, preferable, or superior. It also serves broadly for 'goodness' and that which is good and beneficial.
33.grammar: A noun/adjective bearing the ending -un (nunation): the doubled-u 'n' sound marks the word as both indefinite ('a/an', no 'the') and nominative — the case used for the subject of a sentence or the predicate that describes it.
33.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — good, goodness, that which is choice and beneficial

34.meaning: 'for you,' 'to you,' 'for your benefit' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to 'you (plural).' It marks the party for whose sake, benefit, or possession something exists or is given.
34.grammar: A preposition ('for/to') with the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you, plural'). It assigns a benefit, purpose, or recipient — 'for you (all).' The suffix '-kum' is the plural 'you,' showing the recipients are a group.

35.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
35.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

36.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
36.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
36.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

37.meaning: 'Believers / faithful ones' — the plural of muʾmin, one who has faith and trust in Allah and grants assent to the truth.

parts.en: believers (form IV participle, oblique masculine sound plural)

37.grammar: An active participle ('one who believes') from the form IV pattern, here a masculine sound plural. The single suffix -īna is the oblique (accusative/genitive) form of the masculine plural — used for a direct object or after a preposition — as opposed to the -ūna form used for the subject. Its nūn is part of the one ending and is not a separable morpheme.
37.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — security, trust; hence faith and belief

1.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
1.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

2.meaning: You sit, stay seated, or remain (not rising or going forward) — also figuratively to hold back and keep company in a setting.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb addressed to a plural 'you' ('you sit/remain'). The ta- prefix marks second person and the -ū ending marks masculine plural. The final -na has been dropped (subjunctive/jussive), so it typically follows 'until', 'that', a negation, or 'if'.
2.root: ق-ع-د (q-ʿ-d) — to sit, stay put, remain behind

3.meaning: 'Of every / with all' — the preposition 'bi' ('with / in / by') joined to the word 'every / each / all', expressing comprehensiveness applied to whatever noun follows.
3.grammar: A preposition plus a noun. The prefix bi- ('with / in / by') always places the following noun in the genitive ('of') state. The final -i on 'kull' is that genitive ending, signalling the word is governed by the preposition. 'Kull' denotes totality — 'every (single)' or 'all'.

4.meaning: 'A path / road / way'. It denotes a clear, open road that one travels — often used figuratively for a course of life or conduct.
4.grammar: The '-in' ending (tanwīn) marks the word as indefinite ('a path / some way') and in the genitive case. The genitive typically follows a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').
