4.root: ص-ر-ط (ṣ-r-ṭ) — a road, way, path

5.meaning: You (plural) threaten — you menace or warn people of harm, lying in wait to intimidate them.
5.grammar: A present-tense verb addressed to a masculine plural 'you' (the tu- … -ūna frame). The full -ūna ending (with the nūn) marks the ordinary present indicative — a real, ongoing action: 'you threaten / you keep menacing'.
5.root: و-ع-د (w-ʿ-d) — to promise; in this form, to threaten or warn of harm

6.meaning: And you turn (others) away — you bar, block, or divert people, hindering them from a path or course.
6.grammar: A present-tense verb addressed to a masculine plural 'you' (the ta- … -ūna frame), joined by wa- ('and'). The full -ūna ending marks the ordinary present indicative — a real, ongoing action: 'and you hinder / turn away'.
6.root: ص-د-د (ṣ-d-d) — to turn away, avert, hinder, obstruct

7.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on behalf of,' 'for,' 'about,' or 'away from.' It often conveys removing a burden from someone or acting in their place.

parts.en: on behalf of / for / away from

7.grammar: A preposition (a linking particle). It governs the noun that follows it, putting that noun into the genitive case. It does not change form.

8.meaning: 'path, way, road' — a route or course; figuratively a cause or way of life one travels along. In construct ('the way OF ...').
8.grammar: A singular noun with the '-i' (genitive) ending, which typically links it to a following noun ('the way OF ...') or follows a preposition. It marks the word as connected to or possessed by what comes after.

9.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
9.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

10.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
10.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

11.meaning: 'He believed' — he had faith, trusted, and affirmed. The basic past-tense form of the verb meaning to believe and to find security in faith.
11.grammar: A past-tense verb on the causative (Form IV) pattern, from the root for security and faith. The -a ending marks a third-person masculine singular subject, 'he (believed)', stating a completed act of coming to faith.

12.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
12.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

13.meaning: And you seek to make it (crooked) — you try to render something, desiring and pursuing a particular outcome for it.
13.grammar: A present-tense verb addressed to a masculine plural 'you' (the ta- … -ūna frame), joined by wa- ('and'), with the attached object -hā ('it', referring to something feminine). The full -ūna present indicative marks a real, ongoing action: 'and you seek it'.
13.root: ب-غ-ي (b-gh-y) — to seek, desire, strive after; to overstep bounds

14.meaning: Crookedness, deviation, distortion — a bend or twist away from straightness; figuratively a moral or spiritual deviation from the right path.
14.grammar: A noun. The '-an' ending is accusative and indefinite: the accusative often marks the direct object of a verb or a descriptive complement, and the final 'n' sound marks it indefinite ('crookedness'). The word names a deviation from what is straight.
14.root: ع-و-ج (ʿ-w-j) — to bend, be crooked, deviate

15.meaning: A command to a group meaning 'and remember / and call to mind / and mention.' The root spans both calling something to memory and uttering it aloud.
15.grammar: The connector 'wa' (and) plus a command (imperative) verb 'remember/mention.' The ending -ū addresses a masculine plural group ('you all remember!').
15.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, mention, call to mind

16.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
16.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

17.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
17.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
17.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

18.meaning: 'A little / a small amount' — an adjective/noun meaning small in quantity, few, scant, or trifling.
18.grammar: A noun/adjective 'little' in the accusative case with indefinite marking (the -an ending, tanwīn). The accusative commonly marks an object or specifies amount/manner; the doubled -n sound marks it as indefinite, 'a little.'
18.root: ق-ل-ل (q-l-l) — fewness; being little, scant, or small in amount

19.meaning: So He multiplied you / made you many — He greatly increased your number, causing you to grow numerous.
19.grammar: A past-tense verb in the intensive form ('to make many, multiply'), prefixed by fa- ('so/then'). With no separate subject suffix it carries a 'he' subject, and the attached -kum is the object 'you (all)'. So it reads 'so He multiplied you'.
19.root: ك-ث-ر (k-th-r) — to be much, many, abundant

20.meaning: And look! / and observe! — a command to a group to look at, consider, and reflect upon something.
20.grammar: A command (imperative) verb joined by wa- ('and'). The -ū ending directs the order to a masculine plural 'you', urging them to look and reflect: 'and (you all) look!' / 'and consider!'
20.root: ن-ظ-ر (n-ẓ-r) — to look, see, observe, consider

21.meaning: An interrogative meaning 'how?' — asking about the manner, condition, or state of something ('how?', 'in what way?'). It can also express astonishment.
21.grammar: An interrogative particle (kayfa) ending in an invariable -a; it does not change for case. It asks about the manner or state of an action ('how…?') and is sometimes used rhetorically to express wonder or rebuke rather than a genuine question.

22.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

22.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

23.meaning: The outcome, end-result, or final consequence — what a matter or a course of conduct ultimately comes to. It names the end that follows from a beginning.
23.grammar: A feminine noun. The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or, without nunation as here, the first term of a possessive phrase ('the outcome of …'). It denotes that which comes at the heel — the consequence that follows on.
23.root: ع-ق-ب (ʿ-q-b) — to follow, come after (at the heel); an end, consequence

24.meaning: Those who spread corruption / the workers of mischief — people who ruin, disorder, and lay waste, the opposite of those who set things right.
24.grammar: Prefix 'al-' = 'the.' An active participle (the one who corrupts) from the causative form (afʿala). The '-īna' ending is the masculine sound plural in the accusative/genitive (oblique) case — the form used for the object of a verb or after a preposition.
24.root: ف-س-د (f-s-d) — to be corrupt, spoil, cause ruin/disorder

1.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
1.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

2.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

2.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

3.meaning: Indefinite noun meaning 'a group,' 'a party,' 'a band,' or 'a portion' of people — a section or company of a larger body.
3.grammar: A feminine singular noun. The final '-tun' (feminine ending with tanwīn ḍamma) marks it indefinite ('a group') and in the nominative case — the case used for the subject of a sentence or a stand-alone predicate.
3.root: ط-و-ف (ṭ-w-f) — to go around, circle; a band or group (that moves about)

4.meaning: 'From you / among you (plural)' — indicating a part taken out of, or belonging to, a group of people being addressed.
4.grammar: The preposition min ('from, of, among') joined to the attached pronoun -kum ('you all,' masculine plural). Together they express partition or origin: a part drawn 'from / among' the addressed group.
4.root: — (preposition with pronoun; no root)

5.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
5.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.
5.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, security, trust, faith

6.meaning: A combination meaning 'with/for the one that' or 'in exchange for that which'. It fuses the preposition bi- (with, by, in exchange for) onto the masculine singular relative pronoun alladhī ('the one who/that'), introducing a clause that further identifies the referred-to thing.

parts.en: the one who/that (masc. sing. relative pronoun)

6.grammar: bi- is a preposition that always governs a genitive; alladhī is an indeclinable masculine singular relative pronoun whose form does not change for case. It points to a single masculine entity and requires a following clause to complete its sense ('the one that …').

7.meaning: I have been sent — I was dispatched or commissioned (as a messenger) by someone with a message or task.
7.grammar: A past-tense verb in the passive voice of the causative form ('to be made to go, to be sent'). The attached -tu marks the subject as 'I'. Being passive, the doer is unstated, and the focus is on the one sent: 'I have been sent'.

8.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
8.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

9.meaning: And a group / while a group — the noun for a party or band of people, here joined by an opening connective "and" (which can also carry a "while/whereas" sense linking parallel clauses).
9.grammar: Prefix wa- ("and," or contrastively "while/whereas") plus an indefinite feminine noun. The -un (tanwīn) ending is nominative, which typically marks the noun as the subject of a sentence or as the starting topic. The base noun ends in the feminine tā' marbūṭa (the -t of ṭāifat), sounded before the case-vowel.
9.root: ط-و-ف (ṭ-w-f) — to go around, circle; a ṭāʾifa is a group that 'goes about' together, a faction or party

10.meaning: The particle 'lam', a negating word used to push a verb into the past: it means 'did not' / 'has not'. Though it sits before a present-tense verb form, it negates the action as something that did not happen.
10.grammar: 'lam' is a negating particle that governs a following present-tense verb but gives it past meaning ('did not …'). It also puts that verb into the shortened (jussive) form. 'lam' itself carries no ending.

11.meaning: 'They (masculine) believe' — to have faith in Allah; a present-tense verb with a masculine-plural subject.
11.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb, 3rd-person masculine plural ('they believe'). The yu- prefix with the -ū ending marks 'they (men) do'. The dropped final nūn (yu'minū, not yu'minūna) shows the jussive/subjunctive mood — used after conditional or negative-command particles. From form IV, 'to believe'.
11.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, trust; form IV: to believe, have faith

12.meaning: An imperative addressed to a group: 'be patient, endure steadfastly, hold firm.' The root denotes restraining the self in the face of hardship, persevering without complaint. The opening particle attaches a sense of 'so' or 'then,' linking the command to something that precedes it.
12.grammar: A command verb addressed to a plural masculine 'you.' The -ū ending marks the plural addressee ('all of you, do this'). The prefixed fa- is a connective particle meaning roughly 'so' or 'then,' tying the directive to a preceding statement or condition.

13.meaning: 'Until / up to the point that; so that' — a particle marking a limit or goal. It expresses the end-point reached ('until') or the purpose aimed at ('so that, in order that').
13.grammar: A particle indicating a goal or limit. When followed by a present-tense verb it places that verb in the subjunctive mood (clipping its ending to -a), conveying 'until / so that' something comes about. Ḥattā itself is invariable.

14.meaning: '(That) he judges, decides, rules, or gives a verdict.' The root concerns delivering a binding judgment, settling a matter authoritatively, and the wisdom that underlies sound rule.
14.grammar: A present-tense verb with the ya- prefix marking a third-person masculine 'he.' The final -a vowel is the subjunctive ending, which typically appears after particles meaning 'that' or 'so that,' giving the sense 'that he may judge.'
14.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, rule, decide with wisdom

15.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
15.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
15.root: — (proper divine name)

16.meaning: 'Between us' — the spatial or relational word for 'between/among', with 'us' attached: the space, relation, or matter standing between ourselves.
16.grammar: An adverb of place 'between', fixed in the -a form, with the attached pronoun -na ('us'). Together they mean 'between us / among us', marking a relation linking two or more parties.
16.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

17.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
17.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

18.meaning: 'Best / the best (of)' — superior to all others in goodness, excellence, or worth; the finest in its class.
18.grammar: khayr functions as a comparative/superlative noun ('better / best'). The -u ending marks the nominative case, which typically signals the subject or predicate of a sentence and also opens a possessive phrase ('the best OF …').
18.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — goodness, that which is good or best

19.meaning: 'The judges, the ones who decide' — those who pass verdicts and settle matters authoritatively. As an active participle it names the doers of judging.
19.grammar: A definite plural active participle ('the judges'). The -īna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive state, the form used when the noun is an object or follows a preposition or a possessive construction ('of the judges').
19.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, rule, decide with wisdom

1.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
1.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

2.meaning: The chiefs, leading men, or notables — the prominent council of a people; a collective term for the elite whose standing fills the eyes.
2.grammar: A definite noun (the al- prefix means 'the') with the -u (nominative) ending, the case that typically marks the subject of a sentence — the ones doing or being something. Though singular in form, it refers collectively to the leading body of a people.

3.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
3.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

4.meaning: They were arrogant / haughty — they acted with pride, deeming themselves great and looking down on others, refusing to submit. A past-tense action of a group.
4.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in the derived 'ista-' pattern, which here conveys deeming oneself great or behaving as though great. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). Being perfect, it denotes a completed action.
4.root: ك-ب-ر (k-b-r) — to be great/big; in this pattern, to consider oneself great, i.e. arrogance

5.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
5.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
5.root: — (preposition)

6.meaning: 'His people / his folk' — the community, tribe, or nation to which a person belongs, with the attached pronoun 'his'.
6.grammar: A noun with the attached pronoun '-hi' ('his'). The '-i' ending is genitive: it typically marks the word as the object of a preposition or as linked to a preceding noun ('… of …'). The pronoun appears as '-hi' (rather than '-hu') because of this genitive '-i'.
6.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to rise; a people who stand together

7.meaning: An emphatic threat or vow: 'We will most certainly drive you out / expel you.' The root means to make something come out, to bring forth or expel. Doubled emphasis and a 'we' subject combine with a singular 'you' object.
7.grammar: A present/future verb in a causative pattern ('to make come out, expel'), with the nu- prefix marking a 'we' subject. It is wrapped in double emphasis: the prefixed la- ('surely') and the suffixed -nna (the emphatic ending that turns a statement into a solemn promise or threat). The final -ka is an attached object pronoun, 'you' (a single male).
7.root: خ-ر-ج (kh-r-j) — to go out, come forth; (causative) to expel, bring out

8.meaning: A vocative call addressed to a man named Shuʿayb: 'O Shuʿayb!' The opening particle is the standard Arabic 'O…' used to call or address someone.
8.grammar: A direct address: the particle yā ('O') calls the named person. The name carries a final -u, the vowel typically taken by a singular proper name being called in the vocative.

9.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
9.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.
9.root: — (relative pronoun)

10.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
10.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

11.meaning: 'With you' — alongside or in the company of a single addressed person; expresses togetherness, accompaniment, or being in someone's presence.
11.grammar: An adverb of accompaniment ('with/together with') governing the attached pronoun -ka, 'you (masculine singular)'. The pronoun is in the genitive (the case taken after such words), and maʿa carries a fixed -a ending.
11.root: — (no triliteral root; an adverb of accompaniment)

12.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
12.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

13.meaning: 'Our town / settlement / village' — an inhabited place, a community's dwelling-place, joined to a 'we/our' possessor. The root refers to gathering and to a populated locality.
13.grammar: A feminine noun, 'town' (base form qarya, ending in ta marbuta). When a possessor is attached, the ta marbuta surfaces as a pronounced -t- and takes a linking -i; this -i is the construct (iḍāfa) realization of that feminine ending, not a separate case morpheme. The attached -nā means 'our,' giving 'our town.'
13.root: ق-ر-ي (q-r-y) — to gather; a gathering-place, settled town

14.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
14.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

15.meaning: An emphatic statement or oath-bound assertion addressed to one man: 'you shall surely return / go back.' The root means to return, to come back, or to revert to a former state or practice.
15.grammar: A present/future verb with the ta- prefix marking the addressee 'you.' With no plural marker (no wāw) before the ending, the form is second-person masculine singular — a single man. It carries double emphasis: the prefixed la- ('surely') and the heavy emphatic ending -nna, making it a solemn, almost oath-like assertion ('you absolutely will return').
15.root: ع-و-د (ʿ-w-d) — to return, come back, revert

16.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
16.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
16.root: — (particle)

17.meaning: 'Our way / creed / religious path,' joined to a 'we/our' possessor. The base word denotes a defined body of belief and practice — a religious community's followed way.
17.grammar: A feminine noun, 'creed' or 'religious way' (base form milla, ending in ta marbuta). With a possessor attached, the ta marbuta surfaces as a pronounced -t- and takes a linking -i — the construct (iḍāfa) realization of the feminine ending, not a separate case morpheme — followed by -nā ('our'): 'our creed / our way.'
17.root: م-ل-ل (m-l-l) — a followed creed or religious community

18.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
18.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

19.meaning: A clustered opener used to challenge or press a point: roughly 'even if…?' / 'what, even though…?' It joins a questioning hamza ('really?'), the connector 'wa' (and), and 'law' (if/though), introducing a hypothetical that is being questioned or objected to.
19.grammar: A combination of particles: the question-marker a- (turning the phrase into a rhetorical challenge), the conjunction wa- ('and/even'), and the conditional law ('if/though'), which introduces a hypothetical condition. Being particles, none of them take case endings.

20.meaning: 'We were' — the past tense of the verb 'to be,' establishing a past state or condition for a group including the speaker. It is the basic verb of existence and of 'being something.'
20.grammar: The past tense of 'to be' in the first-person plural ('we were'). The subject suffix is -nā ('we'); its nūn is written with a shadda (نَّ) because it merges with the final nūn of the verb stem kun-, and the alif spells the long -ā. A hollow verb, its middle weak letter drops in this form. It sets up a past state, and what follows describes how 'we' were.
20.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to come into being, existence

21.meaning: 'Ones who are unwilling, who dislike or detest (something),' resisting it inwardly. As an active participle it names those in a state of aversion or reluctance.
21.grammar: A sound masculine plural active participle ('the averse ones'). The -īna ending marks the accusative/genitive plural — the case used for an object or after a preposition, and the form often used to describe the state of a group.
21.root: ك-ر-ه (k-r-h) — to dislike, find hateful, be averse

1.meaning: A particle meaning 'indeed' or 'certainly' when placed before a past-tense verb — it affirms and emphasizes that the action has truly and definitely taken place.
1.grammar: An emphatic particle. Before a past-tense verb it stresses that the act is completed and verified ('has indeed done'). The final -i is not a case ending but a connecting vowel added to prevent two unvowelled consonants from meeting when the next word begins with a cluster.

2.meaning: 'We have invented / fabricated / forged (a falsehood).' The root means to fabricate, to concoct a lie, to invent something falsely and attribute it where it does not belong. The subject is 'we.'
2.grammar: A past-tense verb in a reflexive/intensive pattern ('to fabricate, forge'). The suffix -nā marks the subject 'we' who performed the act ('we fabricated').
2.root: ف-ر-ي (f-r-y) — to fabricate, forge, invent a lie

3.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
3.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
3.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

4.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
4.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

5.meaning: A noun meaning 'a lie / falsehood' — a deliberately false statement, an untruth fabricated against the truth.
5.grammar: An indefinite noun ('a lie') with the accusative -an ending (tanwīn). The accusative commonly marks the object of a verb (e.g. fabricating a lie); the -an tanwīn shows it is indefinite.
5.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie, to declare false

6.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
6.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

7.meaning: 'We returned, went back, reverted.' The root means to come back, to return to a place or to a former state, way, or practice. The subject is 'we.'
7.grammar: A past-tense verb (a hollow root whose middle weak letter contracts in this form). The suffix -nā marks the subject 'we' ('we returned / went back').
7.root: ع-و-د (ʿ-w-d) — to return, come back, revert

8.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
8.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

9.meaning: 'Your way / creed / religious path,' addressed to a group. The base word denotes a defined body of belief and practice — a community's followed religious way.
9.grammar: A feminine noun, 'creed' (base form milla, ending in ta marbuta). With a possessor attached, the ta marbuta surfaces as a pronounced -t- and takes a linking -i — the construct (iḍāfa) realization of the feminine ending, not a separate case morpheme — followed by -kum ('your,' addressing several people): 'your creed / your way.'
9.root: م-ل-ل (m-l-l) — a followed creed or religious community

10.meaning: After; following in time or order — the point or moment subsequent to something.
10.grammar: An adverb of time functioning much like a preposition ('after'). It is fixed in the accusative form ending in -a, and is normally followed by a noun in the 'of' relationship, giving 'after (the) …'.
10.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — afterness, that which comes later; distance/remoteness

11.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
11.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

12.meaning: 'He delivered / rescued / saved us.' The root means to bring to safety, to deliver from danger or harm. In this intensive pattern it stresses a thorough rescue. The object is 'us.'
12.grammar: A past-tense verb in the intensive (doubled-middle) pattern, conveying 'to rescue thoroughly,' with a third-person masculine 'he' as the implied subject. The attached -nā here is the object, 'us' — 'he saved us.'
12.root: ن-ج-و (n-j-w) — to be safe, escape; (causative) to rescue, deliver

13.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
13.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

14.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'min' ('from / out of / some of') joined to the pronoun 'it' (feminine). Together: 'from it / out of it / of it,' indicating a source or a portion taken from a feminine thing.
14.grammar: A preposition 'min' with the attached pronoun '-hā' ('it/her'), referring to a feminine noun. 'Min' indicates origin, source, or a part taken from a whole; the attached pronoun is in the object form required after a preposition.

15.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
15.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
15.root: — (relative pronoun / particle)

16.meaning: 'It is / it comes to be' — the present-tense verb of being and becoming (from kāna). It expresses that something is the case, exists, or comes about.
16.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he/it is, becomes'. The ya- prefix means 'he/it', and the final -u is the indicative ending, marking a plain factual statement (as opposed to a command or a negated/subjunctive form).
16.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

17.meaning: A combination of the preposition 'for / to' with the pronoun 'us', meaning 'for us' or 'to us / on our behalf'.
17.grammar: A preposition ('for / to') joined to the attached pronoun 'us'. The pronoun -nā always means 'us / our' regardless of position. Together they express benefit or direction toward the speakers ('for us').

18.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
18.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

19.meaning: '(That) we return / go back / revert.' The root means to come back, to return to a place or to a former state, way, or practice. The subject is 'we.'
19.grammar: A present-tense verb meaning 'we return,' built on the na- ('we') prefix, in the subjunctive (final -a vowel, used after a 'that / so that' particle). The doubled nūn (shadda) is not the prefix alone: the preceding subjunctive particle 'an' ('that') loses its own nūn into the verb's na- prefix, and the two merge into one geminated nūn — so the cluster carries both 'that' and 'we' ('that we may return').
19.root: ع-و-د (ʿ-w-d) — to return, come back, revert

20.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
20.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

21.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
21.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

22.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
22.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

23.meaning: '(that) he wills / wishes' — to will, intend, or so desire that a thing comes about.
23.grammar: A present-tense verb, third person masculine singular ('he wills'). The final -a is the subjunctive ending, which typically appears after particles meaning 'that/so that/until,' giving the sense 'that he should will.'

24.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
24.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

25.meaning: 'Our Lord' — 'Rabb' (Lord, Master, Sustainer who creates, owns, nurtures and governs) joined to 'our'. A weighty term for Allah as the One who brings up and sustains all that exists.
25.grammar: A noun with the attached possessive pronoun '-nā' ('our'). The -u before the pronoun is the nominative case, used when the word is the subject or predicate of a sentence ('[He] is our Lord').
25.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master; lordship

26.meaning: '(it) extended / encompassed / was vast enough for' — to be wide, spacious, or ample; to take in or embrace something fully within one's capacity. It conveys all-embracing breadth.
26.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it encompassed'). The final -a marks the completed action of a single masculine subject ('he/it did encompass / extend over').
26.root: و-س-ع (w-s-ʿ) — to be wide, spacious, to encompass

27.meaning: 'Our Lord' — 'Rabb' (Lord, Master, Sustainer who creates, owns, nurtures and governs) joined to 'our'. A weighty term for Allah as the One who brings up and sustains all that exists.
27.grammar: A noun with the attached possessive pronoun '-nā' ('our'). The -u before the pronoun is the nominative case, used when the word is the subject or predicate of a sentence ('[He] is our Lord').
27.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master; lordship

28.meaning: All, every, the whole of — totality. When followed by a singular it means 'every (one)'; when followed by a definite plural or whole it means 'all of.'
28.grammar: A noun of totality, almost always joined to a following noun in the genitive ('every … / all of …'). The final -a is the accusative case, the form used when the word functions as an object of a verb.

29.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
29.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
29.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

30.meaning: Knowledge — that which is known; firm, certain awareness and understanding.
30.grammar: An abstract noun, 'knowledge.' The final -an is the accusative with indefinite 'nunation,' commonly marking the noun as a direct object, or as a specification ('in respect of knowledge').

31.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
31.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
31.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

32.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
32.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

33.meaning: 'We have placed our trust, relied wholly (upon someone).' The root means to entrust an affair, to depend on and commit oneself; this pattern expresses fully delegating one's reliance. The subject is 'we.'
33.grammar: A past-tense verb in a reflexive pattern ('to commit one's reliance, put one's trust'). The suffix -nā marks the subject 'we' ('we put our trust').
33.root: و-ك-ل (w-k-l) — to entrust, rely upon, commit an affair

34.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

parts.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

34.grammar: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
34.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

35.meaning: An imperative addressed to one person: 'judge / decide / open (a matter) with a verdict.' The root means to open; by extension it means to render a decisive judgment that settles a dispute, and to grant victory or relief.
35.grammar: A command verb addressed to a single 'you,' with no ending added beyond the bare command form. It calls for an act of deciding or opening — settling a matter with a definitive judgment.
35.root: ف-ت-ح (f-t-ḥ) — to open; to judge decisively, grant victory

36.meaning: 'Between us' — the spatial or relational word for 'between/among', with 'us' attached: the space, relation, or matter standing between ourselves.
36.grammar: An adverb of place 'between', fixed in the -a form, with the attached pronoun -na ('us'). Together they mean 'between us / among us', marking a relation linking two or more parties.
36.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

37.meaning: 'And between'. A connective word meaning 'and between / and amid', used to mark the space, relationship, or distinction lying among two or more parties.
37.grammar: The word bayna ('between') with 'and' in front. It is an adverb of place that always leads into what follows, so it ends in a fixed -a and is normally paired with a following noun or pronoun ('between … and …').

38.meaning: 'Our people / folk / community,' joined to a 'we/our' possessor. The base word denotes a people bound together — a nation, tribe, or community of kin and kind.
38.grammar: A masculine noun meaning 'people.' It takes a linking -i before the attached possessor (here the genitive case, since the word follows a preposition / sits in a possessive link), then -nā ('our'): 'our people.'
38.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a people who stand together

39.meaning: 'With the truth / by means of what is true and right.' Combines the preposition 'with/by' and 'the truth' — that which is real, established, correct, and rightfully due, as opposed to falsehood.
39.grammar: A noun governed by the attached preposition bi- ('with/by'). The -i ending is the genitive case, which is required after a preposition; here it links 'the truth' to 'with', giving 'with the truth'.
39.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, reality, that which is established and due

40.meaning: 'And You' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'you' (addressing a single male). The independent pronoun stresses the subject, as in 'and You [Yourself] …'.
40.grammar: A connective 'and' plus a detached subject pronoun. 'anta' is the masculine-singular 'you'; as a standalone pronoun it adds emphasis or introduces a statement about the addressee ('You are …').

41.meaning: 'Best / the best (of)' — superior to all others in goodness, excellence, or worth; the finest in its class.
41.grammar: khayr functions as a comparative/superlative noun ('better / best'). The -u ending marks the nominative case, which typically signals the subject or predicate of a sentence and also opens a possessive phrase ('the best OF …').
41.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — goodness, that which is good or best

42.meaning: 'Those who open / decide' — the ones who render decisive judgments, settle matters, and grant relief or victory. As an active participle it names the doers of such opening.
42.grammar: A definite sound masculine plural active participle ('those who decide'). The -īna ending marks the accusative/genitive plural — the case used for an object or after a preposition or in a possessive link ('of those who decide').
42.root: ف-ت-ح (f-t-ḥ) — to open; to judge decisively, grant victory

1.meaning: 'And he said' — the act of speaking or stating, attributed to one masculine speaker, joined to what precedes by 'and.'
1.grammar: The connector 'wa-' ('and') with a past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he said.' The ending -a marks a completed action by one male, with the doer 'he' contained in the verb.

2.meaning: The chiefs, leading men, or notables — the prominent council of a people; a collective term for the elite whose standing fills the eyes.
2.grammar: A definite noun (the al- prefix means 'the') with the -u (nominative) ending, the case that typically marks the subject of a sentence — the ones doing or being something. Though singular in form, it refers collectively to the leading body of a people.

3.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
3.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

4.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
4.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

5.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
5.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
5.root: — (preposition)

6.meaning: 'His people / his folk' — the community, tribe, or nation to which a person belongs, with the attached pronoun 'his'.
6.grammar: A noun with the attached pronoun '-hi' ('his'). The '-i' ending is genitive: it typically marks the word as the object of a preposition or as linked to a preceding noun ('… of …'). The pronoun appears as '-hi' (rather than '-hu') because of this genitive '-i'.
6.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to rise; a people who stand together

7.meaning: A combination that sets up an emphatic condition: roughly 'if indeed / surely if.' It joins an emphasis particle ('truly, surely') with the conditional word 'if,' priming a strong 'if… then…' statement.
7.grammar: A particle cluster: the emphatic la- ('surely, truly') prefixed to the conditional particle 'in' ('if'). The final short -i is a connecting vowel added to ease pronunciation before the next word. Together it introduces a forceful condition, often paired later with an emphatic result.

8.meaning: 'You followed, pursued, took as a path / pattern (someone or something),' addressed to a group. The root means to follow after, to come behind and adhere to; this pattern stresses earnest, sustained following.
8.grammar: A past-tense verb in an intensive following-pattern ('to follow closely, adopt'). The suffix -tum marks the subject as a plural 'you' who performed the act ('you [all] followed').
8.root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow, pursue, come after

9.meaning: Shuʿayb — the proper name of a prophet sent to the people of Madyan.
9.grammar: A proper name (the diminutive form of a name) that is fully declinable (triptote). The -an ending marks the accusative case — fitting when the name is the one being sent or mentioned as object. The tanwīn here signals that the name belongs to the fully declinable class, not indefiniteness, since a proper name is inherently definite.

10.meaning: 'Indeed you (plural)' — the emphatic particle inna ('truly, indeed, surely'), which strongly affirms and stresses the statement that follows, fused with the attached pronoun 'you (all)'. Inna has no single English word; it functions to underline certainty.
10.grammar: Inna is an emphasising particle that introduces and strengthens a sentence; grammatically it places the following noun or pronoun in the accusative-like role of its 'subject'. The attached -kum is the masculine plural object/possessive pronoun 'you (all)'. Together: 'indeed you (all)…'.

11.meaning: In that case / then — a response particle signaling that what follows is the consequence of a just-stated condition or supposition ('if so, then…').
11.grammar: A response/consequence particle, not a noun or verb. The -an ending is a fixed part of the word (written with a final alif), not a live grammatical case. It introduces the result side of a hypothetical ('then you would…').

12.meaning: 'Ones who are surely losers' — those who suffer loss, whose effort ends in ruin and deficit. As an active participle it names those in a state of being lost or ruined, here with added emphasis.
12.grammar: A sound masculine plural active participle ('losers') with a prefixed emphatic la- ('surely'). The -ūna ending marks the nominative plural — the form used when the noun is the subject or the thing being described ('they are surely losers').
12.root: خ-س-ر (kh-s-r) — to lose, suffer loss, be ruined

1.meaning: '…so it seized / struck / took hold of them.' The connector 'so/then' plus a past-tense verb of seizing with a feminine-singular subject and an attached object 'them' — a completed act of being gripped or overtaken (as by a punishment or force).
1.grammar: A completed-action (past) verb prefixed with 'fa-' ('so/then'). The '-t' marks the subject as feminine singular ('she/it'). The attached '-hum(u)' is an object pronoun meaning 'them'; its vowel is lengthened to '-humu' to ease pronunciation before the next word.

2.meaning: The earthquake — a violent shaking or convulsion of the ground; a definite singular noun naming the quaking event itself.
2.grammar: A definite singular noun. The prefixed al- ('the') has its 'l' assimilated into the following 'r' (pronounced ar-rajfa). The unit ending -t (tā' marbūṭa) often marks a single instance of an action. The final -u marks the nominative case — typically the subject of a sentence.
2.root: ر-ج-ف (r-j-f) — to quake, shake violently, convulse

3.meaning: "And they came to be / and they became," from a verb that originally means "to enter upon the morning" and by extension "to end up in a certain state / to become." It describes a group transitioning into a new condition.
3.grammar: The "fa-" prefix means "so" or "and then," marking a result or sequence. The verb is in the completed (past) tense; the "-ū" ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ("they"). As one of the "sisters of kāna," this verb links a subject to a predicate state, hence "they became (something)."
3.root: ص-ب-ح (ṣ-b-ḥ) — morning / the coming of daybreak; by extension, to come to be in a state

4.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
4.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
4.root: — (particle)

5.meaning: Their home / dwelling — a dwelling-place or abode belonging to 'them'. Combines the noun 'home' with the possessor 'their'.
5.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The -i ending is genitive — here triggered because the word follows a preposition or links to another noun. The suffix -him means 'their' (referring to a group of males); its 'i' vowel is the form taken after a genitive -i.
5.root: د-و-ر (d-w-r) — to turn/encircle; hence 'dār', an enclosed dwelling or abode

6.meaning: Fallen prone / lying lifeless — describing people collapsed motionless on their knees and faces, crouched and still as in death. A plural descriptive form.
6.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' form) describing those in a state of crouching motionless. The -īna ending marks a masculine plural in the accusative/genitive — the form used for objects, or, as often here, for a descriptive 'state' word (telling how the subjects were: 'fallen prostrate').
6.root: ج-ث-م (j-th-m) — to crouch low and stay still; to lie collapsed/prone

1.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
1.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

2.meaning: They denied / they cried lies; they declared (something or someone) to be false. An intensive verb meaning to reject as a lie, to disbelieve and brand untrue — directed by a plural 'they'.

parts.tr: kadhdhab (doubled dh; simplified transliterations may write 'kadhab')
parts.en: denied / branded as lies (past stem, intensive)

2.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in an intensive pattern (to treat as false, to repeatedly deny). The middle radical carries a shadda (doubling), which is exactly what marks this as the intensive form: kadhdhab- (not the simple kadhab-). The ending -ū marks the doers as 'they' — a plural, grammatically masculine group, so the whole reconstructs to kadhdhabū. Note that simplified transliterations sometimes omit the doubling and write 'kadhabū', but the doubled dh is essential to the form. The perfect tense denotes a completed action.
2.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie; in this form, to call a lie, to deny as false

3.meaning: Shuʿayb — the proper name of a prophet sent to the people of Madyan.
3.grammar: A proper name (the diminutive form of a name) that is fully declinable (triptote). The -an ending marks the accusative case — fitting when the name is the one being sent or mentioned as object. The tanwīn here signals that the name belongs to the fully declinable class, not indefiniteness, since a proper name is inherently definite.

4.meaning: A compound particle meaning 'as if / as though.' It introduces a comparison or likeness, treating a situation as resembling another — presenting something as if it were a certain way, whether or not it truly is.
4.grammar: A particle of comparison formed from 'ka-' ('like / as') joined to a particle meaning 'that.' Together they function as a single linking word, 'as if,' used to liken one circumstance to another. It is a particle, so it has no case ending of its own.
4.root: — (particle of comparison)

5.meaning: The particle 'lam', a negating word used to push a verb into the past: it means 'did not' / 'has not'. Though it sits before a present-tense verb form, it negates the action as something that did not happen.
5.grammar: 'lam' is a negating particle that governs a following present-tense verb but gives it past meaning ('did not …'). It also puts that verb into the shortened (jussive) form. 'lam' itself carries no ending.

6.meaning: '(As though) they had never dwelt / thrived / lived in prosperity (there).' The root means to be free of need, to be self-sufficient and well-off, and to abide or flourish in a place. The subject is 'they.'
6.grammar: A present-tense verb with the ya- prefix and a plural 'they' subject (the weak final root letter drops, leaving the -aw plural marker, with a silent spelling alif). The shortened form (no final -na) reflects that it follows a governing particle such as 'as if' or a negation, giving 'as though they had never thrived.'
6.root: غ-ن-ي (gh-n-y) — to be free of need, well-off; to dwell in plenty

7.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
7.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

8.meaning: Those who / the ones who — a plural relative pronoun (masculine) introducing a description: 'those (people) who …'.
8.grammar: A relative pronoun, masculine plural, meaning 'those who / the ones who'. It refers back to a group already in view and introduces a clause describing them. Its form is fixed and does not change for case.

9.meaning: They denied / they cried lies; they declared (something or someone) to be false. An intensive verb meaning to reject as a lie, to disbelieve and brand untrue — directed by a plural 'they'.

parts.tr: kadhdhab (doubled dh; simplified transliterations may write 'kadhab')
parts.en: denied / branded as lies (past stem, intensive)

9.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in an intensive pattern (to treat as false, to repeatedly deny). The middle radical carries a shadda (doubling), which is exactly what marks this as the intensive form: kadhdhab- (not the simple kadhab-). The ending -ū marks the doers as 'they' — a plural, grammatically masculine group, so the whole reconstructs to kadhdhabū. Note that simplified transliterations sometimes omit the doubling and write 'kadhabū', but the doubled dh is essential to the form. The perfect tense denotes a completed action.
9.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie; in this form, to call a lie, to deny as false

10.meaning: Shuʿayb — the proper name of a prophet sent to the people of Madyan.
10.grammar: A proper name (the diminutive form of a name) that is fully declinable (triptote). The -an ending marks the accusative case — fitting when the name is the one being sent or mentioned as object. The tanwīn here signals that the name belongs to the fully declinable class, not indefiniteness, since a proper name is inherently definite.

11.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
11.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
11.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

12.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (masculine plural). Standing on its own, it typically adds emphasis or marks the group out as the focus ('they, specifically', 'it is they who').
12.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It takes no case endings; the base is hum, and the final vowel appears as -u (humu) as a connecting vowel to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a definite article. Standing alone, it commonly emphasises or isolates the subject.

13.meaning: "The losers / those who lose" — an active participle for those who suffer loss, who lose out or come to ruin, especially the ultimate loss of one's own soul.
13.grammar: An active participle in the masculine sound plural with the definite article 'the'. The -īna ending marks the accusative or genitive case — the form used when such a plural is a direct object, a predicate of 'to be', or follows a preposition (as opposed to the -ūna subject form).
13.root: خ-س-ر (kh-s-r) — to lose / suffer loss / be ruined

1.meaning: So he turned away — he turned his back and went off, departing from something. A past-tense action of a single male, opening with 'so/then'.

parts.en: he (3rd-person masculine singular), on a weak-ending verb

1.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in the reflexive 't-' pattern (turning oneself away). From a root ending in a weak letter, its third-person masculine singular 'he' form ends in the long -ā (written as alif maqṣūra). It denotes a completed action. Prefixed fa means 'so' or 'then'.
1.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — to be near / turn toward; in this pattern, to turn away or take charge

2.meaning: From them; away from them; concerning them. The preposition ʿan conveys moving away from, departing from, or 'on behalf of / concerning', combined with the pronoun 'them'.
2.grammar: A preposition joined to the attached pronoun -hum, 'them' (referring to a group, grammatically masculine plural). The preposition ʿan basically signals separation or removal ('away from'), and can also mean 'about/concerning' or 'on behalf of' depending on usage.

3.meaning: 'And he said' — the act of speaking or stating, attributed to one masculine speaker, joined to what precedes by 'and.'
3.grammar: The connector 'wa-' ('and') with a past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he said.' The ending -a marks a completed action by one male, with the doer 'he' contained in the verb.

4.meaning: 'O my people!' — a vocative call: 'people' (one's own community/folk) addressed directly, with 'my' attached. A speaker uses it to summon and appeal to his own community.
4.grammar: The particle yā- is the vocative ('O …'), used to call or address someone. The final -i here is the remnant of the possessive 'my' (the fuller -ī), commonly shortened to -i in direct address, so the whole means 'O my people!' The case ending proper is suppressed because the noun is being called, not used as subject or object.
4.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to rise; a people who stand together

5.meaning: A two-part emphasis particle meaning 'surely, indeed (already)' — 'la-' strongly affirms, and 'qad' before a past verb stresses that the action has definitely occurred.
5.grammar: Two particles fused for emphasis. 'la-' is the affirming prefix 'surely / truly.' 'qad,' when it precedes a past-tense verb, confirms and intensifies that the action really happened ('has indeed …'). Together they give a strong oath-like assurance to the statement that follows.

6.meaning: I have conveyed to you / delivered to you — I passed on and made reach you (a group) some message in full. Combines the verb 'I delivered' with the object 'you all'.
6.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in the causative 'a-' pattern (to make something reach). The ending -tu marks a first-person singular subject ('I'). The attached -kum is the object pronoun 'you all', the ones reached. A completed action: 'I have conveyed to you'.
6.root: ب-ل-غ (b-l-gh) — to reach/arrive; in this pattern, to make reach, i.e. to convey or deliver

7.meaning: Messages — the communications or dispatches entrusted to be delivered; the plural of a single 'message'.
7.grammar: A feminine plural noun (the -āt ending marks 'more than two' of a feminine word). The final -i is the ending that sound feminine plurals take in both the genitive ('of …' / after a preposition) and the object (accusative) roles — for this class of plural the two share one form.

8.meaning: 'My Lord' — the Master, Sustainer and Nurturer, claimed in close personal relation by the speaker.
8.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord') with the attached pronoun -ī meaning 'my'. This 'my' ending merges with the case-vowel of the noun, so a single long -ī is heard. The sense is 'the Lord who is mine'.
8.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord/master, to nurture and sustain

9.meaning: And I advised / counselled sincerely — and I gave heartfelt, well-meaning counsel, sincerely seeking the good of the one advised. A past-tense action of a single speaker.
9.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb denoting a completed action. The ending -tu marks a first-person singular subject ('I'). Prefixed wa means 'and'. The verb carries the sense of sincere, well-intentioned counsel.
9.root: ن-ص-ح (n-ṣ-ḥ) — to be sincere; to give genuine, well-meaning counsel

10.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
10.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

11.meaning: So how? / Then in what manner or state? — kayfa is the interrogative 'how', asking after the manner, condition or circumstance of something. With the prefixed 'so/then' it introduces a question following from what precedes, often expressing wonder or warning.
11.grammar: An interrogative particle ('how') carrying the connective prefix fa- ('so / then'), which links it to a preceding statement as a consequence or follow-up. As a particle, kayfa is indeclinable: its fixed final -a is not a case ending and does not change.

12.meaning: 'I grieve, I sorrow, I feel distress (over something).' The root denotes grief, sorrow, and regretful sadness. The form expresses the speaker's own grieving.
12.grammar: A present-tense verb, first-person singular 'I.' The opening long ā is the first-person present prefix (the hamza that marks 'I' on a present verb), lengthened here because the root ends in a weak letter; it is a verbal prefix, not a standalone pronoun. That weak final letter shows up as the long -ā at the end. The sense is ongoing: 'I grieve / I am grieving.'
12.root: أ-س-ي (ʾ-s-y) — to grieve, sorrow, feel distress

13.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
13.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

14.meaning: A people, folk, or community — a group of persons bound together (often by kinship or shared identity); a nation or tribe.
14.grammar: A singular collective noun (grammatically masculine, referring to a group). The final -in is the genitive case with nunation (tanwīn), marking it indefinite ('a people'); the genitive typically follows a preposition or links to a preceding noun ('… of a people').
14.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise, establish; a standing group of people

15.meaning: 'Disbelievers, those who reject faith and cover over the truth.' The root literally means to cover or conceal; applied to belief it means to deny and ungratefully reject what is true. As an active participle it names those who do so.
15.grammar: A sound masculine plural active participle ('disbelievers'). The -īna ending marks the accusative/genitive plural — the case used when the noun is an object or follows a preposition, or describes the state of a group ('as disbelievers').
15.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to disbelieve, reject ungratefully

1.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

2.meaning: We sent / dispatched. From the causative verb meaning to send forth or commission, especially the sending of messengers; with 'We' as the subject.
2.grammar: Past/perfect verb in the causative (form IV) pattern meaning 'to send', 1st person plural ('we'). The suffix -nā is the subject ending 'we' on a completed action. The perfect tense presents the sending as accomplished and complete.

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
3.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

4.meaning: a town / a settlement — an inhabited place such as a village or city; a gathering of dwellings.
4.grammar: A singular feminine noun. The final -in ending carries two signals at once: the genitive case (used after prepositions or to link to a preceding word, '… of …') and the indefinite 'a/an' (no definite article), conveying 'a town'.
4.root: ق-ر-ي (q-r-y) — to gather; a settled place

5.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
5.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

6.meaning: 'A prophet' — one to whom Allah grants revelation and through whom He conveys guidance to people.
6.grammar: An indefinite noun in the genitive case: the -in ending (with nunation, the 'n' sound) marks both indefiniteness ('a prophet') and the genitive state, which typically follows a preposition or a quantity word like 'how many of …'. It denotes a bearer of revelation.
6.root: Disputed. Classically derived either from ن-ب-ا (n-b-ʾ — news, tidings: 'one who brings/bears tidings'), or from ن-ب-و (n-b-w — to be elevated, raised: 'one who is exalted in rank'). Both derivations are widely cited.

7.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
7.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

8.meaning: "We took / seized / received" — to take, take hold of, seize, or accept; with a pact it means to bind a party to a covenant. The form carries a 'we' subject.
8.grammar: A past-tense verb with the attached subject suffix '-nā' meaning 'we': it marks a completed action done by a group (or the royal/majestic 'We'). The '-nā' ending is what turns the bare verb into 'we did it'.

9.meaning: Its people, its inhabitants, its folk — those who belong to a place or household. The base word 'ahl' denotes the people proper to something: the members of a family, the residents of a town, or those entitled to a thing.
9.grammar: A noun carrying the accusative -a ending, which typically marks it as the direct object of a verb or the subject following certain particles. The attached suffix -hā means 'its/her', here referring back to a feminine or non-human entity (such as a town); it shows possession ('its people').
9.root: ا-ه-ل (ʾ-h-l) — belonging, family, being a member of a household or community

10.meaning: A noun meaning 'adversity, hardship, misery, or distress' — especially affliction in one's outward circumstances such as poverty or loss. The prefixed 'bi-' adds 'with/by.'
10.grammar: A noun carrying the preposition bi- ('with/by') and the definite article al- ('the'). The final -i is genitive, the case regularly required after a preposition; here it follows bi- to mean 'with the hardship.'

11.meaning: 'And hardship / affliction' — harm, injury, or suffering that touches the body or circumstances (such as illness or loss). Joined by 'and'.
11.grammar: The connector wa ('and') plus a definite feminine noun on the faʿlāʾ pattern, denoting an intense condition (grievous harm or suffering); the article's 'l' is assimilated into the following sun letter 'ḍ'. The final -i is the genitive case, taken after a preposition or as the second term of a possessive construction.

12.meaning: 'So that they may / perhaps they will.' A particle expressing hope, expectation, or purpose, fused with the pronoun 'them'; it introduces a hoped-for or intended outcome.

parts.en: perhaps / so that / in hope that

12.grammar: The particle laʿalla ('perhaps, in the hope that, so that') with the attached pronoun -hum ('them'), which serves as its subject. Laʿalla belongs to a family of particles that put a following noun or pronoun in the accusative; -hum is that fixed object form. It conveys hope or an intended purpose rather than certainty.

13.meaning: They humble themselves, plead lowly, and beseech with submission — to abase oneself before another in earnest entreaty, especially in supplication to Allah, abandoning all pride and showing utter neediness.
13.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form V, tafaʿʿala / yatafaʿʿalu). The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine subject ('he/they'), and the -ūna ending marks 'they' (masculine plural) acting in the ongoing/habitual present. The Form V pattern is reflexive-intensive — doing the action to oneself with effort; here the tāʾ of the original yataḍarraʿūna is assimilated into the following ḍād, giving the doubled ḍḍ cluster (yaḍḍarraʿūna).
13.root: ض-ر-ع (ḍ-r-ʿ) — lowliness, humble pleading, submission and entreaty

1.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
1.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

2.meaning: We exchanged, We replaced, We substituted — to put one thing in the place of another. The intensive stem conveys a thorough swapping of one state or thing for a different one.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -nā ending marks the subject as 'we' having completed the action. The doubled middle consonant (form II) intensifies the basic sense of changing into deliberate, thorough substitution.
2.root: ب-د-ل (b-d-l) — change, substitution, replacing one thing with another

3.meaning: Place, position, location — the spot or stead occupied by something. In phrases it functions like 'in place of' or 'instead of', marking where one thing stands relative to another.
3.grammar: A noun with the accusative -a ending. This ending here signals an adverbial sense of place ('in the place of') or marks it as a direct object; it commonly leads into a following noun in a possessive link ('the place OF …').
3.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be (the place where something 'is')

4.meaning: The bad, the evil one, the harmful deed or affliction (feminine) — that which is ugly, displeasing, or wrongful: a misdeed, a calamity, or anything offensive and disliked.
4.grammar: A definite feminine adjective/noun ('the bad one'). The al- prefix means 'the'. The -ti ending (genitive) typically follows a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun in a possessive chain ('… OF the bad'). The feminine ending -a(t) marks grammatical gender.
4.root: س-و-ء (s-w-ʾ) — badness, evil, harm, that which displeases

5.meaning: The good, the fine one, the beautiful deed or blessing (feminine) — that which is handsome, excellent, and pleasing: a good deed, a benefit, prosperity, or anything fair and welcome.
5.grammar: A definite feminine adjective/noun ('the good one'). The al- prefix means 'the'. The -ta ending is accusative, typically marking it as the direct object of a verb or the subject after certain particles. The feminine ending -a(t) marks grammatical gender.
5.root: ح-س-ن (ḥ-s-n) — goodness, beauty, excellence, that which is fair and pleasing

6.meaning: 'Until / up to the point that; so that' — a particle marking a limit or goal. It expresses the end-point reached ('until') or the purpose aimed at ('so that, in order that').
