9.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on, upon, over,' and by extension 'against' or 'incumbent upon.' It can mark something resting on top of, an obligation laid on someone, or being set over/above something.
9.grammar: An indeclinable preposition (its form never changes). It governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case, and conveys location 'on/upon,' or figuratively duty or opposition ('against').
9.root: — (preposition; no triliteral root)

10.meaning: Idols: carved images or statues set up to be worshipped. A plural noun denoting man-made objects taken as objects of veneration.
10.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun, indefinite. The final -in (tanwīn kasra) marks the genitive case with indefiniteness ('some idols'); this ending typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship.

11.meaning: 'For them / to them / theirs' — a preposition 'for / to / belonging to' joined to the pronoun 'them,' expressing that something pertains, belongs, or is owed to that group.
11.grammar: The preposition li- ('for / to / belonging to'), whose vowel becomes -a before an attached pronoun, joined to -hum ('them'). It commonly expresses possession or benefit — 'theirs / for them.' Particles like this carry no case or tense of their own.

12.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
12.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

13.meaning: O Musa! — a direct call/address to the Prophet Moses by name ('O Moses').
13.grammar: The vocative particle yā ('O') used to call or address someone, joined to the proper name. The name ends in a fixed long -ā and does not change its ending; yā marks it as the one being addressed.

14.meaning: Make! / Set up! / Appoint! A command to bring something into being, fashion it, or designate something as something else.

parts.en: helping vowel for the command (hamzat al-waṣl)
make / appoint (command stem, all three root letters)

14.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a single male: 'make!' The opening i- is a helping vowel (hamzat al-waṣl) that lets the consonant cluster be pronounced; it is not part of the root. The stem جۡعَلۡ carries all three root letters (j-ʿ-l), and its final consonant takes a silent ending (sukūn), the normal way an imperative is closed off.

15.meaning: 'For us / to us' — indicating that something is directed toward, or belongs to, the speaker's group.
15.grammar: The preposition li- ('for / to') with the attached pronoun -nā ('us'). When this pronoun is added, the preposition's vowel becomes 'la-'. The whole expresses benefit or direction toward 'us' — what is done for, or owed to, the speaker's group.
15.root: — (li- is a particle/preposition; -nā is a pronoun)

16.meaning: 'A god / a deity, an object of worship' — the word in its indefinite form, naming a single divine being without specifying which.
16.grammar: A singular indefinite noun. The -an ending combines two things: the accusative case (the form for a verb's object or, often, a noun described by a following adjective) and nunation, the -n sound that signals 'a/an,' i.e. indefiniteness.
16.root: ء-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, that which is worshipped

17.meaning: 'Just as / in the same way that' — a phrase of comparison joining 'like / as' to 'what', meaning 'like that which...' or 'in the manner that...'.
17.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like / as') joined to mā ('what / that which'). Together they introduce a likeness or manner — 'just as...', 'in the same way that...' — comparing one thing or action to another.

18.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
18.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

19.meaning: Gods: beings or objects taken as deities and given worship. The plural of 'ilāh' (a god / object of worship), here in indefinite form.
19.grammar: A broken plural noun, indefinite. The final -un (tanwīn ḍamma) marks the nominative case with indefiniteness — the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or a thing being named or identified.

20.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
20.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

21.meaning: 'Indeed you (plural)' — the emphatic particle inna ('truly, indeed, surely'), which strongly affirms and stresses the statement that follows, fused with the attached pronoun 'you (all)'. Inna has no single English word; it functions to underline certainty.
21.grammar: Inna is an emphasising particle that introduces and strengthens a sentence; grammatically it places the following noun or pronoun in the accusative-like role of its 'subject'. The attached -kum is the masculine plural object/possessive pronoun 'you (all)'. Together: 'indeed you (all)…'.

22.meaning: 'A people / folk / community' — a group of people bound together, often by kinship, tribe, or shared identity.
22.grammar: An indefinite collective noun ('a people'), grammatically singular but referring to a group. The -un ending is indefinite ('a') and nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence.
22.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a group that stands together

23.meaning: You act ignorantly; you behave foolishly without knowledge. The verb conveys being or acting in ignorance — lacking knowledge and behaving rashly because of it.
23.grammar: An imperfect (present/ongoing) verb. The ta- prefix here marks a second-person addressee, and the -ūna ending marks a masculine plural 'you (all)' in the indicative mood, indicating a real, ongoing action. The full -ūna (not shortened to -ū) shows the verb stands free of any particle that would cut it short.

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: These / those — a plural demonstrative pointing to a group of people or things. Its core sense is the near demonstrative 'these', but it is very commonly rendered 'those' in translation when the group it points to has already been described or named rather than being physically present.
2.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, used for a group of either gender. Its base value is near-deixis ('these'), built from an attention-drawing prefix 'hā-' ('lo!, here') plus the base 'ulāʾi'. In practice it is often translated 'those' when the referent is already mentioned or understood rather than literally nearby. Its form is fixed and does not change for grammatical case; it points to a group rather than naming it.

3.meaning: Doomed to ruin; brought to destruction and made utterly worthless. A passive descriptive term for that which is shattered, wrecked, and headed for perdition.
3.grammar: A passive participle (a 'being-…-ed' word) from an intensive verb form, naming something that is destroyed or doomed to destruction. The final -un (tanwīn ḍamma) marks the nominative case with indefiniteness — typically the case of a subject or of something described or identified.

4.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
4.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.
4.root: — (particle; no root)

5.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
5.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

6.meaning: 'In it / in him' — the preposition 'in, inside, within' joined to a pronoun referring to a single masculine or neuter thing. It locates something inside or as part of that referent.
6.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -hi refers to one masculine (or grammatically masculine) thing and stands as the object of the preposition; its vowel is -i because attached pronouns take that shape after the long -i of fi. Together they answer 'in what?' or 'in whom?'.

7.meaning: And false, vain, and futile: that which is empty of truth, baseless, doomed to come to nothing. 'Bāṭil' is the opposite of 'ḥaqq' (truth/reality) — it denotes what is null, void, and ultimately perishing.
7.grammar: A prefixed 'and' (wa) joined to an active participle/adjective meaning 'false, vain.' The final -un (tanwīn ḍamma) marks the nominative case with indefiniteness — the case typically used for a subject or a predicate that describes or identifies something.

8.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
8.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.

9.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
9.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
9.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

10.meaning: 'They do / they work, they act' — a present-tense verb of doing and working, covering deeds and actions carried out by a group.
10.grammar: Present/imperfect verb. The ya-…-ūna frame marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (do).' The -ūna ending also marks the indicative mood, the plain statement form, as opposed to command or negated-future forms.
10.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

1.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
1.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

2.meaning: 'Is it other than…?', 'shall (it be) other than…?' — a questioning expression built from the question particle 'is/shall?' and the word for 'other than / besides'. It challenges whether anything besides the named thing could be intended.
2.grammar: A yes/no question particle attached to the noun 'other than'. The -a ending is accusative, the case that often marks a word as a direct object or otherwise governed into this case (here the questioned object). The opening 'a-' turns the phrase into a question.
2.root: غ-ي-ر (gh-y-r) — otherness, difference, being other than

3.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
3.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

4.meaning: I seek for you; I look for and desire to obtain something on your behalf. Combines the act of seeking/wanting with a beneficiary ('you').
4.grammar: An imperfect (present/ongoing) verb meaning 'I seek,' carried by the a- prefix that marks a first-person singular 'I.' The attached -kum is a pronoun meaning 'you (all)' functioning as the one for whom the seeking is done.
4.root: ب-غ-ي (b-gh-y) — to seek, desire, aspire

5.meaning: 'A god / a deity, an object of worship' — the word in its indefinite form, naming a single divine being without specifying which.
5.grammar: A singular indefinite noun. The -an ending combines two things: the accusative case (the form for a verb's object or, often, a noun described by a following adjective) and nunation, the -n sound that signals 'a/an,' i.e. indefiniteness.
5.root: ء-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, that which is worshipped

6.meaning: And it / and he — a connective joined to the standalone pronoun 'he/it', often introducing a circumstantial clause ('while it…').
6.grammar: The prefix wa- ('and', or 'while' when introducing an accompanying circumstance) joined to the detached subject pronoun huwa, 'he/it' (masculine singular). The shadda on the wa- reflects assimilation of a preceding consonant onto it in connected speech. The pronoun is fixed in form and serves as the subject of its clause.

7.meaning: He favored you; He granted you preference, excellence, or bounty above others. The verb (intensive form) conveys singling someone out for special favor or superiority.
7.grammar: A past-tense verb in an intensive form, 'he favored.' The bare stem with final -a marks a third-person masculine singular 'he' acting in completed past time. The attached -kum is a pronoun 'you (all)' receiving the action.

8.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
8.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
8.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

9.meaning: The worlds, all created realms — the totality of beings and peoples; in 'Lord of the worlds,' the whole of creation across all its kinds.
9.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the worlds') with 'al-' ('the'). The '-īna' ending marks a masculine sound plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) form — the form used after a preposition, in an 'of' linkage, or as a direct object.
9.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; a 'world' as a sign by which the Creator is known

1.meaning: 'And when / and at the time when' — the connective 'and' joined to a word that points to a past moment or circumstance ('when'), introducing the recollection of an event or situation.
1.grammar: A connective particle plus a time-word. The wa- prefix means 'and'. 'Idh' is an invariable adverb pointing to a definite time in the past ('when, at the moment that'); it has no case ending and typically introduces a clause recalling a past event.

2.meaning: We rescued you; We delivered you to safety from danger or destruction. The verb (causative form) means to bring someone out of peril into deliverance.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb in a causative form, 'to deliver/save.' The suffix -nā marks a first-person plural subject 'we' in completed past time, and the further -kum is a pronoun 'you (all)' receiving the rescue.

3.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
3.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

4.meaning: The family, folk, or close people of someone — those belonging to a person's household, following, or kin.
4.grammar: A singular collective noun in the genitive (-i ending), which typically links it to a following noun ('the folk OF …') or follows a preposition. It points to those associated with a named person.
4.root: أ-ه-ل (ʾ-h-l) — family, kinsfolk (āl is derived from ahl by elision of the hāʾ)

5.meaning: Pharaoh — the title/name of the ruler of ancient Egypt, used as a proper name for that figure.
5.grammar: A proper name. Being a foreign, non-inflecting (diptote) name, it takes a single -a for both the accusative and the genitive and never takes tanwīn. Here it follows another noun in a possessive link ('… of Pharaoh').

6.meaning: 'They impose upon you / subject you to' — to burden someone repeatedly with something, usually something harsh or oppressive.
6.grammar: A present-tense verb, masculine plural 'they,' with the attached object -kum 'you all.' The ya-…-ūna frame marks an ongoing plural action; the kept -na (before the suffix) signals the plain (indicative) present.
6.root: س-و-م (s-w-m) — to impose, make to bear, drive

7.meaning: Evil, harm, or grievousness — the bad or distressing aspect of something; in a possessive link, 'the worst of …' or 'a grievous …'.
7.grammar: A singular masculine noun in the accusative (-a ending), which typically marks an object of a verb or the first term of a possessive link ('the evil OF …'). The sense is 'grievous / worst kind of.'
7.root: س-و-ء (s-w-ʾ) — evil, harm, to be bad

8.meaning: The punishment, torment, or chastisement — severe penalty or suffering inflicted as retribution.
8.grammar: A singular masculine noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending is the genitive, which typically links it to a preceding noun ('… of the punishment') or follows a preposition.

9.meaning: They slay relentlessly; they slaughter many, or kill again and again. The intensive verb form stresses the killing as widespread, repeated, or done to many.
9.grammar: An imperfect (present/ongoing) verb in an intensive form that conveys killing in great number or repeatedly. The yu- prefix marks a third-person subject (the yu- vowel signals the intensive pattern), and the -ūna ending marks a masculine plural 'they' in the indicative mood, denoting a real, continuing action.
9.root: ق-ت-ل (q-t-l) — to kill, slay

10.meaning: 'Your sons / your children' — the male offspring (or offspring generally) belonging to the addressed group.
10.grammar: A masculine plural noun ('sons') with the attached possessive -kum ('your,' to a group). The -a ending is the accusative, which typically marks the object of a verb. The case vowel sits before the pronoun suffix.

11.meaning: 'And they spare / let live / keep alive' — to leave women alive (rather than kill them); can also carry the nuance of shaming or seeking to dishonour by keeping them.
11.grammar: Joining 'and' (wa) plus a present-tense verb, masculine plural 'they.' The pattern (form X, ista-) here means 'to let/keep alive.' The ya-…-ūna frame with kept -na marks an ongoing plural action in the plain (indicative) present.

12.meaning: 'Your women' — the women (or wives) belonging to the addressed group.
12.grammar: A plural noun ('women,' the plural used for 'woman') with the attached possessive -kum ('your,' to a group). The -a ending is the accusative, which typically marks the object of a verb. The case vowel sits before the pronoun suffix.

13.meaning: 'And in' — the connector 'and' joined to the preposition 'in / within / during.'
13.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the preposition fī ('in'). Fī governs the following noun, putting it into the genitive case. Neither particle changes form.

14.meaning: A demonstrative meaning 'that' addressed to a group of people (plural 'you'). It points to something at a distance — whether physical, or to a previously mentioned matter — and is directed at multiple listeners.
14.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun for something distant. The base 'dhā' carries the sense 'that', the 'li' is an element of distance, and the ending '-kum' tells you the speaker is addressing a plural 'you' — it specifies the audience, not the thing pointed at. It does not change for case.

15.meaning: A testing or trial — an ordeal or affliction by which someone is tested and proven. It can also denote a trial of blessing, but its core is a probing test that reveals what a person truly is.
15.grammar: A singular indefinite noun. The '-un' ending (nunation) marks it as nominative and indefinite — 'a trial' — and the nominative case typically signals that the word is the subject of a sentence or a predicate ('is/was a trial').
15.root: ب-ل-و (b-l-w) — to test, to try

16.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
16.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

17.meaning: 'Your Lord' (addressing a group). 'Rabb' is a rich term: the Master, Owner, Sustainer and Nurturer who creates, possesses, provides for, and brings a thing to its proper completion — far more than a mere ruler.
17.grammar: A noun ('Lord') with an attached possessive pronoun, forming a possessive pairing. 'Rabb' carries a doubled (geminated) 'b' — the shaddah — at its core. The '-i' vowel on 'rabb' is its case ending, determined by 'Lord's' own role in the sentence (not by the suffix); the attached '-kum' is the possessor ('your'), addressing a plural 'you', and as the possessed-to term it sits in the genitive.
17.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, master, sustain

18.meaning: Great, immense, mighty, or tremendous — describing something vast in scale, weight, or significance.
18.grammar: An adjective on the intensive pattern faʿīl ('great, mighty'). The ending -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite and nominative; an adjective in this form typically agrees with and describes an indefinite nominative noun.
18.root: ع-ظ-م (ʿ-ẓ-m) — to be great, mighty, immense

1.meaning: And We made an appointment; We set a fixed promise or appointed time with someone. The verb (form of mutual engagement) conveys arranging a tryst or settled time-bound commitment.
1.grammar: A prefixed 'and' (wa) joined to a past-tense verb of the 'mutual engagement' pattern, meaning to set a tryst or appointed term. The suffix -nā marks a first-person plural subject 'we' acting in completed past time.

2.meaning: Mūsā (Moses) — the proper name of the prophet. As a name it has no Arabic root meaning; it is a non-inflecting (indeclinable) noun whose ending does not change for case.
2.grammar: A proper name ending in a fixed long -ā (written as alif maqṣūra). It is fully indeclinable (invariable): the final -ā never changes, so the word shows no case distinction at all — it looks and sounds identical whether subject, object, or possessor. (This is unlike a diptote, which still alternates between two case vowels; here there is no alternation.)

3.meaning: Thirty: the cardinal number 30.
3.grammar: A cardinal number inflected like a sound masculine plural. The -īna ending here is the form the number takes in the accusative or genitive (as opposed to -ūna), typically marking it as an object of a verb or as governed by a preposition.

4.meaning: 'A night' — the period of darkness from sunset to dawn; a single night.
4.grammar: A singular indefinite noun with the feminine ending. The '-an' (nunation) marks it accusative and indefinite; a singular noun in this case after a number functions as the 'counted' item that specifies what is being numbered ('… nights').
4.root: ل-ي-ل (l-y-l) — night

5.meaning: And We completed it / brought it to its full measure; We made it whole and finished, leaving nothing lacking. The verb (causative form) means to bring a thing to completion.
5.grammar: A prefixed 'and' (wa) joined to a past-tense verb in a causative form, 'to complete.' The suffix -nā marks a first-person plural subject 'we' in completed past time, and the attached -hā is a pronoun 'it/her' (referring to a feminine or non-human thing) receiving the action.
5.root: ت-م-م (t-m-m) — to be complete, whole, full

6.meaning: With ten / by ten (more): the cardinal number ten, governed by the preposition 'with' to express addition or accompaniment.
6.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with/by') attached to the number 'ten.' Because the noun follows a preposition, it takes the genitive case; the final -in (tanwīn kasra) marks that genitive together with indefiniteness ('with [a set of] ten').

7.meaning: So it was completed / it became whole; it reached its full measure and was finished. An intransitive verb describing something coming to completion of itself.
7.grammar: A connective fa- ('so / then,' implying result or sequence) joined to a past-tense verb 'it was completed.' The bare stem with final -a marks a third-person masculine singular 'it/he' in completed past time.
7.root: ت-م-م (t-m-m) — to be complete, whole, full

8.meaning: An appointed time or fixed term; a precisely set tryst, deadline, or designated point in time (and sometimes place) for an event. The form denotes the instrument or fixed measure of timing.
8.grammar: A noun built on a pattern indicating a set instrument or fixed point (of time). The final -u (ḍamma) marks the nominative case, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or a thing being named or identified. Its definiteness comes from being joined to a following noun.

9.meaning: His Lord, Master, and Sustainer — the One who owns, nurtures, governs, and brings to completion; expressing both ownership and loving care over the one belonging to Him.
9.grammar: A masculine noun with an attached possessive pronoun ("his Lord"). The -i vowel on the noun is genitive, here drawn out because of the following possessive suffix -hi ("his"). The suffix -hi means "his," and its i-form follows naturally after an i-vowel.
9.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, ownership, nurturing and sustaining to completion

10.meaning: 'Forty' — the cardinal number 40.
10.grammar: A cardinal number of the 'tens' family. The '-īna' ending is the form these tens (20, 30, 40 …) take when they are an object or follow a preposition (the accusative/genitive form); the counted thing after it is usually a singular indefinite noun.

11.meaning: 'A night' — the period of darkness from sunset to dawn; a single night.
11.grammar: A singular indefinite noun with the feminine ending. The '-an' (nunation) marks it accusative and indefinite; a singular noun in this case after a number functions as the 'counted' item that specifies what is being numbered ('… nights').

12.meaning: 'And he said' — the act of speaking or stating, attributed to one masculine speaker, joined to what precedes by 'and.'
12.grammar: The connector 'wa-' ('and') with a past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he said.' The ending -a marks a completed action by one male, with the doer 'he' contained in the verb.

13.meaning: Mūsā (Moses) — the proper name of the prophet. As a name it has no Arabic root meaning; it is a non-inflecting (indeclinable) noun whose ending does not change for case.
13.grammar: A proper name ending in a fixed long -ā (written as alif maqṣūra). It is fully indeclinable (invariable): the final -ā never changes, so the word shows no case distinction at all — it looks and sounds identical whether subject, object, or possessor. (This is unlike a diptote, which still alternates between two case vowels; here there is no alternation.)

14.meaning: To / for his brother: the noun 'brother' linked to a possessor ('his') and governed by the preposition 'to/for.'
14.grammar: The preposition li- ('to/for') attached to the noun 'brother,' which then carries the possessive pronoun -hi ('his'). 'Brother' is one of a small set of nouns that shows its case with a long vowel: the -ī here reflects the genitive (required after the preposition), and the pronoun takes the form -hi to harmonize with that i-vowel.

15.meaning: Aaron, the proper name of the brother of Moses, a prophet of Allah.
15.grammar: A proper name. Being a foreign/non-Arabic name, it is a 'diptote': it refuses the usual -i for the genitive and instead shows -a, and it never takes nunation. The -a ending here stands in for the genitive, the case used after a preceding noun ('… OF Aaron') or after a preposition.
15.root: — (proper name; no Arabic root)

16.meaning: Succeed me / take my place / act as my deputy in my absence. A command to stand in for someone and manage affairs on their behalf.

parts.en: succeed / take the place of (command stem)

16.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a single male: 'take my place!' The opening u- is a helping vowel enabling the consonant cluster to be pronounced, the stem ends in a silent ending (sukūn) as imperatives do, and the attached -nī is the object pronoun 'me' (its n protects the verb's ending before the 'me' sound).
16.root: خ-ل-ف (kh-l-f) — to succeed, come after, deputize

17.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
17.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
17.root: — (particle)

18.meaning: My people / my folk: a community or nation, here joined to the possessor 'my.' 'Qawm' denotes a people bound together as a group, often by kinship or shared identity.
18.grammar: A noun 'people' carrying the attached possessive pronoun -ī ('my'). When this 'my' is added, it replaces the noun's normal case-vowel, so the case is not separately shown; the word is understood by context to be definite ('my people').

19.meaning: And set right / put in order / reform: a command to make matters good, repair what is broken, and act righteously. The verb (causative form) means to bring about soundness and well-being.
19.grammar: A prefixed 'and' (wa) joined to a command (imperative) in a causative form, addressed to a single male: 'set right!' The final consonant carries a silent ending (sukūn), the normal closing of an imperative.
19.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound, good, set right

20.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
20.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

21.meaning: '(You) follow / pursue / take as a path' — a verb meaning to walk after, conform to, and adopt something as one's way, in a form that intensively conveys 'to keep following'.
21.grammar: A present/jussive verb in the reflexive-intensive pattern (iftaʿala). The ta- prefix marks the second-person 'you (one male)'. The silent (vowelless) final consonant is the jussive mood, the form used after negative or conditional particles such as 'do not …' or 'if …'.
21.root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow, come after, pursue

22.meaning: Way / path / road: a route taken, and by extension a course of conduct, means, or manner of life. 'Sabīl' is frequently used for a moral or spiritual road one travels.
22.grammar: A noun, 'way/path.' The final -a (fatḥa) marks the accusative case — the case typically used for the direct object of a verb or for nouns governed in similar ways. Its definiteness comes from being joined to a following noun.

23.meaning: Those who spread corruption / the workers of mischief — people who ruin, disorder, and lay waste, the opposite of those who set things right.
23.grammar: Prefix 'al-' = 'the.' An active participle (the one who corrupts) from the causative form (afʿala). The '-īna' ending is the masculine sound plural in the accusative/genitive (oblique) case — the form used for the object of a verb or after a preposition.
23.root: ف-س-د (f-s-d) — to be corrupt, spoil, cause ruin/disorder

1.meaning: A compound meaning 'and when' — it sets up a circumstance in past time, marking the moment at which something occurred, with the result clause typically following. It carries the sense of 'when, at the time that.'
1.grammar: A particle phrase introducing a past-time clause. Lammā signals 'when' for completed events and expects a following clause stating what then happened; the wa- prefix means 'and.'

2.meaning: He/it came, arrived, or came about — the act of coming into presence or of something occurring.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb with no prefix and no personal suffix, naming a completed act by a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it came'). All three letters here are root letters: jā spells the first radical plus the lengthened weak middle radical, and the final hamza (ء) is the third root consonant — not an ending. The fatḥa (-a) on that hamza is simply the past-tense vocalization for a 'he' subject sitting on the last root letter; there is no separable suffix.

3.meaning: Mūsā (Moses) — the proper name of the prophet. As a name it has no Arabic root meaning; it is a non-inflecting (indeclinable) noun whose ending does not change for case.
3.grammar: A proper name ending in a fixed long -ā (written as alif maqṣūra). It is fully indeclinable (invariable): the final -ā never changes, so the word shows no case distinction at all — it looks and sounds identical whether subject, object, or possessor. (This is unlike a diptote, which still alternates between two case vowels; here there is no alternation.)

4.meaning: To / for Our appointed place — and by extension Our appointed time: a fixed meeting-point or designated tryst (here primarily a place) set by Allah, joined to the possessor 'Our' and governed by the preposition 'to/for.' The noun 'mīqāt' can name a fixed point of place as well as of time.

parts.en: appointed place / fixed meeting-point (also appointed time)

4.grammar: The preposition li- ('to/for') attached to 'appointed place/time,' which carries the possessive pronoun -nā ('our'). Because it follows the preposition, the noun is genitive; the linking -i vowel before -nā reflects that genitive case.
4.root: و-ق-ت (w-q-t) — time/place, appointed term

5.meaning: And He spoke to him; He addressed him with speech, directly and distinctly. The verb (intensive form) conveys real, articulate speaking directed at someone.
5.grammar: A prefixed 'and' (wa) joined to a past-tense verb in an intensive form, 'he spoke to.' The bare stem with final -a marks a third-person masculine singular 'he' in completed past time, and the attached -hu is the object pronoun 'him' (its u-vowel form following the -a).
5.root: ك-ل-م (k-l-m) — speech, word, to speak

6.meaning: His Lord, Master, and Sustainer. 'Rabb' denotes the One who owns, nurtures, governs, and brings a thing to its completion; the attached pronoun makes it 'his.'
6.grammar: A noun followed by a possessive pronoun. The -u on 'rabb' is the nominative ending, the case used for the subject/doer of a sentence ('the one who does'). The attached -hu means 'his.'
6.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, lord over

7.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
7.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

8.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'my': the One who owns, sustains, nurtures, and governs — combining mastery, ownership, and loving cultivation. With the attached 'my' it is an intimate address, 'my Lord.'
8.grammar: A noun, rabb, with the first-person possessive (the original 'my' yāʾ being reduced to a final -i, so 'my Lord'). The word denotes the Master who creates, owns, and lovingly sustains. Used as a heartfelt vocative, calling upon one's Lord.
8.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

9.meaning: 'Show me!' or 'let me see!' — a request that someone cause the speaker to see or perceive something; the verb 'to show / cause to see' with 'me' as the one shown.
9.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to one person, from a causative verb ('to make someone see' = 'to show'). The ending '-nī' is the object pronoun 'me' (the 'n' is a connecting sound that links certain pronouns to a verb). So the whole means '(you) cause me to see'.
9.root: ر-ا-ي / ر-ء-ي (r-’-y) — to see, perceive

10.meaning: A verb meaning '(that) I look', '(that) I gaze', or '(that) I direct my sight' — the act of looking performed by a single speaker referring to himself.
10.grammar: A present/future verb whose initial 'a-' prefix (with the short 'a' vowel) marks a first-person singular subject ('I look'). The vowelless ending (sukūn) shows the verb is in the jussive/subjunctive mood — the form used after certain particles or to express purpose ('so that I may look'). (Note: an imperative 'look!' to one male would instead begin with 'u-', as in 'unẓur'.)

11.meaning: 'To you' (addressing one person): indicating direction or motion toward a single individual — that toward which something moves or is directed.
11.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to, towards') with an attached pronoun; before a suffix ilā takes the form ilay-. The -ka ending is the pronoun 'you' for a single male addressee. Pronouns following a preposition stand in the genitive relationship, though their form does not visibly change for case.

12.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
12.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

13.meaning: 'Never / will not' — a particle that negates a future action emphatically. Lan denies that something will ever happen, stronger and more absolute than a simple 'not'.
13.grammar: A negating particle that applies to present-tense verbs to deny them in the future ('will never…'). Grammatically it also puts the following verb into the subjunctive mood, which clips that verb's ending to a short -a. Lan itself does not change.

14.meaning: A verb meaning 'you see Me' or 'you perceive Me' — combining the act of seeing performed by a single addressee with 'Me' as the one seen.
14.grammar: A present/future verb with the 'ta-' prefix marking a single male subject ('you see'). The attached '-nī' is the object 'Me'. Because the root ends in a weak letter, the case-vowel on the verb is not pronounced, but the form functions to express ongoing or potential seeing.

15.meaning: "but / however" — a contrastive particle that sets what follows against what came before, correcting or qualifying the previous statement.
15.grammar: A contrastive particle in its 'light' (single-n) form, which simply links clauses and does not govern a following noun's case. The final -i here is a helping vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word (it is not a case ending). The leading wa- is 'and'.

16.meaning: Look! / Consider! — a command to direct one's eyes or attention toward something, to observe and reflect on it.
16.grammar: A singular command (imperative) addressed to one person, 'look!'. The verb root begins with a cluster, so a helping vowel u- is prefixed to make it pronounceable. The bare stem with no ending and a vowelless final consonant (-ẓur) is the basic command form. Often paired with the preposition ilā ('look AT') or used in the sense 'reflect, consider'.
16.root: ن-ظ-ر (n-ẓ-r) — looking, seeing, regarding and reflecting

17.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
17.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

18.meaning: 'The mountain' — a large natural elevation of rock rising from the earth.
18.grammar: A definite noun ('the mountain'). The '-i' ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… of the mountain') or follows a preposition or oath particle.

19.meaning: A two-part connector meaning 'then if / so if.' It joins a clause to what precedes (fa-) and introduces a hypothetical condition (in, 'if').
19.grammar: A compound of two particles. Fa- means 'then/so,' connecting to a prior statement. In means 'if,' setting up a condition whose outcome follows. The final -i is a helping vowel added to the normally vowel-less in to ease pronunciation before the next word; it carries no grammatical case meaning.

20.meaning: A verb meaning 'it settled', 'it became firmly fixed', or 'it stayed put' — to come to rest and remain stable in place.
20.grammar: A past-tense verb for a single masculine subject ('it settled / remained'), built on Form X, the pattern that conveys seeking or coming to be in a state — here, coming to rest and staying fixed. The doubled final 'r' (shadda) is not a Form X marker but belongs to the root itself, whose second and third letters are both 'r' (q-r-r); this doubling appears in every form of the verb.
20.root: ق-ر-ر (q-r-r) — to settle, be stable, rest firmly

21.meaning: 'Its place' or 'its location' — the spot or position belonging to it.
21.grammar: A noun with the attached pronoun '-hu' ('its / his'). The '-a' ending before the pronoun is accusative, the case that typically marks the direct object of a verb or an adverb of place ('in its place').

22.meaning: A two-part marker meaning 'then/so' plus 'shall/will.' It announces something forthcoming as a consequence: the particle sawfa points to the future, generally a more remote or emphatic future than the shorter prefix sa-.
22.grammar: A linking particle fa- ('then/so,' signalling result or sequence) joined to the future particle sawfa, which is placed before a present-tense verb to throw its action into the future ('will/shall …').

23.meaning: A verb meaning 'you see Me' or 'you perceive Me' — combining the act of seeing performed by a single addressee with 'Me' as the one seen.
23.grammar: A present/future verb with the 'ta-' prefix marking a single male subject ('you see'). The attached '-nī' is the object 'Me'. Because the root ends in a weak letter, the case-vowel on the verb is not pronounced, but the form functions to express ongoing or potential seeing.

24.meaning: A connector meaning 'then, when' — it joins to what came before ('then/so') and sets up a 'when…' clause whose outcome follows. It frames a moment: 'and then, at the point when…'.
24.grammar: A compound of the connecting particle fa- ('then/so', linking to the preceding statement) and lammā, a particle meaning 'when' that introduces a past circumstance and leads the listener to expect a following result clause.

25.meaning: A verb meaning 'it manifested itself', 'it shone forth', or 'it became unveiled and visible' — for something to reveal or display itself openly.
25.grammar: A past-tense verb for a single masculine subject ('it revealed itself / shone forth'). The 'ta-' prefix gives a reflexive sense (an action turning back on the doer), and the doubled 'l' intensifies the meaning of becoming plainly manifest.
25.root: ج-ل-و (j-l-w) — to make clear, unveil, manifest

26.meaning: His Lord, Master, and Sustainer. 'Rabb' denotes the One who owns, nurtures, governs, and brings a thing to its completion; the attached pronoun makes it 'his.'
26.grammar: A noun followed by a possessive pronoun. The -u on 'rabb' is the nominative ending, the case used for the subject/doer of a sentence ('the one who does'). The attached -hu means 'his.'
26.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, lord over

27.meaning: 'To the mountain' or 'for the mountain' — the preposition 'to/for' joined to the word for a great rocky elevation.
27.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('to / for') attached to the definite noun 'the mountain'. The '-i' ending is genitive, which is the case a noun always takes after a preposition; here it marks the mountain as the thing pointed toward or intended.
27.root: ج-ب-ل (j-b-l) — mountain, firmness

28.meaning: A verb meaning 'he made it', 'he rendered it', or 'he turned it into something' — combining the act of making/causing by a single male with 'it' as what is acted upon.
28.grammar: A past-tense verb for a single masculine subject ('he made'), with the attached object pronoun '-hu' ('it / him'). The verb often takes two objects, conveying turning one thing into another ('he made it [into] …').
28.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, render, bring about

29.meaning: Something 'crushed', 'leveled', or 'pounded flat to powder' — flattened and pulverized so that nothing of its form remains.
29.grammar: An indefinite noun/verbal-noun. The '-an' (tanwīn) ending marks the indefinite accusative ('a crushing / flattened'), the case typically used for an object of a verb or to describe how something is made.
29.root: د-ك-ك (d-k-k) — to crush, level, pound flat

30.meaning: 'And he/it fell down' — 'and' joined to a verb meaning to collapse, tumble, or drop heavily to the ground.
30.grammar: The connector 'wa-' ('and') joined to a past-tense verb for a single masculine subject ('he/it fell'). The doubled 'r' (shadda) is part of the root, conveying a sudden, heavy falling or collapsing down.
30.root: خ-ر-ر (kh-r-r) — to fall down, collapse, tumble

31.meaning: Mūsā (Moses) — the proper name of the prophet. As a name it has no Arabic root meaning; it is a non-inflecting (indeclinable) noun whose ending does not change for case.
31.grammar: A proper name ending in a fixed long -ā (written as alif maqṣūra). It is fully indeclinable (invariable): the final -ā never changes, so the word shows no case distinction at all — it looks and sounds identical whether subject, object, or possessor. (This is unlike a diptote, which still alternates between two case vowels; here there is no alternation.)

32.meaning: Someone 'struck senseless', 'thunderstruck', or 'fallen unconscious' — overwhelmed into a faint as if by a stunning blow.
32.grammar: An indefinite descriptive noun (active participle). The '-an' (tanwīn) ending is the indefinite accusative, the case commonly used to describe the state in which a subject is or acts ('… [while] thunderstruck').
32.root: ص-ع-ق (ṣ-ʿ-q) — to be thunderstruck, swoon, fall senseless

33.meaning: A connector meaning 'then, when' — it joins to what came before ('then/so') and sets up a 'when…' clause whose outcome follows. It frames a moment: 'and then, at the point when…'.
33.grammar: A compound of the connecting particle fa- ('then/so', linking to the preceding statement) and lammā, a particle meaning 'when' that introduces a past circumstance and leads the listener to expect a following result clause.

34.meaning: A verb meaning 'he came to', 'he regained consciousness', or 'he recovered his senses' after a faint or daze.
34.grammar: A past-tense Form I (basic) hollow verb for a single masculine subject ('he recovered / came to'). It comes from a root with a weak middle letter, so the middle letter surfaces as a long 'ā'; the opening hamza belongs to the root pattern and is not a causative prefix. The verb means recovering one's senses intransitively (the subject himself comes round).
34.root: ف-و-ق (f-w-q) — to recover, awaken, come back to one's senses

35.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
35.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

36.meaning: 'Glory be to You / how far above all flaw You are' — a set exclamation declaring Allah utterly free of any imperfection, partner, or unworthy attribute, paired with 'You.'
36.grammar: A verbal noun, subḥān ('glorification, utter freedom from imperfection'), bound to the attached pronoun -ka, 'You/Your' (one masculine addressee). It stands in the accusative (-a ending) as the exclamatory object of an understood verb ('I declare Your absolute glory') — a fixed formula of praise.
36.root: س-ب-ح (s-b-ḥ) — glorifying, declaring (Allah) free of all imperfection

37.meaning: 'I have repented / turned back' — from tāba; a first-person declaration of returning to Allah from sin.
37.grammar: A past-tense (completed) verb. The -tu ending marks the speaker as the subject — 'I (did it).' It states that the act of turning back in repentance has been carried out by the one speaking.
37.root: ت-و-ب (t-w-b) — to turn back, repent, return

38.meaning: 'To you' (addressing one person): indicating direction or motion toward a single individual — that toward which something moves or is directed.
38.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to, towards') with an attached pronoun; before a suffix ilā takes the form ilay-. The -ka ending is the pronoun 'you' for a single male addressee. Pronouns following a preposition stand in the genitive relationship, though their form does not visibly change for case.

39.meaning: And I — the standalone first-person singular pronoun 'I,' here joined by 'and.' As a detached pronoun it stands on its own (typically as subject), unlike the attached endings.
39.grammar: Prefix 'wa' = 'and.' 'anā' is the independent (detached) pronoun 'I,' used for emphasis or to begin/identify the subject; it does not take a case ending and is fixed in form.

40.meaning: First, foremost — the one that comes before all others in order, time, or rank. It marks the initial or leading member of a set.
40.grammar: A noun/adjective of the elative-type pattern 'afʿal' ('first'). The final -u is the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or a predicate ('… is the first'). It identifies the foremost in sequence or standing.
40.root: ء-و-ل (ʾ-w-l) — to be first, to precede

41.meaning: A plural noun meaning 'the believers' — those who have faith, who inwardly trust and affirm. The Form IV participle denotes one who brings about belief and security within.
41.grammar: A definite plural active participle of Form IV (āmana 'to believe'). The -īna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) state. The prefixed mu- marks it as a Form IV participle ('one who has/gives faith').

1.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
1.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

2.meaning: O Moses: a direct address (a call) to the Prophet Moses by name.
2.grammar: The vocative particle yā ('O'), used to call or address someone, followed by the proper name Mūsā (Moses). A called noun like this stands in the vocative; for a name ending in a fixed long ā the ending does not visibly change.

3.meaning: 'Truly I' or 'indeed I' — the emphatic affirming particle inna ('truly, indeed, certainly'), which strengthens and confirms a statement, joined to the pronoun 'I'.
3.grammar: An emphasizing particle with an attached pronoun. 'Inna' is a particle of emphasis and affirmation that introduces a statement and lends it certainty ('it is certainly the case that…'). The attached -ī is the first-person singular pronoun ('I / me') in the object form this particle requires. Together: 'Indeed I…'.

4.meaning: A verb meaning 'I chose you', 'I selected you', or 'I picked you out as the elect' — combining the act of choosing by 'I' with a single male as the one chosen.

parts.en: form-VIII infix (t, hardened to ṭ after ṣ)

4.grammar: A past-tense Form VIII verb. The pattern places a prefixed 'i-' before the first root letter ('ṣ') and inserts an infixed 't' after it; here that infix hardens to 'ṭ' because it follows the emphatic 'ṣ'. The '-tu' ending marks the speaker as subject ('I'), and the attached '-ka' is the object 'you' (one male). Form VIII carries the sense of selecting and taking the very best for oneself.
4.root: ص-ف-و (ṣ-f-w) — purity, to choose the choicest

5.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
5.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
5.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

6.meaning: Humankind, people, mankind — the collective of human beings.
6.grammar: A collective noun ('people, mankind') carrying the definite article al- ('the'); the 'l' of the article assimilates into the following 'n', doubling it (al-nās → an-nās). The genitive ending -i marks the word as governed by a preposition or as the second term of a possessive.
6.root: ء-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — humankind, sociability, familiarity; the word for 'people' is most commonly traced to this root (related to insān, 'human being')

7.meaning: 'With My messages' or 'by My missions' — the preposition 'with/by' joined to the plural 'messages' and the possessive 'My', referring to communications entrusted to be delivered.
7.grammar: The preposition 'bi-' ('with / by') attached to a feminine plural noun 'messages', followed by the possessive '-ī' ('My'). The '-i' ending is genitive, the case required after a preposition; the form denotes the means or instrument by which something is done.

8.meaning: 'And with My speech' or 'and by My word' — 'and' plus 'with/by' joined to 'speech/word' and the possessive 'My', referring to direct utterance or address.
8.grammar: The connector 'wa-' ('and') plus the preposition 'bi-' ('with / by'), attached to the noun 'speech', then the possessive '-ī' ('My'). The '-i' ending is genitive, required after the preposition; it marks the means by which an action is carried out.

9.meaning: An imperative meaning 'take!', 'seize!', or 'take hold of!', addressed to a single male, with the attached 'fa-' meaning 'so' or 'then'.
9.grammar: A command (imperative) to one male person ('you'), with the 'you (masc. sing.)' built into the form. 'fa-' is a connecting particle expressing sequence or consequence ('so', 'then').
9.root: ا-خ-ذ / ء-خ-ذ (’-kh-dh) — to take, seize, take hold of

10.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
10.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

11.meaning: A verb meaning 'I gave you', 'I granted you', or 'I bestowed upon you' — combining the act of giving by 'I' with a single male as recipient.
11.grammar: A past-tense verb. The '-tu' ending marks the speaker as subject ('I'), and the attached '-ka' is the object 'you' (one male). The verb commonly takes a further object, conveying granting or handing something over to someone.

12.meaning: 'And be!' — 'and' joined to the command 'be' or 'become', ordering a single male to exist in or assume a certain state.
12.grammar: The connector 'wa-' ('and') joined to an imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male ('be!'). It comes from a hollow root, so the middle weak letter drops in the command; the vowelless ending (sukūn) is the standard close of an order.

13.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
13.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

14.meaning: 'The grateful ones / the thankful' — those who recognize and acknowledge benefit and respond with gratitude, as a defined group.
14.grammar: An active participle ('one who is grateful') made definite by 'al-' ('the') and put in the sound masculine plural with the ending -īna. The -īna ending marks a masculine human plural in the accusative/genitive state (as opposed to -ūna for the nominative). It names 'the grateful ones' as a class.

1.meaning: 'And We decreed / prescribed / wrote down' — to ordain or set down as a binding ruling. At root 'kataba' is 'to write,' and by extension to make something obligatory or fixed. The leading 'wa' is 'and'.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb joined by 'wa' (and). The '-nā' ending attached to a past verb means 'we' did the action. Beyond literal writing, this verb commonly means to prescribe or make binding — to 'write down' something as a decree.
1.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write, inscribe, prescribe, ordain

2.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
2.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
3.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

4.meaning: 'The tablets' — flat slabs or boards used as a writing surface for inscribing text.
4.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the tablets'); this is a 'broken plural' formed by reshaping the singular rather than adding an ending. The '-i' ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… of the tablets') or follows a preposition.
4.root: ل-و-ح (l-w-ḥ) — board, tablet, flat surface

5.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
5.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
5.root: — (preposition)

6.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
6.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.

7.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
7.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
7.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

8.meaning: 'An admonition', 'a counsel', or 'a heartfelt warning' — words of moral exhortation meant to soften the heart and urge right conduct.
8.grammar: An indefinite feminine noun. The '-an' (tanwīn) ending marks the indefinite accusative, the case typically used for the object of a verb or to specify what something consists of ('… [as] an admonition').

9.meaning: 'And a detailing', 'and an explanation', or 'and a setting-out in detail' — a clear, item-by-item exposition that distinguishes and clarifies matters.
9.grammar: The connector 'wa-' ('and') joined to an indefinite verbal noun. The '-an' (tanwīn) ending marks the indefinite accusative, the case commonly used for the object of a verb or to specify what something amounts to ('… and a detailing').
9.root: ف-ص-ل (f-ṣ-l) — to separate, distinguish, set out in detail

10.meaning: For every, for each, belonging to all of. Combines the preposition 'for/to' with the word for 'every/all.'
10.grammar: The preposition li- ('for/to') joined to kull ('every/each/all'). The -i ending on kull is genitive, the case required after a preposition. The combination conveys 'for every / to each.'

11.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
11.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
11.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

12.meaning: 'So take it/them!' — the connector 'so/then' joined to a command 'take' or 'grasp', addressed to a single male, with 'it/them' as what is to be seized and held.
12.grammar: The connector 'fa-' ('so / then') joined to an imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male ('take!'), with the attached object '-hā' ('it / them', feminine). In the command form of this root the prosthetic helping-hamza that the imperative would normally begin with is dropped after the connecting vowel, leaving a short, direct order ('khudh').

13.meaning: "With strength / firmness / resolve" — quwwa is power, strength, or might; with the prefix it means 'with strength', i.e. firmly and resolutely.
13.grammar: The preposition 'bi' ('with, by means of') attached to a feminine noun. The -in ending (tanwīn) marks the noun as indefinite ('a strength') and in the genitive case — the form always required after a preposition.

14.meaning: 'And command!' or 'and order!' — 'and' joined to a command telling a single male to instruct or enjoin others to do something.
14.grammar: The connector 'wa-' ('and') joined to an imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male ('order!'). The vowelless ending (sukūn) is the standard close of a command, conveying a direct instruction to enjoin or bid.

15.meaning: 'Your people' or 'your folk' — the community, kinsfolk, or nation belonging to a single male addressee.
15.grammar: A noun with the attached possessive '-ka' ('your', one male). The '-a' ending before the pronoun is accusative, the case that typically marks the direct object of a verb ('… your people' as the thing acted upon).
15.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a people, community

16.meaning: A verb meaning '(that) they take' or '(that) they grasp' — the act of taking or seizing performed by a group of males.
16.grammar: A present/future verb for a masculine plural subject ('they take'). The dropped final 'n' (the '-ū' ending without a following nūn) shows the verb is in the subjunctive/jussive mood — the form used after certain particles or to express purpose ('so that they take') or command.
16.root: ء-خ-ذ (ʾ-kh-dh) — to take, seize, grasp

17.meaning: with the best/finest of it; the most beautiful or excellent part of something. The phrase joins a preposition meaning 'with/according to' to a superlative noun ('the best') that is in turn linked to an attached possessor ('of it').

parts.en: of it / of her (feminine singular possessor)

17.grammar: A preposition 'bi' (with/by) fused to a superlative noun. The -i ending is genitive, the case required after a preposition; here it links the superlative to the following possessor pronoun '-hā' ('the best OF it'). The pronoun '-hā' refers to a feminine-singular or non-human-plural antecedent.
17.root: ح-س-ن (ḥ-s-n) — to be good, beautiful, excellent

18.meaning: I shall show you (plural); I will cause you to see. It announces a future act of making people perceive or witness something, addressed to more than one person.

parts.en: weak stem letter (from the root hamza in Form IV)

18.grammar: The prefix 'sa-' marks the near future ('will/shall'). The verb is Form IV causative ('to make someone see' = 'to show'). The 'ʾu-' prefix marks a first-person singular subject ('I'); the original root hamza of ر-ء-ي weakens to a long 'ū' (the wāw) within the stem 'ʾūrī'. The ending '-kum' is the object 'you' (masculine plural). So: 'I will show you (all).'

19.meaning: dwelling, abode, home; the place where one settles and resides. It can also denote a realm or sphere (as in 'the abode of the Hereafter').
19.grammar: A singular feminine noun. The -a ending is accusative, the case that typically marks the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or follows certain particles.
19.root: د-و-ر (d-w-r) — to turn, circle, revolve; hence a place one circulates within

20.meaning: A noun/adjective meaning 'those who defiantly disobey', 'the rebellious', 'the morally corrupt' — people who knowingly break away from obedience to Allah and overstep the bounds of right conduct.
20.grammar: Definite plural noun (active participle in form) with the article al- ('the'). The participle stem is fāsiq, and the entire sound-plural ending -īna marks a masculine plural in the accusative or genitive case (the form used as a verb's object or after a preposition). Reconstruction: al + fāsiq + īna = al-fāsiqīna. The participle names the agent: 'those who do the act of fisq', i.e. willful disobedience.
20.root: ف-س-ق (f-s-q) — to forsake obedience, transgress, act rebelliously

1.meaning: I shall turn away / divert / avert; to redirect something or someone from one direction to another. It announces a future act of turning or steering away.
1.grammar: The prefix 'sa-' marks the near future. The 'a-' prefix marks a first-person singular subject ('I'). The verb is present/imperfect, and its final -u ending signals the plain (indicative) mood — a simple statement of action: 'I will turn away.'
1.root: ص-ر-ف (ṣ-r-f) — to turn, divert, direct away

2.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on behalf of,' 'for,' 'about,' or 'away from.' It often conveys removing a burden from someone or acting in their place.

parts.en: on behalf of / for / away from

2.grammar: A preposition (a linking particle). It governs the noun that follows it, putting that noun into the genitive case. It does not change form.

3.meaning: My signs / My tokens; clear indicators that point to a truth. The base word denotes a sign, mark, evidentiary token, or a verse of revelation, here joined to a first-person possessor ('My').
3.grammar: A sound feminine plural ('signs') with an attached possessive '-ya' ('my'). The '-i' before the pronoun is the oblique (genitive/accusative) ending that sound feminine plurals take when not in the subject case; before the '-ya' suffix it links the noun to the possessor: 'my signs.'

4.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
4.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

5.meaning: they act arrogantly; they behave with haughty pride, deeming themselves great and above others. It describes people puffing themselves up and disdaining the truth or other people.
5.grammar: A present/imperfect verb in an intensive reflexive pattern that means 'to make oneself big,' i.e., to be arrogant. The 'ya-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject in the plain (indicative) mood: 'they are arrogant / they act haughtily.'
5.root: ك-ب-ر (k-b-r) — to be great, big; hence pride, arrogance

6.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
6.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

7.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
7.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

8.meaning: 'Without' or 'other than' — the preposition bi- joined to ghayr, a noun meaning 'other than / not / lacking', together conveying the absence of something ('with no …', 'wrongfully').
8.grammar: bi- is a preposition that takes the genitive; ghayr is a noun of exception/negation ('other than'). Its -i ending is genitive (required after bi-) and it also links to a following noun in a possessive 'of' relationship, so 'bi-ghayri X' means 'without X / other than X'.
8.root: غ-ي-ر (gh-y-r) — otherness, difference, being other than

9.meaning: 'The truth', 'the right', 'what is rightfully due' — that which is real, correct, and justly owed; the opposite of falsehood and wrongdoing.
9.grammar: A definite masculine noun (the al- prefix means 'the'). The -i ending is genitive, the case typically taken after a preposition or when the word links to a preceding noun ('… of the truth / by right').
9.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, rightness, that which is established and due

10.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
10.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

11.meaning: "That they should see / lest they see." A present-tense verb of seeing, perceiving with the eyes, or coming to realize.
11.grammar: A present-tense verb, "they" (third-person masculine plural), from a root whose weak final letter drops away. The loss of the full "-ūna" plural ending (leaving "-aw") signals the subjunctive/jussive mood — used after particles meaning "that," "so that," or "lest," or in negation of the completed act. The silent alif is a spelling convention after this plural ending.

12.meaning: All, every, the whole of — totality. When followed by a singular it means 'every (one)'; when followed by a definite plural or whole it means 'all of.'
12.grammar: A noun of totality, almost always joined to a following noun in the genitive ('every … / all of …'). The final -a is the accusative case, the form used when the word functions as an object of a verb.

13.meaning: A sign, token, or miraculous indication; also a discrete verse of revelation — a marker that points beyond itself to a deeper truth or to its Author.
13.grammar: A singular feminine noun, indefinite ('a sign'). The final -in (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite and in the genitive case — the doubled-n 'nunation' shows there is no 'the', and the -i base vowel indicates the genitive (used after prepositions or in a possessive link).

14.meaning: 'Not' — a particle of negation. Depending on context it denies a present fact, forbids an action, or rules something out ('do not / there is no').
14.grammar: A negating particle, 'not / no'. It is used to deny or prohibit — negating present-tense statements, expressing 'there is no...', or, with a command form, forbidding an action ('do not...').

15.meaning: 'They (masculine) believe' — to have faith in Allah; a present-tense verb with a masculine-plural subject.
15.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb, 3rd-person masculine plural ('they believe'). The yu- prefix with the -ū ending marks 'they (men) do'. The dropped final nūn (yu'minū, not yu'minūna) shows the jussive/subjunctive mood — used after conditional or negative-command particles. From form IV, 'to believe'.
15.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, trust; form IV: to believe, have faith

16.meaning: with it / by it — a preposition meaning 'with' or 'by means of' joined to a pronoun referring to a single feminine (or grammatically feminine) thing.
16.grammar: The bi- prefix is a preposition meaning 'with', 'by', or 'by means of'. The attached -hā is an object pronoun meaning 'it' or 'her', referring to something feminine in gender. Together they mean 'with it' or 'by means of it'.
16.root: — (preposition with pronoun)

17.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
17.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

18.meaning: "That they should see / lest they see." A present-tense verb of seeing, perceiving with the eyes, or coming to realize.
18.grammar: A present-tense verb, "they" (third-person masculine plural), from a root whose weak final letter drops away. The loss of the full "-ūna" plural ending (leaving "-aw") signals the subjunctive/jussive mood — used after particles meaning "that," "so that," or "lest," or in negation of the completed act. The silent alif is a spelling convention after this plural ending.

19.meaning: Way / path / road: a route taken, and by extension a course of conduct, means, or manner of life. 'Sabīl' is frequently used for a moral or spiritual road one travels.
19.grammar: A noun, 'way/path.' The final -a (fatḥa) marks the accusative case — the case typically used for the direct object of a verb or for nouns governed in similar ways. Its definiteness comes from being joined to a following noun.

20.meaning: right guidance, sound judgment, maturity of conduct; the state of being rightly directed and acting with good sense. It denotes integrity and correct, mature discernment as opposed to error and folly.
20.grammar: A definite verbal noun (the 'l-' is 'the'; its 'l' assimilates into the following 'r'). The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF …') or follows a preposition.
20.root: ر-ش-د (r-sh-d) — to be rightly guided, to follow the right course

21.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
21.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

22.meaning: they take it / adopt it / seize it for themselves; the verb means to take something up, acquire it, or turn something into an object of one's choosing. With the attached 'it,' it means they make something their own or treat it as such.
22.grammar: A present/imperfect verb meaning 'to take/adopt for oneself.' The 'ya-' prefix with the '-ū' ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The expected indicative '-na' (of '-ūna') regularly drops whenever an object pronoun is attached — a morphophonological rule that applies in every mood, not a sign of subjunctive or jussive. The ending '-hu' is the object 'it/him': 'they take it.'

23.meaning: A way, path, road, or means — a route to a destination, hence also a way or means of accomplishing something.
23.grammar: A singular noun. The '-an' ending is accusative and indefinite: the accusative case commonly marks the direct object of a verb, and the final 'n' sound marks it indefinite ('a way'). It denotes a path one travels or a means to an end.

24.meaning: and if; but if. It combines a connective 'and/but' with a conditional particle that introduces a hypothetical or possible case ('if such-and-such happens…').
24.grammar: Two particles joined: the connector 'wa' ('and/but') and 'in' ('if'). 'In' introduces a condition and typically puts the verb that follows into the jussive mood, setting up an 'if … then …' relationship. Neither particle takes a case ending.

25.meaning: "That they should see / lest they see." A present-tense verb of seeing, perceiving with the eyes, or coming to realize.
25.grammar: A present-tense verb, "they" (third-person masculine plural), from a root whose weak final letter drops away. The loss of the full "-ūna" plural ending (leaving "-aw") signals the subjunctive/jussive mood — used after particles meaning "that," "so that," or "lest," or in negation of the completed act. The silent alif is a spelling convention after this plural ending.
25.root: ر-ء-ي (r-ʾ-y) — to see, perceive, consider

26.meaning: Way / path / road: a route taken, and by extension a course of conduct, means, or manner of life. 'Sabīl' is frequently used for a moral or spiritual road one travels.
26.grammar: A noun, 'way/path.' The final -a (fatḥa) marks the accusative case — the case typically used for the direct object of a verb or for nouns governed in similar ways. Its definiteness comes from being joined to a following noun.
26.root: س-ب-ل (s-b-l) — way, path, road
