27.meaning: Error, going astray, deviation; the misguided wrong course, the loss of right direction that stands opposite to sound guidance.
27.grammar: A definite masculine noun. The -i ending is genitive, the case that typically follows a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ("… OF …"). The al- prefix makes it definite ("the").
27.root: غ-و-ي (gh-w-y) — going astray, error, deviation from the right way

28.meaning: they take it / adopt it / seize it for themselves; the verb means to take something up, acquire it, or turn something into an object of one's choosing. With the attached 'it,' it means they make something their own or treat it as such.
28.grammar: A present/imperfect verb meaning 'to take/adopt for oneself.' The 'ya-' prefix with the '-ū' ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The expected indicative '-na' (of '-ūna') regularly drops whenever an object pronoun is attached — a morphophonological rule that applies in every mood, not a sign of subjunctive or jussive. The ending '-hu' is the object 'it/him': 'they take it.'

29.meaning: A way, path, road, or means — a route to a destination, hence also a way or means of accomplishing something.
29.grammar: A singular noun. The '-an' ending is accusative and indefinite: the accusative case commonly marks the direct object of a verb, and the final 'n' sound marks it indefinite ('a way'). It denotes a path one travels or a means to an end.

30.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
30.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

31.meaning: A connector meaning 'because they…' or 'by reason that they…'. It fuses the preposition bi- (here giving a cause, 'because of') with anna ('that', an emphatic particle introducing a fact) and the attached pronoun -hum ('they').
31.grammar: bi- here gives a causal sense ('because of'). anna is an emphatic particle meaning 'that' which introduces a statement of fact and takes a following noun or pronoun in the accusative; the attached -hum is that pronoun, a masculine plural 'they'. Together they give a reason: 'because they …'.

32.meaning: They denied / they cried lies; they declared (something or someone) to be false. An intensive verb meaning to reject as a lie, to disbelieve and brand untrue — directed by a plural 'they'.

parts.tr: kadhdhab (doubled dh; simplified transliterations may write 'kadhab')
parts.en: denied / branded as lies (past stem, intensive)

32.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in an intensive pattern (to treat as false, to repeatedly deny). The middle radical carries a shadda (doubling), which is exactly what marks this as the intensive form: kadhdhab- (not the simple kadhab-). The ending -ū marks the doers as 'they' — a plural, grammatically masculine group, so the whole reconstructs to kadhdhabū. Note that simplified transliterations sometimes omit the doubling and write 'kadhabū', but the doubled dh is essential to the form. The perfect tense denotes a completed action.
32.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie; in this form, to call a lie, to deny as false

33.meaning: By/in Our signs. Āyāt is the plural of āya — a sign, token, or evidence. Signs are pointers that indicate a greater reality. With the prefixed particle and pronoun it means 'with/in Our signs'.
33.grammar: A plural noun preceded by the preposition bi- ('with, in, by'), which requires the following noun to take the -i (genitive) ending. The attached -nā means 'our' when joined to a noun. The genitive here is governed by the preposition.

34.meaning: A compound meaning 'and they were' or 'and they used to' — it sets a state or habit in the past. The verb 'to be/become' here establishes an ongoing past condition, often paired with a following verb to express habitual action.
34.grammar: A past-tense verb ('to be') in the third-person masculine plural — the -ū ending means 'they' did/were. It commonly conveys a continued past state or habit, especially when followed by another verb. The wa- prefix means 'and.'
34.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to come into being

35.meaning: From it / about it / away from it — a preposition meaning 'from' or 'off of', attached to a feminine 'it'.
35.grammar: 'ʿan' is a preposition conveying departure or removal — 'away from / off of / concerning'. The attached -hā is 'it/her', referring to a single feminine thing. Prepositions like this put the following pronoun in the genitive.

36.meaning: 'Ones who are heedless / unaware / inattentive.' An active participle (doer-noun) describing those characterized by ghaflah — neglect, inattention, being oblivious or off-guard, failing to notice or pay heed. The plural refers to a group sunk in such heedlessness.
36.grammar: A masculine plural active participle ('the heedless ones'). The pattern ghāfil- is a doer-noun from the verb 'to be heedless/unaware.' The -īna ending is the masculine plural marker in the accusative/genitive ('object' or 'oblique') case — the form used when the word is a direct object, follows a preposition, or completes another word. (Its counterpart for the subject case would be -ūna.)
36.root: غ-ف-ل (gh-f-l) — to be heedless, inattentive, unaware

1.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

2.meaning: They denied / they cried lies; they declared (something or someone) to be false. An intensive verb meaning to reject as a lie, to disbelieve and brand untrue — directed by a plural 'they'.

parts.tr: kadhdhab (doubled dh; simplified transliterations may write 'kadhab')
parts.en: denied / branded as lies (past stem, intensive)

2.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in an intensive pattern (to treat as false, to repeatedly deny). The middle radical carries a shadda (doubling), which is exactly what marks this as the intensive form: kadhdhab- (not the simple kadhab-). The ending -ū marks the doers as 'they' — a plural, grammatically masculine group, so the whole reconstructs to kadhdhabū. Note that simplified transliterations sometimes omit the doubling and write 'kadhabū', but the doubled dh is essential to the form. The perfect tense denotes a completed action.
2.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie; in this form, to call a lie, to deny as false

3.meaning: By/in Our signs. Āyāt is the plural of āya — a sign, token, or evidence. Signs are pointers that indicate a greater reality. With the prefixed particle and pronoun it means 'with/in Our signs'.
3.grammar: A plural noun preceded by the preposition bi- ('with, in, by'), which requires the following noun to take the -i (genitive) ending. The attached -nā means 'our' when joined to a noun. The genitive here is governed by the preposition.

4.meaning: and the meeting / encounter; the act of meeting, encountering, or coming face to face. It joins a connective 'and' to a verbal noun denoting an encounter (often used of meeting one's Lord).
4.grammar: A connective 'wa' ('and') prefixed to a verbal noun. The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a following noun ('the meeting OF …') or follows a preposition.
4.root: ل-ق-ي (l-q-y) — to meet, encounter, come upon

5.meaning: The Hereafter — the final, lasting life that comes after death and the present world; literally 'the last/latter (abode or life)', as opposed to the first, nearer life.
5.grammar: A feminine adjective used as a noun, with 'the'. The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF …'), or follows a preposition or oath particle.
5.root: ء-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be last, to come after, end

6.meaning: It came to nothing / became void / was wasted — of deeds, to be rendered worthless and to lose all reward.

parts.en: to come to nothing / be nullified

6.grammar: A past-tense verb describing a completed event. The -at ending marks a feminine singular subject ('it/she'), used because the thing that becomes void (e.g. 'deeds') is grammatically feminine. The root pictures effort that swells up and then bursts into nothing.
6.root: ح-ب-ط (ḥ-b-ṭ) — coming to nothing, nullification of works

7.meaning: Their deeds / works / actions — the things they have done.
7.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of 'deed', meaning 'deeds/works'. The attached -hum means 'their' (masculine plural), forming a possessive link. The -u before the pronoun is nominative, marking the whole phrase ('their deeds') as a subject. The -hum form keeps its u-vowel after this nominative ending.

8.meaning: An interrogative particle that turns a statement into a yes/no question, roughly "is it that…?" or "do…?". It can also carry a rhetorical or expectant tone rather than a literal request for information.
8.grammar: A question particle placed before a sentence to ask whether something is the case. It has no case ending and does not change form; it simply marks the words that follow as a yes/no question.

9.meaning: they are repaid / recompensed / requited; they receive the return owed for their deeds, whether reward or penalty. The verb is passive — the recompense is given to them by another.
9.grammar: A present/imperfect passive verb ('to be recompensed'). The 'yu-' prefix together with the '-na' ending and the passive vowelling marks a third-person masculine plural subject who receives the action: 'they are repaid.' The retained '-na' shows the plain (indicative) mood, a simple statement.
9.root: ج-ز-ي (j-z-y) — to recompense, repay, requite

10.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
10.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

11.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
11.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

12.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
12.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
12.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

13.meaning: 'They do / they work / they act' — to perform deeds or carry out actions, ongoing or habitual.
13.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya-…-ūna frame marks third-person masculine plural ('they do/work'). The retained final -na (the 'ūna' ending) is the indicative form, used for a plain, ongoing, or habitual action that is simply being stated.
13.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

1.meaning: 'and he took / adopted (for himself)' — to take something up and make it one's own, e.g., to take as a friend, protector, or object of devotion; the reflexive (self-benefiting) form of 'to take.'
1.grammar: A past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular ('he …'), in the reflexive (self-benefiting) stem 'to take for oneself / adopt.' The final -a marks a completed act done by 'he.' The leading 'wa-' means 'and'; the initial alif of the stem is a 'helping' vowel pronounced only when the word begins after a pause.

2.meaning: a people, folk, community; a group of human beings bound together (by kinship, locality, or allegiance). The word often carries the sense of one's own people or nation.
2.grammar: A collective singular noun (singular in form, plural in sense). The -u ending is nominative, the case that typically marks the subject — the one doing or being something in a sentence.
2.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; hence a group that stands together

3.meaning: Mūsā (Moses) — the proper name of the prophet. As a name it has no Arabic root meaning; it is a non-inflecting (indeclinable) noun whose ending does not change for case.
3.grammar: A proper name ending in a fixed long -ā (written as alif maqṣūra). It is fully indeclinable (invariable): the final -ā never changes, so the word shows no case distinction at all — it looks and sounds identical whether subject, object, or possessor. (This is unlike a diptote, which still alternates between two case vowels; here there is no alternation.)

4.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
4.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
4.root: — (preposition)

5.meaning: 'After him / it' — 'baʿd' denotes what comes afterward in time or sequence, here joined to 'him/it'.
5.grammar: A time-noun 'baʿd' (afterness) with an attached pronoun, forming a possessive pairing. The '-i' vowel on 'baʿd' is its case ending, set by 'baʿd's' own position in the sentence (commonly governed by a preceding preposition), not by the suffix; the attached '-hi' is the possessor ('him/it'), and as the possessed-to term it sits in the genitive. The pronoun's 'i'-vowel (-hi rather than -hu) follows because it comes after a genitive '-i'.
5.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — afterness, distance

6.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
6.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

7.meaning: their ornaments / jewelry / adornments; decorative items such as jewelry worn for beauty, here joined to a plural possessor ('their'). The base word denotes finery and ornamentation.
7.grammar: A plural noun ('ornaments') with an attached possessive '-him' ('their'). The -i ending is the oblique (genitive) case, used after a preposition or when linking to a possessor; the form '-him' (rather than '-hum') is the regular shape this pronoun takes after an '-i' vowel: 'their ornaments.'
7.root: ح-ل-ي (ḥ-l-y) — to adorn, deck with ornaments

8.meaning: a calf; a young bovine. Grammatically indefinite ('a calf'), the word names the offspring of a cow.
8.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The '-an' ending combines the accusative case (typically marking the direct object — the thing acted upon) with indefiniteness ('a calf' rather than 'the calf').
8.root: ع-ج-ل (ʿ-j-l) — connected with a calf; the same root also conveys haste

9.meaning: a body, a physical form, a lifeless figure or effigy; a corporeal frame as opposed to a living, breathing being. It often stresses mere outward shape without spirit or speech.
9.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The '-an' ending combines the accusative case (often marking a direct object, or here a descriptive/explanatory noun set beside another) with indefiniteness ('a body / a mere figure').
9.root: ج-س-د (j-s-d) — body, corporeal form

10.meaning: A two-part phrase 'for Him' or 'to Him belongs,' expressing possession, ownership, or that something is due to one masculine being.
10.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('for/to/belonging to') with its vowel shifted to 'la-' before the pronoun. The attached -hu means 'Him', so the whole means 'for Him' or 'His'; the preposition signals possession or that something is owed or directed to that person.

11.meaning: a lowing, a mooing; the sound a calf or cow makes. The word names that bellowing animal cry. Grammatically indefinite ('a lowing sound').
11.grammar: A singular masculine verbal noun naming a sound. The '-un' ending combines the nominative case (typically the subject, or the thing being affirmed to exist/belong) with indefiniteness ('a lowing sound').

12.meaning: 'Did not…?' — a particle combining a question with negation, used to ask 'Have I/has he not…?', often expecting agreement or serving as a gentle reminder.
12.grammar: An interrogative prefix 'a-' ('?') joined to the negation 'lam'. 'lam' negates a verb and places it firmly in the past ('did not'), and grammatically puts the following present-tense verb into the jussive (clipped) form. Together they form a rhetorical or confirming question.

13.meaning: To see, perceive, or behold — and, by extension, to realize, observe, or come to recognize. The bare form here is the 'cut-short' (jussive) shape used after certain particles, so it reads 'they (do not) see'.
13.grammar: A present-tense verb in its shortened (jussive) form, used after particles such as those that negate the past or express purpose/condition. The third-person masculine plural subject 'they' here takes the distinct jussive plural ending '-aw' (written wāw + a silent 'alif al-fāriqa). This '-aw' is the jussive paradigm's own ending in its own right, not the indicative '-ūna' with the 'na' stripped off.

14.meaning: 'That He …' — an emphatic particle meaning 'that / indeed' joined to the pronoun 'he'; it introduces and affirms a clause reporting something about a single masculine subject (most often Allah).
14.grammar: The emphatic particle 'anna' ('that, indeed') with the attached pronoun '-hu' ('he/it') as its subject. 'Anna' introduces a subordinate clause ('… that He …') and gives it certainty; '-hu' identifies a single masculine subject. (The pronoun is pronounced '-hu' here following the 'a' vowel.)

15.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
15.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

16.meaning: he speaks to them / addresses them; the verb means to talk to and converse with someone, conveying words to them. With the attached 'them,' it means he directs speech to a group.
16.grammar: A present/imperfect verb in an intensive pattern meaning 'to speak to / address.' The 'yu-' prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'); the final -u (on the stem) signals the plain (indicative) mood, a simple statement. The ending '-hum' is the object 'them.'
16.root: ك-ل-م (k-l-m) — to speak, utter words

17.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
17.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

18.meaning: he guides them / leads them; the verb means to show the way, direct rightly, and lead toward a goal. With the attached 'them,' it means he directs a group along a path.
18.grammar: A present/imperfect verb meaning 'to guide.' The 'ya-' prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). The ending '-him' is the object 'them' (its '-i' vowel arising from the preceding long 'ī' of the stem): 'he guides them.'

19.meaning: A way, path, road, or means — a route to a destination, hence also a way or means of accomplishing something.
19.grammar: A singular noun. The '-an' ending is accusative and indefinite: the accusative case commonly marks the direct object of a verb, and the final 'n' sound marks it indefinite ('a way'). It denotes a path one travels or a means to an end.

20.meaning: they took it / adopted it / made it their own; the past-tense act of taking something up or turning it into an object of one's choosing. With the attached 'it,' it means a group seized or adopted something.
20.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb meaning 'to take/adopt for oneself,' built on a pattern whose initial vowel 'i-' begins the word. The '-ū' ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they') acting in completed past time; the ending '-hu' is the object 'it/him': 'they took it.'

21.meaning: A compound meaning 'and they were' or 'and they used to' — it sets a state or habit in the past. The verb 'to be/become' here establishes an ongoing past condition, often paired with a following verb to express habitual action.
21.grammar: A past-tense verb ('to be') in the third-person masculine plural — the -ū ending means 'they' did/were. It commonly conveys a continued past state or habit, especially when followed by another verb. The wa- prefix means 'and.'
21.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to come into being

22.meaning: Those who do wrong — wrongdoers who put things out of their right place: unjust people, oppressors, and especially those who transgress against the truth and against the rights of Allah or of others. The root sense is placing something where it does not belong.
22.grammar: This is an active participle ('one who wrongs') made plural. The -īna ending marks a masculine plural in the accusative or genitive case — the form used when the word is an object, or follows a preposition, or is linked to a preceding noun ('of the wrongdoers').

1.meaning: A compound meaning 'and when' — it sets up a circumstance in past time, marking the moment at which something occurred, with the result clause typically following. It carries the sense of 'when, at the time that.'
1.grammar: A particle phrase introducing a past-time clause. Lammā signals 'when' for completed events and expects a following clause stating what then happened; the wa- prefix means 'and.'

2.meaning: it was dropped / made to fall / let fall; describes something brought down or cast down by an unstated agent. The passive form conveys that the falling was caused, not self-initiated. (Idiomatically the phrasing can depict overwhelming regret.)

parts.en: was made to fall, was dropped

2.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) passive verb. The 'u-i' vowel pattern (su-qi-ṭa) marks the passive — the action was done to the subject by someone unnamed. The final -a is the regular ending of a third-person masculine singular perfect verb: 'it was made to fall.'

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
3.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

4.meaning: Their hands. The plural noun 'hands' carrying the masculine plural possessive 'their'; often used idiomatically for what people do, produce, or are responsible for through their own deeds.
4.grammar: A plural noun with an attached possessive pronoun '-him' meaning 'their' (a group of males, or mixed). 'aydī' is the irregular ('broken') plural of 'yad' (hand). The pronoun ending makes the whole construction definite and possessed; the 'i'-coloured stem before the suffix reflects its genitive/possessed state, the form typically following a preposition or standing as object.
4.root: ي-د-ي (y-d-y) — hand

5.meaning: and they saw / perceived; a past-tense act of seeing with the eyes or realizing, joined to a connective 'and.' It reports that a group came to see or behold something.
5.grammar: A connective 'wa' ('and') prefixed to a past-tense (perfect) verb 'to see.' The '-aw' ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they') acting in completed past time (this verb's weak final letter yields '-aw' rather than the usual '-ū'): 'and they saw.'
5.root: ر-ء-ي (r-ʾ-y) — to see, perceive

6.meaning: 'That they…' — an emphatic connector 'anna' ('that, indeed') fused with the pronoun 'they,' used to introduce an affirmed clause as the content of a thought or statement.
6.grammar: Built on the particle 'anna' ('that…, indeed'), which introduces and affirms a following clause (often after verbs of knowing, thinking, or saying) and puts its noun into the accusative. The attached '-hum' is the pronoun 'they/them' for a male-inclusive group.

7.meaning: A short particle placed before a verb to emphasize or affirm it. Before a past-tense verb it means 'indeed / certainly / has already (happened)'; before a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes / may'. It sharpens and confirms the verb that follows.
7.grammar: An indeclinable particle (its form never changes). It does not take case or tense endings; its job is to color the following verb — affirming and intensifying a past action ('has indeed done') or signaling occasional possibility with a present verb.

8.meaning: 'they went astray / erred' — to lose the right way, to wander off into error or misguidance.
8.grammar: A past-tense verb with the -ū ending meaning 'they' (masculine plural). It conveys a completed action: 'they went astray / erred.'
8.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, lose the way, go astray

9.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
9.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.
9.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, utterance

10.meaning: An emphatic conditional opener combining an oath-like emphasis with 'if' — roughly 'most certainly, if (such-and-such happens)…', strongly stressing the condition and the response that follows.
10.grammar: Two particles fused together: an emphatic la- that signals a coming oath or strong assertion, plus in ('if') introducing a condition. Together they set up an emphatic 'if… then surely…' construction. Neither has a case ending; particles do not inflect.

11.meaning: The particle 'lam', a negating word used to push a verb into the past: it means 'did not' / 'has not'. Though it sits before a present-tense verb form, it negates the action as something that did not happen.
11.grammar: 'lam' is a negating particle that governs a following present-tense verb but gives it past meaning ('did not …'). It also puts that verb into the shortened (jussive) form. 'lam' itself carries no ending.

12.meaning: He has mercy on us / shows us mercy; the verb means to be merciful and compassionate toward someone. With the attached 'us,' it means an agent extends mercy to the speaker's group.
12.grammar: A present/imperfect verb meaning 'to have mercy on.' The 'ya-' prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'); the bare, vowelless stem-ending (rather than '-u') reflects the jussive/conditional mood, often used after particles or in 'if … then …' clauses. The ending '-nā' is the object 'us.'

13.meaning: 'Our Lord' — 'Rabb' (Lord, Master, Sustainer who creates, owns, nurtures and governs) joined to 'our'. A weighty term for Allah as the One who brings up and sustains all that exists.
13.grammar: A noun with the attached possessive pronoun '-nā' ('our'). The -u before the pronoun is the nominative case, used when the word is the subject or predicate of a sentence ('[He] is our Lord').
13.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master; lordship

14.meaning: A compound: 'and He will forgive' / 'and may He forgive'. It joins 'and' to an imperfect verb meaning to forgive, pardon, and cover over sins — to wipe away guilt and shield the wrongdoer from its consequences.
14.grammar: The wa- prefix is the connective 'and'. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). The verb stands in the jussive mood — shown by its clipped, vowel-less ending — typically appearing after certain particles or as the result-clause of a condition ('… he will forgive / that he may forgive').
14.root: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to cover, shield, and pardon; forgiveness

15.meaning: A combination of the preposition 'for / to' with the pronoun 'us', meaning 'for us' or 'to us / on our behalf'.
15.grammar: A preposition ('for / to') joined to the attached pronoun 'us'. The pronoun -nā always means 'us / our' regardless of position. Together they express benefit or direction toward the speakers ('for us').

16.meaning: We shall most certainly be — an emphatic assertion that a group will indeed come to be in some state. Carries a built-in stress: 'we will surely, definitely be'.
16.grammar: Verb 'to be' carrying strong emphasis at both ends: the prefixed la- ('surely') and the suffixed -nna (the heavy emphatic ending, 'most certainly'). The na- prefix marks a first-person plural subject ('we').
16.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to become

17.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
17.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

18.meaning: "The losers / those who lose" — an active participle for those who suffer loss, who lose out or come to ruin, especially the ultimate loss of one's own soul.
18.grammar: An active participle in the masculine sound plural with the definite article 'the'. The -īna ending marks the accusative or genitive case — the form used when such a plural is a direct object, a predicate of 'to be', or follows a preposition (as opposed to the -ūna subject form).
18.root: خ-س-ر (kh-s-r) — to lose / suffer loss / be ruined

1.meaning: A compound meaning 'and when' — it sets up a circumstance in past time, marking the moment at which something occurred, with the result clause typically following. It carries the sense of 'when, at the time that.'
1.grammar: A particle phrase introducing a past-time clause. Lammā signals 'when' for completed events and expects a following clause stating what then happened; the wa- prefix means 'and.'

2.meaning: he returned / came back / went back; a past-tense act of going back to a place or state previously left. It reports a completed return.
2.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The final -a is the regular ending marking a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') acting in completed past time: 'he returned.'

3.meaning: Mūsā (Moses), the prophet — a proper name.
3.grammar: A proper name of non-Arabic origin. It is indeclinable — its ending (the long final 'ā') does not change to show case — so the same form serves whether it functions as subject, object, or after a preposition.

4.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
4.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

5.meaning: 'His people / his folk' — the community, tribe, or nation to which a person belongs, with the attached pronoun 'his'.
5.grammar: A noun with the attached pronoun '-hi' ('his'). The '-i' ending is genitive: it typically marks the word as the object of a preposition or as linked to a preceding noun ('… of …'). The pronoun appears as '-hi' (rather than '-hu') because of this genitive '-i'.
5.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to rise; a people who stand together

6.meaning: angry, enraged, full of wrath; describing someone overcome with anger. The intensive form conveys a strong, filling emotion rather than mild displeasure.
6.grammar: An adjective in an intensive pattern ('-ān') that depicts a state filling the person (here, anger). The -a ending is accusative; for this class of word it also serves as the case marking it commonly takes when describing the state or condition in which someone does something ('he came back angry'). This pattern does not take indefinite '-an' tanwīn.

7.meaning: Deeply sorrowful, grieved, sorely distressed; describing someone overcome with sadness and regret over something that has gone wrong.
7.grammar: A stative adjective on the pattern faʿil (فَعِل), denoting one characterized by an inner state of grief (not an active participle, which would be on the pattern fāʿil). The final -an (tanwīn fatḥ) is the indefinite accusative ending, which commonly marks a word as a circumstantial description ('being grieved') or as the object of a verb.

8.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
8.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

9.meaning: A compound of censure meaning 'evil is that which' or 'wretched is what' — it expresses strong blame or disapproval of a thing about to be named. Biʾsa is the standard verb of dispraise, the opposite of 'how excellent.'
9.grammar: A verb of blame fixed in the -a form (it does not conjugate for tense), joined to mā ('that which/what'). The phrase pronounces something to be evil or wretched, with the thing blamed typically specified afterward.
9.root: ب-أ-س (b-ʾ-s) — hardship, misery, wretchedness

10.meaning: You acted as my successors / you took my place and carried on after me; said of a group who stood in for someone during their absence.
10.grammar: A past-tense verb. The suffix -tum marks 'you' (a group of males) as the doer; its vowel is lengthened to -tumū before the attached pronoun. The closing -nī ('me') is the object pronoun receiving the action.
10.root: خ-ل-ف (kh-l-f) — to succeed, come after, take the place of

11.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
11.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

12.meaning: 'After me' — the noun baʿd ('after, afterwards, the time following') joined to the possessive 'my', i.e. the period or state following the speaker.
12.grammar: A noun (baʿd, 'after') of time/sequence with the first-person possessive suffix -ī ('my') attached. The noun's original case vowel is replaced by a connecting kasra, which IS pronounced before the possessive yāʾ — hence baʿdī ('after me'). baʿd commonly functions adverbially, indicating 'following' in time.
12.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — afterness, distance, what comes later

13.meaning: Did you act hastily / were you in a rush, getting ahead of something before its due time? A question implying premature, impatient action.
13.grammar: An interrogative past-tense verb. The opening hamza (a-) turns the statement into a question ('did you…?'). The suffix -tum marks the doer as 'you,' a group of males, who completed the action in the past.

14.meaning: A matter, affair, command, or decree; can mean both 'an order given' and 'a state of affairs / business at hand,' depending on usage.
14.grammar: A noun. The final -a (fatḥa) is the accusative ending, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb or otherwise governed into the accusative case.
14.root: أ-م-ر (ʾ-m-r) — to command; an affair or matter

15.meaning: 'Your Lord' — Rabb denotes the Master, Owner, Sustainer, and Nurturer who creates, possesses, and brings each thing to its completion; joined to 'your' (plural).
15.grammar: A noun 'Lord' in the genitive case (the -i ending), which typically follows a preposition or links it to a preceding noun ('… of …'). The suffix -kum is the possessive 'your' addressed to a group.
15.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship: nurturing, mastering, owning, sustaining

16.meaning: And he threw down / flung / cast (something), often forcefully; the verb conveys casting an object away or to the ground.
16.grammar: A past-tense verb (form IV) with the prefixed conjunction wa- ('and'). With no attached subject pronoun, the form itself indicates a single male doer ('he') who completed the action; the final long -ā is the natural ending of this weak (defective) verb.
16.root: ل-ق-ي (l-q-y) — to meet, encounter; (form IV) to cast, throw, deliver

17.meaning: The tablets / writing-boards — flat slabs or panels on which something is inscribed.
17.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the tablets'); alwāḥ is the broken (irregular) plural of lawḥ, 'tablet.' The al- prefix makes it definite, and the final -a is the accusative ending, which usually marks a direct object of a verb.
17.root: ل-و-ح (l-w-ḥ) — a tablet, board, or flat plate

18.meaning: And he took hold of / seized / grasped; the verb means to take, often firmly or to take to task.
18.grammar: A past-tense verb with the prefixed conjunction wa- ('and'). With no separate subject attached, the form itself signals a single male doer ('he') who completed the action; the final -a is the standard past-tense ending.

19.meaning: By / with the head of (someone); 'head' as the part of the body, here introduced by a preposition expressing grasping by means of it.
19.grammar: A noun governed by the preposition bi- ('with / by'). The final -i (kasra) is the genitive ending, which is required after a preposition and also links a noun to a following noun ('the head OF …').

20.meaning: 'His brother' — a male sibling, joined to the possessive 'his'. The word can also extend to a close kinsman, companion, or fellow within a shared group or bond.
20.grammar: The base word 'brother' here shows the long -ī linking vowel it takes when it is possessed and stands in the genitive (the 'of' / after-preposition form). The attached -hi means 'his'; its 'i' vowel harmonises with that preceding genitive form.

21.meaning: He drags / pulls him along; an ongoing or repeated action of hauling someone toward oneself.
21.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb. The ya- prefix marks a single male doer ('he'). The -u ending is the indicative, signalling a plain, ongoing statement of fact (not a command or 'so that…'). The attached -hu ('him') is the object being dragged.
21.root: ج-ر-ر (j-r-r) — to drag, pull, draw along

22.meaning: 'To Him' or 'toward Him' — the preposition expressing direction or endpoint ('to / toward') combined with a pronoun referring to a single masculine person, indicating motion or attention directed at him.
22.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base 'ilā shifts to 'ilay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -hi is the third-person masculine singular object of a preposition, 'him'; its -i vowel is the form the pronoun takes after the 'ay' sound.

23.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
23.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

24.meaning: "son" — a male child or descendant.
24.grammar: A noun beginning with a helping (elidable) vowel. The -a ending is accusative, which marks the word as the object of a verb or as an appositive describing a preceding accusative noun. When placed between two names, it functions as "son of …"

25.meaning: 'mother; source, origin, foundation'. Umm literally means 'mother', and by extension the origin or principal thing from which others derive — the central or 'mother' instance.
25.grammar: The -a ending is the accusative case: it commonly marks the direct object of a verb, or the first term of a possession phrase when that phrase as a whole is an object ('the mother OF …'). The doubled m (umm) is part of the root itself.
25.root: ا-م-م (ʾ-m-m) — to head toward; mother, source, that which is foremost

26.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
26.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

27.meaning: the people / the folk — a body of people, a community or group regarded collectively (here in the accusative form).
27.grammar: The l- prefix is the definite article 'the'. The final -a ending is accusative. Since the verb it follows is passive (and so takes no direct object), this accusative is adverbial — marking the circumstance or setting of the action ('before / in front of the people') rather than a thing being acted upon.
27.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to arise; a people standing together

28.meaning: They reckoned me weak / treated me as feeble and of no account; to deem someone powerless and so to oppress or belittle them.
28.grammar: A past-tense verb (form X, which carries the sense of 'regarding/treating someone as'). The suffix -ū marks the doers as 'they' (a group of males) who completed the action; the final -nī ('me') is the object pronoun.
28.root: ض-ع-ف (ḍ-ʿ-f) — weakness; (form X) to deem weak, to oppress the weak

29.meaning: And they were on the verge of / nearly / were about to (do something); kāda expresses that an action came close to happening without quite occurring.

parts.en: almost / was on the point of

29.grammar: A past-tense 'verb of approach' (kāda) with prefixed wa- ('and'). It is normally paired with a following present-tense verb to mean 'almost did.' The suffix -ū marks the subject as 'they,' a group of males.
29.root: ك-و-د (k-w-d) — nearness, being on the verge of

30.meaning: They kill me / are about to kill me; an ongoing or imminent act of slaying directed at the speaker.
30.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb. The ya- prefix plus the -ūna ending mark the doers as 'they' (a group of males), and the retained -na shows the indicative — a plain statement of an ongoing/about-to-happen act. The closing -nī ('me') is the object.

31.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
31.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

32.meaning: Do not let (someone) gloat / rejoice maliciously over another's misfortune; the verb means to give an enemy cause for spiteful glee.
32.grammar: A present-tense verb (form IV, 'to make someone gloat') in the jussive mood — its ending is cut to a vowelless -t, the form used after a prohibition ('do not…') or command. The tu- prefix addresses a single person, 'you.'
32.root: ش-م-ت (sh-m-t) — malicious joy at another's misfortune

33.meaning: With me / over me / at me; the preposition bi- joined to the pronoun 'me,' expressing association, cause, or 'concerning me.'
33.grammar: A preposition (bi-) with the attached pronoun 'me.' Pronouns after a preposition stand in the genitive; here the first-person 'me' takes the form -ya, giving the sense 'with/over me.'

34.meaning: The enemies, foes, adversaries — those who bear hostility and opposition.
34.grammar: A definite plural noun; aʿdāʾ is the broken (irregular) plural of ʿaduww, 'enemy.' The al- makes it definite, and the final -a is the accusative ending, which commonly marks the word as a direct object.

35.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
35.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

36.meaning: Place me / put me / count me (among); to set someone in a category, state, or position.
36.grammar: A present-tense verb in the jussive mood — its stem ends in a vowelless -l, the form used in requests/commands and after 'do not.' The ta- prefix addresses a single 'you,' and the attached -nī ('me') is the object placed.
36.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, render, place, appoint

37.meaning: With, together with, alongside — indicating company, accompaniment, or being in the same place or time as another.
37.grammar: A preposition of accompaniment ('with, alongside'); grammatically it is an adverbial of place/time (ẓarf) that governs the genitive. It is placed before a following noun to put one thing in the company of another, and that following noun stands in the genitive. The -a is its fixed ending.

38.meaning: 'The people / the folk' — a collective noun for a community, nation, or group of people regarded as a body. Often it carries the nuance of one's own people or a particular group sharing a trait.
38.grammar: A collective noun with the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The final '-i' is the genitive ending, which typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun in an 'of …' relationship.
38.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand/rise; a people, community

39.meaning: The wrongdoers — those who do wrong or injustice; literally those who put things out of their rightful place, transgressing limits and harming themselves or others. The root sense is darkness.
39.grammar: 'al-' is 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the 'ẓ', doubling it). The stem is an active participle ('one who wrongs') made plural for masculine people. The -īna ending is the object/genitive form of the sound masculine plural, marking the word as an object of a verb or governed by a preposition.

1.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
1.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

2.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'my': the One who owns, sustains, nurtures, and governs — combining mastery, ownership, and loving cultivation. With the attached 'my' it is an intimate address, 'my Lord.'
2.grammar: A noun, rabb, with the first-person possessive (the original 'my' yāʾ being reduced to a final -i, so 'my Lord'). The word denotes the Master who creates, owns, and lovingly sustains. Used as a heartfelt vocative, calling upon one's Lord.
2.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

3.meaning: Forgive! — a plea or command to pardon, to cover over and blot out wrongdoing. It carries the sense of veiling a fault so it is no longer held against the offender.
3.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a single person: 'forgive!'. The vowelless final -r reflects the imperative form. It is commonly followed by 'us' or 'for me' to specify whom to pardon.
3.root: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to cover, conceal, and pardon; mercy that blots out sin

4.meaning: 'to Me' or 'for Me' — the preposition 'to/for' fused with the first-person pronoun, expressing direction, benefit, or belonging toward the speaker.
4.grammar: A preposition ('to/for') with the attached pronoun '-ī' ('me'). Together they express benefit, direction, or attribution toward the first person.

5.meaning: And for / to my brother; the kinsman 'brother,' joined to 'and' and a preposition meaning 'for / belonging to,' with 'my' attached.
5.grammar: The noun 'brother' carries the conjunction wa- ('and') and the preposition li- ('for / to'). The final -ī is the attached possessive pronoun 'my.' After a preposition the noun stands in the genitive, here absorbed into the possessive ending.
5.root: أ-خ-و (ʾ-kh-w) — brotherhood, a brother

6.meaning: And admit us / cause us to enter; to bring a group inside or into a state or place.
6.grammar: A Form IV causative imperative (a command, amr: 'make/let enter'), prefixed with wa- ('and'). The opening hamza (a-) is the imperative hamza of Form IV, not a present-tense prefix — the corresponding present tense would instead begin with tu- (tudkhilu). The command addresses a single 'you' as the doer, and -nā ('us') is the object being admitted.
6.root: د-خ-ل (d-kh-l) — to enter; (form IV) to bring/make enter

7.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
7.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

8.meaning: Your mercy / Your compassion — mercy understood as active tenderness, care, and the will to relieve and forgive, here possessed by the One addressed.
8.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The -i is the genitive ending (seen on the t before the suffix), the case used after a preposition or when a noun is possessed. The final -ka is 'your,' addressing a single male.

9.meaning: 'And You' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'you' (addressing a single male). The independent pronoun stresses the subject, as in 'and You [Yourself] …'.
9.grammar: A connective 'and' plus a detached subject pronoun. 'anta' is the masculine-singular 'you'; as a standalone pronoun it adds emphasis or introduces a statement about the addressee ('You are …').

10.meaning: Most merciful / more merciful — the superlative or comparative of 'merciful': the one whose mercy surpasses all others'.
10.grammar: A comparative/superlative adjective on the pattern afʿal ('most/more …'). The final -u (ḍamma) is the nominative ending, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or a word standing as a predicate.

11.meaning: The merciful ones / those who show mercy — people characterized by compassion and tenderness toward others.
11.grammar: A definite active participle (pattern fāʿil) in the masculine plural ('the merciful ones'). The ending -īna is the plural form used in the genitive or accusative case — typically when the word follows a preposition, is possessed ('… OF the merciful'), or is a direct object.

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: Past-tense verb (reflexive form), third person plural: 'they took for themselves, adopted, chose.' A completed act of taking something on as one's own.
3.grammar: A completed-action (past) verb in a reflexive pattern (taking something for oneself). The '-ū' ending (with silent trailing alif) marks the subject as 'they' (masculine plural). The opening 'i-' is a helping vowel that lets the cluster of consonants be pronounced.

4.meaning: 'The calf' — a young bovine; the offspring of a cow.
4.grammar: A definite noun ('the calf'). The '-a' ending is the accusative case, which commonly marks the direct object of a verb (the thing taken or acted upon).
4.root: ع-ج-ل (ʿ-j-l) — calf; (also haste)

5.meaning: It will reach them / overtake them / befall them; the verb nāla means to attain or obtain, and so for something to come upon a group.
5.grammar: A present-tense verb made future by the prefix sa- ('will, shortly'). The ya- marks a single masculine subject ('it/he'), and the -u ending is the indicative — a plain statement of fact. The attached -hum ('them') is the object reached.
5.root: ن-ي-ل (n-y-l) — to attain, reach, obtain, befall

6.meaning: Anger, wrath, indignation — intense displeasure; when ascribed to Allah it denotes His just rejection and condemnation of wrongdoing, free of human passion.
6.grammar: A noun. The final -un (tanwīn ḍamm) is the indefinite nominative ending, the case used for the subject of a sentence ('[some] wrath …'), and the tanwīn marks it as indefinite ('a/an').

7.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
7.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

8.meaning: 'Their Lord / their Sustainer.' The noun 'rabb' — a master who owns, nurtures, sustains, and brings to maturity all under His care — joined to 'their.' It conveys far more than 'lord': the one who creates, provides for, and governs His servants.
8.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun -him ('their,' masculine plural). The -i ending is the genitive case, which typically appears after a preposition or links the word to another in an 'of / belonging to' relationship; here it pairs with the attached 'their.'
8.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master; lordship, ownership, care

9.meaning: And lowliness / humiliation / abasement — a state of disgrace and being brought low.
9.grammar: A noun with prefixed wa- ('and'). The final -un (tanwīn ḍamm) is the indefinite nominative ending, used for the subject of a sentence, with the tanwīn marking it as indefinite ('a/an').
9.root: ذ-ل-ل (dh-l-l) — lowliness, humility, abasement

10.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
10.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

11.meaning: 'The life' — living existence, the state of being alive.
11.grammar: The definite article al- with the feminine noun ḥayāt ('life'); the waw belongs to the stem and the tā' marbūṭa is its feminine suffix. The final -i is the genitive case vowel, which typically marks the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to a following noun.

12.meaning: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
12.grammar: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
12.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world

13.meaning: 'And likewise / and in the same way / and thus' — a connective phrase pointing back to a manner just mentioned and saying 'in that very way…'. Built from 'and' + 'like' + 'that'.
13.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'; the prefix ka- means 'like/as'; 'dhālika' is the demonstrative 'that' (pointing to something distant or already mentioned). Because ka- acts like a preposition, the word after it stands in the genitive, though the demonstrative 'dhālika' keeps a fixed form and shows no visible case change. The whole means 'and just like that / and thus'.

14.meaning: 'We reward / We requite' — to repay or recompense someone for their deeds, whether with good or with due consequence.
14.grammar: A present-tense verb. The 'na-' prefix means 'we'. The stem ends in a long '-ī' (a weak final root letter); in the plain indicative this final '-ī' is what is heard, giving 'we reward'.
14.root: ج-ز-ي (j-z-y) — to repay, to recompense, to requite

15.meaning: Those who fabricate and invent falsehood — people who deliberately concoct lies, especially lies attributed to Allah or about sacred matters. The active participle names the doers of such fabrication.
15.grammar: A definite masculine plural active participle ('the ones who fabricate'). The -īna ending is the sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) case, used when the word is a direct object or follows a preposition, as opposed to the -ūna form used for the subject.
15.root: ف-ر-ي (f-r-y) — to fabricate, invent, concoct (a lie)

1.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

2.meaning: They did / they worked — to perform a deed or action, to do work. The base word covers purposeful action and labor.
2.grammar: A completed-action (past-tense) verb. The -ū ending marks 'they' (a group of males) as the doers (the silent alif after it is a spelling convention).
2.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, act, work, perform a deed

3.meaning: 'The evil deeds / bad actions' — plural of sayyi'a, a wrong or evil act, a misdeed or sin; the opposite of a good deed.
3.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun ('the misdeeds'). The -i ending here is the case marker for the sound feminine plural in the genitive/accusative state, typically signalling that it follows a preposition, links to a preceding noun, or stands as an object.
3.root: س-و-أ (s-w-ʾ) — to be bad/evil; misdeed, wrong

4.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
4.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

5.meaning: They turned back in repentance — a third-person masculine plural past verb meaning 'they repented,' i.e. they returned to Allah, abandoning sin and re-orienting the heart toward Him.
5.grammar: Past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks the subject as 'they' (a group of males or mixed). As a perfect verb it presents the action as completed: 'they turned (back) in repentance.'
5.root: ت-و-ب (t-w-b) — turning back, repenting

6.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
6.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

7.meaning: After it / afterward — a time expression meaning the period following something previously mentioned, with an attached pronoun referring back to a feminine or abstract antecedent.
7.grammar: The noun 'after' carries the -i (genitive) ending because it functions as an adverb of time in the oblique case and is in a possessive construction with the following pronoun. The suffix -hā means 'her/it,' referring to a feminine or abstract thing.
7.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — afterness, being subsequent in time or place

8.meaning: And they believed — they came to faith, placing trust and secure conviction (in Allah and His message). The verb conveys an inner act of believing and committing.
8.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in Form IV with the subject suffix -ū meaning 'they' (masculine plural). It reports a completed act of coming to faith. The wa- prefix is the connective 'and.'
8.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — security, trust, faith; to be safe and to give one's trust

9.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
9.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

10.meaning: 'Your Lord' — the noun 'Lord' (Master, Sustainer, Owner, the One who nurtures and brings to completion) combined with 'your'. 'Rabb' carries the linked senses of ownership, authority, and ongoing care that raises a thing to its perfection.
10.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive. The -a ending is accusative, which typically marks the word as a direct object or governed element. The attached -ka means 'your', addressed to a single male.
10.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, nurturing care, ownership and mastery

11.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
11.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

12.meaning: After it / afterward — a time expression meaning the period following something previously mentioned, with an attached pronoun referring back to a feminine or abstract antecedent.
12.grammar: The noun 'after' carries the -i (genitive) ending because it functions as an adverb of time in the oblique case and is in a possessive construction with the following pronoun. The suffix -hā means 'her/it,' referring to a feminine or abstract thing.
12.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — afterness, being subsequent in time or place

13.meaning: Surely most forgiving — abundantly and repeatedly forgiving, One who covers over and pardons sins again and again. The intensive form stresses the fullness and constancy of the forgiving.
13.grammar: The prefix la- is an emphatic 'surely/indeed' (often answering or stressing a statement). The stem is the intensive adjective 'faʿūl' ('much-forgiving'). The final -un is the nominative case with nunation, typically marking a predicate ('… is surely Most-Forgiving'). It conveys constant, abundant forgiveness.
13.root: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to forgive, cover over, pardon

14.meaning: Most merciful, ever-merciful; one whose mercy is constant and abundant. As a divine attribute it denotes Allah's enduring, all-embracing compassion toward His creation.
14.grammar: An intensive adjective on the form faʿīl ('abundantly/constantly merciful'). The ending -un (tanwīn) is the nominative case with indefiniteness, the form typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it ('[He] is most merciful').

1.meaning: A compound meaning 'and when' — it sets up a circumstance in past time, marking the moment at which something occurred, with the result clause typically following. It carries the sense of 'when, at the time that.'
1.grammar: A particle phrase introducing a past-time clause. Lammā signals 'when' for completed events and expects a following clause stating what then happened; the wa- prefix means 'and.'

2.meaning: It subsided / fell silent / was stilled — said of anger, emotion, or sound that calms down and ceases. The verb pictures a turbulent thing growing quiet.

parts.en: it became calm / fell silent (he/it, masculine singular, past)

2.grammar: A simple past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person masculine singular. The third-person masculine singular has no separate suffix; the bare stem ending in -a expresses 'he/it did' as a completed event.

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on behalf of,' 'for,' 'about,' or 'away from.' It often conveys removing a burden from someone or acting in their place.

parts.en: on behalf of / for / away from

3.grammar: A preposition (a linking particle). It governs the noun that follows it, putting that noun into the genitive case. It does not change form.

4.meaning: Mūsā (Moses) — the proper name of the prophet Mūsā. As a foreign/proper name it does not derive from an Arabic root.
4.grammar: A proper noun (personal name). It is grammatically indeclinable: the final long -ā does not change for case, so the same form serves whether the name is subject, object, or possessor.

5.meaning: The anger — intense displeasure and wrath. The word denotes a strong emotion of indignation, whether of a person or, in a fitting sense, the wrath of Allah.
5.grammar: A definite singular noun. The final -u marks the nominative case, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence.
5.root: غ-ض-ب (gh-ḍ-b) — anger, wrath, indignation

6.meaning: He took, he seized — a past-tense verb meaning to take hold of, receive, or take up. With certain objects (like a covenant or pledge) it carries the sense of formally taking or binding. The subject is 'he'.
6.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The bare stem with the final -a marks a completed action by a 'he' (third-person masculine singular) subject — 'he took'.

7.meaning: The tablets — flat slabs or boards used as a writing surface. The plural refers to inscribed tablets such as those on which scripture or law is written.
7.grammar: A definite broken (irregular) plural of lawḥ ('tablet'). The final -a marks the accusative case, the form used when the noun is the direct object of a verb.
7.root: ل-و-ح (l-w-ḥ) — a tablet, board, or flat plate for writing

8.meaning: 'And in' — the connector 'and' joined to the preposition 'in / within / during.'
8.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the preposition fī ('in'). Fī governs the following noun, putting it into the genitive case. Neither particle changes form.

9.meaning: Its copy / its inscription / its written content — the text written upon something, with an attached pronoun pointing to what was inscribed (a feminine/abstract antecedent).
9.grammar: A feminine singular noun bearing the -i (genitive) ending because it is joined in a possessive construction to the following pronoun. The suffix -hā means 'its/her,' referring back to a feminine or abstract thing.
9.root: ن-س-خ (n-s-kh) — to copy, transcribe, write out (also to abrogate/supersede)

10.meaning: Guidance — right direction, the showing of the correct way and the leading along it. The term combines pointing out the path and granting success in following it; more than mere information, it is direction toward what is right.

parts.en: indefinite (tanwin) ending on a shortened final vowel

10.grammar: An indefinite masculine singular noun. The -an (tanwin) ending marks indefiniteness — 'a guidance' rather than 'the guidance'. Because the word ends in a weak final letter, its case is not audibly distinguished, so this single form covers more than one grammatical position.

11.meaning: And mercy — compassion, tenderness, and active kindness shown to others; clemency that issues in relief and care.
11.grammar: An indefinite feminine singular noun. The ending -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a mercy') and in the nominative case, the form used for a subject or for something simply being named. The wa- prefix is 'and.'

12.meaning: 'For/to those who …' — a preposition 'for / to / belonging to' joined to the masculine plural relative pronoun 'those who,' which introduces a description of a group by something they do.
12.grammar: The preposition li- ('for / to / belonging to') fused with the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'). Relative pronouns like this do not change for case; they point ahead to a clause that describes the group ('those who …').

13.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
13.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

14.meaning: For / to their Lord — directed toward the Lord (Rabb): the One who creates, owns, sustains, and nurtures, guiding His creation to its completion. The phrase links an attitude or action to Him.
14.grammar: The preposition li- ('for/to') puts the noun in the genitive case (seen in the -i of rabbi). 'Rabb' is then joined to the possessive suffix -him ('their,' masculine plural). The whole phrase marks a relation directed toward the Lord.
14.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, ownership, nurturing and sustaining mastery

15.meaning: They hold in awe / they are in reverent dread — they feel a fear mixed with reverence that makes them shrink back. The verb conveys awe-filled apprehension before something great.
15.grammar: A present/imperfect verb. The ya- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks 'they' (masculine plural) acting in the present or ongoing/habitual sense. The -ūna ending also shows the verb is in its base (indicative) mood, the form used for plain statements.
15.root: ر-ه-ب (r-h-b) — fear, awe, reverent dread

1.meaning: And he chose / selected — he picked out and preferred some over others. The Form VIII verb stresses a deliberate, discriminating selection.

parts.en: he chose / selected (he/it, masculine singular, past)

1.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in Form VIII, third-person masculine singular ('he chose'). The third-person masculine singular has no separate suffix; the bare stem ending in -a reports a completed act. The wa- prefix is 'and.'
1.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — goodness; to choose what is best, to prefer

2.meaning: Mūsā (Moses) — the proper name of the prophet. As a name it has no Arabic root meaning; it is a non-inflecting (indeclinable) noun whose ending does not change for case.
2.grammar: A proper name ending in a fixed long -ā (written as alif maqṣūra). It is fully indeclinable (invariable): the final -ā never changes, so the word shows no case distinction at all — it looks and sounds identical whether subject, object, or possessor. (This is unlike a diptote, which still alternates between two case vowels; here there is no alternation.)

3.meaning: His people / his folk — the community, nation, or kinfolk belonging to him, with the attached pronoun marking possession.
3.grammar: A noun with the accusative -a ending, the form used when the word is a direct object, followed by the possessive suffix -hu ('his,' masculine singular).
3.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand/rise; a group that stands together, a people

4.meaning: Seventy — the cardinal number 70. It can also stand more loosely for a large, indefinite count.
4.grammar: A 'tens' number formed like a sound masculine plural. The -īna ending marks the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) case, used when the number stands as an object or after a preposition, as opposed to the -ūna form used for the subject.
4.root: س-ب-ع (s-b-ʿ) — the number seven

5.meaning: 'A man' — an adult male human being. The word denotes a man specifically as a male individual, often with a sense of full-grown manhood.
5.grammar: A singular indefinite noun. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥ) marks the indefinite accusative, typically the case of a direct object or of a predicate following certain particles.
5.root: ر-ج-ل (r-j-l) — manhood, the adult male; (also the foot/to go on foot)

6.meaning: For Our appointed time / appointed meeting — a fixed term or set tryst, an appointment whose time and place are determined; here joined to a pronoun marking it as belonging to the speaker (plural 'Our').

parts.en: appointed time / fixed term or place

6.grammar: The preposition li- ('for/to') governs the noun in the genitive case (the -i ending), and the noun is joined to the possessive suffix -nā ('our'). The phrase marks something set toward or for an appointed time.
6.root: و-ق-ت (w-q-t) — time, a fixed or appointed moment

7.meaning: A connector meaning 'then, when' — it joins to what came before ('then/so') and sets up a 'when…' clause whose outcome follows. It frames a moment: 'and then, at the point when…'.
7.grammar: A compound of the connecting particle fa- ('then/so', linking to the preceding statement) and lammā, a particle meaning 'when' that introduces a past circumstance and leads the listener to expect a following result clause.

8.meaning: It seized them / overtook them — it took hold of them suddenly and forcibly, as a punishment, calamity, or overpowering event grips its victims.
8.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The -t marks a feminine singular subject ('she/it seized'), and the attached -humu is the object 'them' (masculine plural). The final vowel on -humu is a connecting helper before the next word.

9.meaning: The earthquake — a violent shaking or convulsion of the ground; a definite singular noun naming the quaking event itself.
9.grammar: A definite singular noun. The prefixed al- ('the') has its 'l' assimilated into the following 'r' (pronounced ar-rajfa). The unit ending -t (tā' marbūṭa) often marks a single instance of an action. The final -u marks the nominative case — typically the subject of a sentence.
9.root: ر-ج-ف (r-j-f) — to quake, shake violently, convulse

10.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
10.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

11.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'my': the One who owns, sustains, nurtures, and governs — combining mastery, ownership, and loving cultivation. With the attached 'my' it is an intimate address, 'my Lord.'
11.grammar: A noun, rabb, with the first-person possessive (the original 'my' yāʾ being reduced to a final -i, so 'my Lord'). The word denotes the Master who creates, owns, and lovingly sustains. Used as a heartfelt vocative, calling upon one's Lord.
11.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

12.meaning: A conditional particle introducing a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact supposition: 'if (it were the case that…)'. It typically presents a condition that is unfulfilled or merely imagined, often implying the result did not or would not happen.
12.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case ending). It signals a hypothetical 'if': it sets up a supposed condition whose consequence is then stated, frequently with the sense 'if X were so, then Y would be so' — often where X is contrary to fact.

13.meaning: You willed / you wished — you chose and intended something to be. The verb expresses an act of will and desire on the part of the one addressed.
13.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb with the subject suffix -ta meaning 'you' (a single male addressee). It reports a completed act of willing.
13.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — to will, to wish; the root behind 'thing'

14.meaning: You destroyed them / caused them to perish — you brought them to ruin and made them die out. The Form IV verb means to cause destruction, with an object 'them.'
14.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in Form IV (causative: 'to make perish'). The suffix -ta is the subject 'you' (single male addressee), and -hum is the object 'them' (masculine plural).

15.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
15.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

16.meaning: An adverb of time meaning 'before / beforehand / previously,' pointing to a moment or state that precedes something else in time. When used with the final vowel -u (qablu), it stands cut off from an explicit following noun, conveying 'before(hand)' or 'previously' in an absolute sense — the thing it is 'before' is understood rather than stated.
16.grammar: An adverb of time. The final -u ending here is the indeclinable (mabnī) form taken when the word is severed from a following genitive: rather than 'before X,' it means 'before(hand)' on its own, with the reference point left implicit.
16.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to come before, precede, be in front; to receive/accept

17.meaning: 'And Me / Me alone' — an emphatic, standalone object pronoun singling out 'me' as the one acted upon, with prefixed 'wa' ('and'). The word 'iyyā' exists only to carry an object pronoun when it stands apart from its verb.
17.grammar: 'And' (wa) plus the special object-pronoun carrier 'iyyā' bearing the suffix '-ya' ('me'). This construction places the object first for emphasis or exclusivity ('and Me — specifically Me'); it does not change for case, and '-ya' marks the first-person singular as the object.
17.root: — (pronoun construction; no root)

18.meaning: Will You destroy us? / Would You cause us to perish? — a present-tense verb of causing ruin, addressed to a single 'You,' fronted by the questioning particle, with 'us' as its object.
