33.grammar: An imperative (command) verb. The -ū ending directs the command at a group ('you all, eat!'). This verb's command form drops its original first root letter, so the stem appears simply as kul-. The silent alif written after the wāw is a spelling convention for the plural ending.

34.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
34.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

35.meaning: 'Good things' — wholesome, pure, pleasant things; that which is lawful, agreeable, and beneficial, especially good foods. A feminine plural of an adjective used as a noun.
35.grammar: A sound feminine plural noun. The ending -āt marks it as a feminine plural ('good things'). The final -i vowel is the genitive case, which typically links the word to a following noun ('the good things OF…') or follows a preposition. For this plural pattern the genitive and accusative share the same -i form.

36.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
36.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

37.meaning: 'We provided you' / 'we granted you sustenance' — to bestow provision, livelihood, or sustenance upon someone. Marked for a 'we' subject acting upon 'you (plural)'.
37.grammar: A past-tense verb carrying two attached pronouns. The first suffix -nā marks the doer, 'we'; the second suffix -kum marks the receiver, 'you (plural)'. So the form means 'we provided you'. The verb denotes granting provision or sustenance.

38.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
38.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

39.meaning: 'They wronged us' — to act unjustly, to wrong or oppress. Built on the past-tense verb 'they wronged' with an attached 'us' as the one wronged. The root's core image is putting something out of its rightful place.
39.grammar: A past-tense verb with attached subject and object. The -ū ending marks a plural 'they' as the doers; the suffix -nā marks 'us' as the ones acted upon — together 'they wronged us'. The silent alif after the wāw is the standard spelling of the plural ending.
39.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — wrongdoing, injustice, oppression (lit. misplacing something)

40.meaning: 'But / however / yet' — a particle of correction and contrast that sets aside what came before and affirms something different instead.
40.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to lākin ('but / however'). Lākin is a particle of rectification: it draws a contrast with, or corrects, the preceding idea and introduces an opposing or qualifying statement ('... but rather...').

41.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
41.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
41.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

42.meaning: A noun meaning 'their own selves' or 'themselves' — the plural of 'nafs' (self, soul, person, inner self), joined to the pronoun 'their.' It commonly conveys the reflexive idea of acting upon one's own self.
42.grammar: A noun (a broken/irregular plural of 'nafs') with the attached possessive pronoun '-hum' ('their/them,' masculine plural). The -a case ending before the pronoun is accusative, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb — i.e. the self upon which the action falls.

43.meaning: 'They wrong / they do wrong' — to act unjustly or oppressively, presented as an ongoing or repeated action. The same root pictures putting things out of their proper place.
43.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb. The ya- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks a plural masculine 'they' doing the action now or habitually ('they wrong / keep wronging'). The full -ūna ending (with its final -na) is the mark of the ordinary, uninterrupted present tense for a plural subject.

1.meaning: 'And when / and at the time when' — the connective 'and' joined to a word that points to a past moment or circumstance ('when'), introducing the recollection of an event or situation.
1.grammar: A connective particle plus a time-word. The wa- prefix means 'and'. 'Idh' is an invariable adverb pointing to a definite time in the past ('when, at the moment that'); it has no case ending and typically introduces a clause recalling a past event.

2.meaning: 'It was said' — speech was uttered or a statement was made. The passive form: the saying is reported without naming who spoke.

parts.en: was said (passive verb stem of the root q-w-l)
he/it (default short vowel of the 3rd masc. sg. past)

2.grammar: A past-tense verb in the passive voice (pattern qīla) from the hollow root ق-و-ل. The passive is formed by internal vowel change: the middle radical (wāw) is replaced by a long 'ī', which marks the verb as passive (the doer is left unnamed). The lām is the third root letter, not an ending; the final -a is simply the default short vowel of the third-person masculine singular past, here used impersonally as 'it was said'.

3.meaning: To them / for them — the preposition li- ('to, for') joined to the pronoun 'them'. It expresses that something is directed toward, belongs to, or is for the benefit of a group.
3.grammar: The preposition li- ('to/for') combined with the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). When li- takes a pronoun its vowel becomes 'la-'. The final -u here is a connecting vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word; it carries no case meaning of its own.

4.meaning: Dwell! / Reside! / Live (in a place)! — a command to settle down and inhabit, to take up residence and remain at rest in a location. The root also conveys stillness and tranquility.
4.grammar: An imperative (command) verb in the basic (faʿala) form. The suffix -ū addresses a masculine plural 'you all', issuing the order to several people. The initial u- is a helping (prosthetic) vowel whose u-sound matches the verb's inner vowel; it carries no separate meaning.
4.root: س-ك-ن (s-k-n) — to dwell, settle, be still and at rest

5.meaning: This (feminine) — a pointing word ('this one here') used for a single nearby thing that is grammatically feminine.
5.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun ('this') for a single feminine thing close at hand. It is fixed in form and does not change for case; it commonly precedes the noun it points to.

6.meaning: 'The town' / 'the settlement' — a populated place, village, or town where people gather and dwell. Carries the definite article 'the'.
6.grammar: A definite feminine noun ('the town'). The -a final vowel is accusative, the case typically marking the direct object of a verb (the thing entered or acted upon). The -at- is the feminine noun-ending (the 'tied tā'). The al- prefix makes it 'the' specific town.
6.root: ق-ر-ي (q-r-y) — to gather; a place where people are gathered (settlement)

7.meaning: A command, 'and eat.' To consume food; addressed to a group, directing them to partake.
7.grammar: A command verb ('eat!') addressed to a masculine-plural 'you,' marked by the -ū ending; as a command it has no final -na, and the original first root letter is dropped in this imperative. Wa- means 'and.'

8.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'min' ('from / out of / some of') joined to the pronoun 'it' (feminine). Together: 'from it / out of it / of it,' indicating a source or a portion taken from a feminine thing.
8.grammar: A preposition 'min' with the attached pronoun '-hā' ('it/her'), referring to a feminine noun. 'Min' indicates origin, source, or a part taken from a whole; the attached pronoun is in the object form required after a preposition.

9.meaning: Wherever / in whatever place — an adverb pointing to an unspecified location, 'in the place where ...'.
9.grammar: An invariable adverb of place ('where / wherever'). Although it ends in -u, it is fixed in form and does not change for case; it is normally followed by a clause stating the situation tied to that place.

10.meaning: 'You wished / you willed' — to want, will, or desire something. Past tense, addressed to a group: 'you (all) wished'.
10.grammar: A past-tense verb. The suffix -tum marks the doer as a plural 'you (all)', giving 'you wished'. It denotes an act of will or desire. The stem carries a hamza (the glottal catch written ئ).
10.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-') — willing, wishing; (the same root gives the word 'thing')

11.meaning: And say! / and speak! — a command to a group to utter or express something in words.
11.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a group. The -ū ending marks a masculine-plural command ('you all, say!'). Because it is a command, it has no subject prefix and drops the final -na that a plain statement ('you say') would carry; the silent alif after the -ū is just a spelling convention.

12.meaning: 'Removal of the burden of sin' — a request for one's sins or burdens to be taken away; a plea for relief from the weight of wrongdoing. The root's core sense is the putting-down or lowering of a load.
12.grammar: An indefinite feminine noun. The ending -un is the indefinite nominative, the case that typically marks the subject of a sentence or a stand-alone naming/exclamatory statement ('[may there be] relief from sin!'). The -at- is the feminine noun-ending. The doubled middle letter (shadda) is part of the word, not an ending.
12.root: ح-ط-ط (ḥ-ṭ-ṭ) — to put down, lower, lay down a load

13.meaning: 'And enter!' — a command to a group to go into a place, joined by 'and'.
13.grammar: An imperative (command) verb joined by wa- 'and'. The -ū ending directs the command at a group ('you all, enter!'). The initial alif of the stem is a helping-vowel that lets the word begin; it drops in pronunciation after the connecting 'and', so the two run together. The silent alif after the wāw spells the plural ending.

14.meaning: 'The gate' / 'the door' — an entrance, doorway, or gateway. Carries the definite article 'the'.
14.grammar: A definite noun ('the gate'). The -a ending is accusative, the case typically marking the direct object of a verb (the thing entered or acted upon). The al- prefix makes it 'the' specific gate.

15.meaning: 'Prostrating' / 'in prostration' — bowing down low with the face to the ground, the posture of deepest humility and worship. A plural describing a group in that humble, bowed state.
15.grammar: A plural active descriptor ('those prostrating'). The -an ending is the indefinite accusative, which here works adverbially — describing the manner or state in which the subject acts (i.e. doing something 'while prostrating'). The doubled middle letter marks the intensive plural pattern used for a group performing the action.
15.root: س-ج-د (s-j-d) — prostration, bowing down in worship

16.meaning: A first-person plural verb meaning 'we forgive / we pardon, cover over, and blot out (sins)'. The underlying sense is of veiling or covering a wrong so that it is no longer held against the person.

parts.en: we (subject prefix, with an extra assimilated 'n' fused onto it)

16.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb in the first-person plural, in the jussive (apocopate) mood shown by the bare, vowelless ending (-r with sukūn) — the form that follows conditional particles ('if … we forgive') or commands, carrying a present-or-future sense rather than completed action. The doubling (shaddah) on the initial nūn is not part of the verb itself: it arises when the final nūn of a preceding particle (such as 'an, 'if/that') is assimilated forward onto the verb's own subject-prefix nūn, so two n-sounds merge into one geminated نّ.
16.root: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to cover, veil, and so pardon/forgive

17.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
17.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

18.meaning: Your sins / wrongdoings / faults — moral lapses and errors, the offenses one commits. The plural denotes a collection of such faults, and the pronoun assigns them to a group of people ('your', plural).
18.grammar: A feminine plural noun ('sins/faults', plural ending -āt) with an attached possessive pronoun. The -i ending is genitive, which typically links the word to a following possessor, follows a preposition or oath particle. The suffix -kum means 'your' addressed to a masculine plural 'you all', identifying the owners of the sins.
18.root: خ-ط-أ (kh-ṭ-ʾ) — to err, do wrong, sin, miss the mark

19.meaning: We shall increase / We will add more — to give an increase, to add to an amount so it grows. The prefixed particle fixes the action firmly in the future ('we will surely increase').
19.grammar: A present/imperfect verb made future by the prefixed particle sa- ('shall/will'). The na- prefix marks a first-person plural subject ('we'). The final -u ending is the indicative mood, the default form for a plain statement of what will happen. The combination means 'we will increase/add'.
19.root: ز-ي-د (z-y-d) — to increase, grow, add, exceed

20.meaning: 'The doers of good / those who act with excellence and beauty'. It denotes people who do what is good and do it well — acting righteously, generously, and with sincerity, as if conscious of being watched by Allah.

parts.en: good-doers / those who excel in doing good

20.grammar: A definite plural active participle (the 'doer' form of the verb 'to do good'). The prefixed al- means 'the'. The ending -īna marks a sound masculine plural in the object/oblique state — the form used when the noun is a direct object or follows a preposition. It refers to male (or mixed) persons characterized by the action.
20.root: ح-س-ن (ḥ-s-n) — to be good, beautiful; to do well and excellently

1.meaning: 'Then/so he changed, altered, or substituted (one thing for another)'. The verb is intensive: it means to exchange a thing for something different, replacing it.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third-person masculine singular ('he …'), with the prefixed connector fa- ('then/so', often showing sequence or consequence). The doubled middle consonant marks the intensive form (deliberate, thorough substitution). The final -a is the standard past-tense ending for a completed act done by 'he'.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: 'They wronged / did injustice / acted unjustly'. The core idea is putting something out of its rightful place — oppression, transgression, or wronging oneself or others.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb with the plural subject ending -ū ('they', masculine/mixed group), referring to a completed action done by many. The -ū suffix is written with a silent 'alif' after it. It states that a group performed the act of wronging.
3.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — to wrong, oppress; to put a thing out of its proper place

4.meaning: From them / among them — the preposition min ('from, out of, part of') joined to the pronoun 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
4.grammar: The preposition min ('from / among / part of') with the attached third-person masculine plural pronoun -hum ('them'). Pronouns after a preposition are in the genitive; the combination expresses origin, partition ('some of them'), or belonging to that group.
4.root: — (preposition with pronoun, no root)

5.meaning: 'A saying / word / statement' — an utterance or speech; that which is said.
5.grammar: A verbal noun meaning 'a saying.' The ending -an is the indefinite accusative (tanwīn fatḥ): it marks an indefinite noun in the accusative case, the form used for the object of a verb (e.g., 'to say a word') among other roles.
5.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say / speak / utter

6.meaning: 'Other than / different from / not'. A noun used to express difference or negation — 'something other than X', and so 'not-X'. It functions to exclude or contrast with what follows.
6.grammar: A noun of difference/exception. The -a ending marks the accusative case, the form it takes when it serves as a direct object or as a descriptive substitute standing in an object position; it governs a following noun in the genitive ('other than …'). That it takes case endings and tanwīn confirms it is a true noun, not a particle.
6.root: غ-ي-ر (gh-y-r) — to be other, different; otherness, change

7.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
7.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

8.meaning: 'It was said' — speech was uttered or a statement was made. The passive form: the saying is reported without naming who spoke.

parts.en: was said (passive verb stem of the root q-w-l)
he/it (default short vowel of the 3rd masc. sg. past)

8.grammar: A past-tense verb in the passive voice (pattern qīla) from the hollow root ق-و-ل. The passive is formed by internal vowel change: the middle radical (wāw) is replaced by a long 'ī', which marks the verb as passive (the doer is left unnamed). The lām is the third root letter, not an ending; the final -a is simply the default short vowel of the third-person masculine singular past, here used impersonally as 'it was said'.

9.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
9.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

10.meaning: So We sent / dispatched — to send forth a messenger, a message, or (as here) something loosed upon people. The form has the subject 'we'.
10.grammar: A past-tense verb in the form IV pattern (arsala, 'to send'), with the attached subject pronoun -nā ('we'). The fa- prefix marks consequence or sequence ('so, then'). The -nā ending shows that 'we' performed the completed action.

11.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
11.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
11.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

12.meaning: 'A torment / plague / punishment / scourge'. It names a defiling, distressing affliction sent as a penalty — a foul, agitating chastisement.
12.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The ending -an (tanwīn fatḥa) marks the accusative used indefinitely — typically the direct object of a verb ('He sent down a punishment'). The nunation signals 'a/an', i.e. some unspecified instance.

13.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
13.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

14.meaning: The sky or heaven — the canopy overhead; the expanse above the earth, also that which is elevated or raised over something. With the definite article it means 'the sky / the heaven'.
14.grammar: A noun with the definite article al- ('the'), in the genitive marked by the -i ending. (The 'l' of al- assimilates in sound into the following 's', a 'sun letter', though it is still written.) The genitive -i ending typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').

15.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
15.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.
15.root: — (particle + relative pronoun)

16.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
16.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
16.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

17.meaning: They do wrong / they act unjustly. A verb describing the ongoing committing of injustice — wronging others or oneself by placing things outside their rightful order, transgressing limits, and withholding what is due.
17.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb. The ya- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The bare imperfect stem ends in a vowelless consonant (sukūn); the -u that joins it to -ūna is the indicative marker, signalling a real, ongoing or habitual action ('they are doing / they do').
17.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — wrongdoing, injustice, placing something where it does not belong

1.meaning: And ask them / question them. A command to put a question to a group, joined to a preceding word by 'and'.
1.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a single 'you', built on the bare jussive stem (hence the sukūn / no final vowel on the root). The attached -hum is the object pronoun 'them' (masculine plural). The prefixed wa- means 'and'.

2.meaning: About / concerning; a particle marking the topic of inquiry or the thing one moves away from.
2.grammar: A preposition meaning 'about, concerning, away from'. Its base form is ʿan; the final -i here is a helping vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a connecting 'al-'. It governs the genitive case on whatever noun follows.

3.meaning: A settled place where people live — a town, village, or populated locality. It denotes a community gathered in one inhabited place.
3.grammar: A feminine singular noun marked with 'the'. The final -i is the genitive case: it typically marks the word as linked to a preceding preposition or oath particle, or as the second term of a possessive phrase ('… of …').
3.root: ق-ر-ي (q-r-y) — gathering, bringing together (people in a settlement)

4.meaning: A feminine singular relative pronoun: 'the one which / that which / who' (referring to a single feminine thing). It introduces a descriptive clause that tells us more about a preceding feminine noun.
4.grammar: A relative pronoun, feminine singular, fixed in form (it does not change for case). It links a feminine noun to a following clause describing it, the equivalent of English 'which,' 'that,' or 'who.'

5.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'she was / it was / it became' — from the core verb of being, linking a subject to a description or state, often setting it in past or established time.
5.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb of being. The ending -at marks a third-person feminine-singular subject, 'she' or 'it (feminine)', so it reads 'she/it was'. As a being-verb it normally introduces a description of that subject.
5.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

6.meaning: Present, in attendance, situated right at hand; a feminine singular describing something that is physically there before one, as opposed to absent or distant.
6.grammar: An active participle (a describing word, 'one that is present') in the feminine singular, marked by the tā' marbūṭa. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks a word as the object of a verb or otherwise governed within the sentence.
6.root: ح-ض-ر (ḥ-ḍ-r) — to be present, to attend, to be at hand

7.meaning: The sea, the great body of salt water; figuratively any vast expanse of water.
7.grammar: A definite singular masculine noun ('the …'). The final -i ending is genitive, the case taken after a preposition or when a noun is possessed by a preceding noun ('… of the sea').

8.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
8.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

9.meaning: They overstep / they transgress; to go beyond a set limit or boundary, to exceed what is permitted.

parts.en: transgress, exceed a limit (imperfect stem, wāw-final)

9.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb from a defective root whose final radical is wāw. The ya- prefix with the masculine-plural -na ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The root's wāw is retained in the stem (ʿdū) before the plural ending, and the form is indicative, signalling a real, ongoing or habitual action.
9.root: ع-د-و (ʿ-d-w) — to overstep, transgress, show hostility

10.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
10.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

11.meaning: The Sabbath — the sacred day of rest and worship, on which ordinary labour was set aside. Here in an 'of/after a preposition' relationship.

parts.en: Sabbath / day of rest (with the article's 'l' assimilated, plus the genitive vowel -i)

11.grammar: A definite noun: 'al-' is 'the', and because the next letter is a 'sun letter' (س), the article's 'l' sound merges into it, giving 'as-sabt'. The final -i is the genitive case vowel sitting on the noun's own last root letter (ت), not a separate suffix; this vowel appears when the noun follows a preposition or is linked to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship.
11.root: س-ب-ت (s-b-t) — to rest, cease (from work); the Sabbath

12.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
12.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

13.meaning: 'It comes to them' — to arrive at or reach them. Combines the verb 'to come/arrive' with the object pronoun 'them', expressing that something approaches or presents itself to a group.
13.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb with a feminine-singular 'it/she' subject (the 'ta-' prefix), carrying the object pronoun '-him' ('them'). The 'ta-' prefix signals that the doer is a single feminine (or grammatically feminine) thing; the attached '-him' names the ones reached by the action.

14.meaning: Their fish / their large fish. A plural noun for fish (of the larger, whale-like kind) joined to a possessor 'their'.
14.grammar: A noun in the broken plural with the attached possessive pronoun -hum ('their', masculine plural). The -u before the pronoun is the nominative case, which typically marks the word as the subject of a verb or the topic being spoken about.

15.meaning: The noun 'day' — a span of time, often used for a momentous Day or appointed time; in the accusative it frequently functions as 'on the day (when…)', marking the time at which something occurs.
15.grammar: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
15.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

16.meaning: Their Sabbath / their day of rest. The Sabbath is the appointed day of cessation from work observed in the Mosaic law; the word ties this day to a possessor 'their'.
16.grammar: A noun with the attached possessive pronoun 'their'. The -i before the pronoun is the genitive case, which typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship.
16.root: س-ب-ت (s-b-t) — to rest, cease from labour; the Sabbath

17.meaning: Coming to the surface / showing themselves openly; a plural describing creatures that appear visibly, rising up plainly into view.
17.grammar: An intensive plural describing-word in the accusative indefinite case, marked by the -an ending (tanwīn). This ending typically marks a word as an object or, as here, a circumstantial description of how something appears or behaves ('openly visible').
17.root: ش-ر-ع (sh-r-ʿ) — to approach openly, to come to a watering place; to lay out a way

18.meaning: And on the day (of) / and the day (of). The word for 'day' set as an adverb of time, joined by 'and'.
18.grammar: A noun in the accusative case, shown by the final -a, which here functions adverbially to mark a point in time ('on the day …'). The prefixed wa- means 'and'.
18.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a defined span of time

19.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
19.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

20.meaning: They keep the Sabbath / they cease work for the day of rest. A verb describing the observance of the Sabbath by abstaining from labour.

parts.en: keep the Sabbath, cease from work (imperfect stem)

20.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb. The ya- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The bare imperfect stem ends in a vowelless consonant (sukūn); the -u that joins it to -ūna is the indicative marker, signalling a real, ongoing or habitual action.
20.root: س-ب-ت (s-b-t) — to rest, cease from labour; the Sabbath

21.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
21.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

22.meaning: 'It comes to them' — to arrive at or reach them. Combines the verb 'to come/arrive' with the object pronoun 'them', expressing that something approaches or presents itself to a group.
22.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb with a feminine-singular 'it/she' subject (the 'ta-' prefix), carrying the object pronoun '-him' ('them'). The 'ta-' prefix signals that the doer is a single feminine (or grammatically feminine) thing; the attached '-him' names the ones reached by the action.

23.meaning: 'Like that / thus / in this manner.' A comparison word meaning that something is done or is the case in the way just mentioned.
23.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like/as') prefixed to the demonstrative 'that'. Together they form a fixed adverbial expression, 'like that / thus', which does not change its ending with grammatical position.
23.root: — (a particle of comparison joined to a demonstrative; no root)

24.meaning: We test / we try them. A verb meaning to put someone to the test or trial — to examine through ease or hardship in order to bring out what is within. Carries the attached object 'them'.
24.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb. The na- prefix marks a first-person plural subject ('we'). The attached -hum is the object pronoun 'them' (masculine plural).
24.root: ب-ل-و (b-l-w) — to test, try, put to proof

25.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
25.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.
25.root: — (particle + relative pronoun)

26.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
26.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
26.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

27.meaning: 'They act wickedly / rebel / forsake obedience' — to break away from what is right and overstep the bounds set by Allah, departing from due obedience into corruption.
27.grammar: A present-tense verb. The 'ya-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they') in an ongoing or habitual action. The full '-ūna' ending signals the plain indicative — a straightforward statement of what they do.
27.root: ف-س-ق (f-s-q) — departing from obedience, rebellion, moral corruption

1.meaning: 'And when / and at the time when' — the connective 'and' joined to a word that points to a past moment or circumstance ('when'), introducing the recollection of an event or situation.
1.grammar: A connective particle plus a time-word. The wa- prefix means 'and'. 'Idh' is an invariable adverb pointing to a definite time in the past ('when, at the moment that'); it has no case ending and typically introduces a clause recalling a past event.

2.meaning: She said — a completed act of speaking or saying, attributed to a single female.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb with the -at ending that marks a single female doer ('she said'). The plain past form presents the action as a completed whole.

3.meaning: 'A community / a nation, a people' — a body of people bound together as a single group, often by shared faith, way, or era.
3.grammar: A singular indefinite noun. The -un ending is nominative plus nunation: the -n sound signals 'a/an' (indefinite), and the -u marks the nominative case, the form used when the word is the subject or the thing being named.
3.root: ء-م-م (ʾ-m-m) — to head toward; a community, way, model

4.meaning: 'Among them / from them / some of them' — the preposition 'min' ('from, of, among') joined to the attached pronoun 'hum' ('them').
4.grammar: The preposition 'min' ('from / of / among') with the attached pronoun 'hum' ('them'), referring to a masculine plural group. Together they often express 'part of them' or 'some among them'.

5.meaning: An interrogative meaning 'why? / for what reason?' — a question asking the cause or purpose of something. It is formed from the preposition 'for/about' fused with the question-word 'what'.
5.grammar: A question particle built from li- ('for, about') joined to mā ('what'); when these combine, the long vowel of 'what' is shortened to give li-ma ('for what?, why?'). It opens a question seeking a reason or motive.

6.meaning: You admonish / you exhort. A verb for offering counsel that stirs the heart — warning, reminding, and urging toward what is right with an appeal to consequences.
6.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb. The ta- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'). The bare imperfect stem ends in a vowelless consonant (sukūn); the -u that joins it to -ūna is the indicative marker, signalling a real, ongoing action.
6.root: و-ع-ظ (w-ʿ-ẓ) — to admonish, exhort, give heart-moving counsel

7.meaning: A people / a folk / a community; a body of people bound together, often by kinship or shared standing.
7.grammar: A noun in the accusative indefinite case, marked by the -an ending (tanwīn). The accusative typically marks a word as the object of a verb. Though grammatically singular, it denotes a group.
7.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a people who stand together

8.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
8.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

9.meaning: One who destroys them / about to destroy them. An active participle naming the doer of destruction — the one who brings ruin — joined to the object 'them'.

parts.en: destroyer, one who brings to ruin

9.grammar: An active participle ('one who destroys') from the causative form, carrying the object pronoun -hum ('them'). The -u before the pronoun reflects the nominative case, typically marking the word as the subject or predicate ('[He is] their destroyer').
9.root: ه-ل-ك (h-l-k) — to perish; (causative) to destroy, bring to ruin

10.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
10.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

11.meaning: One who punishes them / about to punish them. An active participle naming the one who inflicts punishment or torment, joined to the object 'them'.
11.grammar: An active participle ('one who punishes') from the intensive form, carrying the object pronoun -hum ('them'). The -u before the pronoun reflects the nominative case, typically marking the word as the subject or predicate ('[He is] their punisher').
11.root: ع-ذ-ب (ʿ-dh-b) — to punish, torment, inflict pain

12.meaning: 'A punishment / torment.' A noun naming chastisement or painful suffering inflicted as a penalty.
12.grammar: A masculine noun. The -an ending marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the accusative case — the form a noun takes as the object of a verb or as the thing being described/quantified.

13.meaning: 'Severe / intense / harsh.' An adjective describing something strong, forceful, and hard to bear.
13.grammar: An adjective in an intensive pattern ('very strong/severe'). The -an ending marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case, the form used when it describes a noun that is itself indefinite and accusative.
13.root: ش-د-د (sh-d-d) — to be strong, intense, severe

14.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
14.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

15.meaning: An excuse / a plea for exoneration; something offered to clear oneself of blame and seek to be absolved before another.
15.grammar: A verbal noun in the feminine, in the accusative indefinite case, marked by the -tan ending (tā' marbūṭa with tanwīn). The accusative here typically expresses purpose or reason — doing something 'as an excuse / in order to be excused'.
15.root: ع-ذ-ر (ʿ-dh-r) — to excuse, absolve, offer a plea

16.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
16.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

17.meaning: 'Your Lord' — Rabb denotes the Master, Owner, Sustainer, and Nurturer who creates, possesses, and brings each thing to its completion; joined to 'your' (plural).
17.grammar: A noun 'Lord' in the genitive case (the -i ending), which typically follows a preposition or links it to a preceding noun ('… of …'). The suffix -kum is the possessive 'your' addressed to a group.
17.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship: nurturing, mastering, owning, sustaining

18.meaning: And so that they may / and perhaps they will. The particle laʿalla expresses hope or expectation that something may come about ('it may be that…'), often introducing a hoped-for purpose; attached to 'them' and joined to a preceding word by 'and'.

parts.en: perhaps, so that, it may be that

18.grammar: The particle laʿalla ('perhaps / so that') is one that puts the following noun in the accusative; the attached -hum ('they') is therefore its accusative subject. It conveys hope, expectation, or a hoped-for outcome. The prefixed wa- means 'and'.

19.meaning: They are mindful of Allah / they guard themselves; to live in reverent awareness that shields one from wrongdoing (the verb behind taqwā).
19.grammar: A Form VIII present-tense verb. The ya-…-ūna frame means 'they (do)' for a group of males, with the final -na marking the indicative mood — a plain statement of an ongoing or habitual reality.
19.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to protect, shield, guard against harm

1.meaning: A connector meaning 'then, when' — it joins to what came before ('then/so') and sets up a 'when…' clause whose outcome follows. It frames a moment: 'and then, at the point when…'.
1.grammar: A compound of the connecting particle fa- ('then/so', linking to the preceding statement) and lammā, a particle meaning 'when' that introduces a past circumstance and leads the listener to expect a following result clause.

2.meaning: A verb meaning 'they forgot' or 'they neglected/abandoned.' The root spans both genuine forgetfulness and the willful neglect of something one chooses to put out of mind.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb. The ending -ū marks a completed action by 'they' (masculine plural). The silent 'alif' written after the -ū is a spelling convention and is not pronounced.

3.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
3.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

4.meaning: A passive past-tense verb meaning 'they were reminded / admonished.' The intensive form of the root means to have something brought back to one's mind and conscience — to be called to remember and take heed.
4.grammar: A completed (past-tense) action in the passive voice — the vowel pattern (u–i) shows the subject had the action done to them ('they were reminded') rather than doing it. The -ū ending marks a masculine plural 'they.' The doubled middle root letter gives the intensive sense of being earnestly admonished.
4.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, mention; to remind, admonish

5.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
5.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

6.meaning: We delivered / we rescued. A verb meaning to bring someone to safety, saving them from danger or destruction. Carries the 'we' subject.
6.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb from the causative form, denoting a completed action. The suffix -nā marks the subject as first-person plural ('we'), indicating that the doers are 'we'.
6.root: ن-ج-و (n-j-w) — to be safe, escape; (causative) to deliver, rescue

7.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
7.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

8.meaning: "They forbid, prohibit, hold (others) back." A present-tense verb for restraining others from something or telling them not to do it.
8.grammar: A present-tense verb, "they" (third-person masculine plural), from a root with a weak final letter. The full "-na" of the plural ending is intact, marking the default present tense used when the verb stands on its own (not made subjunctive or conditional).

9.meaning: About / concerning; a particle marking the topic of inquiry or the thing one moves away from.
9.grammar: A preposition meaning 'about, concerning, away from'. Its base form is ʿan; the final -i here is a helping vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a connecting 'al-'. It governs the genitive case on whatever noun follows.

10.meaning: The evil / the bad; that which is harmful, wicked, or distressing — the opposite of good.
10.grammar: A noun with the definite article al- ('the'); the sun-letter s causes the 'l' to assimilate into the doubled 's'. The final -i is the genitive case, which typically follows a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship.
10.root: س-و-ء (s-w-ʾ) — to be bad, evil; harm, ill

11.meaning: 'And We took / received / seized.' A first-person plural past-tense verb from the root meaning 'to take.' It conveys a completed act of taking hold of something — and idiomatically, of taking a pledge or covenant FROM someone, i.e. binding them to it.
11.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb expressing a completed action. The attached -nā ending is the first-person plural subject 'we,' so the whole word means 'we took.' The prefixed wa- simply joins this statement to what precedes it ('and').
11.root: ا-خ-ذ (ʾ-kh-dh) — to take, seize, take hold of

12.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
12.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

13.meaning: 'They wronged / did injustice / acted unjustly'. The core idea is putting something out of its rightful place — oppression, transgression, or wronging oneself or others.
13.grammar: A past-tense verb with the plural subject ending -ū ('they', masculine/mixed group), referring to a completed action done by many. The -ū suffix is written with a silent 'alif' after it. It states that a group performed the act of wronging.
13.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — to wrong, oppress; to put a thing out of its proper place

14.meaning: With/of a punishment: 'with' joined to a word for a chastisement, torment, or penalty inflicted as recompense; indefinite ('a punishment').
14.grammar: An indefinite noun with the prefixed preposition 'bi-' ('with / of'). The ending -in does two things: the final -n (nunation) marks it indefinite ('a punishment'), and the -i vowel is the genitive case required after the preposition 'bi-'.

15.meaning: Severe / dire / wretched; an intensive describing-word for something grievously harsh or distressing.
15.grammar: An intensive adjective in the genitive indefinite case, marked by the -in ending (tanwīn). The stem carries a hamza between the bāʾ and yāʾ (baʾīs). The genitive typically follows a preposition or links to a preceding noun; the absence of 'the' marks it as indefinite ('a severe …').
15.root: ب-أ-س (b-ʾ-s) — hardship, distress, might/severity

16.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
16.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.
16.root: — (particle + relative pronoun)

17.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
17.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
17.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

18.meaning: 'They act wickedly / rebel / forsake obedience' — to break away from what is right and overstep the bounds set by Allah, departing from due obedience into corruption.
18.grammar: A present-tense verb. The 'ya-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they') in an ongoing or habitual action. The full '-ūna' ending signals the plain indicative — a straightforward statement of what they do.
18.root: ف-س-ق (f-s-q) — departing from obedience, rebellion, moral corruption

1.meaning: A connector meaning 'then, when' — it joins to what came before ('then/so') and sets up a 'when…' clause whose outcome follows. It frames a moment: 'and then, at the point when…'.
1.grammar: A compound of the connecting particle fa- ('then/so', linking to the preceding statement) and lammā, a particle meaning 'when' that introduces a past circumstance and leads the listener to expect a following result clause.

2.meaning: They were insolent / they exceeded all bounds; a verb describing arrogant, defiant rebellion that breaks past every limit of obedience or decency.
2.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb denoting a completed action. The ending -aw (written with a final silent alif) marks the subject as third-person masculine plural ('they'), so the deed is 'they did' it.
2.root: ع-ت-و (ʿ-t-w) — to be insolent, overbearing, exceed all bounds

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on behalf of,' 'for,' 'about,' or 'away from.' It often conveys removing a burden from someone or acting in their place.

parts.en: on behalf of / for / away from

3.grammar: A preposition (a linking particle). It governs the noun that follows it, putting that noun into the genitive case. It does not change form.

4.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
4.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.
4.root: — (particle; no root)

5.meaning: 'They were forbidden / prohibited' — said of people who were told not to do something; the passive of forbidding directed at a group.
5.grammar: A past-tense passive verb (the u-vowelling signals the passive: the subjects had the prohibition imposed on them). The long -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. The written alif after it is a spelling convention on plural verbs and is not pronounced.
5.root: ن-ه-ي (n-h-y) — to forbid, to prohibit, to restrain

6.meaning: A combination meaning 'from him / from it / about him.' The preposition denotes moving away from, departing from, or concerning a thing, and the pronoun refers to a single masculine entity.
6.grammar: A preposition with a fused object pronoun. ʿan governs the genitive and conveys separation or 'concerning.' The attached -hu marks a third-person masculine singular object ('him/it').

7.meaning: 'We said' — the act of speaking or uttering, completed in the past, with 'we' as the speakers (a plural, or the royal/majestic 'We').
7.grammar: A past-tense verb 'to say' with the suffix '-nā' marking the doer as 'we' (first-person plural). This is a hollow verb (its middle root letter is a weak 'w'), which contracts before the suffix to leave 'qul-' before the ending.

8.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
8.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

9.meaning: Be! Become! A command to exist as, or to enter into, whatever is then described.
9.grammar: An imperative (command) verb from the verb 'to be / to become', addressed to a group. The long -ū ending (و followed by a silent alif) marks the command as directed at 'you all' (masculine plural). As a command it carries no case ending of its own.
9.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to become, to come into existence

10.meaning: Apes / monkeys — the plural of the word for an ape, used for the creature as a category.

parts.en: ending of this plural pattern + indefinite 'an' (accusative)

10.grammar: A broken (internal) plural of 'ape', formed by reshaping the singular rather than adding a regular plural suffix; the tā' marbūṭa here belongs to the plural pattern itself, not to a singular unit-noun or a sound feminine plural. The 'an' sound (tā' marbūṭa with tanwīn) marks the word as indefinite ('apes', not 'the apes') and in the accusative case — the case typically used for the predicate after 'be/become' or for the object of a verb.

11.meaning: Despised / driven away in disgrace; a plural describing-word for those rendered lowly, rejected, and abased.

parts.en: despised, abased, driven off in disgrace

11.grammar: A masculine plural active participle ('ones who are abased'). The sound-plural ending -īna marks it as accusative or genitive, the case that typically marks an object, a description of state, or a word governed by a preposition — as opposed to the nominative -ūna.
11.root: خ-س-أ (kh-s-ʾ) — to be driven away in disgrace, to be abased and despised

1.meaning: 'And when / and at the time when' — the connective 'and' joined to a word that points to a past moment or circumstance ('when'), introducing the recollection of an event or situation.
1.grammar: A connective particle plus a time-word. The wa- prefix means 'and'. 'Idh' is an invariable adverb pointing to a definite time in the past ('when, at the moment that'); it has no case ending and typically introduces a clause recalling a past event.

2.meaning: He proclaimed / gave clear notice; a verb of solemn announcement, declaring something openly and definitively so that all are put on notice.

parts.en: Form V prefix (reflexive of the intensive)

2.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in Form V (tafaʿʿala), the reflexive-intensive derived stem built from the Form II intensive (faʿʿala) by prefixing ta-. It denotes a completed action; with no attached subject pronoun, the bare -a ending carries a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). Form V here conveys a deliberate, emphatic proclamation.
2.root: أ-ذ-ن (ʾ-dh-n) — to give ear, to announce, to make a proclamation

3.meaning: 'Your Lord / your Master' — the word for 'Lord' (one who owns, sustains, nurtures and has authority over) combined with 'your' (a single addressee); rabb carries the layered sense of master, sustainer, and the one who brings to maturity.
3.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The -u ending is the nominative case — the basic 'subject' state, used for the doer of an action or the topic of a sentence. The suffix -ka means 'your', addressed to a single masculine person. 'Rabb' bundles ownership, lordship, nurturing care, and sustaining authority into one term.

4.meaning: He will surely raise up / send forth. A verb for sending or rousing someone forth (and, in another sense, raising the dead), delivered as a heavily emphasized assurance ('He shall most certainly send').
4.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb framed by a double emphasis: the prefixed la- ('surely') and the heavy nūn ending -anna ('most certainly'), which together turn it into a solemn oath-like promise. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he').
4.root: ب-ع-ث (b-ʿ-th) — to send forth, rouse, raise up

5.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
5.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
5.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

6.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
6.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

7.meaning: 'Day' — a span of time. It denotes a day or a definite point/period of time; it links to a following word to specify which day (e.g., 'the day of …').
7.grammar: A masculine noun. Its final -i vowel is the genitive case: it typically appears after a preposition or when the word is linked to a following noun in an 'of …' relationship (as in 'the day OF …').

8.meaning: "the Resurrection" — the standing-up of all people from death to be judged; literally the act of rising or standing up.
8.grammar: The al- prefix means "the." The -i ending (on the feminine -t) is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ("the … OF this") or follows a preposition.

9.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
9.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.
9.root: — (pronoun)

10.meaning: He inflicts upon them / makes them suffer; a verb of imposing something burdensome on someone, subjecting them to harsh treatment. Carries the object 'them'.
10.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'), and the -u indicative ending signals a real, ongoing action. The attached -hum is the object pronoun 'them' (masculine plural).
10.root: س-و-م (s-w-m) — to impose, subject someone to, drive toward something burdensome

11.meaning: Evil, harm, or grievousness — the bad or distressing aspect of something; in a possessive link, 'the worst of …' or 'a grievous …'.
11.grammar: A singular masculine noun in the accusative (-a ending), which typically marks an object of a verb or the first term of a possessive link ('the evil OF …'). The sense is 'grievous / worst kind of.'
11.root: س-و-ء (s-w-ʾ) — evil, harm, to be bad

12.meaning: The punishment, torment, or chastisement — severe penalty or suffering inflicted as retribution.
12.grammar: A singular masculine noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending is the genitive, which typically links it to a preceding noun ('… of the punishment') or follows a preposition.

13.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
13.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

14.meaning: 'Your Lord' — the noun 'Lord' (Master, Sustainer, Owner, the One who nurtures and brings to completion) combined with 'your'. 'Rabb' carries the linked senses of ownership, authority, and ongoing care that raises a thing to its perfection.
14.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive. The -a ending is accusative, which typically marks the word as a direct object or governed element. The attached -ka means 'your', addressed to a single male.
14.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, nurturing care, ownership and mastery

15.meaning: An emphatic statement that something is very swift, quick, or fast — that it comes about with great speed. The word combines an emphasis marker with the adjective 'swift', so it asserts: 'is indeed swift / surely quick.'
15.grammar: An adjective in the intensive pattern faʿīl, meaning 'very swift.' The attached la- at the front is an emphatic particle ('indeed, surely') that strengthens the assertion. The final -u ending is nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or for a predicate that describes the subject ('… IS swift').
15.root: س-ر-ع (s-r-ʿ) — speed, swiftness

16.meaning: The punishment, penalty, or retribution; a consequence imposed in requital for wrongdoing.
16.grammar: A definite noun with prefixed al- ("the"). The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ("… of …") or follows a preposition.
16.root: ع-ق-ب (ʿ-q-b) — to follow/come after; consequence, punishment

17.meaning: A linkage of 'and' with the emphatic particle inna ('truly, indeed') plus 'he' — meaning 'and truly he…', opening a clause with firm assurance about the person referred to.
17.grammar: 'wa' is the connector 'and'. 'inna' is an emphatic particle that strongly affirms the statement and grammatically governs the following noun/pronoun in the accusative. The attached -hu ('he/him') is the subject of the inna-clause, expressed in object form as inna requires.

18.meaning: Surely most forgiving — abundantly and repeatedly forgiving, One who covers over and pardons sins again and again. The intensive form stresses the fullness and constancy of the forgiving.
18.grammar: The prefix la- is an emphatic 'surely/indeed' (often answering or stressing a statement). The stem is the intensive adjective 'faʿūl' ('much-forgiving'). The final -un is the nominative case with nunation, typically marking a predicate ('… is surely Most-Forgiving'). It conveys constant, abundant forgiveness.
18.root: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to forgive, cover over, pardon

19.meaning: Most merciful, ever-merciful; one whose mercy is constant and abundant. As a divine attribute it denotes Allah's enduring, all-embracing compassion toward His creation.
19.grammar: An intensive adjective on the form faʿīl ('abundantly/constantly merciful'). The ending -un (tanwīn) is the nominative case with indefiniteness, the form typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it ('[He] is most merciful').

1.meaning: To cut something up thoroughly, to break it into many separate pieces, or to scatter and divide a group into fragments — said by a 'we' subject about a 'them' object. The intensive form conveys repeated or extensive cutting/dividing.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb in the intensive (doubled-middle) pattern, which signals doing the action thoroughly or repeatedly — 'cut into many pieces, broke apart, divided up.' The opening wa- means 'and.' The -nā ending marks a first-person plural doer ('we'), and the final -hum is an attached object pronoun ('them').

2.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
2.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

3.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
3.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

4.meaning: Communities / nations / peoples — distinct groups of people bound together as a body, each a 'community' with its own collective identity. The indefinite plural denotes 'communities' in general.
4.grammar: A feminine plural noun (broken/internal plural of umma, pattern fuʿal) meaning 'communities/nations'. The -an ending is accusative with nunation (the doubled-n sound marking indefiniteness); the accusative typically marks a direct object or a word describing the state/category into which something is made.
4.root: أ-م-م (ʾ-m-m) — community, nation, a people united

5.meaning: 'From them / among them' (a group of males or a mixed group) — indicating origin, source, or partitive 'some of them'.
5.grammar: The preposition min ('from, of, among'). The attached pronoun -hum ('them', masculine/mixed plural) takes a helping vowel -u (becoming -humu) for ease of pronunciation before a following word. The whole means 'from/among them'.

6.meaning: Those who are righteous, morally upright, and sound in conduct — people whose deeds are good and who set things right. As a plural noun it denotes the class of virtuous, godly people collectively.
6.grammar: An active participle ('one who is righteous / does good') made definite by the prefix al- ('the'). The -ūna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the nominative case — the form typically used when such a plural is the subject of a sentence ('the righteous ones [are/do] …').

7.meaning: 'And among them / and some of them' — a connective 'and' plus a preposition meaning 'from / among / part of,' joined to the pronoun 'them'; often introduces a subgroup ('among them are …').
7.grammar: A connective wa- ('and') with the preposition min ('from / among'), which always governs a following word in the genitive. Here that word is the attached pronoun -hum ('them'), giving 'and among them / and from them.' Particles like these do not themselves carry case or tense.

8.meaning: An adverb/preposition meaning 'apart from, other than, short of, below.' It points to something falling outside or beneath a named thing — 'aside from X' or 'lesser than X'.
8.grammar: An invariable adverbial noun used like a preposition. It carries a fixed -a ending and governs a following noun in the genitive, yielding the sense 'other than …' or 'short of …'.
8.root: د-و-ن (d-w-n) — to be below, lesser, or beneath

9.meaning: A demonstrative meaning 'that' — pointing to something distant or already mentioned, the more remote counterpart to 'this.' It singles out a particular thing or matter ('that one, that very thing').
9.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun for a single masculine thing, 'that.' The middle -li- adds a sense of distance ('that, yonder'), and the final -ka is an element directed at the person addressed ('to you'). It does not change for grammatical case; it simply points something out.

10.meaning: To test, try, or put to the proof — to subject someone to a trial in order to bring out what they truly are. Said by a 'we' subject about a 'them' object, conveying 'and We tried/tested them.'
10.grammar: A past-tense verb meaning 'tested, tried.' The opening wa- means 'and.' The -nā ending marks a first-person plural doer ('we'), and the final -hum is an attached object pronoun ('them'). The verb root carries the sense of testing to reveal a person's real nature.

11.meaning: 'With good things' — referring to blessings, benefits, prosperity, and pleasant circumstances. The plural noun denotes good deeds or, more often, the good fortunes and favorable conditions a person experiences.
11.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun ('the good things') preceded by the preposition bi- ('with, by means of'). The -ti ending is genitive, the case automatically taken by a noun governed by a preposition like bi- (so: 'with the good things').

12.meaning: 'And the bad things' — referring to misfortunes, hardships, afflictions, and evils. The plural noun denotes evil deeds or, frequently, the bad circumstances and calamities a person undergoes.
12.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun ('the bad things'), opening with wa- ('and'). The -ti ending is genitive — the case for a noun joined by 'and' to a preceding genitive noun, or governed by a preposition (so: 'and the bad things').

13.meaning: 'So that they may / perhaps they will.' A particle expressing hope, expectation, or purpose, fused with the pronoun 'them'; it introduces a hoped-for or intended outcome.

parts.en: perhaps / so that / in hope that

13.grammar: The particle laʿalla ('perhaps, in the hope that, so that') with the attached pronoun -hum ('them'), which serves as its subject. Laʿalla belongs to a family of particles that put a following noun or pronoun in the accusative; -hum is that fixed object form. It conveys hope or an intended purpose rather than certainty.

14.meaning: To return, go back, or turn back — to come back to a place, state, or point of origin. Used of a group: 'they return / come back'.
14.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they return'). The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending marks an ongoing or repeated action by a group of males or a mixed group. The -ūna 'indicative' ending appears when nothing precedes the verb to shorten it.

1.meaning: To come after and take the place of someone — to succeed them, follow in their footsteps, or replace them. Said of a single masculine subject in the past: 'then [he/it] succeeded / came after.'
1.grammar: A past-tense verb with a single masculine doer ('he/it'), meaning 'succeeded, came after, took the place of.' The opening fa- means 'then' or 'so,' linking it as a consequence to what precedes. The final -a is the normal past-tense vowel for a third-person masculine singular subject.

2.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
2.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

3.meaning: "after them / following them" — the noun baʿd ('after, afterward') with the attached pronoun 'them', denoting what comes later in time than a group.
3.grammar: A time-noun used like a preposition, with an attached pronoun. The -i ending is genitive, the form taken after a preposition or as the second term of a possessive link. The suffix -him means 'them' (its vowel is -hi- to harmonise with the preceding -i).

4.meaning: A successor or generation that comes after — those who follow and take the place of an earlier group. Often carries the nuance of a later, lesser generation. As an indefinite noun: 'a successor / a following generation.'
4.grammar: A noun meaning 'a successor / a generation that comes after.' The -un ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a successor') and nominative — the case typically used for the subject of a sentence.
4.root: خ-ل-ف (kh-l-f) — succeeding, coming after, replacing

5.meaning: To inherit — to receive something handed down from those who came before, whether property, a book, or a legacy. Said of a 'they' subject in the past: '[they] inherited / received as an inheritance.'
5.grammar: A past-tense verb meaning 'inherited, received as a legacy.' The opening wa- means 'and' (and can introduce a descriptive 'who …'). The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural doer ('they'); the silent alif after it is a spelling convention and is not pronounced.
5.root: و-ر-ث (w-r-th) — inheriting, succession of legacy

6.meaning: The Book, the Scripture — a written revelation; the term for a divinely revealed text.
6.grammar: A definite noun ('the Book') with attached 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb.
6.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write; a writing, book

7.meaning: To take, seize, or grasp — to receive or lay hold of something. Said of a 'they' subject in the present/ongoing sense: '[they] take / are taking / keep taking.'
7.grammar: A present-tense verb meaning 'take, seize, grasp.' The ya-…-ūna frame marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they take'). The final -na (the full -ūna ending) signals the indicative mood — the form used for a plain, ongoing or habitual statement of fact ('they [do] take').

8.meaning: Something fleeting and incidental — a passing gain, a transient benefit or worldly advantage that quickly comes and goes, with no lasting permanence.
8.grammar: A noun with the '-a' accusative ending, which typically marks it as the direct object of a verb (the thing sought or pursued) or otherwise the receiver of the action.
8.root: ع-ر-ض (ʿ-r-ḍ) — to present/occur; that which is incidental or transient

9.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
9.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

10.meaning: 'The nearer / the lower' — the closer of two things. Used of what is nearest at hand, hence the immediate, present, lower world or its fleeting goods, as opposed to what is higher or further. As an adjective: 'the nearest, the lowest, the more immediate.'
10.grammar: A definite comparative/superlative adjective ('nearer, nearest; lower, lowest') made definite by al- ('the'). Its ending is a fixed long -ā that does not change for case; the word stays in this form whatever its grammatical role.

11.meaning: A verb meaning 'and they say / and they keep saying' — to utter or assert in speech. The structure presents an ongoing or repeated act of speaking by a group.
11.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb joined by wa- ('and'). The ya-…-ūna frame marks the 3rd-person masculine plural ('they'); the full -ūna ending is the inseparable indicative-plural suffix, showing the verb is in its base (indicative) form and expressing an ongoing or habitual action.

12.meaning: An assertion that forgiveness will be granted in the future — 'it will be forgiven.' The word combines a future marker with a passive verb, so the act of pardoning is stated as something that will happen, without naming the one who forgives.
12.grammar: A present-tense passive verb ('is/will be forgiven') with a third-person masculine singular subject. The prefixed sa- means the action lies in the near future ('will'). The vowel pattern yu-…-a marks it as passive (the deed is done TO the subject), and the final -u is the indicative ending used for a plain statement of fact.

13.meaning: A combination of the preposition 'for / to' with the pronoun 'us', meaning 'for us' or 'to us / on our behalf'.
13.grammar: A preposition ('for / to') joined to the attached pronoun 'us'. The pronoun -nā always means 'us / our' regardless of position. Together they express benefit or direction toward the speakers ('for us').

14.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
14.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

15.meaning: To come to or reach someone — for a thing or person to arrive at them. Said in the present of a single masculine subject acting upon 'them': '[it] comes to them / should come to them.'
15.grammar: A present-tense verb meaning 'come, arrive.' The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it').
