5.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — soul, self, breath

6.meaning: Describes something as being one, single, or a sole individual — the feminine form of 'one', used of a single female or grammatically feminine entity.

parts.en: and (the conjunction, fused into the following word)
one/single (feminine) — body of 'wāḥidah' after its initial waw merges with the conjunction

6.grammar: An adjective/numeral in the feminine singular, 'a single (one)'. There is only one written waw here, carrying a shadda: the conjunction waw ('and') and the initial waw of 'wāḥidah' have merged into a single doubled letter (assimilation/idgham), so the segmentation must not duplicate the waw. The final -in (tanwīn kasra) is the indefinite genitive, which typically signals that the word follows a preposition or links to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship.

7.meaning: And He made / placed / appointed — a versatile verb meaning to make, render, set in place, or assign something a role or state; the leading 'wa' means 'and'.
7.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') plus a past-tense verb. The -a ending marks a third-person masculine singular doer ('he'). This verb commonly takes two objects (to make X into Y) or sets a thing in place.
7.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, render, place, appoint

8.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'min' ('from / out of / some of') joined to the pronoun 'it' (feminine). Together: 'from it / out of it / of it,' indicating a source or a portion taken from a feminine thing.
8.grammar: A preposition 'min' with the attached pronoun '-hā' ('it/her'), referring to a feminine noun. 'Min' indicates origin, source, or a part taken from a whole; the attached pronoun is in the object form required after a preposition.

9.meaning: A mate, spouse, or partner forming one of a pair — with the attached pronoun, 'its/his/her mate'.
9.grammar: A noun carrying the accusative -a ending, which typically marks it as the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon) or otherwise governed into the accusative. The suffix -hā is the attached possessive pronoun 'its/her', referring to a feminine or grammatically feminine antecedent.
9.root: ز-و-ج (z-w-j) — pairing, joining as a couple

10.meaning: So that he may find rest/dwell — a verb meaning to grow calm, settle, and find repose toward something; 'li-' here means 'so that / in order to'.
10.grammar: Present-tense verb with the prefix ya- marking a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). The preceding li- ('so that') is a purpose particle that puts the verb in the subjunctive mood, shown by the final -a ending — expressing intended result ('… so that he may …').

11.meaning: Toward it / to her — the directional preposition 'ilā' ('to, toward'), expressing motion or inclination toward a goal, here joined to a feminine 'it/her'.
11.grammar: A preposition meaning 'to/toward', whose form shifts from 'ilā' to 'ilay-' when a pronoun attaches. The suffix -hā is the feminine singular object ('it/her'). It marks the endpoint or direction of motion or leaning.

12.meaning: A connector meaning 'then, when' — it joins to what came before ('then/so') and sets up a 'when…' clause whose outcome follows. It frames a moment: 'and then, at the point when…'.
12.grammar: A compound of the connecting particle fa- ('then/so', linking to the preceding statement) and lammā, a particle meaning 'when' that introduces a past circumstance and leads the listener to expect a following result clause.

13.meaning: He covered/enfolded it — a verb meaning to overspread, envelop, or come over something so as to cover it completely, stated as a past act with a feminine 'it/her' object.
13.grammar: Past-tense verb in Form V (tafaʿʿala), the reflexive-intensive pattern. The ta- here is intrinsic to the Form V stem, not a person prefix; in the past tense a third-person masculine singular ('he') carries no separate person prefix. The stem ends in a weak long vowel (-ā, from the final root letter). The attached -hā is the feminine singular object ('it/her').
13.root: غ-ش-و / غ-ش-ي (gh-sh-w/y) — to cover, overspread, envelop

14.meaning: It (she) carried, bore, or held. A past-tense verb of bearing a load or carrying something.
14.grammar: A past/perfect-tense verb. The -at ending marks a third-person feminine singular subject ('she/it'), used when the doer is grammatically feminine (or for non-human plurals treated as feminine).

15.meaning: A load, a thing carried — a burden borne, and specifically that which a womb carries (a pregnancy). A concrete noun for what is carried.
15.grammar: A noun with the ending -an: accusative case with 'tanwīn' (the -n marking an indefinite 'a …'). The accusative is typically used for the direct object of a verb or other complements.
15.root: ح-م-ل (ḥ-m-l) — to carry, bear; a load

16.meaning: Light (in weight) — not heavy; by extension easy, slight, or readily borne. A descriptive adjective.
16.grammar: An adjective in the steady-quality pattern (faʿīl). The ending -an is accusative with 'tanwīn' (the -n marking an indefinite 'a …'); an adjective takes the same case as the noun it describes, here an accusative object.
16.root: خ-ف-ف (kh-f-f) — to be light, slight, nimble

17.meaning: Then she/it passed on, went about, carried on — a verb meaning to pass by, move along, or proceed; 'fa-' adds 'then / and so', marking what follows next.
17.grammar: The connector fa- ('then/so', marking sequence) plus a past-tense verb. The -at ending marks a third-person feminine singular doer ('she/it').
17.root: م-ر-ر (m-r-r) — to pass, go by, proceed

18.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
18.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

19.meaning: A connector meaning 'then, when' — it joins to what came before ('then/so') and sets up a 'when…' clause whose outcome follows. It frames a moment: 'and then, at the point when…'.
19.grammar: A compound of the connecting particle fa- ('then/so', linking to the preceding statement) and lammā, a particle meaning 'when' that introduces a past circumstance and leads the listener to expect a following result clause.

20.meaning: She/it became heavy — a verb meaning to grow weighty or burdened. Built on the causative-style pattern, it conveys the onset of heaviness.
20.grammar: Past-tense verb in the afʿala pattern (often causative or 'to come to be in a state'). The -at ending marks a third-person feminine singular doer ('she/it').
20.root: ث-ق-ل (th-q-l) — to be heavy, weighty, burdensome

21.meaning: They two called upon / supplicated — a verb meaning to call, summon, or pray to, here done by exactly two people (a dual subject).
21.grammar: Past-tense verb. The -ā ending marks a dual subject — exactly two doers ('they two'). The verb's core sense is to call out to or invoke someone.

22.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
22.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

23.meaning: Their (two) Lord — 'rabb' is the Master, Owner, and Sustainer who creates, nurtures, and governs; not merely a 'lord' but the one who brings up and cares for all under His charge. Here possessed by exactly two ('their').
23.grammar: The noun 'Lord' with the dual possessive -humā ('of them two'). The -a on the stem is the accusative case, used when the noun is the direct object of a verb (e.g., the one called upon).
23.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, lord over

24.meaning: An emphatic conditional opener combining an oath-like emphasis with 'if' — roughly 'most certainly, if (such-and-such happens)…', strongly stressing the condition and the response that follows.
24.grammar: Two particles fused together: an emphatic la- that signals a coming oath or strong assertion, plus in ('if') introducing a condition. Together they set up an emphatic 'if… then surely…' construction. Neither has a case ending; particles do not inflect.

25.meaning: You gave us / granted us — a verb meaning to give, bring, or bestow, with the giver being 'You' and the recipient 'us'.
25.grammar: Past-tense verb in the causative pattern (afʿala: 'to cause to come', i.e., to give). The suffix -ta marks the doer as 'you' (masculine singular); the attached -nā is the object 'us'.
25.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (causative) to give, bring

26.meaning: "Righteous / good / sound" — an active participle describing one who or that which is upright and wholesome and acts rightly; as a description of deeds it means good, virtuous works.
26.grammar: An active participle used as a noun or adjective. The -an ending (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a righteous one / a good deed') and in the accusative case — the form used for a direct object or other complement.
26.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound / upright / righteous

27.meaning: We shall most certainly be — the verb 'to be/become' carrying a double layer of emphasis, asserting with full force that 'we will indeed be'.
27.grammar: Present/future verb of 'being'. The na- prefix marks a first-person plural subject ('we'). It is framed by two emphasizers: the prefixed la- (lām of the oath, 'surely') and the suffixed heavy -anna (the emphatic nūn), together giving a solemn, emphatic assertion ('we shall most certainly be').
27.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, become, come into existence

28.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
28.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

29.meaning: 'The grateful ones / the thankful' — those who recognize and acknowledge benefit and respond with gratitude, as a defined group.
29.grammar: An active participle ('one who is grateful') made definite by 'al-' ('the') and put in the sound masculine plural with the ending -īna. The -īna ending marks a masculine human plural in the accusative/genitive state (as opposed to -ūna for the nominative). It names 'the grateful ones' as a class.

1.meaning: A connector meaning 'then, when' — it joins to what came before ('then/so') and sets up a 'when…' clause whose outcome follows. It frames a moment: 'and then, at the point when…'.
1.grammar: A compound of the connecting particle fa- ('then/so', linking to the preceding statement) and lammā, a particle meaning 'when' that introduces a past circumstance and leads the listener to expect a following result clause.

2.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'He gave them (two)' or 'He brought to them (two).' From the verb meaning to come; in its causative (Form IV) form it means to give, grant, or bring something to someone. The attached object refers to a pair (a dual 'them two').
2.grammar: A completed (past-tense) action with a built-in 'he' subject. The verb is the causative (Form IV) of 'to come,' giving the sense 'to bring/give.' The ending -humā is an attached object pronoun used specifically for two people or things ('them both,' the dual).
2.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (causative) to bring, give

3.meaning: "Righteous / good / sound" — an active participle describing one who or that which is upright and wholesome and acts rightly; as a description of deeds it means good, virtuous works.
3.grammar: An active participle used as a noun or adjective. The -an ending (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a righteous one / a good deed') and in the accusative case — the form used for a direct object or other complement.
3.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound / upright / righteous

4.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'they two made' or 'they two set up / appointed.' The core verb covers making, rendering something into a certain state, placing, or assigning. The subject is specifically a pair.
4.grammar: A completed (past-tense) action. The final -ā (alif) marks a dual subject: 'the two of them did it.' Distinct from the singular 'he did' and the plural 'they did.'
4.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, render, place, appoint

5.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
5.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

6.meaning: Associates, partners, or co-sharers — those set up as participants alongside another in ownership, authority, or worship. In theological usage it denotes rivals falsely placed beside Allah.
6.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of sharīk ('partner'), following the pattern faʿalāʾ. This pattern is a diptote, so it takes no nunation. The word is in the accusative case, marked by the short -a vowel on the word-final hamzah (آءَ); that hamzah is part of the plural pattern itself and cannot be split off as a separate ending. The accusative is the case typically used for the direct object of a verb ('they made/claimed partners') or after certain particles.

7.meaning: A compound particle joining the preposition 'in/about' with the relative pronoun 'what', yielding 'in that which' or 'concerning what' — pointing to the matter or subject about which something is said or done.
7.grammar: A fixed combination of the preposition 'fī' and the indeclinable relative 'mā'. Being particles, neither takes a case ending; the phrase functions as 'in/about what…'.

8.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'He gave them (two)' or 'He brought to them (two).' From the verb meaning to come; in its causative (Form IV) form it means to give, grant, or bring something to someone. The attached object refers to a pair (a dual 'them two').
8.grammar: A completed (past-tense) action with a built-in 'he' subject. The verb is the causative (Form IV) of 'to come,' giving the sense 'to bring/give.' The ending -humā is an attached object pronoun used specifically for two people or things ('them both,' the dual).
8.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (causative) to bring, give

9.meaning: 'So He is exalted high above (it)' or 'then He is far transcendent.' Built on a verb meaning to be lofty/elevated, this form expresses that someone is utterly high and above something — used of Allah being far beyond any deficiency or false association. The opening fa- links it to what precedes as a consequence.
9.grammar: A 'he' verb expressing height and transcendence. The prefix fa- means 'so/then,' drawing a consequence. The verb pattern intensifies the sense of being elevated and removed far above something lower.
9.root: ع-ل-و (ʿ-l-w) — to be high, lofty, exalted

10.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
10.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

11.meaning: 'About what' / 'of that which' — the preposition 'ʿan' ('about, concerning, away from') merged with 'mā' ('what, that which').
11.grammar: A fusion of the preposition 'ʿan' ('about, concerning') with the relative/interrogative 'mā' ('what'); the 'n' of 'ʿan' assimilates into 'mā' to give 'ʿammā'. It introduces the thing being spoken about.

12.meaning: 'They associate (partners with Him)' — an ongoing/present verb. From the root for partnership, this form (causative, Form IV) means to make something a partner or associate, especially to set up partners alongside Allah in worship or divinity (the act underlying shirk).
12.grammar: A present/ongoing action. The yu- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a masculine plural 'they' doing the action now or habitually. The yu- prefix is the marker of Form IV (causative): 'to make (something) a partner.' The full -ūna ending signals the verb is in its ordinary (indicative) state, not cut short by a governing particle.
12.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to share, partner; (causative) to associate partners

1.meaning: 'Do they associate (partners)?' — the same present-tense verb 'they associate as partners,' carrying a questioning, often rebuking, force through its opening hamza.
1.grammar: The prefixed hamza (a-) turns the statement into a question — often a rhetorical, disapproving one. The yu-…-ūna frame marks a masculine plural 'they' in an ongoing/habitual action, and the yu- prefix marks Form IV (causative, 'to make a partner'). The full -ūna ending shows the verb stands in its ordinary (indicative) state.
1.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to share, partner; (causative) to associate partners

2.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

3.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
3.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

4.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he creates / he brings into being'. It denotes originating and forming something, bringing it into existence — an act distinctively ascribed to Allah.
4.grammar: A present/future verb (Form I, khalaqa, 'to create'). The ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular ('he'). The final -u ending is indicative, expressing a plain statement of present or ongoing/repeated action (as opposed to subjunctive or jussive forms).
4.root: خ-ل-ق (kh-l-q) — to create, originate, shape, measure out

5.meaning: A thing; something or anything. With a negation it commonly amounts to 'nothing at all.'
5.grammar: A singular masculine noun, indefinite ('a thing'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative, often used here as an object or an adverbial 'in any respect / at all.'
5.root: ش-ي-أ (sh-y-ʾ) — thing, to will

6.meaning: 'And they.' The opening 'and' joined to the standalone subject pronoun 'they' (a group of males). A standalone pronoun like this typically begins or emphasizes a statement about its referent.
6.grammar: The conjunction wa ('and') with the detached subject pronoun hum ('they,' masculine plural). As an independent (not attached) pronoun, it serves as the subject of a clause and often lends emphasis to the ones spoken about.

7.meaning: 'They are created' — a present-tense passive verb. From the root for creating/originating, the passive form states that the subjects are the ones being brought into being by another, not the ones who create.
7.grammar: A present, passive action: the subject receives the act rather than performs it ('are being created'). The yu-…-ūna frame marks a masculine plural 'they.' The internal vowels (yu-…-a-) are what make it passive. The full -ūna ending shows the ordinary (indicative) state.

1.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
1.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

2.meaning: They are able / they have the power and capacity — to be capable of doing something, to have the strength, means, or ability to carry it out.
2.grammar: Present-tense verb, 3rd person masculine plural ('they'). The ya- prefix marks the present tense and the 'they' subject; the -ūna ending marks the plural and the indicative mood — the plain factual form for an ongoing state. From form X, which often carries the sense of 'seeking/having the capacity for' something, here simply 'to be able.'
2.root: ط-و-ع (ṭ-w-ʿ) — to obey, to be capable, willing capacity

3.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
3.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

4.meaning: 'Help, assistance, victory' — a noun naming the act of aiding someone against an adversary or granting them triumph. The -an ending presents it as an indefinite 'some help / any help.'
4.grammar: A noun in the indefinite accusative: the -an ending (written with a final alif) typically marks the word as a direct object of a verb, or as 'some/any (help)' without 'the.'
4.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, aid, give victory

5.meaning: 'And not' — a connector 'and' joined to the negative particle 'not,' negating a following statement.
5.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the negator lā ('not'). Lā commonly negates a present-tense verb or a noun. Neither particle takes case endings.

6.meaning: A noun meaning 'their own selves' or 'themselves' — the plural of 'nafs' (self, soul, person, inner self), joined to the pronoun 'their.' It commonly conveys the reflexive idea of acting upon one's own self.
6.grammar: A noun (a broken/irregular plural of 'nafs') with the attached possessive pronoun '-hum' ('their/them,' masculine plural). The -a case ending before the pronoun is accusative, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb — i.e. the self upon which the action falls.

7.meaning: 'They help / they give victory' — a present-tense verb meaning to come to someone's aid or support them against an enemy.
7.grammar: A present/ongoing action. The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a masculine plural 'they' acting now or habitually. The full -ūna ending shows the verb is in its ordinary (indicative) state, not shortened by a governing particle.
7.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, aid, give victory

1.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
1.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

2.meaning: 'You call them / you invoke them' — a present-tense verb. From the root for calling, it covers summoning, appealing to, or invoking someone (as in calling upon a deity). The attached pronoun is the object, 'them.'
2.grammar: A present-tense action with a 'you' (masculine) subject built into the ta- prefix. The attached -hum is the object pronoun 'them' (masculine plural). The verb commonly carries the sense of calling upon or invoking.
2.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, summon, invoke, pray to

3.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
3.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

4.meaning: The guidance; the right leading and true direction (with the definite article, 'the Guidance').
4.grammar: A definite verbal noun: the prefix al- means 'the'. It ends in a long -ā (from a weak-final root), an ending that does not change for case. It denotes the abstract reality of right guidance, made specific and definite by 'the'.
4.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, lead rightly, show the way

5.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
5.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

6.meaning: 'They follow you' — a present-tense verb meaning to follow, pursue, go after, or obey. The attached pronoun is the object, 'you (plural).'
6.grammar: A present action with a masculine plural 'they' subject (ya-…-ū). The attached -kum is the object pronoun 'you all.' The usual plural ending -ūna appears here as -ū because an object pronoun is attached directly to the verb, which regularly causes the final -na to drop. The verb pattern (Form VIII) adds effort/diligence to the bare idea of following.
6.root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow, pursue, come after

7.meaning: 'Equal / the same / all alike' — a noun-adjective expressing that two or more things make no difference and are on a par. It often appears in the sense 'it is all the same (whether… or…)'.
7.grammar: A singular indefinite noun used to mean 'equal/the same'. The final -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a/an…') and in the nominative case — the case used for the subject or for the predicate that describes what something is.
7.root: س-و-ي (s-w-y) — to be even, equal, level

8.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
8.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

9.meaning: 'Whether you (all) called them' — a past-tense verb 'you called/invoked them,' opened by a questioning hamza that often sets up a 'whether… or…' comparison. The attached pronoun is the object, 'them.'
9.grammar: A completed (past-tense) action. The prefixed hamza (a-) makes it a question, often the first half of a 'whether X or Y' pairing. The -tum ending marks a plural 'you' as the doer; it is lengthened to -tumū before the attached object -hum ('them'). The verb often means to call upon or invoke.
9.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, summon, invoke, pray to

10.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'or', specifically the 'or' that pairs with a preceding question to offer an alternative ('…or…?'). It links two possibilities being weighed against each other, often after an opening interrogative.

parts.en: or (in alternatives, esp. after a question)

10.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case or tense ending). It typically introduces the second branch of a two-part question or a balanced alternative, presenting the two as equally consequential.

11.meaning: You — the standalone pronoun for a group of people ('you all', masculine or mixed). It is used for emphasis or as the subject standing on its own.
11.grammar: A detached subject pronoun meaning 'you all' (second-person masculine/mixed plural). Unlike pronoun endings attached to verbs or nouns, this word stands alone — typically to emphasize the subject or to begin an equational sentence ('you [are]…'). Its form is fixed and does not change for case.

12.meaning: 'Ones who keep silent / remain silent' — a plural describer (active participle) for those characterized by silence, saying nothing, making no response.
12.grammar: A doer/describer noun (active participle) naming the quality of one who is silent. The -ūna ending marks a masculine plural and signals the subject/predicate role ('they are ones who…'), the form such a noun takes when standing as topic or predicate.
12.root: ص-م-ت (ṣ-m-t) — to be silent, say nothing

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (all) call upon, invoke, summon, or pray to.' The root spans calling out, naming, inviting, and supplicating — especially calling on someone for help.
3.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ta- prefix with the -ūna ending marks 'you all' (masculine plural) as the doers. The final -na is the indicative marker, signalling an ongoing or habitual action (a complete, non-shortened present-tense verb).
3.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, invoke, summon, pray

4.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
4.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
4.root: — (preposition)

5.meaning: A noun used to mean 'besides', 'other than', 'apart from', or 'short of'. It points to something or someone set apart from, or lower/lesser than, a named party. Often used in the phrase 'besides Allah'.
5.grammar: 'dūn' functions as an adverb-like noun of place/relation. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, which appears because it follows a preposition (such as 'min', 'from') and because it links to a following noun ('other than …'). It commonly heads the construction 'besides/other than [someone]'.
5.root: د-و-ن (d-w-n) — to be low/beneath, to fall short; hence 'below, other than, besides'

6.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
6.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

7.meaning: 'Servants / slaves / worshippers' — a plural noun for those who are owned by and devoted to a master; in religious usage, the created beings who serve and worship Allah. The -un ending presents it indefinitely ('servants').
7.grammar: A plural noun in the indefinite nominative: the -un ending typically marks the word as a subject or as the thing being described ('they are servants'), and the absence of 'the' makes it general.
7.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to serve, worship, be a devoted servant

8.meaning: A noun phrase meaning 'the likes of you / ones similar to you' — peers or counterparts resembling the people addressed.
8.grammar: A plural noun ('likenesses, equals', plural of 'mithl') with an attached pronoun. The -u ending marks the nominative case — the naming form for a subject or predicate. The attached -kum ('your / you') stands in the possessive role, giving 'the likes of you'.

9.meaning: 'So call upon them / so invoke them' — a command to a group, 'call / summon / invoke,' with the linking fa- ('so, then') and the attached object 'them.'
9.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a masculine plural 'you all,' marked by the -ū ending. The prefix fa- means 'so/then,' drawing a consequence or instruction. The attached -hum is the object 'them.' The verb often means to call upon or invoke.
9.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, summon, invoke, pray to

10.meaning: A phrase meaning 'so let them respond / answer favourably' — combining a command directed at a group with the act of replying to or complying with a call.
10.grammar: Opens with fa ('so, then') and the prefixed lām of command ('let them…'). The verb is form X (to seek/give a response), third-person masculine plural ('they'). The command (jussive) form drops the plural's final nūn, leaving -ū (written with a silent alif): 'so let them respond'.

11.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
11.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

12.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
12.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

13.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
13.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
13.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

14.meaning: The plural of 'ṣādiq': 'truthful ones', 'those who speak the truth', 'the sincere and reliable'. It describes people whose words and conduct match reality.
14.grammar: 'ṣādiq' is an active participle ('one who is truthful'). The '-īna' ending is a 'sound' masculine plural marker; the '-ī-' form (rather than '-ū-') signals that the noun is functioning as an object or is governed by a preposition/particle, while the '-na' completes the plural ('the truthful ones').
14.root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q) — truthfulness, sincerity, to speak truly

1.meaning: 'Do they have…? / Are there for them…?' — a questioning particle joined to 'for them.' The little word la- here means 'belonging to / for,' and with the opening hamza it asks whether something is possessed by or available to them.
1.grammar: A question particle (a-) plus the preposition la- ('for, belonging to') with the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). Together they ask, in a rhetorical or challenging way, whether a thing belongs to or exists for them. The -hum ending is the object of the preposition.

2.meaning: 'Feet / legs' — the plural of the noun for a foot or leg. The -un ending presents it indefinitely ('feet').
2.grammar: A plural noun in the indefinite nominative: the -un ending typically marks it as a subject or as something whose existence is being affirmed/questioned, and the absence of 'the' keeps it general.
2.root: ر-ج-ل (r-j-l) — foot, leg; (relatedly) to go on foot

3.meaning: 'They walk / they go on foot' — a present-tense verb for walking, moving along, or going by foot.
3.grammar: A present/ongoing action. The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a masculine plural 'they' walking now or habitually. The full -ūna ending shows the verb is in its ordinary (indicative) state.
3.root: م-ش-ي (m-sh-y) — to walk, go on foot

4.meaning: 'With it / by it / by means of it' — the preposition bi- ('with, by') joined to the pronoun 'it' (referring to a feminine or non-human-plural thing).
4.grammar: A preposition (bi-, 'with/by/by means of') plus the attached pronoun -hā ('it/her'), which stands for a feminine singular or a non-human plural. The -hā is in the object position required after a preposition.

5.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'or', specifically the 'or' that pairs with a preceding question to offer an alternative ('…or…?'). It links two possibilities being weighed against each other, often after an opening interrogative.

parts.en: or (in alternatives, esp. after a question)

5.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case or tense ending). It typically introduces the second branch of a two-part question or a balanced alternative, presenting the two as equally consequential.
5.root: — (particle; no triliteral root)

6.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
6.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

7.meaning: 'Hands' — the plural of the noun for a hand. The -in ending presents it as an indefinite noun in a possessive or after-preposition setting ('hands').
7.grammar: A plural noun in the indefinite genitive: the -in ending (the indefinite form of the genitive) typically appears after a preposition, in a possessive link ('… of …'), or on this kind of shortened noun, and marks it as indefinite ('some hands').

8.meaning: 'They grasp / seize / strike with force' — a present-tense verb for taking hold of something forcefully, gripping, or assaulting.
8.grammar: A present/ongoing action. The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a masculine plural 'they' acting now or habitually. The full -ūna ending shows the verb is in its ordinary (indicative) state. The verb denotes a forceful grasp or strike.
8.root: ب-ط-ش (b-ṭ-sh) — to seize forcefully, grasp, strike

9.meaning: 'With it / by it / by means of it' — the preposition bi- ('with, by') joined to the pronoun 'it' (referring to a feminine or non-human-plural thing).
9.grammar: A preposition (bi-, 'with/by/by means of') plus the attached pronoun -hā ('it/her'), which stands for a feminine singular or a non-human plural. The -hā is in the object position required after a preposition.

10.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'or', specifically the 'or' that pairs with a preceding question to offer an alternative ('…or…?'). It links two possibilities being weighed against each other, often after an opening interrogative.

parts.en: or (in alternatives, esp. after a question)

10.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case or tense ending). It typically introduces the second branch of a two-part question or a balanced alternative, presenting the two as equally consequential.

11.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
11.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

12.meaning: Eyes — the plural of 'eye,' the organs of sight.
12.grammar: An indefinite plural noun: 'eyes.' This is a 'plural of paucity' pattern (af'ul). The -un ending (tanwīn) is the indefinite nominative, marking the word as 'eyes' and as the subject or the thing being described.

13.meaning: 'They see / perceive' — a present-tense verb for seeing with the eyes, and by extension perceiving or discerning clearly.
13.grammar: A present/ongoing action. The yu- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a masculine plural 'they' seeing now or habitually. The yu- prefix is the marker of Form IV (the أفعل / causative pattern, أبصَرَ → يُبصِرُ), which here carries the sense of having sight or insight. The full -ūna ending shows the verb is in its ordinary (indicative) state.
13.root: ب-ص-ر (b-ṣ-r) — to see, perceive, have insight

14.meaning: 'With it / by it / by means of it' — the preposition bi- ('with, by') joined to the pronoun 'it' (referring to a feminine or non-human-plural thing).
14.grammar: A preposition (bi-, 'with/by/by means of') plus the attached pronoun -hā ('it/her'), which stands for a feminine singular or a non-human plural. The -hā is in the object position required after a preposition.

15.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'or', specifically the 'or' that pairs with a preceding question to offer an alternative ('…or…?'). It links two possibilities being weighed against each other, often after an opening interrogative.

parts.en: or (in alternatives, esp. after a question)

15.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case or tense ending). It typically introduces the second branch of a two-part question or a balanced alternative, presenting the two as equally consequential.
15.root: — (particle; no triliteral root)

16.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
16.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

17.meaning: Ears — the plural of 'ear,' the organs of hearing.
17.grammar: An indefinite plural noun: 'ears.' The -un ending (tanwīn) is the indefinite nominative, marking the word as 'ears' and as the subject or the thing being described.
17.root: ا-ذ-ن (ʾ-dh-n) — ear; to listen, give heed, permit

18.meaning: 'They hear / listen' — a present-tense verb for hearing sounds, and by extension listening or heeding.
18.grammar: A present/ongoing action. The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a masculine plural 'they' hearing now or habitually. The full -ūna ending shows the verb is in its ordinary (indicative) state.

19.meaning: with it / by it — a preposition meaning 'with' or 'by means of' joined to a pronoun referring to a single feminine (or grammatically feminine) thing.
19.grammar: The bi- prefix is a preposition meaning 'with', 'by', or 'by means of'. The attached -hā is an object pronoun meaning 'it' or 'her', referring to something feminine in gender. Together they mean 'with it' or 'by means of it'.

20.meaning: 'Say!' — a command to utter or declare something aloud, addressed to a single male.
20.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to one male: 'say!'. Its natural form ends in a silent consonant (qul), but here a short -i vowel is added simply to smooth pronunciation before a following word that begins with a connecting sound; it carries no case meaning of its own.

21.meaning: 'Call! / invoke! / summon! (you all)' — a command to a group, from the root for calling, covering summoning someone, appealing to them, or invoking (as in calling upon a deity).
21.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a masculine plural 'you all.' The plural is marked by the -ū (the waw); the verb directs the group to call upon, summon, or invoke. The final alif after the waw is purely orthographic (a silent scribal convention on plural verb endings) and carries no sound or grammatical meaning of its own.
21.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, summon, invoke, pray to

22.meaning: 'Your partners / your associates' — a plural noun for those taken as partners or associates, joined to 'your.' Often it refers to the partners falsely set up alongside Allah.
22.grammar: A plural noun with the attached possessive -kum ('your,' addressing a group). The base شُرَكَآء is a diptote broken plural (a noun class that refuses the normal indefinite -un/-in/-an tanwin); such nouns take a single fatḥa (-a) for both the accusative and the genitive instead of the usual endings. So the -a here is the diptote's case vowel, a property of this noun pattern, not a separate object suffix. The noun names partners or associates.

23.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
23.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

24.meaning: An imperative addressed to a group: 'plot against me' or 'devise your scheme against me.' It commands more than one person to set their plans, tricks, or stratagems in motion, with the speaker as the target.
24.grammar: A command directed at a plural 'you' (the -ū ending marks the masculine plural addressee). The final -ni is the nūn al-wiqāya (protective nūn) inserted to shield the verb's ending before a first-person object; the object pronoun 'me' (yāʾ) is elided, leaving only this nūn but still understood. So the whole = 'you all, scheme against me.'
24.root: ك-ي-د (k-y-d) — to plot, scheme, devise a stratagem

25.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
25.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

26.meaning: A negated or conditional verb meaning 'you (all) grant respite / give a delay.' From a root for looking and waiting, it means to give someone time, hold off, or postpone action against them.
26.grammar: Present-tense verb for a plural 'you,' shown by the tu- prefix ('you') and the -ū ending (masculine plural). The verb is in a subjunctive/jussive mood (after a negating or conditioning particle), which drops the mood-marking nūn (nūn al-iʿrāb) of the plural; the nūn that then appears, -ni, is the nūn al-wiqāya (protective nūn) that precedes a first-person object, whose pronoun yāʾ is elided but understood as 'me.' The causative form (Form IV) gives the sense 'cause to wait, grant a delay.'
26.root: ن-ظ-ر (n-ẓ-r) — to look, wait, observe; (Form IV) to grant respite

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: 'My guardian / my protecting ally.' A walī is a close protector, patron, and supporter who takes charge of one's affairs; with the possessive it means 'the one who is my guardian and ally.'
2.grammar: A noun with the attached possessive 'my' (-iya/-ī). The base word waliyy denotes a guardian-protector; the suffix makes it 'my guardian.' The case ending is largely absorbed into the possessive 'my,' which is its grammatical anchor.
2.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — nearness, guardianship, alliance, protective authority

3.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
3.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

4.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
4.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

5.meaning: A verb meaning 'he sent down / brought down', especially in stages or portions. The Form II shape adds intensity or gradualness to the basic 'descend', hence 'to send down piece by piece'.
5.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person masculine singular, Form II. The doubled middle letter marks the intensive/gradual sense; the final -a is the standard ending for a completed past-tense action done by 'he'.
5.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down, send down

6.meaning: 'The Book' — the written Scripture, a revealed text gathered and inscribed. Al-kitāb refers to a divine writing or revealed record.
6.grammar: A definite noun: al- = 'the.' The final -a is the accusative ending, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon) or follows certain particles.

7.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
7.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

8.meaning: 'He takes as a protecting friend / He takes charge of and befriends.' From the guardianship root, this verb means to ally oneself with someone, take them as a patron, turn toward them in loyalty and protection.
8.grammar: Present-tense verb for 'he,' marked by the ya- prefix. The form (Form V, tafaʿʿala) carries a reflexive/intensive sense — 'to take (someone) for oneself as an ally' or 'to turn oneself toward.' The final long -ā is the weak ending of a verb whose root ends in -y.
8.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — nearness, guardianship, alliance, taking as protector

9.meaning: The righteous, upright, and morally sound ones — people who are good, virtuous, and act rightly, putting things into proper order. Plural and referring to people.
9.grammar: A definite noun/adjective ('al-' = 'the') in the sound masculine plural. The -īna ending marks the plural in its accusative/genitive (object or 'of/from') form — the form used as a direct object or after a preposition; the parallel subject form would be -ūna.
9.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — soundness, righteousness, setting things right

1.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

2.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (all) call upon, invoke, summon, or pray to.' The root spans calling out, naming, inviting, and supplicating — especially calling on someone for help.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ta- prefix with the -ūna ending marks 'you all' (masculine plural) as the doers. The final -na is the indicative marker, signalling an ongoing or habitual action (a complete, non-shortened present-tense verb).
2.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, invoke, summon, pray

3.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
3.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

4.meaning: Other than Him / apart from Him / besides Him. A relational word expressing the idea of being below, short of, or to the exclusion of something or someone.

parts.en: other than, apart from, besides, below

4.grammar: A relational noun/quasi-preposition meaning 'apart from / instead of'. It is followed by a possessive pronoun -hi ('Him'), which puts it in the genitive 'of' relationship; the kasra written under the pronoun reflects this genitive linkage.
4.root: — (no triliteral root; a relational particle/noun)

5.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
5.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

6.meaning: They are able / they have the power and capacity — to be capable of doing something, to have the strength, means, or ability to carry it out.
6.grammar: Present-tense verb, 3rd person masculine plural ('they'). The ya- prefix marks the present tense and the 'they' subject; the -ūna ending marks the plural and the indicative mood — the plain factual form for an ongoing state. From form X, which often carries the sense of 'seeking/having the capacity for' something, here simply 'to be able.'
6.root: ط-و-ع (ṭ-w-ʿ) — to obey, to be capable, willing capacity

7.meaning: 'Your help / your aiding (you all).' Naṣr is victory-bringing aid — support given to make someone prevail. With the suffix it means the help that belongs to, or is owed to, a group 'you.'
7.grammar: A verbal noun 'help' with the possessive 'your' for a plural addressee (-kum). The -a before the suffix reflects the accusative ending, typically marking the word as a direct object or otherwise governed noun.
7.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, aid, give victory

8.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
8.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

9.meaning: A noun meaning 'their own selves' or 'themselves' — the plural of 'nafs' (self, soul, person, inner self), joined to the pronoun 'their.' It commonly conveys the reflexive idea of acting upon one's own self.
9.grammar: A noun (a broken/irregular plural of 'nafs') with the attached possessive pronoun '-hum' ('their/them,' masculine plural). The -a case ending before the pronoun is accusative, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb — i.e. the self upon which the action falls.
9.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — self, soul, person; breath

10.meaning: 'They help / they give victory' — a present-tense verb meaning to come to someone's aid or support them against an enemy.
10.grammar: A present/ongoing action. The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a masculine plural 'they' acting now or habitually. The full -ūna ending shows the verb is in its ordinary (indicative) state, not shortened by a governing particle.
10.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, aid, give victory

1.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
1.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

2.meaning: 'You call them / you invoke them' — a present-tense verb. From the root for calling, it covers summoning, appealing to, or invoking someone (as in calling upon a deity). The attached pronoun is the object, 'them.'
2.grammar: A present-tense action with a 'you' (masculine) subject built into the ta- prefix. The attached -hum is the object pronoun 'them' (masculine plural). The verb commonly carries the sense of calling upon or invoking.
2.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, summon, invoke, pray to

3.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
3.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

4.meaning: The guidance; the right leading and true direction (with the definite article, 'the Guidance').
4.grammar: A definite verbal noun: the prefix al- means 'the'. It ends in a long -ā (from a weak-final root), an ending that does not change for case. It denotes the abstract reality of right guidance, made specific and definite by 'the'.
4.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, lead rightly, show the way

5.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
5.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

6.meaning: 'They hear / they listen.' A verb of perceiving sound; by extension, to heed or pay attention to what is said.
6.grammar: Present-tense verb for a plural 'they' (masculine): the ya- prefix with the -ū ending marks the masculine plural subject. The missing final nūn indicates a subjunctive/jussive mood, typical after a negating or conditioning particle.

7.meaning: 'And you see them / and you observe them.' Combines 'and' with the verb 'you see,' followed by 'them.' From a root for sight and perception.
7.grammar: wa- = 'and.' The verb is present tense for 'you' (singular), marked by the ta- prefix; its root ends in a weak letter, giving the long -ā. The attached -hum means 'them' (masculine plural), the object of seeing.

8.meaning: They look toward, watch for, or await; a present-tense act of a group either gazing at something or expecting/waiting for it to happen.
8.grammar: A present/ongoing verb. The ya- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ("they"). The full -ūna ending also signals the indicative mood, used for stating an action that is happening or habitual.

9.meaning: 'To you' (addressing one person): indicating direction or motion toward a single individual — that toward which something moves or is directed.
9.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to, towards') with an attached pronoun; before a suffix ilā takes the form ilay-. The -ka ending is the pronoun 'you' for a single male addressee. Pronouns following a preposition stand in the genitive relationship, though their form does not visibly change for case.
9.root: — (preposition + pronoun)

10.meaning: 'While they / and they' — the word 'wa' (here 'while' or 'and') joined to the standalone pronoun 'hum' ('they'), referring to a masculine plural group.
10.grammar: A connective 'wa' — often circumstantial 'while' — plus the independent subject pronoun 'hum' ('they'), used for a masculine plural group. As an independent pronoun it usually stands as the subject of a following statement.

11.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
11.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

12.meaning: To see, perceive with the eyes, or have insight — to look and take in, with a nuance of clear perception and understanding, not mere glancing. Used of a group: 'they see / perceive'.
12.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they see'). The yu- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks an ongoing or repeated action done by a group of males or a mixed group. The -ūna ending is the 'indicative' form used when the verb is not preceded by something that would shorten it.

1.meaning: 'Take! / Hold! / Adopt!' A direct command to one person to take hold of, seize, accept, or adopt something.
1.grammar: A singular imperative ('you, take'). The base command is khudh; the final -i here is a connecting vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a cluster, not a case ending. The verb comes from a root whose initial hamza is dropped in the command form.
1.root: ء-خ-ذ (ʾ-kh-dh) — to take, seize, grasp, adopt

2.meaning: The surplus or excess (what is left over beyond one's needs); also pardon, forgiveness, and overlooking faults. The same root joins the senses of 'what is easily given/spared' and 'to pardon'.
2.grammar: A noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The final -a ending marks the accusative case, the form typically used for the object of a verb ('[give] the surplus') or as the answer to a question.
2.root: ع-ف-و (ʿ-f-w) — to pardon; to be in excess/spare

3.meaning: 'And command / and enjoin.' Combines 'and' with the singular imperative 'order' — to instruct or bid someone to do something.
3.grammar: wa- = 'and.' The rest is a singular imperative 'command/order' (you, one person). The form comes from a root whose initial hamza is normally elided, leaving 'mur'; the ending has no vowel (jussive/command form).

4.meaning: 'With/by what is recognized as good' — al-ʿurf denotes the customary good, what is commonly acknowledged as right and fitting, kindness and decency that people recognize.
4.grammar: bi- = 'with/by'; l- = 'the.' The final -i is the genitive ending, which here is required because the noun follows the preposition bi- ('with'). The word names the good that is customarily recognized.
4.root: ع-ر-ف (ʿ-r-f) — to know, recognize; what is recognized as good and fitting

5.meaning: and turn away / avert yourself, disregard. A command to draw back from something and present one's side to it rather than engaging, from a root tied to a 'side' and to turning aside.
5.grammar: A command (imperative) to a single male: 'turn away!' The final consonant takes no case vowel (jussive form), which is standard for an order. The a- at the start is the command prefix of this verb pattern.
5.root: ع-ر-ض (ʿ-r-ḍ) — side, breadth; turning aside, presenting/averting

6.meaning: About / concerning; a particle marking the topic of inquiry or the thing one moves away from.
6.grammar: A preposition meaning 'about, concerning, away from'. Its base form is ʿan; the final -i here is a helping vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a connecting 'al-'. It governs the genitive case on whatever noun follows.

7.meaning: 'The ignorant ones' — those marked by jahl: ignorance of the truth, or the reckless, unrestrained conduct that springs from it. It describes people who act without knowledge or proper self-control.
7.grammar: A definite active participle ('the ignorant ones'): 'al-' is 'the', and jāhil is the doer-noun 'one who is ignorant'. The -īna ending is the masculine sound-plural in its accusative/genitive form, used when the word is an object, follows a preposition, or completes a verb like 'to be'.

1.meaning: And if (ever), and whenever. Combines 'and' with a conditional particle that introduces a possibility, often paired with an emphatic verb ('and should it ever happen that...').
1.grammar: The conjunction wa- ('and') plus immā, a conditional particle (the conditional 'in' fused with emphatic '-mā'). It sets up a hypothetical — 'and if it should ever be that...' — and frequently precedes a verb stressed with a heavy 'definitely' ending.

2.meaning: 'There should surely incite you / prompt you (a provocation).' From a root for goading and stirring up; it describes an impulse or instigation prodding a person toward discord or wrong.
2.grammar: Present-tense verb for 'it/he' (ya- prefix). The doubled -nna is the heavy emphatic ending ('shall surely / certainly'), often used after a conditioning particle. The attached -ka means 'you' (one male). Together: 'should it ever surely prod you.'
2.root: ن-ز-غ (n-z-gh) — to goad, incite, stir up discord

3.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
3.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

4.meaning: The Shayṭān — Satan, the devil: a rebellious, evil being who tempts and misleads; the term suggests one who is far removed from goodness and burning in defiance.
4.grammar: A definite masculine noun ('the Satan / the devil'). The final -i is the genitive ending, which generally links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …') or follows a preposition.
4.root: ش-ط-ن (sh-ṭ-n) — to be remote (from good/mercy); a devil

5.meaning: 'A goading / an incitement / a prompting (to evil).' The noun for a stirring impulse that prods one toward discord or wrongdoing.
5.grammar: A noun with the ending -un, which marks it as indefinite ('a/an…') and in the nominative case — the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or a thing simply being named.
5.root: ن-ز-غ (n-z-gh) — to goad, incite, stir up discord

6.meaning: 'Then seek refuge / so take protection.' Combines 'then/so' with the command to seek shelter and protection (with Allah) from a danger.
6.grammar: fa- = 'then/so' (linking a response to what precedes). The verb is a singular imperative in the seeking-form (Form X, istafʿala = 'to seek/ask for'), so it means 'seek protection for yourself' (with Allah). The unvoweled ending is the command/jussive form.
6.root: ع-و-ذ (ʿ-w-dh) — to seek refuge, take shelter, protect oneself

7.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
7.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
7.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

8.meaning: An emphasis particle fused with a pronoun, meaning 'indeed He' or 'truly He'. The particle inna strongly affirms and certifies the statement that follows ('it is certainly the case that…'), with 'He' as its subject.
8.grammar: The emphasising particle inna ('indeed/truly') with the attached pronoun -hu ('He'). inna affirms and strengthens the whole statement and grammatically takes a following noun or pronoun as its subject. The lengthened -hū is how this pronoun is pronounced after an -u vowel.

9.meaning: All-Hearing / ever-hearing — one who hears completely and perfectly, missing nothing of what is uttered or whispered; an intensive form stressing the fullness of the quality. The '-un' nunation marks it as indefinite nominative.
9.grammar: An intensive adjective (faʿīl pattern) conveying a constant, perfect quality. The '-un' (nunation on the ḍamma) marks it as indefinite and in the nominative case, typically used for a subject or predicate ("is all-hearing").
9.root: س-م-ع (s-m-ʿ) — to hear, listen

10.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'All-Knowing / fully aware' — one whose knowledge is complete, deep, and all-encompassing; as a divine attribute it denotes Allah's perfect knowledge.
10.grammar: An intensive adjective (the pattern faʿīl conveys 'thoroughly, abundantly'). The ending -un is the indefinite nominative — the nominative case marks it as the subject or the quality being affirmed, and the -n (nunation) signals 'a / an', i.e. indefinite. So it reads '(is) all-knowing'.

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: 'They were mindful of Allah / guarded themselves'. This is the act of taqwā: being conscious of Allah, guarding oneself against wrongdoing out of reverence for Him, and shielding oneself from His displeasure. Past tense, masculine plural.

parts.en: to be mindful of Allah / guard oneself

3.grammar: This is a past-tense verb of the reflexive/intensive pattern (form VIII), conveying that the subjects actively guarded and protected themselves. The '-aw' (written ـوا) ending marks a masculine plural subject acting in completed past time ('they did').

4.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
4.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.
4.root: — (a time particle; no triliteral root)

5.meaning: 'It touched them / afflicted them.' From a root for touching or contact; used of something (often harm, hardship, or an influence) coming into contact with people.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb for 'he/it' (massa), with no prefix — past tense is shown by the bare stem and its -a ending. The attached -hum means 'them' (masculine plural), the ones touched. The doubled middle letter is part of the root.
5.root: م-س-س (m-s-s) — to touch, make contact, afflict

6.meaning: 'A visitation / a passing touch' — ṭāʾif is something that circles round and comes upon a person, used of an intruding impulse, a passing affliction, or a hovering thought.
6.grammar: An active participle (one 'that goes around / visits') used as a noun. The -un ending marks it as indefinite ('a…') and nominative — the case for a subject or a thing simply named. From a root meaning to circle or go around.
6.root: ط-و-ف (ṭ-w-f) — to circle, go around, visit, come upon

7.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
7.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

8.meaning: The Shayṭān — Satan, the devil: a rebellious, evil being who tempts and misleads; the term suggests one who is far removed from goodness and burning in defiance.
8.grammar: A definite masculine noun ('the Satan / the devil'). The final -i is the genitive ending, which generally links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …') or follows a preposition.
8.root: ش-ط-ن (sh-ṭ-n) — to be remote (from good/mercy); a devil

9.meaning: 'They remembered / became mindful / took heed.' From a root for remembering; in this intensified form it means to call to mind, reflect, and become conscious (especially of Allah and the truth).
9.grammar: A past-tense verb for 'they' (masculine plural), shown by the -ū ending. The form (Form V, tafaʿʿala) adds a reflexive/effortful nuance: to bring something to one's own mind, to reflect and heed. The doubled middle letter belongs to this pattern.
9.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, mention, call to mind, take heed

10.meaning: A connecting phrase meaning 'then when / and when', introducing a circumstance whose occurrence triggers a following response. 'Fa-' links it to what precedes; 'idhā' sets up a 'when … (then) …' condition for something expected to happen.
10.grammar: A particle cluster, not a noun or verb, so it has no case ending. 'Idhā' is a conditional/temporal particle ('when') used for events regarded as bound to occur, and it normally introduces a clause followed by a main response. The prefixed fa- ('then/so') ties the whole condition to the preceding statement.

11.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
11.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

12.meaning: 'Ones who see clearly / those given sight and discernment.' The plural of one who perceives — by extension, those who see the truth plainly and have insight.
12.grammar: An active participle (Form IV, 'one who has sight / sees clearly') in the masculine plural. The -ūna ending marks a masculine plural in the nominative case — the case used for the subject or for a predicate describing the subject.
12.root: ب-ص-ر (b-ṣ-r) — to see, perceive, have insight and discernment

1.meaning: 'And their brothers / brethren.' Ikhwān is a plural of 'brother,' used for brethren, kin, or close associates and companions; with the suffix, 'the brethren belonging to them.'
1.grammar: wa- = 'and.' The base is a plural noun 'brethren.' The -u before the possessive is the nominative ending — the case for a subject or a thing simply named. The attached -hum = 'their' (masculine plural).

2.meaning: 'They extend / draw them on / prolong them.' From a root for stretching and extending; used of leading someone ever onward (here, drawing them further into error).
2.grammar: Present-tense verb for 'they' (masculine plural). The -ū marks the plural subject and the retained -na shows the indicative mood (a plain, ongoing statement). The attached -hum = 'them,' the object. The doubled middle letter is part of the root.
2.root: م-د-د (m-d-d) — to extend, stretch out, prolong, draw on

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
3.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

4.meaning: Error, going astray, deviation; the misguided wrong course, the loss of right direction that stands opposite to sound guidance.
4.grammar: A definite masculine noun. The -i ending is genitive, the case that typically follows a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ("… OF …"). The al- prefix makes it definite ("the").
4.root: غ-و-ي (gh-w-y) — going astray, error, deviation from the right way

5.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
5.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

6.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
6.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

7.meaning: 'They desist / fall short / leave off.' From a root for shortening and falling short; in this form it means to stop short of something, to slacken or cease an effort.
7.grammar: Present-tense verb for 'they' (masculine plural). The yu- prefix marks the Form IV pattern (here meaning 'to desist, fall short, leave off' — not a causative sense), the -ū marks the plural subject, and the retained -na shows the indicative mood (a plain ongoing statement). Sense: to stop short or slacken.
7.root: ق-ص-ر (q-ṣ-r) — to fall short, shorten, desist, slacken

1.meaning: 'And when...' — a linking phrase joining 'and' to 'when', used to introduce a circumstance or a recurring situation: 'and whenever / and at the time that...'.
