1.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to idhā ('when'). Idhā is a particle pointing to a time or condition, generally referring to something expected or recurring in the future ('when / whenever' it happens), and it normally introduces a following clause that states what occurs at that time.

2.meaning: A negating particle, 'not', used specifically to deny that an action happened in the past, even though it attaches to a present-tense verb form. It turns 'you do X' into 'you did not do X'.

parts.en: did not (negation of a completed act)

2.grammar: An indeclinable particle that governs the verb after it, putting that verb into the jussive (clipped) mood and giving it past-time meaning. In short: lam + a present-form verb = 'did not [verb]'.

3.meaning: 'You bring them / you come to them with (something).' From a root for coming/bringing; the verb 'you bring' with 'them' attached.
3.grammar: Present-tense verb for 'you' (singular), with the ta- prefix. Its weak final root letter and the unvoweled ending reflect the jussive/conditional mood (typical after a conditioning particle). The attached -him = 'them' (the -i vowel of the pronoun follows a preceding -i sound).

4.meaning: With a sign — by means of an indicative token, miracle, or evidentiary proof that points to a truth.
4.grammar: The prefix bi- means 'with / by means of' and always pulls the following noun into the genitive. The final -in (tanwīn) is the indefinite genitive: 'with a sign', the ending required after this preposition and marking the noun as indefinite ('a', not 'the').
4.root: أ-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — sign, mark, token; a verse of scripture

5.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.
5.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, utterance

6.meaning: A particle of urging or exhortation meaning 'why not …?' — used to press for or demand that something be done, and sometimes to express a wish, often with a tone of reproach ('why does … not happen?').
6.grammar: An indivisible particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ). Although written as one form, it is not built up from the conditional 'if' plus a negation; in this prompting usage it is a single fixed particle meaning 'why not?' / 'if only.' Followed by a verb it presses for that action. (Note: in a different construction the same form can mean 'were it not for,' but that is a separate usage.) It is a particle and takes no case ending.

7.meaning: 'You chose it / selected it / picked it out.' From a root for gathering and selecting; in this form it means to single something out and choose it for oneself, often with the sense of fabricating or hand-picking.
7.grammar: A past-tense verb in the self-selecting form (Form VIII, iftaʿala). The -ta ending marks 'you' (one person) as the doer. The attached -hā means 'it' (a feminine or non-human thing), the object chosen. The root's final weak letter appears as -ay-.
7.root: ج-ب-ي (j-b-y) — to gather, collect, select, single out

8.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
8.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

9.meaning: 'Only / nothing but' — a restrictive particle that limits and emphasizes, asserting that the matter is exclusively so and no other ('it is only...'). It combines the emphatic 'inna' with the restricting 'mā'.
9.grammar: A compound particle formed from the emphatic inna ('indeed') and mā, which together work as a tool of restriction meaning 'only / nothing but'. It both stresses and confines the statement that follows to a single truth, excluding all alternatives.

10.meaning: 'I follow / pursue / adhere to' — to go after something and take it as one's guide or example, following in its track. The form conveys actively following or conforming to something.

parts.en: follow / adhere to (present-tense stem of the 'follow closely' pattern)

10.grammar: A present-tense verb with the 'a-' prefix meaning 'I'. The doubled 't' at the start of the stem belongs to the verb-pattern that means following closely or taking as a guide. The '-u' ending is the ordinary present-tense form for an ongoing action: 'I follow'.

11.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
11.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

12.meaning: 'It is revealed / inspired' — for a message to be conveyed by Allah to a prophet, whether by inspiration, sign, or revealed word. This is the passive sense: the revelation is sent to the recipient.

parts.en: he/it (third-person masculine present prefix, passive vowel)
is revealed / inspired (passive stem ending in a long final vowel)

12.grammar: A present-tense verb in the passive voice: the 'yu-' prefix with the internal vowel pattern means 'it is (being) revealed' — the action is done TO the subject. The verb ends in a fixed long '-ā' vowel because its final root letter is weak; this form is the same in the passive present regardless of case.
12.root: و-ح-ي (w-ḥ-y) — revelation, inspiration, conveying a message

13.meaning: 'To me / toward me.' It joins the preposition ilā, meaning 'to / toward,' with an attached first-person 'me,' expressing motion or direction toward the speaker.
13.grammar: A preposition meaning 'to / toward' with the attached pronoun 'me.' The base preposition is ilā, ending in a long vowel (written with alif maqsūra, ى). When the 'me' pronoun attaches, that final long vowel turns into yāʾ and merges with the pronoun's yāʾ, giving a doubled, stressed -ayya — the whole word reading ilayya, 'to me.'

14.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
14.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

15.meaning: 'My Lord' — the word 'rabb' denotes the Lord, Master, Sustainer and Nurturer who creates, owns, governs and brings a thing to its full development; with the attached 'my' it expresses one's own Lord and Caretaker.
15.grammar: A noun followed by the possessive ending '-ī' meaning 'my', which joins to the noun and also serves the genitive (possessive) relationship. The attached '-ī' both makes the noun definite and shows ownership: 'my Lord'.
15.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, nurturing, sustaining

16.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
16.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

17.meaning: Insights, clear proofs, or means of perception — things that bring inner sight and discernment, enabling one to see truth clearly. The plural of baṣīra ('inner vision, insight').
17.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of baṣīra, following the diptote pattern. The final -u is the nominative ending, the case typically marking the subject or a noun standing on its own. (As a diptote, this plural pattern does not take nunation.)
17.root: ب-ص-ر (b-ṣ-r) — to see, perceive, have insight

18.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
18.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

19.meaning: 'Your Lord' (addressing a group). 'Rabb' is a rich term: the Master, Owner, Sustainer and Nurturer who creates, possesses, provides for, and brings a thing to its proper completion — far more than a mere ruler.
19.grammar: A noun ('Lord') with an attached possessive pronoun, forming a possessive pairing. 'Rabb' carries a doubled (geminated) 'b' — the shaddah — at its core. The '-i' vowel on 'rabb' is its case ending, determined by 'Lord's' own role in the sentence (not by the suffix); the attached '-kum' is the possessor ('your'), addressing a plural 'you', and as the possessed-to term it sits in the genitive.

20.meaning: A connective 'and' plus 'guidance' — 'and guidance': right direction, the showing of the correct way, that which leads one rightly.
20.grammar: The prefix wa- is the connective 'and'. 'hudā' is a noun meaning 'guidance'; because it ends in a special shortened alif, its indefinite ending appears as -an (written with tanwīn over the preceding letter). This -an is the indefinite marker; on such alif-ending nouns the case is not separately shown, so the word can stand as subject, object, or predicate alike.

21.meaning: And mercy — compassion, tenderness, and active kindness shown to others; clemency that issues in relief and care.
21.grammar: An indefinite feminine singular noun. The ending -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a mercy') and in the nominative case, the form used for a subject or for something simply being named. The wa- prefix is 'and.'

22.meaning: For a people, for a folk or community; a group of human beings considered together. Joined to the preposition 'li' ('for / to').
22.grammar: The preposition 'li' ('for / to') plus an indefinite singular noun ('a people'). The -in ending (nunation) marks indefiniteness; it is the genitive form, required because nouns governed by 'li' stand in the genitive.
22.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a people/community

23.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'they believe / they have faith' — to trust and affirm with the heart, to hold something true and place one's security in it.
23.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb built on the form IV pattern, which here functions intransitively, 'to have faith / to believe' (not a causative making someone else believe). The yu- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they.' The full -ūna ending (indicative mood) presents the action as ongoing or habitual fact: 'they (do) believe.'

1.meaning: 'And when...' — a linking phrase joining 'and' to 'when', used to introduce a circumstance or a recurring situation: 'and whenever / and at the time that...'.
1.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to idhā ('when'). Idhā is a particle pointing to a time or condition, generally referring to something expected or recurring in the future ('when / whenever' it happens), and it normally introduces a following clause that states what occurs at that time.

2.meaning: 'It was recited / it was read aloud.' From the root for reading and reciting; the passive past tense — the action of reciting done to the thing, with no doer named.
2.grammar: A past-tense passive verb for 'it/he.' The internal vowel pattern (u after the first letter, i before the last) marks the passive voice — 'was recited' rather than 'recited' — and the final -a is the past-tense ending for a 'he/it' subject. No actor is stated; the focus is on what is recited.
2.root: ق-ر-ء (q-r-ʾ) — to read, recite, gather words together

3.meaning: The Qur'ān — literally 'the Recitation' or 'that which is read aloud'; the name of the revealed Scripture, understood as something recited.
3.grammar: A definite verbal noun ('the recitation') used as a proper name. The final -u is the nominative case, the ending that typically marks the subject or the thing being identified.
3.root: ق-ر-ا (q-r-ʾ) — to read, recite, gather together

4.meaning: A command addressed to a group: 'so/then listen!' The base verb istamaʿa means to listen attentively, to lend one's ear and take in what is said — stronger and more deliberate than merely hearing. The opening fa- adds the sense of 'and so' or 'then', linking the command to something preceding it as a consequence.
4.grammar: A command (imperative) directed at more than one person. The -ū ending marks a masculine plural addressee, i.e. 'you all (do this)'. The prefixed fa- is a connecting particle meaning 'then / so / and as a result', tying the order to what came before. The verb belongs to Form X (istafʿala, pattern istaf'ala, with the characteristic ist- prefix), which often adds the sense of seeking or applying oneself — hence active, attentive listening.
4.root: س-م-ع (s-m-ʿ) — hearing, listening

5.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
5.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

6.meaning: A command addressed to a group: 'and be silent / pay close attention!' The verb anṣata means to fall silent in order to listen, to give one's quiet, undivided attention to a speaker. It pairs the idea of hushing oneself with that of heeding.
6.grammar: A command (imperative) to more than one person; the -ū ending marks a masculine plural addressee ('you all'). The prefixed wa- means 'and', joining this order to another. The verb is Form IV (afʿala), a pattern that here conveys entering into a state — becoming silent and attentive.

7.meaning: 'so that you may…,' 'in the hope that you…' — a particle expressing purpose, expectation, or hopeful anticipation, fused with 'you (plural).' It introduces a hoped-for or intended outcome; when used of Allah it conveys the desired result rather than uncertainty.

parts.en: so that / perhaps / in hope that

7.grammar: An emphatic particle of hope/purpose belonging to the 'inna' family, which attaches a pronoun as its subject. The particle's fixed form ends in '-a,' and the suffix '-kum' is 'you (plural),' giving 'so that you (all) may…'

8.meaning: '(that) you may receive mercy / be shown mercy' — to be treated with compassion and mercy by another. Addressed to a group, with the doer of the mercy unnamed.
8.grammar: A present-tense passive verb, second-person masculine plural ('you all are shown mercy' — the subject receives the action rather than doing it). The full '-ūna' ending is the indicative, marking a plain ongoing statement; it often follows a particle expressing hoped-for result ('so that you may be shown mercy').

1.meaning: And remember / call to mind / mention — a command to bring something to mind, keep it in remembrance, or speak of it; in religious usage it carries the sense of mindful, devotional remembrance.
1.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to one male, 'remember!' / 'mention!', prefixed by 'and'. The vowelless ending (sukūn on the final r) is the normal form of a singular masculine command.
1.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, mention, call to mind

2.meaning: Your Lord — Rabb denotes the Lord, Master, Sustainer and Nurturer who creates, owns, and continually cares for and brings to maturity all that He governs; here addressed to a single male possessor.
2.grammar: A masculine noun with the accusative -a ending (commonly marking the object of a verb) plus the possessive suffix -ka ('your', one male). Rabb is a rich term — far more than 'lord' in the social sense — combining ownership, authority, and nurturing care.
2.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, lord over

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
3.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

4.meaning: 'Yourself / your own self / your soul' — the noun 'nafs' (self, soul, person, inner being) carrying the possessive 'your' (single male).
4.grammar: The noun 'nafs' ('self/soul') with the second-person masculine-singular possessive ending '-ka' (here '-ika'): 'your self'. The attached possessive can sit on any case, so it alone does not mark subject or object.
4.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — soul, self, breath; the inner being of a person

5.meaning: In humble entreaty, beseeching submission — the manner of one who lowers himself and pleads earnestly. Describes how an action is performed: humbly and imploringly.
5.grammar: A verbal noun (tafaʿʿul pattern) naming the act of humble pleading. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative, here functioning adverbially to describe the manner of an action ('… in/with humility').
5.root: ض-ر-ع (ḍ-r-ʿ) — to humble oneself, to plead

6.meaning: 'And (with / in) fear, awe.' The noun khīfa denotes fear, dread, or reverent awe — an inner trembling before something great or feared. It often carries the nuance of a humble, reverent fear rather than mere fright.
6.grammar: A feminine singular noun. The -an (tanwīn) ending marks the indefinite accusative case, which commonly signals that the word functions as an object, or expresses manner or state — i.e. doing something 'in a state of fear' or 'fearfully'. The prefixed wa- means 'and'.

7.meaning: 'And without / beneath / short of.' Dūna is a preposition-like word meaning 'without', 'apart from', 'below', or 'less than' — it points to something falling short of, or excluded from, a stated level or thing.
7.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/preposition of place and degree that governs a following noun in the genitive ('… without / below X'). Its fixed -a ending does not change for case here. The prefixed wa- means 'and'.
7.root: د-و-ن (d-w-n) — lowness, being below / short of

8.meaning: 'The loudness / the raising of the voice.' Al-jahr refers to openness, audibility, and speaking aloud — making something plainly heard or done in the open, the opposite of what is hidden or whispered.
8.grammar: A masculine noun made definite by the prefixed al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding preposition or another noun in an 'of / from' relationship.
8.root: ج-ه-ر (j-h-r) — to be loud, open, audible

9.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
9.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

10.meaning: Speech, an utterance, a statement, or a saying — that which is said. It denotes the act or content of speaking.
10.grammar: A definite noun ('the speech'). The -i ending is the genitive case: it typically links the word to a preceding noun in an 'of …' relationship or follows a preposition.

11.meaning: 'In / at the morning(s).' Al-ghuduww denotes the early part of the day, the time of forenoon or morning — the period of setting out at daybreak. The prefixed bi- adds 'in', 'at', or 'during'.
11.grammar: A masculine noun made definite by al- ('the') and governed by the preposition bi- ('in / at'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which is the case a noun takes after a preposition such as bi-.

12.meaning: 'And in the evenings / late afternoons.' Al-āṣāl is the plural of aṣīl, the time of late afternoon stretching toward sunset — the closing part of the day. It is a natural counterpart to the morning hours.
12.grammar: A masculine broken (irregular) plural noun made definite by al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, here following from a governing preposition carried over earlier in the phrase. The prefixed wa- means 'and'.

13.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
13.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

14.meaning: A short (jussive) form of the verb 'to be / to become', meaning 'be' or 'does not become / is not'. It expresses being, existing, or coming to be in a clipped form that typically follows a particle such as a negator or a command.
14.grammar: Present-tense verb with the ta- prefix marking a second-person masculine singular ('you') or third-person feminine singular ('it/she') subject. The clipped final consonant (sukun, no vowel) is the jussive/apocopated mood, the form used after negative particles ('did not / was not') or as a command or prohibition.
14.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

15.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
15.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

16.meaning: 'The heedless / the unaware ones.' Al-ghāfilīn are those who are negligent, inattentive, and oblivious — people sunk in heedlessness, failing to take notice or remember what they should mind. The -īn ending is the oblique (genitive/accusative) form of the masculine sound plural.
16.grammar: An active participle ('one who is heedless') in the masculine sound plural, made definite by al- ('the'). The -īna ending marks the masculine plural in the genitive or accusative case — typically used when the word is an object, or follows a preposition or another governing noun.
16.root: غ-ف-ل (gh-f-l) — heedlessness, negligence, inattention

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: 'With / in the presence of / near' — an adverb of place and relation meaning at, by, in the sight or estimation of someone. It indicates nearness, possession, or what holds in someone's view (as in 'with Allah' = in His sight).
3.grammar: An adverb of place that is always followed by a noun it relates to. It carries a fixed -a ending; this accusative-type vowel is characteristic of such adverbs of place and shows the word is functioning to locate something ('at, near, in the presence of').

4.meaning: A noun with an attached pronoun meaning 'your Lord' — the Lord/Master/Sustainer of a single person addressed. Rabb conveys an owner who creates, nurtures, sustains, and governs all that is under His care.
4.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord, Sustainer') carries the -i genitive vowel, which typically appears when the noun follows a preposition or is itself possessed by a following noun ('… of your Lord'). The suffix -ka means 'your', addressed to a single male.
4.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship; to nurture, sustain, master

5.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
5.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

6.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'they act arrogantly, deem themselves great, behave with haughty pride' — to puff oneself up and disdain to submit or yield.
6.grammar: A present-tense (form X) verb. The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The full -ūna ending signals the indicative mood, used for a plain, ongoing statement of fact. Form X here carries the sense of considering oneself great.
6.root: ك-ب-ر (k-b-r) — greatness, bigness; here, self-magnification and pride

7.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on behalf of,' 'for,' 'about,' or 'away from.' It often conveys removing a burden from someone or acting in their place.

parts.en: on behalf of / for / away from

7.grammar: A preposition (a linking particle). It governs the noun that follows it, putting that noun into the genitive case. It does not change form.

8.meaning: 'His worship / service' — the act of worshipping and serving, joined to a possessor ('His'). ʿibāda denotes devoted worship and humble servitude offered to Allah.
8.grammar: A verbal noun (the noun of the act of worshipping), feminine, with the attached possessive suffix meaning 'his/His'. The -i ending is genitive, the case taken when a noun is possessed by a following pronoun or governed by a preposition; the suffix form -hi (rather than -hu) follows that -i vowel.

9.meaning: 'And they glorify Him' / 'they declare Him free of all imperfection.' The verb sabbaḥa means to extol Allah's absolute transcendence and perfection, proclaiming Him far above any flaw or unworthy attribute. The attached pronoun 'Him' is its object.

parts.en: he glorifies / declares free of fault

9.grammar: A present-tense verb in Form II (the doubled-middle pattern, which intensifies the action). The ya- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks a masculine plural 'they (do)' in the ongoing/present sense; the -ūna ending also signals the indicative (a statement of fact). The suffix -hu is an object pronoun, 'Him'. The prefixed wa- means 'and'.
9.root: س-ب-ح (s-b-ḥ) — to glorify, declare free of imperfection (also: to swim, move swiftly)

10.meaning: And for him / and he has — the connector 'and', the preposition 'for/to', and the pronoun 'him'. Together it expresses possession or belonging ('and to him belongs …', 'and he has …').
10.grammar: A small phrase, not a verb: the connector wa- ('and') + the preposition la- ('for/to') + the pronoun -hu ('him'). The preposition with a pronoun commonly conveys having or belonging ('he has', 'belonging to him').

11.meaning: 'They prostrate / they bow down in worship.' The verb sajada means to lower oneself to the ground in prostration — placing the forehead down in the deepest posture of submission and humility before Allah.
11.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a masculine plural 'they (do)' in the ongoing/present sense; the -ūna ending also marks the indicative mood (a plain statement of fact). The mark ۩ following it is a recitation symbol indicating a place of prostration, not part of the word.
11.root: س-ج-د (s-j-d) — prostration, bowing down in worship
